nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning

**Discipline / Category**: Chemical Processing  
**Target Generation**: Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type**: Make

---

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / ISO Class 6 laminar flow bench, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (acid/solvent exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Substrate Fixturing
- Mount substrate securely onto vacuum chuck stage and align mechanical/optical fiducials.
- Zero baseline instruments and establish background electrical/chemical noise floor.

### 3. Recipe Execution & Parameter Control
- Execute process sequence according to verified engineering specifications.
- Monitor thermal, optical, or chemical rate transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Acceptance
- Perform quantitative verification using 4-Point Probe / Ellipsometer / Fume Hood Interlock.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Station exhaust and DI water loop (18.2 MOhm-cm, particle filter 0.1 um) must interlock prior to wafer boat immersion. Rinse cascade must terminate downstream acid carries before SC-2.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: BOE 6:1 (NH4F:HF) etch rate must be calibrated at 70-80 nm/min at 25°C. SC-1 (5:1:1 H2O:NH4OH:H2O2) must be maintained at 75°C +/- 2°C to eliminate light organics without pitting Si.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Electronic-grade semiconductor reagents (VLSI/MOS grade) must be procured from certified chemical distributors; technical-grade chemicals will induce metallic surface poisoning (Fe, Cu, Ni > 1e10 atoms/cm2).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 24-32 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Chemical cross-contamination or incomplete dump rinse leaves watermark defects and micro-masking during subsequent etch).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Watermark defect formation during static pull-out from hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic transition.
1. Exhaust face-velocity drop below 0.5 m/s causing acid vapor condensation on cleanroom tooling.
1. Over-etch in BOE undercut exceeding 50 nm, destroying contact via dimensional margins.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-01` | **Post-Clean Particle & Metallic Trace Contamination Assay** | Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner (KLA-Tencor / Surfscan) & TXRF Spectrometer | 1. Load unpatterned witness silicon wafer into darkfield laser scatterometer. 2. Scan complete surface for light point defects (LPD) at size bin >= 180 nm. 3. Perform Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) for trace Fe, Cu, Ni surface concentrations. | `LPD count (>= 180 nm) < 10 defects/wafer (Pass); Transition metals (Fe, Ni, Cu) < 5e10 atoms/cm2 (Pass).` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-02` | **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) Step Height & Lateral Undercut Profilometry** | Stylus Profilometer (Veeco Dektak XT) / Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) | 1. Zero stylus force baseline at 3 mg on planar SiO2 field. 2. Scan 200 um profile across etched contact window step at 20 um/s scan speed. 3. Record step height h_step and lateral undercut under resist margin. | `Etch depth matches target +/- 5% (Pass); lateral undercut <= 35 nm (Pass); surface roughness Ra < 0.5 nm (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty butyl/neoprene gloves (0.7 mm thickness, tested for HF permeation), Full-face polycarbonate splash shield over ANSI Z87.1 safety goggles, Acid-resistant chemical apron with sleeves (PVC/Neoprene), Acid gas vapor cartridge respirator (NIOSH approved for HF/HCl)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: MANDATORY ON-SITE ANTIDOTE: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%). In case of HF skin contact: Flush immediately under emergency drench shower for 2-3 minutes, then vigorously massage Calcium Gluconate Gel into affected skin continuously until emergency medical response arrives. Never apply standard burn creams.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated polypropylene wet bench with vertical laminar exhaust face velocity >= 0.55 m/s. Interlocked with wet acid scrubber.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate fluoride effluent. Neutralize with Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2). Verify pH 7.0-8.5 before drain discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF)** | `7664-39-3` | VLSI/MOS Electronic Grade (< 1 ppb metals) | `49% conc. or 1:50 DHF` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (NH4F)** | `12125-01-8` | Electronic Grade | `40% aq (for BOE 6:1 buffer)` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)** | `7722-84-1` | Electronic Grade (unstabilized) | `30% aq (for SC-1 & SC-2)` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)** | `7647-01-0` | Electronic Grade | `37% aq (for SC-2 clean)` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (NH4OH)** | `1336-21-6` | Electronic Grade | `29% aq (for SC-1 clean)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic with native chemical oxide (Tox ~1.0 nm) and organic particulates.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic H-terminated bare silicon (water contact angle > 75°), zero watermarks, Tox < 0.2 nm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native SiO2 spontaneously regrows in ambient air at ~0.1 nm/hr, degrading interface state density Dit and causing uncontrolled threshold voltage shift in downstream gate oxidation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning: Chemical cleaning and surface preparation verified with zero watermark defects, bare hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated silicon, and calibrated oxide etch rate.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Surface_particle_laser_scan_Surfscan.pdf`
- [ ] `Sessile_drop_contact_angle_measurement.png`
- [ ] `DHF_BOE_calibrated_etch_rate_sheet.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-DHF bare silicon water contact angle** | `>= 75.0 deg` | +/- 5.0 deg | Automated Sessile Drop Goniometer (DI water droplet) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Surface particulate defect density (> 0.1 um)** | `< 15 particles/wafer` | Max acceptable particle count on 100mm wafer | Darkfield Laser Surface Inspection (Surfscan) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Surface metallic impurity concentration (Fe, Ni, Cu)** | `< 1.0e10 atoms/cm²` | Max allowable contamination | Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer surface exhibits 100% uniform dewetting / hydrophobicity with zero visible drying marks under bright light; residual native oxide Tox < 0.2 nm confirmed by spectroscopic ellipsometry.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Procurement of Electronic-Grade BOE 6:1 Chemical Solution & Safety Supplies

**Discipline / Category**: Wet Chemistry  
**Target Generation**: Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type**: Buy

---

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / ISO Class 6 laminar flow bench, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (acid/solvent exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Substrate Fixturing
- Mount substrate securely onto vacuum chuck stage and align mechanical/optical fiducials.
- Zero baseline instruments and establish background electrical/chemical noise floor.

### 3. Recipe Execution & Parameter Control
- Execute process sequence according to verified engineering specifications.
- Monitor thermal, optical, or chemical rate transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Acceptance
- Perform quantitative verification using 4-Point Probe / Ellipsometer / Fume Hood Interlock.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Procurement of pre-mixed BOE 6:1 with surfactant must specify fluorosurfactant compatibility with our downstream megasonic wet-bench recirculation plumbing and PFA filter membranes (0.05 um pore size). Using unformulated surfactant or non-electronic grade containers will induce particle precipitation, leading to severe killer-defect micro-masking during the active area isolation oxide etch.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Specifying electronic-grade (SEMI Tier 1 / Grade 1) BOE 6:1 (6 parts 40% NH4F : 1 part 49% HF) requires tight verification of trace metal contaminants (Fe, Cu, Ni < 1 ppb) to prevent surface electrochemical plating onto bare silicon areas post-etch, as well as strict bath temperature stabilization (25.0 +/- 0.5 °C) to hold thermal SiO2 etch rate repeatability within +/- 3 nm/min.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Pre-mixed BOE 6:1 with surfactant has an active shelf-life limitation of 12 months in HDPE/fluoropolymer containers due to surfactant degradation and gradual HF/NH3 outgassing. Local Vietnamese hazmat logistics mandate controlled-temperature transport (<30 °C) and rigorous customs clearance for hazardous fluorinated chemicals alongside dual-sourced calcium gluconate antidote kits.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement lead time for imported SEMI-grade chemicals averages 6 to 10 weeks into Vietnam. Safety supplies (HF gas/vapor monitoring sensors, face shields, fluoroelastomer aprons, and unexpired 2.5% calcium gluconate gel) must clear EHS signoff and be staged on-site at least two weeks before any wet-chemistry chemical delivery.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Micro-masking and localized residue formation from trace metal contamination (>10 ppb Fe/Cu) or surfactant agglomeration, resulting in incomplete oxide etching and gate-to-substrate bridging.
1. Lethal dermal exposure and delayed systemic hypocalcemia/cardiac arrest caused by inadequate PPE, lack of immediate calcium gluconate application, or failure of wet-bench fume exhaust.
1. Extreme lateral undercut and photoresist delamination due to sub-optimal surfactant wetting or out-of-spec queue time before DI water cascade rinse.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-1-01` | **BOE 6:1 Thermal Oxide Etch Rate and Uniformity Benchmark** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam / Rudolph Focus FE-III), Constant-Temperature Recirculating Wet Bath (25.0 +/- 0.2 °C), DI Water Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) | 1. Measure baseline 49-point oxide thickness (T0). 2. Immerse test wafer in BOE 6:1 bath for exactly 30.0 seconds with gentle 0.5 Hz agitation. 3. Immediately transfer to QDR for 5 cycles of dump-rinse followed by spin-rinse drying with hot N2 (50 °C). 4. Re-measure 49-point oxide thickness (T1). 5. Compute etch rate = (T0 - T1) / 0.5 min and across-wafer uniformity = (Max - Min) / (2 * Mean) * 100%. | `Pass if mean thermal SiO2 etch rate is between 85.0 nm/min and 105.0 nm/min (equivalent to 45.0 nm to 55.0 nm etched in 30 s) and across-wafer 49-point etch uniformity is <= 2.5%.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-1-02` | **Trace Metal Contamination & Liquid Particle Count Verification of Raw Chemical Lot** | Liquid Optical Particle Counter (PMS UltraChem 40 or equivalent, calibrated down to 0.1 um), ICP-MS (Agilent 8900 Triple Quad) | 1. Connect PFA sampling siphon to chemical drum under Class 100 flow hood. 2. Draw 250 mL of BOE 6:1 and run three consecutive 50 mL runs through Liquid Particle Counter to measure particles >= 0.1 um/mL. 3. Extract 10 mL aliquot into pre-cleaned PFA vial, dilute 1:10 with ultrapure deionized water, and inject into ICP-MS to quantify Fe, Cu, Ni, and Ca concentrations. | `Pass if liquid particle count (>= 0.1 um) is <= 25 counts/mL and each key trace metal species (Fe, Cu, Ni, Ca) is strictly <= 1.0 ppb (w/w).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full-face neoprene/butyl-rubber vapor respirator or positive-pressure supplied air mask, Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl rubber gloves over cleanroom nitrile inner gloves, Full-length chemical apron fabricated from Neoprene, Viton, or heavy PVC, Full-coverage wrap-around polycarbonate face shield with ANSI Z87.1 chemical splash goggles, Acid-resistant chemical safety boots (heavy-duty PVC/rubber with steel toe and shank)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Active, unexpired Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5% USP) must be visibly present at the wet-bench station, within 5 seconds reach. In case of skin exposure: immediately flush area with cold running water for 2 minutes, then generously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into the affected area continuously while seeking emergency medical evacuation. In case of eye contact: flush with sterile isotonic saline or 1% calcium gluconate eye flush for at least 15 minutes. Administer 100% O2 if inhaled.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated acid exhaust wet bench constructed of PVDF or polypropylene. Fume exhaust velocity maintained at 100 +/- 10 LFPM at sash opening (0.5 m/s) with continuous automated static differential pressure monitoring and scrubbed acid exhaust ducting.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent BOE solution must be drained via dedicated fluoride-compatible PVDF plumbing directly to a segregated chemical precipitation tank. Neutralize HF/NH4F using Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2 / Slaked Lime) slurry to precipitate Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) sludge at pH 8.5 to 9.5; decanted liquid effluent must comply with industrial discharge standards (<10 ppm F-).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Fluoride** | `12125-01-8` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI Electronic Grade | `34.0% - 35.0% w/w (derived from 40% stock)` |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI Electronic Grade | `6.5% - 7.2% w/w (derived from 49% stock)` |
| **Fluorosurfactant (Perfluoroalkyl surfactant / wetting agent)** | `Proprietary / 29457-72-5` | Electronic Grade / Ultra-Pure | `0.05% - 0.15% w/w` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: HMDS vapor-primed (120 °C), i-line or DUV photoresist-patterned wafer, clean and hard-baked with zero solvent or developer residue, hydrophobic resist lines with hydrophilic open SiO2 windows.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Completely etched oxide windows exposing bare single-crystal silicon or polysilicon, completely hydrophobic (water contact angle > 75 degrees), thoroughly rinsed to UPW resistivity > 17.5 MOhm-cm and spin-dried under clean N2.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding the queue time prior to post-etch clean or subsequent thin-film deposition results in uncontrolled native oxide re-growth (1.5 to 3.0 nm thickness), severe atmospheric hydrocarbon contamination, and irreversible contact resistance degradation across transistor source/drain nodes.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full receipt, analytical qualification, and EHS commissioning of SEMI Tier 1 BOE 6:1 chemical stock and safety infrastructure for the 180nm DRAM Gen 1 oxide etch module, verified against strict particle, trace metal, and thermal oxide etch rate standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `BOE_6to1_CoA_and_Purity_Analysis.pdf`
- [ ] `BOE_Oxide_Etch_Rate_Uniformity_Report.csv`
- [ ] `Wet_Bench_HF_Safety_and_Exhaust_Commissioning.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **BOE 6:1 thermal SiO2 etch rate in temperature-controlled bath at 25.0 °C** | `95.0 nm/min` | +/- 5.0 nm/min | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry 49-point wafer mapping on thermally oxidized monitor wafer |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum concentration of critical trace metallic impurities (Fe, Cu, Ni, Ca) in incoming chemical batch** | `0.50 ppb` | <= 1.0 ppb maximum allowable | Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Wet-bench face sash exhaust velocity under steady-state operating conditions** | `100.0 LFPM` | +/- 10.0 LFPM | Calibrated hot-wire anemometer grid measurement across open sash plane |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Chemical Certificate of Analysis meets SEMI Grade 1 specifications, ICP-MS and particle counts conform to pass criteria, 49-point etch rate verification yields 95 +/- 5 nm/min with <= 2.5% non-uniformity, and facility EHS officer signs off on dedicated exhaust velocity, acid waste neutralization plumbing, and verified on-site unexpired calcium gluconate stocks.

In case of eye contact: flush with sterile isotonic saline or 1% calcium gluconate eye flush for at least 15 minutes. Administer 100% O2 if inhaled.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Dedicated acid exhaust wet bench constructed of PVDF or polypropylene. Fume exhaust velocity maintained at 100 +/- 10 LFPM at sash opening (0.5 m/s) with continuous automated static differential pressure monitoring and scrubbed acid exhaust ducting.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent BOE solution must be drained via dedicated fluoride-compatible PVDF plumbing directly to a segregated chemical precipitation tank. Neutralize HF/NH4F using Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2 / Slaked Lime) slurry to precipitate Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) sludge at pH 8.5 to 9.5; decanted liquid effluent must comply with industrial discharge standards (<10 ppm F-).

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: HMDS vapor-primed (120 °C), i-line or DUV photoresist-patterned wafer, clean and hard-baked with zero solvent or developer residue, hydrophobic resist lines with hydrophilic open SiO2 windows.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-180NM-BOE-001`
**Title:** HMDS Vapor Prime, Resist Patterning & Wet Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution  
**Discipline:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Architecture & Integration > Wet Chemistry  
**Action Type:** Make (Gen 1)

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│     Wafer Prep &      │
│      Dehydration      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  HMDS Vapor Prime at  │
│         120 °C        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│     Resist Coat &     │
│       Softbake        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   Photolithography    │
│      Patterning       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Hardbake & Inspect   │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch at  │
│         25 °C         │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   DI Water Cascade    │
│   Rinse & Spin Dry    │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### SiO2 Etch Rate Benchmarks (BOE 6:1 @ 25 °C)

```text
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                      │
Thermal SiO2 (Min)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                      │
Thermal SiO2 (Max)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                   │
                  │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                   │
     CVD/TEOS SiO2┤████████████████████████████████████│
                  │████████████████████████████████████│
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                   0       55       110     165     220 
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

> [!CAUTION]
> **Hydrofluoric Acid Safety Protocol:**
> HF penetrates dermal tissue rapidly and complexes systemic calcium. Calcium gluconate gel must be on-station, inspected, and immediately accessible at the wet bench before opening chemical baths. Full PPE (acid apron, face shield, heavy neoprene gloves) is mandatory.

#### Step 1: Substrate Dehydration & HMDS Vapor Prime
1. Load wafer into the priming oven chamber.
2. Evacuate and conduct vapor priming using **HMDS (Hexamethyldisilazane)** at a chamber temperature of **120 °C** to passivate polar hydroxyl surface groups and ensure resist adhesion during fluoride immersion.

#### Step 2: Resist Coat & Softbake
1. Transfer wafer to coater chuck under laminar flow.
2. Dispense photoresist over the wafer and spin to achieve target thickness.
3. Perform softbake to drive out casting solvents.

#### Step 3: Photolithography Patterning & Develop
1. Expose the 180nm device active/contact geometries (e.g., cell contact pads and bitline contact apertures).
2. Develop pattern using standard developer chemistry.
3. Perform post-develop inspection for pinholes or resist lifting.
4. Execute hardbake step to crosslink resist and withstand wet chemical attack.

#### Step 4: BOE 6:1 Solution Formulation & Bath Conditioning
1. Verify bath formulation ratio: **6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ (Ammonium Fluoride) : 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$ (Hydrofluoric Acid)**.
2. Confirm solution maintains a buffered $\mathbf{pH \sim 4.5}$ to prevent local HF depletion and guarantee steady fluoride ion activity.
3. Add **0.1% surfactant wetting agent** (Triton X-100 or Fluorad) to lower liquid surface tension and prevent bubble entrapment in sub-micron features.
4. Stabilize bath temperature strictly at **25 °C**.

#### Step 5: Oxide Dip-Etch Execution
1. Immerse wafer carrier vertically into the conditioned BOE 6:1 bath with moderate fluid agitation.
2. Timed etch duration is calculated by target oxide thickness:
   - For **Thermally Grown $\text{SiO}_2$**: Etch at **80 nm/min to 100 nm/min** (800 to 1000 Å/min).
   - For **CVD / TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$**: Etch at **150 nm/min to 220 nm/min**.
   - For **Native Oxide**: Etch cycle is complete within **10 to 15 seconds**.

#### Step 6: Cascade Quick-Dump Rinse (QDR) & Spin Dry
1. Transfer carrier within 3 seconds into a continuous DI water cascade overflow tank.
2. Rinse until resistivity of effluent DI water reaches $> 18\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
3. Spin-rinse dry under heated filtered $\text{N}_2$.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **HMDS Vapor Prime Temperature** | $120 \pm 2$ | °C | Integrated In-situ Pyrometer / Thermocouple |
| **BOE Bath Operating Temperature** | $25.0 \pm 0.5$ | °C | Wet Bench In-line RTD Sensor |
| **BOE Solution Acidity** | $\sim 4.5 \pm 0.2$ | pH | Automated In-line pH Meter |
| **Thermally Grown $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $80 \text{ to } 100$ | nm/min | Ellipsometry / Optical Spectroscopic Reflectometry |
| **CVD / TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $150 \text{ to } 220$ | nm/min | Ellipsometry / Optical Spectroscopic Reflectometry |
| **$\text{SiO}_2$ to Si Etch Selectivity** | $> 100 : 1$ | ratio | Step-Height Profilometry / Spectroscopic Ellipsometry |
| **$\text{SiO}_2$ to $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ Etch Selectivity** | $> 20 : 1$ | ratio | Step-Height Profilometry / Spectroscopic Ellipsometry |
| **Wetting Agent Concentration** | $0.1$ | wt% | Precision Volumetric Dispenser (Triton X-100 / Fluorad) |

---

### 3. Source Citations
- **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates**: Formulation ratio (6:1 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : 49% $\text{HF}$), buffered pH $\sim 4.5$, thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate (80–100 nm/min at 25 °C), CVD/TEOS etch rate (150–220 nm/min), native oxide strip duration (10–15 s), selectivities ($>100:1$ to Si, $>20:1$ to $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$), and HF systemic toxicity protocols.
- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**: 100 nm/min (1000 Å/min) thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ nominal etch rate at 25 °C, HMDS vapor prime process setpoint at 120 °C for resist adhesion, 0.1% surfactant addition (Triton X-100/Fluorad) for micro-trench de-bubbling, and calcium gluconate gel safety requirement.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: 180nm DRAM architecture context, bitline and cell contacts, and capacitor dielectric stacks.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The integration sequence tightly couples HMDS vapor priming at 120°C with resist coat and buffered oxide etching (BOE 6:1). In an open-source 180nm DRAM node (Gen 1 mm scale), wet oxide dip-etching is inherently isotropic with lateral undercutting matching vertical etch depth (etch bias ratio ~1:1). Thermal budgets from the 120°C HMDS dehydration bake will not degrade the underlying substrate, but lack of automated cassette immersion in a wet bench will introduce meniscus run-off artifacts, variable agitation dynamics across the 150mm/200mm wafer, and uncontrolled boundary layer depletion at critical line-space interfaces.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Photoresist adhesion failure during BOE dip is catastrophic if native silanol (Si-OH) groups are not completely transformed into hydrophobic trimethylsilyl groups via HMDS. Without surfactant addition (0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad FC-93), surface tension of BOE (~70 mN/m) prevents complete wetting of high-aspect-ratio oxide trenches, trapping micro-bubbles that act as local etch masks and result in unetched oxide pillars. Furthermore, bath temperature must be strictly controlled at 25.0 ± 0.5°C because the etch activation energy yields an etch rate sensitivity of ~2.5% per °C.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Pre-mixed electronic grade (SEMI Grade C1 to C7) BOE 6:1 (40% NH4F : 49% HF) and semiconductor-grade anhydrous HMDS have limited shelf-life and require hazardous chemical handling import clearances in Vietnam. Sourcing Triton X-100/Fluorad with sub-ppb metal contamination is bottlenecked. Secondary containment, dedicated PTFE/PFA dipping ware (no borosilicate glass), and validated Calcium Gluconate stock with active expiration tracking are mandatory gating items before purchase orders can be released.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: From a fab execution and schedule standpoint, this recipe establishes a critical Q-time bottleneck: post-HMDS queue time to resist coat must not exceed 30 minutes in cleanroom ambient to prevent moisture re-adsorption, and post-develop to BOE etch queue time must be strictly throttled to <45 minutes to prevent photoresist footing and skin rehydration. Incurring an expired Q-time necessitates complete resist strip, piranha clean, and rework, which incurs severe cycle time penalties.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Resist lifting and delamination at the oxide interface during BOE immersion due to inadequate HMDS vapor prime or moisture re-adsorption, leading to severe lateral over-etch and bridge shorts.
1. Bubble entrapment (pinhole formation or unetched SiO2 micro-islands) caused by omission or depletion of the surfactant wetting agent in high surface tension BOE bath.
1. Excessive lateral undercut (loss of critical dimension) and profile slope degradation from uncontrolled immersion time or temperature drift exceeding ±0.5°C.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-01` | **HMDS Monolayer Hydrophobicity & Contact Angle Verification** | Automated Optical Goniometer / Contact Angle Meter (e.g., Ramé-Hart 250) with 18.2 MOhm-cm DI water micro-syringe dispensing. | 1. Transfer wafer to goniometer stage within 15 minutes of prime. 2. Dispense a 2.0 uL droplet of deionized water at 5 points (center, top, bottom, left, right at 10mm edge exclusion). 3. Capture droplet profile images at 50 ms intervals for 2 seconds. 4. Compute static contact angle using Young-Laplace baseline fitting. | `Pass if mean contact angle across all 5 sites is 75° <= theta <= 85° with within-wafer standard deviation 1-sigma <= 2.0°. Fail if theta < 70° (insufficient prime) or theta > 90° (polymerized HMDS residue).` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-02` | **BOE 6:1 Thermal Oxide Etch Rate, Uniformity & Undercut Measurement** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (e.g., Woollam M-2000) and Top-down/Cross-Section CD-SEM (Hitachi S-9380). | 1. Measure initial oxide thickness at 49 points using ellipsometry. 2. Dip wafer into BOE 6:1 with continuous reciprocal 0.5 Hz agitation for exactly 60.0 seconds. 3. Immediate dump rinse in quick-dump-rinser (QDR) with DI water for 5 cycles (<5 s transfer time), followed by spin-rinse-dry (SRD). 4. Measure remaining oxide thickness at matching 49 points. 5. Cleave witness die and inspect lateral undercut and CD loss under cross-sectional SEM. | `Pass if mean vertical etch rate is 95.0 to 105.0 nm/min (950 to 1050 A/min), within-wafer non-uniformity (NU) <= 3.0% (1-sigma), and lateral undercut is <= 110 nm per edge with zero resist peel-off.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full-face transparent chemical-splash shield over ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses, Heavy-duty 22-mil neoprene or butyl gloves over secondary inner nitrile gloves, Acid-resistant heavy chloroprene/neoprene chemical apron with sleeves, Steel-toe neoprene or chemical-resistant overboots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: HF penetrates skin and soft tissue, dissociating into fluoride ions that scavenge systemic calcium and magnesium (causing lethal hypocalcemia and cardiac arrest). Flush exposure site immediately with continuous flowing water for 2-3 minutes, gently blot dry, and massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel continuously into the affected area with a gloved hand until medical staff arrives. If eye contact occurs, flush continuously with sterile 1% Calcium Gluconate ophthalmic solution or isotonic saline. Seek immediate emergency medical evacuation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated acid wet bench constructed exclusively of virgin polypropylene/PVDF. Continuous dedicated exhaust with face velocity maintained at 100 ± 10 FPM (0.51 m/s) connected directly to an active wet scrubber with caustic scrubbing liquor (pH >= 9.0). HMDS exhaust routed to dedicated solvent exhaust lines.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aqueous spent BOE effluent must be collected in dedicated fluoropolymer tanks for Fluoride Waste Neutralization (FWN). Neutralize with Slaked Lime / Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) sludge (solubility ~16 mg/L at 20°C). Supernatant pH adjusted to 6.5-8.5 prior to secondary industrial discharge testing.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF)** | `7664-39-3` | Electronic / SEMI Grade 1 | `49.0 wt%` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (NH4F)** | `12125-01-8` | Electronic / SEMI Grade 1 | `40.0 wt%` |
| **Hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS)** | `999-97-3` | Semiconductor VLSI Grade (>=99.8%) | `>= 99.8 wt%` |
| **Surfactant (Triton X-100 / Octylphenol Ethoxylate)** | `9002-93-1` | Electronic Grade | `0.1 wt% in BOE` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic clean thermal SiO2 surface, zero organic residues (post-SC-1/Piranha), contact angle < 10°.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Exposed single-crystal silicon or polysilicon gate layer exhibiting hydrophobic H-terminated Si surface (DI water contact angle > 70°) in etched pattern windows, protected by intact hard-baked resist.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture re-adsorption onto primed oxide hydrolyzes siloxane bonds, causing catastrophic resist peeling during BOE immersion; delay between resist develop and BOE etch causes photoresist dewetting and parasitic lateral etching.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful vapor-phase HMDS silanization yielding a stable hydrophobic oxide surface, followed by sub-micron photoresist lithography and a controlled BOE 6:1 wet dip-etch that completely clears 100 nm thermal SiO2 down to underlying silicon substrate with <= 100 nm lateral undercut and zero resist lifting or pinhole pitting.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TC_BOE_OXIDE_ETCH_RUN_SUMMARY.csv`
- [ ] `ELLIPSOMETRY_49PT_THICKNESS_MAP.pdf`
- [ ] `CROSS_SECTION_CDSEM_UNDERCUT_INSPECTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Vertical thermal SiO2 etch rate in BOE 6:1 at 25.0°C** | `100.0 nm/min` | ± 5.0 nm/min | Pre/Post 49-point Spectroscopic Ellipsometry thickness delta divided by dip duration |
| `ASSERT-02` | **HMDS Primed Surface Static DI Water Contact Angle** | `80.0 degrees` | ± 5.0 degrees | 5-point automated optical goniometer droplet profile analysis |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Etch selectivity of Thermal SiO2 over Single-Crystal Silicon Substrate** | `120:1` | >= 100:1 minimum | Ellipsometric oxide loss versus profilometric substrate silicon loss in etched field |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Thermal oxide in patterned trenches is completely cleared to substrate silicon (confirmed by hydrophobic rinse-off and ellipsometric residual thickness < 1.0 nm), lateral undercut per edge is <= 110 nm, macro/micro resist peeling count is zero across the active wafer area, and all 49-point thickness maps meet the 3.0% uniformity threshold.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## HMDS Vapor Prime Adhesion & I-line Photoresist Patterning

- **Task Title**: HMDS Vapor Prime Adhesion & I-line Photoresist Patterning
- **Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning > HMDS Vapor Prime, Resist Patterning & Wet Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution > HMDS Vapor Prime Adhesion & I-line Photoresist Patterning
- **Generation**: Gen 1 (mm scale alignment)
- **Action Type**: Make

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|               HMDS VAPOR PRIME & I-LINE PHOTORESIST PROCESS FLOW                  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  [Dehydration Bake]   -->   [HMDS Vapor Prime]   -->   [Spin Coating]
   150°C-200°C, 30 min        120°C Vapor Chamber        Shipley 1813 (4000 RPM)
                                                                   |
  [DI Water Rinse & Dry] <--   [MF-319 Develop]   <--   [Soft Bake & Exposure]
   Rigorous Rinse / N2          45-60 sec dwell          115°C, 60s / 365nm UV
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

#### Step 1: Substrate Dehydration Bake
1. Load cleaned silicon wafer onto a hot plate or into a clean convection oven.
2. Perform dehydration bake at **150°C – 200°C for 30 minutes** to desorb physisorbed water molecules from the surface.

#### Step 2: HMDS Vapor Prime
1. Transfer wafer to an HMDS priming environment at **120°C**.
2. Expose the substrate to Hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) vapor to reactively silylate hydrophilic surface silanol groups (`-Si-OH`) into hydrophobic methyl-siloxane bonds (`-Si-O-Si(CH3)3`), ensuring chemical adhesion during subsequent wet etching.

#### Step 3: Photoresist Dispense & Spin Coating
1. Center wafer on the vacuum chuck of the spin coater.
2. Dispense **2–3 mL of Shipley 1813** positive photoresist onto the center of the wafer.
3. **Spread Cycle**: Ramp to **500 RPM for 5 seconds**.
4. **Spin Cycle**: Accelerate at an acceleration rate of **10,000 RPM/s** up to **4,000 RPM** and hold for **30 seconds**.
5. Apply Edge Bead Removal (EBR) using PGMEA solvent jet to prevent clamp/stage contamination.

#### Step 4: Soft Bake (Post-Apply Bake)
1. Transfer wafer onto a flat aluminum hot plate.
2. Soft bake at **115°C for 60 seconds** to drive off residual casting solvents.

#### Step 5: Photolithographic Exposure
1. Mount wafer onto the aligner stage under a contact aligner or optical projection system (e.g., 10x Plan Achromat objective, NA 0.25).
2. Align fiducials within the Gen 1 macroscopic tolerance boundary of **±100 µm (±0.1 mm)**.
3. Expose the resist using a high-power **365 nm i-line UV LED** or mercury vapor lamp source.

#### Step 6: Development & Rinse
1. Immerse wafer into **Microposit MF-319 developer** for **45 to 60 seconds** with gentle agitation.
2. Immediately transfer to a cascade deionized (DI) water bath and perform a rigorous DI water rinse to halt development.
3. Blow-dry gently with filtered dry nitrogen gas ($N_2$).

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value | Tolerance / Window | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Resist Film Thickness** | `1.30` | `± 0.015` (±15 nm) | µm | Optical Spectroscopic Reflectometry / Ellipsometry |
| **Gen 1 Alignment Error** | `≤ 100` | Max allowable: `100` | µm | Optical Inspection Microscope / Vernier Target |
| **HMDS Silylation Chamber Temp** | `120` | `± 2` | °C | Calibrated Thermocouple / Chamber Sensor |
| **Development Immersion Time** | `45 – 60` | Operational dwell | s | Automated Process Timer |

---

### 3. Citations & Context Traceability

- **Dehydration bake (150°C–200°C, 30 min), HMDS silanol conversion chemistry, spin recipe (2–3 mL, 500 RPM/5s spread, 10,000 RPM/s ramp, 4000 RPM/30s spin, 1.30 µm ± 15 nm thickness, PGMEA EBR)**:
  *Source: Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming*
- **HMDS vapor priming temperature (120°C) and adhesion requirement for BOE acid resilience**:
  *Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*
- **Soft bake (115°C for 60s on flat aluminum hot plate), 365 nm i-line exposure, Microposit MF-319 developer dwell (45–60s) with DI water rinse, and Gen 1 alignment tolerance (±100 µm / ±0.1 mm)**:
  *Source: Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Wedge Error Compensation (WEC) on the Karl Suss MA6 chuck must maintain planar contact parallelism under 1 um across the substrate to avoid non-uniform focal shifts and edge run-out during 365nm i-line exposure. Soft-contact air pressure must be strictly regulated to 0.3 bar to prevent mechanical resist abrasion against the emulsion mask while maintaining adequate resolution for Gen 1 targets.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Liquid-phase HMDS application generates inconsistent monolayer silylation and particle contamination; vapor prime at 110°C to 150°C in an enclosed vacuum chamber is mandatory to achieve contact angles >70° on hydrated SiO2. Shipley 1813 soft bake at 115°C for 60 seconds on a calibrated aluminum hot plate is required to drive out ethyl lactate solvent without inducing thermal decomposition of diazonaphthoquinone (DNQ) photoactive compounds.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Microposit MF-319 (TMAH-based developer) and Shipley 1813 photoresist are subject to export compliance and hazardous logistics constraints in Vietnam; cold-chain storage at 2°C to 8°C must be maintained, with certified local distributors and dedicated chemical inventory monitoring to prevent viscosity degradation from solvent evaporation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Gen 1 target overlay error of ±100 um is loose enough for manual split-field microscope crosshair alignment on the MA6, but operators must ensure cycle times for exposure and development remain under 3 minutes per wafer to support the batch throughput schedule before BOE 6:1 dip etching.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial delamination and resist lifting during BOE 6:1 wet dip due to incomplete SiO2 dehydration or sub-threshold HMDS vapor prime coverage.
1. Resist scumming and incomplete development in MF-319 from localized underexposure or optical diffraction gaps exceeding 30 um in proximity/soft-contact modes.
1. Over-baking induced thermal cross-linking of Shipley 1813 leading to insolubility in MF-319 and extreme critical dimension (CD) expansion.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-01` | **HMDS Vapor Prime Hydrophobicity and Water Contact Angle Verification** | Optical Goniometer / Sessile Drop Contact Angle Meter with automated DI water micro-dispenser (2 uL droplet) | 1. Position wafer on goniometer horizontal stage. 2. Dispense a 2.0 uL sessile droplet of 18.2 MOhm-cm DI water onto center and 4 quadrant positions (r = 25 mm). 3. Capture droplet profile using CMOS camera within 5 seconds of deposition. 4. Calculate baseline tangent contact angle via Young-Laplace fitting across all 5 measurement points. | `Pass if mean contact angle is >= 75.0° with standard deviation <= 3.0° across 5 points; Fail if any individual point is < 70.0°.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-02` | **Post-Development I-Line Photoresist Thickness and Feature Resolution Inspection** | Spectroscopic Reflectometer (Filmetrics F20 or equivalent) and Calibrated Optical Inspection Microscope (100x Plan Achromat) | 1. Measure unexposed resist field thickness using spectroscopic reflectometer at 9 points across the wafer. 2. Inspect Gen 1 alignment targets and resolution line-space grating structures under optical microscope at 100x magnification. 3. Verify clearing of unexposed/exposed boundaries and absence of residual resist scum or micro-bridging. | `Resist thickness must be 1.30 um ± 0.05 um. Cleared line-space resolution must resolve down to <= 5.0 um without scumming, peeling, or footing under 100x optical microscopy.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical splash goggles and full-face polycarbonate shield, Nitrile gloves (outer) over cleanroom vinyl/nitrile gloves (inner) with minimum 6 mil thickness, Flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat or chemical apron, Closed-toe ESD-safe chemical-resistant footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush with isotonic eyewash solution or copious DI water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing immediately and drench affected skin under emergency safety shower for 15 minutes; TMAH is a neurotoxin via dermal absorption. Inhalation: Move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: All open chemical handling, spin coating, and development must occur inside dedicated laminar flow chemical fume hoods with face velocity maintaining 100 FPM (0.5 m/s) connected to dedicated volatile organic solvent exhaust ducting.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate organic resist and solvent rinses into labeled hazardous flammable organic solvent carboys. Collect spent TMAH MF-319 developer into separate alkaline developer waste containers; do not mix TMAH with acidic or fluoride waste streams.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS)** | `999-97-3` | VLSI / Semiconductor Grade | `>= 99.0%` |
| **Microposit S1813 Photoresist (Propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate, Diazo photoactive compound, Cresol novolak resin)** | `108-65-6` | Electronic Grade | `70-85% solvent base` |
| **Microposit MF-319 Developer (Tetramethylammonium Hydroxide aqueous solution)** | `75-59-2` | Semiconductor Grade | `2.2 - 2.4% TMAH in H2O` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Thermally grown SiO2 surface, free of organic contamination (post-Piranha/RCA clean), dehydrated at >= 120°C.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Silylated SiO2 surface patterned with hard-baked Shipley 1813 photoresist, completely cleared in exposure windows, dried and inspected for immediate BOE dip.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture adsorption on primed HMDS surface from ambient cleanroom humidity causes hydrolysis of trimethylsilyl groups, leading to severe resist adhesion failure and complete pattern lift-off during wet oxide etching.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full wafer HMDS vapor priming, Shipley 1813 spin-coating, soft bake, 365nm UV exposure on Suss MA6 aligner, MF-319 development, and CD/microscopy qualification completed with verified adhesion and zero resist lifting readiness for BOE wet chemical etch.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `HMDS_PR_Patterning_RunReport_Lot01.pdf`
- [ ] `Thickness_ContactAngle_Mapping_Lot01.csv`
- [ ] `Developed_Pattern_Optical_Inspection_100x.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Shipley 1813 Post-Soft-Bake Resist Film Thickness** | `1.30 um` | ±0.05 um | Spectroscopic Reflectometry (9-point wafer mapping) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **HMDS Primed Surface Deionized Water Contact Angle** | `78.0 degrees` | ±5.0 degrees | Optical Goniometer Sessile Drop Analysis (5-point average) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Gen 1 Alignment Overlay Error on Suss MA6** | `0.0 um` | ±15.0 um | Split-Field Optical Vernier Overlay Measurement |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher confirms mean contact angle >= 70°, uniform resist thickness between 1.25 um and 1.35 um across 9 points, zero resist peeling or blistering after 115°C bake, and clear development of Gen 1 test pattern windows with overlay error <= 15 um.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Wafer Dehydration Bake and HMDS Vapor Prime Silylation

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Wafer Load       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Dehydration Bake    │
│    150°C-200°C, 30 min │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    HMDS Vapor Prime    │
│    120°C Silylation    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Cooling & Transfer   │
│   To Spin Coater Track │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
Execute surface preparation for 180nm DRAM wafers prior to I-line photoresist (Shipley 1813) application. The process desorbs physisorbed ambient moisture and chemically converts hydrophilic surface silanol groups ($\text{Si-OH}$) into hydrophobic trimethylsiloxane bonds ($\text{-Si-O-Si(CH}_3)_3$) via hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) vapor priming, preventing photoresist lifting during downstream Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) wet chemistry.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Inspection & Cassette Loading:**
   - Transfer wafer batch to quartz or vacuum-compatible bake boat.
   - Verify surface cleanliness and absence of gross particulate contamination under cleanroom yellow light.

2. **Thermal Dehydration Bake:**
   - Load wafers into the vacuum oven / bake hotplate.
   - Set chamber temperature between **$150^\circ\text{C}$ and $200^\circ\text{C}$**.
   - Dwell for **$30\text{ minutes}$** to completely desorb physisorbed water molecules from the silicon/dielectric surface.

3. **Chamber Evacuation & Purge:**
   - Pump down the reaction chamber under nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) backfill cycle to eliminate residual moisture and ambient air.

4. **HMDS Vapor Priming (Reactive Silylation):**
   - Stabilize vapor prime chamber at **$120^\circ\text{C}$**.
   - Introduce pure HMDS vapor into the heated chamber.
   - Reactively silylate hydrophilic surface silanol ($\text{-Si-OH}$) groups into hydrophobic methyl-siloxane ($\text{-Si-O-Si(CH}_3)_3$) bonds.

5. **Post-Prime Purge & Controlled Cool-down:**
   - Evacuate HMDS vapor effluent through dedicated chemical scrubbers.
   - Perform cyclic $\text{N}_2$ chamber purges to remove unreacted vapor.
   - Transfer wafers to a temperature-controlled chill plate ($20^\circ\text{C} - 25^\circ\text{C}$) to equilibrate prior to photoresist dispense.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dehydration Bake Temperature** | $150 - 200$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Embedded In-Situ RTD / Thermocouple |
| **Dehydration Bake Duration** | $30$ | $\text{min}$ | Automated Process Controller Timer |
| **HMDS Vapor Prime Temperature** | $120$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Chamber Thermal Controller Sensor |
| **Subsequent Resist Film Thickness Uniformity** | $1.30 \pm 0.015$ ($1.30\,\mu\text{m} \pm 15\,\text{nm}$) | $\mu\text{m}$ / $\text{nm}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Film Reflectometry across 100mm wafer |

---

### 4. Safety & Processing Notes
- **Downstream Etch Resilience:** Ensures photoresist withstands BOE 6:1 ($\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate $\sim 100\,\text{nm/min}$ / $1000\,\text{Å/min}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$) without edge lifting or acid under-seepage.
- **Safety Precaution:** Have calcium gluconate gel immediately accessible in processing areas where BOE / HF wet etching stations operate downstream.

---

### 5. Context Literature Citations
- **Source: Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming**
  - *Wafer Dehydration:* Bake at $150^\circ\text{C}-200^\circ\text{C}$ for 30 minutes to desorb physisorbed water.
  - *HMDS Priming:* Silylates hydrophilic silanol ($\text{-Si-OH}$) to hydrophobic methyl-siloxane ($\text{-Si-O-Si(CH}_3)_3$) bonds to prevent peel-off during acid wet etching.
  - *Film Uniformity Target:* $1.30\,\mu\text{m} \pm 15\,\text{nm}$ across 100mm wafers.
- **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**
  - *Adhesion Requirement:* HMDS vapor prime at $120^\circ\text{C}$ prior to resist coating to withstand BOE 6:1 ($100\,\text{nm/min}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$). Safety mandate for calcium gluconate gel.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal budget integration between dehydration bake and vapor prime must maintain sub-degree temperature repeatability across the chuck to prevent asymmetric radial surface silylation. If dehydration is conducted on an open hot plate rather than under active vacuum or inert purge, ambient moisture re-adsorption occurs during transfer to the priming station, degrading process repeatability.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Liquid-dispense HMDS creates non-uniform poly-siloxane aggregate micro-droplets that disrupt spin dynamics for 1.30 um Shipley 1813. Gas-phase vapor priming at elevated temperature (110°C-150°C) with hexamethyldisilazane vapor is essential to achieve a uniform monolayer substitution of surface hydroxyls (-Si-OH) to trimethylsiloxane (-Si-O-Si(CH3)3), targeting a DI water contact angle of 60° to 75° for resist adhesion during aggressive BOE 6:1 immersion.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade HMDS (>=99.5% purity) degrades rapidly into hexamethyldisiloxane and ammonia when exposed to atmospheric humidity. Sourcing sealed anhydrous ampoules or bubbler canisters with dry nitrogen headspace is necessary; secondary local storage requires a dedicated desiccator cabinet to avoid premature chemical hydrolysis and loss of priming efficacy.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: For Gen 1 (mm) baseline prototyping, avoid over-engineering with full track cluster integration, but ensure the dual-station hotplate/priming chamber cycle time stays under 40 minutes per batch. Adhere to a strict 30-minute air queue time to resist spin coat to prevent rework cycles and wafer scrap.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete surface dehydration leaving physisorbed water, leading to resist lifting and severe lateral undercut during subsequent 6:1 BOE isotropic oxide etching.
1. Over-priming or HMDS vapor condensation causing excessive hydrophobicity (contact angle > 85°), resulting in resist de-wetting, pinholes, and radial striations during spin coating.
1. Moisture ingress into the HMDS priming vessel inducing ammonia precipitation and particulate contamination across active 100mm wafer sites.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-1-01` | **Silylation Surface Energy Contact Angle Measurement** | Optical Goniometer / Sessile Drop Contact Angle Analyzer with calibrated micro-syringe | 1. Transfer wafer immediately from vapor prime chamber to goniometer stage within 5 minutes. 2. Dispense a 2.0 uL droplet of HPLC-grade deionized water onto the center, top, bottom, left, and right (5-point pattern, 10mm edge exclusion). 3. Capture droplet profile via high-resolution CCD within 5 seconds of sessile contact. 4. Calculate advancing contact angle using Young-Laplace fitting across all 5 test locations. | `Mean DI water contact angle must be 68.0° ± 7.0° (range 61.0° to 75.0°) with cross-wafer non-uniformity (1-sigma) <= 3.0°.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-1-02` | **Post-Dehydration Surface Particulate and Condensation Density** | Darkfield Optical Surface Defect Scanner / High-Resolution Optical Inspection Microscope (50x objective) | 1. Place wafer onto motorized inspection stage. 2. Perform automated darkfield scanning across the 100mm substrate (5mm edge exclusion). 3. Tally scattered-light defect events corresponding to particles >= 1.0 um diameter. 4. Review 10 highest-intensity defect locations under 50x magnification to confirm absence of HMDS droplet condensation rings. | `Total added particle count >= 1.0 um must be <= 15 particles per 100mm wafer; zero visible liquid condensation droplets or polymer stains detected across active area.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 3 chemical-resistant Nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 approved full wrap-around splash safety goggles and face shield, Static-dissipative, flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat / gowning, Dedicated organic vapor / ammonia respirator cartridge if outside chemical fume hood
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: HMDS reacts with water/mucous membranes to liberate ammonia and hexamethyldisiloxane. Inhalation: Immediately move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored. Skin Contact: Flush affected epidermis with copious lukewarm water for >=15 minutes; remove contaminated garments. Eye Contact: Irrigate eyes immediately with sterile isotonic saline or DI water at an eyewash station for >=20 minutes holding eyelids open. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth and seek immediate emergency medical care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: All handling and vapor priming exhaust must be vented through a dedicated volatile organic chemical / solvent scrubber exhaust system with continuous duct airflow >= 100 FPM face velocity. Do not exhaust into acid/flammable oxidizer extract ducts due to risk of exothermic ammonia reaction.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect residual liquid HMDS in dedicated, properly labeled, airtight glass or steel solvent waste containers under dry nitrogen purge. Do not pour into aqueous, acidic, or BOE drains. Neutralize trace vapor effluent via inline acidic scrubbers or carbon-bed adsorption columns.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS)** | `999-97-3` | VLSI / Electronic Grade (>=99.5%) | `100% (pure liquid for vapor generation)` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Carrier/Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | UHP Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

critics.systems_engineer: Thermal budget integration between dehydration bake and vapor prime must maintain sub-degree temperature repeatability across the chuck to prevent asymmetric radial surface silylation. If dehydration is conducted on an open hot plate rather than under active vacuum or inert purge, ambient moisture re-adsorption occurs during transfer to the priming station, degrading process repeatability.
critics.domain_expert: Liquid-dispense HMDS creates non-uniform poly-siloxane aggregate micro-droplets that disrupt spin dynamics for 1.30 um Shipley 1813. Gas-phase vapor priming at elevated temperature (110°C-150°C) with hexamethyldisilazane vapor is essential to achieve a uniform monolayer substitution of surface hydroxyls (-Si-OH) to trimethylsiloxane (-Si-O-Si(CH3)3), targeting a DI water contact angle of 60° to 75° for resist adhesion during aggressive BOE 6:1 immersion.
critics.supply_chain: Electronic-grade HMDS (>=99.5% purity) degrades rapidly into hexamethyldisiloxane and ammonia when exposed to atmospheric humidity. Sourcing sealed anhydrous ampoules or bubbler canisters with dry nitrogen headspace is necessary; secondary local storage requires a dedicated desiccator cabinet to avoid premature chemical hydrolysis and loss of priming efficacy.
critics.laya_pm: For Gen 1 (mm) baseline prototyping, avoid over-engineering with full track cluster integration, but ensure the dual-station hotplate/priming chamber cycle time stays under 40 minutes per batch. Adhere to a strict 30-minute air queue time to resist spin coat to prevent rework cycles and wafer scrap.
critical_failure_modes: Incomplete surface dehydration leaving physisorbed water, leading to resist lifting and severe lateral undercut during subsequent 6:1 BOE isotropic oxide etching.
Over-priming or HMDS vapor condensation causing excessive hydrophobicity (contact angle > 85°), resulting in resist de-wetting, pinholes, and radial striations during spin coating.
Moisture ingress into the HMDS priming vessel inducing ammonia precipitation and particulate contamination across active 100mm wafer sites.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-LITHO-DEHYD-001`
**Title:** Wafer Surface High-Temperature Dehydration Bake & Moisture Desorption  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Photolithography > Wafer Surface High-Temperature Dehydration Bake & Moisture Desorption  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Objective & Principle
Desorb physisorbed water molecules and eliminate surface moisture monolayers from bare silicon or silicon dioxide ($SiO_2$) substrates prior to HMDS (Hexamethyldisilazane) vapor silylation. Moisture removal prevents the competitive hydrolysis of HMDS, ensuring high-density conversion of silanol ($-Si-OH$) groups to hydrophobic methyl-siloxane ($-Si-O-Si(CH_3)_3$) bonds, thereby preventing photoresist delamination during subsequent Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) immersion.

---

### 2. Physical Process Parameters & Recipe

| Step | Parameter | Target / Value | Tolerance / Range |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bake Temperature** | Setpoint | **150°C – 200°C** | $\pm 2.0\text{°C}$ |
| **Duration** | Bake Time | **30 minutes** | $+2 / -0\text{ min}$ |
| **Atmosphere / Pressure** | Nitrogen ($N_2$) Purge / Convection | Atmospheric / Clean Dry $N_2$ | Class 100 cleanroom air / dry purge |
| **Cool-Down** | Chill Plate / Transfer | Room Temperature ($20\text{°C} - 25\text{°C}$) | Cooled before HMDS/spin dispense |

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Substrate Inspection & Load into Quartz/Teflon Carrier |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Thermal Dehydration Bake (150°C - 200°C for 30 min)    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Controlled Chill Plate Cooling (to 20°C - 25°C)        |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. Transfer to HMDS Vapor Prime Chamber (Queue < 15 min)  |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
```

1. **Substrate Pre-Check & Loading:**
   - Inspect wafer cassette/carriers. Verify wafers are free of gross particulate contamination.
   - Load wafers onto an oven shelf or vacuum hotplate using clean vacuum wands handling wafer edges only.

2. **Thermal Dehydration Execution:**
   - Initiate dehydration bake program with thermal setpoint stabilized between **150°C and 200°C**.
   - Maintain continuous isothermal soak for **30 minutes** to thermally desorb surface-physisorbed moisture.

3. **Controlled Post-Bake Cooling:**
   - Transfer wafers immediately to an enclosed $N_2$-purged cooling plate or vacuum chill chuck.
   - Cool wafers down to ambient processing temperature (**20°C – 25°C**) to prevent uncontrolled solvent boil-off during subsequent coating.

4. **Queue Control & Downstream Hand-off:**
   - Transfer wafers directly to the HMDS vapor prime chamber.
   - Enforce a maximum post-bake queue time of $\le 15\text{ minutes}$ in cleanroom ambient to prevent re-adsorption of atmospheric moisture before priming.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric # | Acceptance Parameter | Target Value | Unit | Verification Method |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **1** | Bake Temperature Stability | **150 – 200** | $\text{°C}$ | Multi-point thermocouple / pyrometer |
| **2** | Thermal Soak Duration | **30** | $\text{minutes}$ | Automated tool timer log ($\pm 10\text{ s}$) |
| **3** | Post-Bake Ambient Hand-off Time | **$\le 15$** | $\text{minutes}$ | Cleanroom MES queue timer |
| **4** | Post-Prime Water Contact Angle (WCA)* | **$> 70$** | $\text{degrees (°)}$ | Automated Optical Goniometer |

*\*Note: Validates functional desorbed state leading to complete HMDS silylation.*

---

### 5. Context Citations

- **Source:** *Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming*  
  - Wafer Dehydration thermal parameters: *Silicon wafers must be baked at 150°C–200°C for 30 minutes to desorb physisorbed water molecules.*  
  - Resist adhesion dependence: *HMDS Priming reactively silylates hydrophilic silanol (-Si-OH) groups into hydrophobic methyl-siloxane (-Si-O-Si(CH3)3) bonds, increasing resist adhesion and preventing peel-off during acid wet etching.*
- **Source:** *Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*  
  - Adhesion requirement context: *Photoresist adhesion during BOE requires HMDS vapor prime at 120°C prior to resist coating to withstand wet acid attack.*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal integration across Gen 1 garage-scale equipment introduces significant wafer temperature gradient risks. A standard laboratory hot plate lacking multi-zone PID loop control or nitrogen shower lid will induce lateral temperature non-uniformity (>5°C variation across 100mm wafer), resulting in uneven moisture desorption rates and patchy subsequent HMDS monolayer formation. Tooling must integrate calibrated vacuum chuck or thermally coupled aluminum ballast blocks to guarantee uniform convective and conductive heat transfer.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Dehydration bake at 150°C-200°C effectively eliminates multi-layer physisorbed molecular water, but does not desorb chemically bound silanol (-Si-OH) groups, which only condense above 400°C. Maintaining the bake window at 180°C for 30 minutes establishes a clean stoichiometric monolayer of silanol sites essential for reaction with hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS). If the wafer is under-baked (<150°C), residual physisorbed water rapidly hydrolyzes incoming HMDS vapor into hexamethyldisiloxane [(CH3)3Si-O-Si(CH3)3] and ammonia (NH3), suppressing silylation and causing photoresist lift-off during subsequent wet BOE etch.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: In a distributed Vietnamese garage foundry environment, sourcing high-purity semiconductor-grade nitrogen (N5.0 or 99.999% purity) for bake purge gas represents a frequent single-point supply vulnerability. Industrial grade cylinder N2 or compressed shop air contains excessive moisture (>10 ppm H2O) and volatile hydrocarbon oil mist, which permanently poisons the silicon dioxide surface. The recipe must mandate molecular sieve 13X in-line hydrocarbon/desiccant filter traps or specify certified VLSI-grade dry nitrogen bottles.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Dehydration bake represents the strict initial gating node of the photolithography loop. Operators face high scrap rates if queue times between dehydration completion, cooling, and vapor priming are breached due to garage ambient humidity (frequently >70% RH in local VN tropical climate). An uncompromising timer must be enforced, and hot plate warm-up sequences must be automated to avoid fabrication queue bottlenecks during manual multi-wafer batch runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete physisorbed moisture desorption due to hot plate thermal droop (<150°C actual wafer surface temperature), leading to HMDS vapor hydrolysis and catastrophic Shipley 1813 resist delamination during 6:1 BOE dip.
1. Post-bake ambient moisture readsorption caused by exceeding the 15-minute cleanroom queue time prior to HMDS prime chamber loading in high ambient relative humidity (>60% RH).
1. Wafer thermal shock fracture or slip dislocation generation caused by sudden transfer of 200°C quartz/silicon substrates directly onto cold metal surfaces without stepped cooling.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-1-1-01` | **Thermal Surface Uniformity and Steady-State Bake Verification** | Calibrated 4-point thermocouple wafer or K-type surface contact probe connected to data logger (Fluke 52 II / Keysight 34970A), IR pyrometer (calibrated emissivity e=0.68 for thermal SiO2) | 1. Place instrumented thermocouple wafer onto hot plate surface and engage vacuum hold-down (if equipped). 2. Record temperature across center, mid-radius, and edge points every 10 seconds for a total duration of 30 minutes. 3. Verify steady-state stabilization time to reach target temperature. 4. Transfer wafer to closed cooling stage under dry N2 purge and measure cooling curve to ambient (25°C). | `Wafer surface temperature must remain at 180°C ± 5°C continuously for >= 28 minutes of the 30-minute cycle across all measurement points. Center-to-edge gradient must not exceed 4°C.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-1-1-02` | **Desorption Efficacy via Sessile Drop Water Contact Angle (WCA) Screening** | Optical contact angle goniometer with microliter dispensing syringe (drop volume 2.0 uL DI water, 18.2 MOhm-cm) and high-resolution camera | 1. Position dehydrated wafer on goniometer sample stage. 2. Dispense a 2.0 uL droplet of HPLC-grade DI water onto wafer center and two peripheral zones. 3. Capture droplet profile immediately (<5 seconds post-dispense) using tangent-line profile analysis software. 4. Record static contact angle at 5 distinct spatial locations. | `Immediately post-dehydration (pre-HMDS), the clean hydrophilic oxide surface must exhibit a baseline water contact angle of < 10° (indicating clean silanol surface free of hydrocarbon contaminants and physisorbed multi-layer water), transitioning to > 70° only after subsequent HMDS silylation.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: High-temperature thermal protective gloves (Nomex or Kevlar) rated to 250°C, UV-absorbing safety glasses with side shields (ANSI Z87.1), Cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, dual layer), Flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat (anti-static ESD polyester-cotton blend), PTFE wafer handling tweezers with thermal insulation
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn treatment: Immediately immerse affected skin area under cool running clean water for at least 15 minutes. Do not apply ice or oil-based ointments. Cover with sterile non-adherent dressing. In case of inert gas (N2) asphyxiation risk in confined space, relocate victim immediately to fresh air, administer supplemental oxygen if trained, and call emergency services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation must be conducted within a Class 1000 clean hood equipped with dedicated hot plate local thermal exhaust ventilation (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s or 100 FPM) to vent heated vapors and avoid cleanroom ambient temperature elevation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: No hazardous chemical effluent generated during dehydration thermal bake. Spent nitrogen gas is vented directly through thermal fume extraction. Defective test wafers with clean SiO2 are collected in standard solid semiconductor silicon scrap bins.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (99.999% VLSI Semiconductor Grade) | `>= 99.999 vol%` |
| **Deionized Water (Testing Verification)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 Ultra-Pure Semiconductor Grade | `100 vol%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `15 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Piranha/RCA-cleaned or wet-processed silicon wafer with native or thermally grown silicon dioxide (SiO2), bearing multi-layer physisorbed atmospheric moisture (H2O) and terminal silanol groups.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Moisture-desorbed, dry oxide surface terminated by activated silanol (-Si-OH) reactive sites, stabilized at 22°C-25°C under dry N2 ambient, ready for immediate reactive HMDS vapor silylation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding the 15-minute ambient air threshold results in atmospheric moisture re-adsorption (>10 molecular water layers in humid ambient), which hydrolyzes HMDS vapor during subsequent processing, terminating adhesion promotion and causing complete resist lift-off during wet 6:1 BOE etching.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Wafer surface achieves complete desorption of physisorbed atmospheric moisture through a validated 180°C hot-plate thermal cycle of 30 minutes, producing an activated silanol surface with verified thermal uniformity, zero particulate contamination, and immediate transfer capability to the HMDS vapor prime chamber.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DEHYDRATION_BAKE_THERMAL_PROFILE_RUN_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `SURFACE_INSPECTION_OPTICAL_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `CONTACT_ANGLE_BASELINE_METROLOGY.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wafer center-to-edge steady-state dehydration bake temperature** | `180.0°C` | ±5.0°C | In-situ calibrated surface thermocouple array logging across 5 wafer coordinates at 1 Hz for 30 minutes |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Effective dwell time at dehydration temperature (T >= 175°C)** | `30.0 minutes` | +2.0 / -0.0 minutes | Automated digital recipe timer integrated with hot-plate temperature interlock |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Transfer cool-down duration inside dry nitrogen box to ambient before prime** | `180 seconds` | ±30 seconds | Non-contact infrared pyrometer reading wafer surface at 22°C - 25°C prior to chamber load |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Continuous 30-minute thermal bake profile logged with zero temperature drop below 175°C, post-cool surface contact angle confirmed < 10°, wafer transferred to HMDS vapor prime station within <= 15 minutes of bake completion, and sign-off recorded in DRAM Foundation VN fabrication lot traveler.

q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding the 15-minute ambient air threshold results in atmospheric moisture re-adsorption (>10 molecular water layers in humid ambient), which hydrolyzes HMDS vapor during subsequent processing, terminating adhesion promotion and causing complete resist lift-off during wet 6:1 BOE etching.

expected_result.summary: Wafer surface achieves complete desorption of physisorbed atmospheric moisture through a validated 180°C hot-plate thermal cycle of 30 minutes, producing an activated silanol surface with verified thermal uniformity, zero particulate contamination, and immediate transfer capability to the HMDS vapor prime chamber.

quantitative_assertions.verification_method: In-situ calibrated surface thermocouple array logging across 5 wafer coordinates at 1 Hz for 30 minutes

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Effective dwell time at dehydration temperature (T >= 175°C)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Automated digital recipe timer integrated with hot-plate temperature interlock

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Transfer cool-down duration inside dry nitrogen box to ambient before prime
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Non-contact infrared pyrometer reading wafer surface at 22°C - 25°C prior to chamber load

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Continuous 30-minute thermal bake profile logged with zero temperature drop below 175°C, post-cool surface contact angle confirmed < 10°, wafer transferred to HMDS vapor prime station within <= 15 minutes of bake completion, and sign-off recorded in DRAM Foundation VN fabrication lot traveler.
