nodes.label: EBR Arm Trajectory, Flow Rate & Spin-Sync Dispense Recipe Optimization
nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## EBR Arm Trajectory, Flow Rate & Spin-Sync Dispense Recipe Optimization

**Generation Target**: Gen 2 (µm)  
**Process Step**: Photolithography / Edge Bead Removal (EBR) & Resist Conditioning  
**Hierarchy Context**: `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip` > `Shipley 1813 Spin Coating, Edge Bead Removal and Softbake` > `Automated PGMEA Solvent Edge Bead Removal (EBR) Dispense Calibration`

---

### Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Start: 100mm Wafer   │
│        Chucked         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Spin-Sync        │
│  Acceleration to 1000  │
│          RPM           │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   EBR Arm Trajectory   │
│     to Wafer Edge      │
│        R=48.5mm        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   PGMEA Solvent Jet    │
│        Dispense        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Ramp to 4000 RPM    │
│    Final Spin & Dry    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Softbake 115C 60s    │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Substrate Pre-Conditioning Verification**:
   - Confirm 100 mm silicon wafer has completed dehydration bake at 150°C–200°C for 30 minutes and reactive HMDS vapor priming (silanol silylation into hydrophobic methyl-siloxane bonds).
   - Secure wafer onto the vacuum chuck of the spin coater.

2. **Resist Dispense & Meyerhofer Radial Spread Cycle**:
   - Dispense 2–3 mL of Shipley 1813 positive photoresist at wafer center.
   - Initiate spread cycle: spin at 500 RPM for 5 seconds to uniformly wet the surface before solvent flash evaporation.

3. **Spin-Sync & EBR Arm Trajectory Homing**:
   - Drive the EBR dispensing arm along precision ground linear guide rails (MGN12H) via NEMA 17 stepper drive (1/16 microstepping, ball/lead screw mechanism).
   - Home and position the EBR solvent nozzle over the wafer edge zone (Gen 2 alignment tolerance: $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$, encoder resolution: $1\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Set nozzle dispense angle at 45° directed radially outwards towards wafer bevel edge to eliminate solvent splashback onto the central die area.

4. **Synchronous PGMEA Solvent Dispense**:
   - Trigger the automated PGMEA solvent jet at the peripheral rim while the wafer rotates at a synchronized intermediate spin-speed (800–1,000 RPM).
   - Dispense PGMEA jet for 3–5 seconds to dissolve and clear the peripheral edge bead buildup, preventing clamp contamination during subsequent handling.

5. **Main Spin Thinning & Film Uniformity Ramp**:
   - Retract the EBR arm safely beyond the chuck perimeter.
   - Ramp the spin chuck at 10,000 RPM/s to a terminal speed of 4,000 RPM for 30 seconds to evacuate residual solvent and planarize the resist film.

6. **Post-EBR Softbake**:
   - Transfer wafer immediately to a flat aluminum hot plate.
   - Softbake at 115°C for 60 seconds to drive off volatile casting solvents and stabilize the layer for exposure.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value & Tolerance | Verification Equipment / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Resist Film Thickness & Uniformity** | $1.30\ \mu\text{m} \pm 15\ \text{nm}$ ($\sim 1.3\ \mu\text{m}$) | Spectroscopic Reflectometry / Ellipsometry across 100 mm wafer |
| **EBR Arm Stage Positioning Accuracy** | Gen 2 tolerance: $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ (Encoder resolution: $1\ \mu\text{m}$) | Linear optical / magnetic encoder feedback along MGN12H rails |
| **Spin Acceleration & Terminal Speed** | Ramp: $10,000\ \text{RPM/s}$; Terminal: $4,000\ \text{RPM} \pm 10\ \text{RPM}$ for $30\ \text{s}$ | Optical tachometer / closed-loop spin chuck servo encoder |
| **Softbake Temperature & Dwell** | $115^\circ\text{C} \pm 1^\circ\text{C}$ for $60\ \text{seconds}$ | Calibrated surface thermocouple on aluminum hot plate |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Context Traceability

- **Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming**:
  - *Spin Parameters & Film Profile*: Dispense 2–3 mL Shipley 1813 at 500 RPM for 5 s; ramp at 10,000 RPM/s to 4,000 RPM for 30 s; yielding $1.30\ \mu\text{m} \pm 15\ \text{nm}$ uniform film on 100 mm wafers.
  - *EBR Chemistry*: Applied PGMEA solvent jet to eliminate edge bead and prevent clamp contamination.
  - *Dehydration & Priming*: Wafer dehydration at 150°C–200°C for 30 min followed by HMDS vapor silylation.
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:
  - *Coating & Thermal Budget*: Shipley 1813 coated at 4,000 RPM yields $\sim 1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ thickness; softbake specified at 115°C for 60 s on a flat aluminum hot plate.
  - *Gen 2 Alignment Budget*: Micron-scale feature resolution with Gen 2 stage alignment tolerance of $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **Precision Linear Stage Design & Vibration Damping**:
  - *Mechanical Architecture*: MGN12H precision linear guide rails, NEMA 17 stepper drive with 1/16 microstepping, straightness $< 5\ \mu\text{m} / 100\ \text{mm}$, and closed-loop optical/magnetic encoder resolution down to $1\ \mu\text{m}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Synchronizing the EBR linear stage (NEMA 17 stepper + MGN12H linear guide rail) with the spin coater chuck speed profile requires deterministic real-time hardware triggering; microstepping quantization or non-real-time USB serial latency will introduce non-repeatable dwell times at the wafer bevel, leading to splash-back and irregular solvent dispense cut lines.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Dispensing PGMEA at the wafer edge while spinning Shipley 1813 at 2000-3000 RPM must balance centrifugal capillary forces against solvent vapor dry-out; excessive flow rate creates back-splash mist deposits across the active exposure field, whereas an undersaturated stream or inaccurate radial nozzle offset (> 2.5 mm exclusion) leaves resist bead rims that cause contact mask cracking or optical out-of-focus during 180nm BOE patterning.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade PGMEA (propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate, VLSI or SEMI Grade) and solvent-compatible PTFE/PFA dispense tubing with Kalrez perfluoroelastomer seals are constrained in local supply; using generic hardware-grade tubing introduces plasticizer leaching, pinhole chemical swelling, and nozzle droplet clogging.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibrating this Gen 1 open-source EBR recipe must not exceed 2 shifts of wafer budget (maximum 10 test coupons); the dispense recipe, nozzle trajectory limits, and optical exclusion metrology must be locked into machine-executable G-code/firmware recipes before committing multi-die 180nm DRAM test silicon.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Solvent droplet back-splash onto the active DRAM device die area causing pinhole dissolution and catastrophic oxide patterning defects during BOE dip-etch.
1. Mechanical collision of the EBR dispense nozzle with the spinning vacuum chuck or wafer bevel due to lost stepper motor steps or improper home-limit switch calibration.
1. Incomplete edge bead clearance (>3.0 mm non-uniform edge ring) causing variable gap wedge during contact alignment and subsequent sub-micron focal plane defocus.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-2-2-2-01` | **Radial EBR Exclusion Width and Edge Uniformity Verification** | Calibrated optical metallurgical microscope with 10x/50x Plan Achromat objectives, motorized XY stage with 1 µm digital readout, and top-down CCD camera metrology software. | 1. Position wafer on vacuum chuck, verify vacuum interlock (> -70 kPa). 2. Initiate spin sequence ramp to 2500 RPM. 3. Trigger EBR arm trajectory to radial coordinate R = 48.0 mm (2.0 mm nominal exclusion border). 4. Dispense PGMEA at 1.8 mL/min for 8.0 seconds synchronized with 2500 RPM rotation. 5. Retract EBR arm to home park position. 6. Ramp spin coater to 4500 RPM for 15.0 seconds to spin-dry residual solvent. 7. Execute softbake at 115°C for 60 seconds on hotplate. 8. Measure residual resist exclusion width at 8 equidistant azimuth angles (0°, 45°, 90°, 135°, 180°, 225°, 270°, 315°) using optical microscope. | `Exclusion border width must be 2.0 mm ± 0.25 mm across all 8 measurement points, with total circumferential width variation (3-sigma) ≤ 0.15 mm and zero resist residue or solvent splash droplets observed within R < 47.0 mm.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-2-2-2-02` | **EBR Dispense Cut-off Cleanliness and Active Area Defect Density Audit** | High-intensity darkfield inspection lamp (green/white LED grazing incidence) and spectroscopic reflectometer / thin-film thickness mapping tool. | 1. Mount wafer under darkfield inspection station at 15-degree grazing incidence angle. 2. Scan wafer surface from R = 0 to R = 47.0 mm for satellite solvent mist marks, micro-droplets, or secondary striations. 3. Measure resist film thickness along a radial line across the boundary zone at 50 µm pitch using the reflectometer to record the edge transition slope. 4. Record particle count and splash-back defect counts using digital imaging inspection software. | `Zero solvent mist spots or satellite pinholes detected in the device area (R ≤ 46.0 mm); edge transition boundary slope thickness drops from 1.3 µm to < 0.05 µm within a radial transition width of ≤ 150 µm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Solvent-resistant butyl or double-gloved nitrile cleanroom gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles with side shields, Polypropylene full chemical apron over cleanroom garment, Face shield (polycarbonate) during chemical bottle replacement and line priming
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored. Skin contact: Flush affected area immediately with copious flowing water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated clothing. Eye contact: Irrigate eyes gently with isotonic saline or eyewash station stream for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids retracted, seek immediate medical evaluation. Ingestion: Never induce vomiting in an unconscious person; rinse mouth thoroughly with water and seek emergency medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation must be strictly confined to a dedicated solvent wet bench or laminar exhaust spin hood with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); ductwork must be VOC-rated and grounded to prevent static discharge spark ignition.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All spent PGMEA and solvent spin waste must be collected through segregated stainless steel or conductive polypropylene flammable waste lines into dedicated grounded Class IB flammable solvent waste carboys; do not mix with aqueous acids, BOE fluoride waste, or oxidizers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Propylene Glycol Monomethyl Ether Acetate (PGMEA / 1-Methoxy-2-propyl acetate)** | `108-65-6` | VLSI / Electronic Grade (>= 99.5%) | `>= 99.5 wt%` |
| **Shipley Microposit 1813 Photoresist (containing Propylene Glycol Monomethyl Ether Acetate, Mixed Diazo Photoactive Compound, Cresol Novolak Resin)** | `108-65-6` | Semiconductor Grade | `60-80% solvent vehicle, 10-30% Novolak polymer` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly HMDS vapor-primed, spun Shipley 1813 resist coating (unbaked or post-spin dry, tacky film, thickness ~1.3 µm) on 100mm silicon wafer.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Completed EBR edge bead cleared (2.0 mm perimeter clear of resist, dried bevel edge), ready for immediate 115°C hotplate softbake.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive queue time prior to softbake leads to uncontrolled room-temperature solvent evaporation, non-uniform skinning of the Novolak resin, edge reflow into the cleared EBR zone, and moisture absorption from cleanroom air causing resist micro-crystallization and blister defects during bake.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Calibrated and verified automated EBR dispense process operating on an MGN12H linear rail arm that delivers a uniform 2.0 mm edge exclusion ring on Shipley 1813 resist-coated 100mm wafers without splash-back defects, fully synchronized with chuck spin-dry profiles.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ebr_trajectory_spin_recipe_v1.0.csv`
- [ ] `ebr_exclusion_radial_metrology_report.pdf`
- [ ] `ebr_bevel_boundary_darkfield_micrograph.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **EBR radial exclusion width around wafer perimeter** | `2.0 mm` | ± 0.25 mm | Calibrated optical microscope cross-hair measurements taken at 8 equidistant angular positions (0° to 315°). |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Back-splash solvent pinhole defect density inside active device die zone (R < 46 mm)** | `0 defects/wafer` | +0 defects/wafer (zero tolerance) | Full-wafer darkfield optical grazing-incidence inspection under high-intensity 532nm monochromatic surface inspection lamp. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Resist edge bead profile transition width from nominal thickness (1.3 µm) to zero (< 0.05 µm)** | `100 µm` | ≤ 150 µm maximum | Radial thin-film spectroscopic reflectometer profile step scan with 25 µm beam spot size. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Five consecutive 100mm wafers processed through the automated EBR trajectory recipe achieving 2.0 ± 0.25 mm clear perimeter exclusion, zero active area solvent splash marks under darkfield inspection, and signed approval by both the Systems Engineer and Domain Expert.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Title:** Optical Profilometry & Microscopic Edge Bead Exclusion Zone Metrology  
**Module:** `[Metrology] < [Photolithography]` | **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### Metrology Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Wafer Load &      │
│       Centering        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Microscopic Edge    │
│     Exclusion Scan     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     White Light /      │
│  Optical Profilometry  │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Bead Profile & Step   │
│   Height Extraction    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acceptance Criteria   │
│      Verification      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Substrate Mounting & Datum Alignment:**
   - Load the post-softbake (115°C, 60 s) 100 mm wafer onto the vacuum chuck of the optical metrology stage.
   - Use microscopic edge detection (Plan Achromat objective, 10x, NA 0.25) to locate the wafer edge bevel and register physical $(X, Y, \theta)$ coordinate zero.

2. **Optical Exclusion Zone Edge Bead Inspection:**
   - Translate the stage radially inward from the physical wafer perimeter toward the active die region.
   - Inspect the PGMEA solvent-cleared boundary under calibrated darkfield/brightfield microscopic illumination to verify clear transition from bare silicon/oxide to continuous photoresist film without solvent splash or residue streaks.

3. **Optical Profilometry & Film Step Height Metrology:**
   - Position the non-destructive optical profilometer / reflectometer head across the cleared transition zone.
   - Execute a line scan from the stripped edge bead exclusion zone across the transition shoulder into the bulk resist.
   - Apply Cauchy optical dispersion modeling to acquire the step-height profile and verify that residual bead build-up is eliminated.

4. **Multi-Point Radial Uniformity Verification:**
   - Transition to automated multi-point (9-point / 49-point) mapping across the 100 mm wafer substrate.
   - Measure nominal bulk Shipley 1813 photoresist thickness and ensure radial film variations stay within tolerance limits prior to UV exposure.

---

### Target Acceptance Criteria Metrics

```text
                       Metrology Nominal Targets        
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 Pos Tol (±um)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Film Tol (±nm)┤▒                                       │
              │▒                                       │
Bulk Film (um)┤███████████                             │
              │███████████                             │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
              0.0       1.2       2.5      3.8      5.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Tolerance | Inspection Tool / Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bulk Resist Film Thickness** | `1.30 µm` (`~1.3 µm`) | `±15 nm` (within `±2 nm` precision) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Reflectometry (Cauchy Model) |
| **Exclusion Boundary Position Alignment** | Edge Bead Transition Zone | `±5 µm` | Gen 2 Calibrated Macroscopic Optical Stage (10x NA 0.25) |
| **Pre-Metrology Softbake Thermal Baseline** | `115°C` | `60 s` dwell time | Flat Aluminum Hot Plate Surface Probe |
| **Wafer Mapping Radial Uniformity** | 9-point / 49-point array | Uniform across `100 mm` wafer | Automated Stage Optical Wafer Mapping |

---

### Literature Citations & Traceability

- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018):**
  - Shipley 1813 film thickness baseline (~1.3 µm at 4000 RPM).
  - Soft bake thermal processing (115°C for 60 s on aluminum hot plate).
  - Optical microscopy resolution setup (10x Plan Achromat, NA 0.25).
  - Gen 2 alignment positioning tolerance limit (`±5 µm`).
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology:**
  - Non-destructive optical thin-film metrology, Cauchy dispersion optical modeling parameterizing refractive index $n(\lambda)$.
  - Photoresist measurement precision capability within `±2 nm`.
  - Radial non-uniformity tracking via automated 9-point and 49-point wafer mapping.
- **Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming:**
  - Shipley 1813 spin dynamics yielding `1.30 µm ± 15 nm` nominal film uniformity across `100 mm` wafers.
  - Integration with automated PGMEA solvent Edge Bead Removal (EBR) to prevent edge clamp contamination.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Optical profilometry must integrate directly with the spin-coater chuck coordinate system and automated stage encoders. At Gen 1 macroscopic dimensions, radial runout and tilt of manual wafer mounting can distort the measured edge bead profile by >15 µm vertically, which will cause false positives in edge bead exclusion zone (EEZ) clearance verification unless dynamic planar tilt correction is executed.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Shipley 1813 positive resist (nominal 1.3 µm thickness) forms a prominent surface tension bead at the wafer periphery that can reach 3.5 to 5.0 µm without proper PGMEA EBR. Because 1813 is partially transparent at standard profilometer wavelengths, white-light optical profilometry (coherence scanning interferometry) requires careful refractive index deconvolution (n ~ 1.65 at 633 nm) or specular reflection filtering at the steep bead transition boundary to prevent phase unwrapping errors.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Research-grade optical profilometers (e.g., Zygo or Bruker) and calibrated 100-micron pitch optical grid reticles carry long lead times and high capital cost; the garage/pilot fab line must secure a secondary non-contact sensor option (such as a 3D confocal laser displacement sensor or calibrated 10x Plan Achromat metallurgical microscope with digital micrometric reticle) to avoid stalling production.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Edge exclusion zone metrology must complete within 8 minutes per wafer to respect downstream queue-time budgets before i-line UV exposure; prolonged ambient hold-time under white cleanroom illumination risks partial uncrosslinking/parasitic exposure or airborne amine poisoning of the photoresist film.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interferometric fringe contrast loss at the steep edge-bead slope (>15° meniscus), causing profile data dropouts and miscalculation of the bead exclusion boundary.
1. Solvent splashback or airborne PGMEA redeposition onto the active field during EBR spin calibration, causing localized resist thinning and premature BOE oxide pinhole punch-through.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-2-2-3-01` | **Optical Profilometry of Residual Edge Bead Peak Height and Taper Meniscus** | White-light optical profilometer / non-contact 3D optical surface profiler with 10x objective and automated motorized XY stage | 1. Mount wafer onto optical profilometer vacuum chuck and level to within 0.05 degrees tilt. 2. Align objective at wafer edge (radius = 50.0 mm) covering the 0 to 5 mm radial perimeter band. 3. Acquire 3D surface topography across 4 cardinal wafer positions (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°). 4. Extract 2D radial step-height cross-sections from raw silicon substrate to bulk photoresist plateau. 5. Measure residual bead peak height relative to bulk resist thickness (1.30 µm). | `Maximum residual edge bead peak height <= 1.35 µm (<= 50 nm bead crown above 1.30 µm nominal bulk resist plateau) across all 4 measurement points.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-2-2-3-02` | **Microscopic Edge Bead Exclusion Zone (EEZ) Radial Width Verification** | Calibrated metallurgical brightfield/darkfield microscope with 10x Plan Achromat objective (NA 0.25), digital CMOS camera, and NIST-traceable stage micrometer | 1. Position wafer edge under brightfield illumination at 10x magnification. 2. Identify physical wafer bevel perimeter and set radial coordinate R_edge = 0.00 mm. 3. Translate stage radially inward toward wafer center until the continuous homogeneous photoresist film edge boundary is reached. 4. Record linear distance from physical bevel edge to resist threshold at 8 equidistant radial angles (every 45°). 5. Inspect exclusion zone for splash droplets, scalloping, or residual resist ribbons. | `Edge Bead Exclusion Zone width = 3.00 mm ± 0.50 mm across all 8 measurement angles; zero residual resist residue, splash droplets, or scalloping exceeding 50 µm inside the exclusion band.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, 6 mil minimum), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and hood, Full face shield during chemical handling or solvent spill mitigation
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush with sterile isotonic eyewash solution or copious clean water for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Remove contaminated apparel immediately; wash skin thoroughly with non-abrasive soap and water. Inhalation: Relocate individual to fresh ambient air; administer oxygen if respiration is labored. Ingestion: Rinse mouth thoroughly; do NOT induce vomiting; seek immediate emergency medical care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Metrology tool must reside in an ISO Class 5 laminar flow hood within an ISO Class 6 yellow cleanroom enclosure (UV-filtered <500 nm). Exhaust air face velocity must be maintained at 0.45 m/s ± 20% to sweep residual PGMEA solvent vapors away from operator breathing zones.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Contaminated cleanroom wipes, swab applicators, and solvent-bearing pipettes must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-arrestor stainless-steel hazardous solvent waste cans designated for flammable organic non-halogenated solvents. Do not mix with acid or BOE fluoride waste streams.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate (PGMEA)** | `108-65-6` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / SLSI) | `>= 99.5%` |
| **Shipley Microposit 1813 Photoresist (Diazonaphthoquinone/Cresol Novolak in PGMEA)** | `108-65-6` | Semiconductor Grade | `100% formulated mixture` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Soft-baked (115°C, 60s) Shipley 1813 photoresist film on 6:1 BOE thermal oxide with automated top/backside PGMEA EBR completed; non-tacky, dry surface.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Inspection-verified, clean wafer with uniform 3.0 mm edge exclusion band and <=1.35 µm total edge profile, ready for contact/proximity UV mask aligner chucking.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive cleanroom air exposure causes airborne base/amine contamination and moisture reabsorption, resulting in resist foot formation, interfacial T-topping, and altered optical sensitivity during subsequent i-line UV exposure.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full quantitative validation of the Shipley 1813 edge bead removal process demonstrating complete elimination of circumferential bead crown buildup and establishing an edge exclusion zone of 3.0 mm ± 0.5 mm around the 100mm wafer perimeter to prevent mask contamination during contact photolithography.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `EEZ_METROLOGY_RADIAL_PROFILE_MAP.csv`
- [ ] `EEZ_OPTICAL_SURFACE_TOPOGRAPHY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `MICROSCOPIC_PERIMETER_CLEARANCE_IMAGE_SET.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum residual edge bead peak height above bulk resist surface** | `0.00 nm` | +50 nm | White-light coherence scanning optical profilometry line scan across 4 cardinal edge locations |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Radial Edge Bead Exclusion Zone width from physical wafer perimeter** | `3.00 mm` | ±0.50 mm | Calibrated 10x metallurgical brightfield microscopy with digital micrometer measurement at 8 perimeter angles |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Bulk photoresist film thickness outside the exclusion zone** | `1300 nm` | ±25 nm | Spectroscopic reflectometry/ellipsometry wafer mapping at 9 radial sites |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 4 profilometry cardinal scans confirm peak bead height <= 1.35 µm, all 8 microscopic inspection points show EEZ clearance within 2.50 mm to 3.50 mm with no solvent residue, and research engineer counter-signs the automated metrology log before wafer enters the 30-minute UV exposure queue.

critics.supply_chain: Research-grade optical profilometers (e.g., Zygo or Bruker) and calibrated 100-micron pitch optical grid reticles carry long lead times and high capital cost; the garage/pilot fab line must secure a secondary non-contact sensor option (such as a 3D confocal laser displacement sensor or calibrated 10x Plan Achromat metallurgical microscope with digital micrometric reticle) to avoid stalling production.
critics.laya_pm: Edge exclusion zone metrology must complete within 8 minutes per wafer to respect downstream queue-time budgets before i-line UV exposure; prolonged ambient hold-time under white cleanroom illumination risks partial uncrosslinking/parasitic exposure or airborne amine poisoning of the photoresist film.
critical_failure_modes: Interferometric fringe contrast loss at the steep edge-bead slope (>15° meniscus), causing profile data dropouts and miscalculation of the bead exclusion boundary.
Solvent splashback or airborne PGMEA redeposition onto the active field during EBR spin calibration, causing localized resist thinning and premature BOE oxide pinhole punch-through.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Metadata
- **Title**: Contact Hotplate Softbake (115°C) & Spectroscopic Reflectometry Resist Thickness Verification
- **Process Line**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Photolithography & Metrology
- **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type**: Make

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Transfer from   │
│       Spin Chuck       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Contact Hotplate    │
│   Softbake @ 115°C /   │
│          60s           │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Active Cooling @ 20°C │
│         / 30s          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Spectroscopic      │
│     Reflectometry      │
│       Alignment        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Cauchy Dispersion    │
│  Model Fit & 9-Point   │
│          Map           │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Resist Thickness &   │
│       Uniformity       │
│      Verification      │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

### Phase A: Contact Hotplate Softbake
1. **Pre-Bake Thermal Stabilization**:
   - Power on the vacuum-assisted flat aluminum contact hotplate and allow the PID controller to equilibrate at **115°C**.
   - Verify surface temperature across the chuck with a calibrated contact surface probe to ensure thermal gradient stability.
2. **Wafer Transfer & Vacuum Chucking**:
   - Transfer the freshly coated wafer (dispensed with 2–3 mL Shipley 1813 and edge-bead removed) using vacuum tweezers onto the lift pins.
   - Lower the pins to achieve conformal backside contact with the flat aluminum surface and engage vacuum hold-down to prevent air-gap thermal gradients.
3. **Timed Bake Execution**:
   - Execute the softbake cycle for exactly **60 seconds** at **115°C** to drive off residual casting solvents and stabilize the resist matrix.
4. **Post-Bake Chill Cycle**:
   - De-energize chuck vacuum, raise lift pins, and transfer the wafer onto an aluminum chill plate at **20°C** for **30 seconds** to arrest thermal processing before measurement.

---

### Phase B: Spectroscopic Reflectometry Resist Thickness Verification
1. **Optical System Baseline Calibration**:
   - Initialize the spectroscopic reflectometer / ellipsometer light source across the UV-visible inspection band.
   - Run baseline calibration (Dark spectrum and Reference Silicon blank) measuring reflection coefficients:
     $$\rho = \frac{r_p}{r_s} = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$$
2. **Dispersion Modeling Setup**:
   - Select the **Cauchy dispersion model** for Shipley 1813 photoresist parameterizing refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$ over bare silicon substrate.
3. **Automated Wafer Mapping**:
   - Load the baked wafer onto the metrology vacuum stage.
   - Execute an automated **9-point radial wafer map** covering wafer center, mid-radius, and outer edge perimeter exclusion zones.
4. **Data Acquisition & Run Qualification**:
   - Collect reflectance spectra at each point; fit interference oscillation fringes using the Cauchy optical model.
   - Record the extracted thickness values, mean film thickness, and standard deviation across all 9 measurement points.

---

## 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Physical Unit | Tolerance / Limit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hotplate Surface Bake Temperature** | `115` | `°C` | `±1.0 °C` | Calibrated surface thermocouple probe |
| **Softbake Duration** | `60` | `s` | `±1.0 s` | Integrated tool digital process timer |
| **Mean Photoresist Film Thickness** | `1.30` (1300) | `µm` (`nm`) | `±15 nm` (1.30 µm ± 15 nm) | 9-point spectroscopic reflectometer / ellipsometer |
| **Thickness Measurement Gauge Precision** | `±2` | `nm` | `≤ ±2 nm` | Repeatability fit of Cauchy optical model |

---

## 3. Literature Context Citations

- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**:
  - *Shipley 1813 spin-coated at 4000 RPM yields ~1.3 micron thickness.*
  - *Soft bake at 115°C for 60 seconds on a flat aluminum hot plate.*
  - *Gen 2 alignment tolerance baseline (±5 microns).*
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
  - *Physical principle measuring reflection coefficients $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$.*
  - *Cauchy dispersion model parameterizing $n(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$.*
  - *Metrology precision for photoresist (1.3 µm measured within ±2 nm).*
  - *Automated 9-point wafer mapping tracking radial film non-uniformity.*
- **Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming**:
  - *Dispense parameters (2–3 mL Shipley 1813).*
  - *Post-spin film uniformity benchmark producing 1.30 µm ± 15 nm across 100mm substrates.*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Contact hotplate softbake at 115°C establishes the solvent matrix baseline that directly dictates the subsequent i-line photolithography exposure dose and wet chemical buffered oxide etch (BOE) undercut profile. If radial thermal gradients exceed ±0.5°C across the vacuum chuck plate, differential residual solvent (propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate, PGMEA) creates radial refractive index and optical absorption variations, invalidating fixed Cauchy dispersion models in downstream spectroscopic reflectometry and inducing systematic thickness calculation errors.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Shipley Microposit S1813 requires precise solvent evaporation dynamics; unbaked or insufficiently baked resist exhibits excessive dark erosion rate in MF-319 developer and erratic isotropic wet etching rates during BOE 6:1 exposure. Softbaking at 115°C for 60 seconds on a calibrated contact vacuum hotplate must target a nominal dried thickness of 1.33 µm with Cauchy parameters (A_n ≈ 1.585, B_n ≈ 0.0094 µm², C_n ≈ 0.0003 µm⁴). Spectroscopic reflectometry must utilize at least a 9-point diameter or 49-point polar map with non-destructive broadband normal incidence (400–800 nm) to avoid partial cross-linking from deep UV illumination during optical thickness scanning.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Shipley 1813 positive photoresist, optical calibration silicon reference wafers with certified 100 nm thermally grown SiO2 (VLSI standards), and high-purity nitrogen lines for hotplate vacuum chuck ejectors are subject to strict shelf-life and supply constraints. S1813 requires 4°C refrigerated storage and warm-up cycles; reflectometer optical lamps (tungsten-halogen/deuterium) have finite continuous-burn lifespans (typically 1000–2000 hours) and must be sourced with redundant spares to prevent metrology line downtime during Gen 1 prototyping.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To maintain pilot fab throughput on the 180nm open-source DRAM process line, wafer bake-to-metrology-to-stepper queue times must be strictly disciplined. Reflectometry sampling cannot become a bottleneck; an automated 9-point thickness verification routine must execute in under 45 seconds per wafer with real-time automated logging into the fab MES/SPC database to ensure instantaneous lot disposition prior to i-line stepper alignment.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal gradient non-uniformity across hotplate causing >3% radial resist thickness variation and erratic wet etch undercut profiles.
1. Inadequate solvent outgassing leading to resist blistering, optical scattering, or optical model mismatch (poor Goodness-of-Fit GoF < 0.98 in reflectometry).
1. Vacuum chuck particle entrapment causing local thermal standoff, hot spots, and localized resist thickness anomalies.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-2-3-01` | **Contact Hotplate Thermal Uniformity and S1813 Thickness/Uniformity 9-Point Verification** | Calibrated surface contact multi-point TC wafer (SensArray), vacuum contact bake plate (115°C), spectroscopic reflectometer (Filmetrics F20 or equivalent with 400-800 nm optical spectrometer and automated mapping stage). | 1. Verify hotplate surface temperature across 9 points using thermocouple test wafer to ensure thermal delta <= 0.5°C across the heated zone. 2. Transfer freshly spun S1813 wafer to 115°C hotplate, initiate vacuum clamping, and softbake for exactly 60.0 seconds. 3. Transfer to chill plate at 22°C for 30.0 seconds. 4. Transfer wafer to spectroscopic reflectometer stage. 5. Acquire normal-incidence reflectance spectra (400–800 nm) across a 9-point diameter pattern (center, ±30mm, ±60mm, ±80mm in X and Y). 6. Fit spectra using Cauchy dispersion model (S1813 on SiO2 on Si stack) and extract film thickness and Goodness-of-Fit (GoF). | `Mean photoresist thickness = 1330 nm ± 25 nm (1.305 µm to 1.355 µm); 9-point thickness non-uniformity (3*sigma/mean) <= 1.5%; Goodness-of-Fit (GoF) >= 0.985 across all 9 measurement points.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-2-3-02` | **Residual Solvent Desorption and Optical Dispersion Index Stability Verification** | Spectroscopic reflectometer with broadband UV-Vis spectrometer (Cauchy parameter fitting module), multi-wavelength spectroscopic ellipsometer (Woollam M-2000 or equivalent for cross-verification). | 1. Load softbaked wafer onto reflectometer vacuum chuck. 2. Measure center-point refractive index dispersion across the 400–800 nm band. 3. Extract refractive index at i-line wavelength (lambda = 365 nm) and reference wavelength (lambda = 632.8 nm). 4. Compare extracted refractive index against fully baked S1813 baseline database values. 5. Verify absence of optical absorbance anomalies or spectral interference shift indicative of trapped PGMEA solvent. | `Refractive index n at 632.8 nm = 1.615 ± 0.005; refractive index n at 365 nm = 1.680 ± 0.010; spectral shift between t=5 min and t=30 min post-bake <= 0.2 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom chemical splash safety goggles (ANSI Z87.1 approved), High-temperature heat-resistant cleanroom thermal handling gloves / Nomex gauntlets for hotplate servicing, Double-layered disposable nitrile cleanroom gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness), Static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and ESD conductive cleanroom boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal contact burns: Immediately immerse burned area in cold cleanroom deionized water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply chemical ointments; seek cleanroom emergency medical response. Solvent vapor inhalation: Remove personnel immediately to fresh laminar air zone; administer oxygen if respiration is depressed. Skin/Eye contact: Flush affected areas with copious clean water or eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated dedicated solvent/flammable cleanroom exhaust canopy over hotplate module with constant face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); continuous interlocked photoresist spin-coater/bake track exhaust monitoring with automatic thermal cut-off if exhaust static pressure drops below -0.25 inches of water column.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Thermal baking primarily releases volatilized PGMEA vapors into the dedicated solvent exhaust scrubbers (VOC thermal oxidizer/carbon adsorption bed). Spent solvent wipes or edge-bead purge residues collected in sealed, grounded, flame-proof polyethylene-lined stainless steel hazardous waste drums categorized for hazardous solvent disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate (PGMEA / 1-Methoxy-2-propanol acetate)** | `108-65-6` | Electronic Grade / VLSI Grade (Cleanroom >= 99.8%) | `70-85% (in Shipley 1813 casting solvent matrix)` |
| **Mixed Diazo Photoactive Compound (Diazo-naphthoquinone / DNQ sulfonate ester)** | `68510-93-0` | Semiconductor Grade | `10-20% (solid active component)` |
| **Cresol Novolak Resin** | `117520-84-0` | Semiconductor Grade | `10-20% (polymer matrix)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly spun Shipley 1813 liquid film over HMDS-primed thermal oxide (SiO2), edge bead trimmed, wet solvent-bearing (approx. 20-25 wt% residual PGMEA).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Solidified, thermally densified, uniform 1.33 µm S1813 photoresist film with residual solvent <= 4 wt%, stress-relaxed, cooled to 22°C cleanroom equilibrium, ready for reticle alignment and exposure.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive moisture absorption from cleanroom ambient humidity (relative humidity > 45%) causes photoactive compound (DNQ) premature chemical degradation, acid generator drift, and optical thickness swelling, leading to severe focus shift and exposure dose drift on the i-line lithography stepper.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Photoresist softbake at 115°C fully completed with solvent outgassing stabilized, followed by spectroscopic reflectometry thickness verification confirming nominal 1.33 µm film thickness with <1.5% non-uniformity across the entire wafer surface.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `S1813_Softbake_115C_Recipe_RunLog.csv`
- [ ] `Spectroscopic_Reflectometry_9Point_ThicknessMap.pdf`
- [ ] `Cauchy_Dispersion_Fit_RawSpectra_GoF.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean dried photoresist thickness across wafer 9-point grid** | `1330 nm` | ±25 nm | Spectroscopic reflectometry Cauchy optical model fitting (400-800 nm spectrum) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Radial film thickness non-uniformity (3-sigma / mean)** | `1.0%` | <= 1.5% | Statistical evaluation of 9-point polar/cartesian automated wafer map |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Optical model fitting Goodness-of-Fit (GoF)** | `0.995` | >= 0.985 | Filmetrics / Woollam spectrometer regression analysis across 400-800 nm |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit sign-off requires: Hotplate thermal profile confirmed at 115°C ± 0.5°C; 9-point reflectometer mean thickness between 1305 nm and 1355 nm with <= 1.5% 3-sigma non-uniformity; zero optical interference fit anomalies (GoF >= 0.985); and completion of chill plate transfer within 30 seconds.

# Standard Operating Procedure: I-line Stepper Exposure, Post-Exposure Bake and Development Metrology

**Project:** DRAM Foundation VN — 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip  
**Module:** Photolithography & Metrology (Gen 2: µm scale)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Workflow Diagram

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   HMDS Vapor Prime    │
│         120C          │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Spin-Coat Shipley   │
│     1813 4000 RPM     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Soft Bake 115C 60s   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    I-line Stepper     │
│    Exposure 365nm     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  MF-319 Development   │
│    45-60s DI Rinse    │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Metrology & Overlay  │
│      Inspection       │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Substrate Dehydration & HMDS Vapor Prime:**
   - Transfer wafer into the primer chamber.
   - Perform Hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS) vapor prime at **120°C** to promote adhesion on the oxide layer prior to resist dispensing.
2. **Resist Spin Coating:**
   - Dispense Shipley 1813 positive photoresist onto the center of the wafer.
   - Accelerate and spin-coat at **4000 RPM** to establish a nominal resist thickness of **~1.3 µm**.
3. **Soft Bake (Pre-Exposure Bake):**
   - Place wafer onto a calibrated flat aluminum hot plate.
   - Bake at **115°C for 60 seconds** to drive off excess casting solvents and stabilize the film.
4. **I-line Stepper Alignment & Exposure:**
   - Load wafer onto the projection aligner / stepper stage equipped with a 10x Plan Achromat objective (NA 0.25).
   - Perform fiducial mark alignment to align the layer with a tolerance of **≤ ±5 µm** (Gen 2 specification).
   - Expose the pattern using a high-power **365nm i-line UV LED source** or mercury vapor lamp.
5. **Development & Deionized Rinse:**
   - Immerse and gently agitate wafer in **Microposit MF-319 developer** for **45 to 60 seconds**.
   - Immediately quench reaction by transferring into a cascade deionized (DI) water rinse tank for a thorough wash.
   - Blow dry with filtered dry $N_2$.
6. **Critical Dimension (CD) & Alignment Metrology:**
   - Inspect wafer under calibrated optical metrology for feature resolution and residual resist in cleared areas.
   - Measure overlay offsets relative to prior alignment targets.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │■■                                │
Gen 2 Alignment (um)┤■■                                │
                    │██████████████████                │
    Dev Time Max (s)┤██████████████████                │
  Soft Bake Time (s)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                │
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                │
  Soft Bake Temp (C)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
                    │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Spin Speed (RPM/100)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░                      │
                    │░░░░░░░░░░░░                      │
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                    0.0    28.8     57.5    86.2  115.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Resist Film Thickness** | **1.3** | $\mu\text{m}$ (nominal) | Optical reflectometry / profilometry post 4000 RPM coat |
| **Soft Bake Temperature** | **115** | $^{\circ}\text{C}$ ($\pm 1^{\circ}\text{C}$) | Thermocouple / Pyrometer surface contact sensor |
| **Soft Bake Duration** | **60** | $\text{seconds}$ | Automated hot plate timer |
| **Exposure Wavelength** | **365** | $\text{nm}$ (i-line) | Spectroradiometer / i-line sensor |
| **Development Immersion Time**| **45 – 60** | $\text{seconds}$ | Wet bench chemical immersion timer |
| **Layer Alignment Tolerance** | **$\le \pm 5$** | $\mu\text{m}$ | Optical overlay metrology Vernier / split-field microscope |

---

### Literature Citations
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018):** 10x Plan Achromat (NA 0.25) projection optics; Shipley 1813 spin-coated at 4000 RPM (~1.3 µm); soft bake at 115°C for 60 seconds; 365nm i-line source; Microposit MF-319 developer for 45–60 s and DI water rinse; Gen 2 alignment target of $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE):** HMDS vapor prime adhesion at 120°C prior to resist coating.

---

> [!NOTE]
> Micro-knowledge for this procedure has been persisted to [sop_iline_exposure_dev_metrology.md](docs/knowledge/sop_iline_exposure_dev_metrology.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Linear translation stage integration using MGN12H guide rails and NEMA 17 steppers presents Abbe offset risks when measuring critical dimension (CD) across Gen 1 macro-fields; stage tilt and pitch over a 100mm travel must be compensated or strictly bounded to avoid optical defocus and field-curvature errors during development metrology inspection.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Post-Exposure Bake (PEB) thermal budget is exceptionally sensitive for standard diazonaphthoquinone (DNQ)-novolac resists like Shipley 1813; hotplate non-uniformity exceeding ±1.0°C directly perturbs standing wave smoothing and PAC dissolution kinetics in MF-319, inducing line-edge roughness (LER) and CD bias prior to buffered oxide etch.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-sourcing Microposit MF-319 (TMAH-based) developer presents regional logistics vulnerabilities in Vietnam; qualifying commercial Grade Electronic/VLSI 0.26N TMAH or standard potassium/sodium hydroxide based alternatives requires cross-checking surfactant additives and etch selectivity preservation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Strict buy-off milestones for Gen 1 metrology must enforce quantitative throughput: CD optical metrology and overlay registration verification across 5 points per wafer must complete within the 30-minute queue-time window before post-development resist degradation or airborne contamination occurs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Over-development or thermal runaway during PEB resulting in complete footing or resist lifting at the SiO2 interface due to inadequate prior HMDS silylation.
1. Abbe and lead-screw backlash error exceeding ±10 microns during optical stage registration, causing false-positive CD drift and misclassification of optical exposure dose.
1. Developer residue and salt precipitation from incomplete DI water rinse quenching, blocking subsequent BOE 6:1 wet etch penetration.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-3-01` | **Post-Development Critical Dimension (CD) and Profile Line Width Verification** | Calibrated Optical Metallurgical Microscope (100x / 0.90 NA Objective) with Sub-Micron Digital Camera & Reticle Stage Micrometer (1.0 um/pixel) | 1. Mount coupon on the precision linear stage under optical microscope. 2. Focus on the central 5-point test array containing 50 um and 10 um nominal test lines. 3. Acquire 5 high-resolution micrographs at center, top, bottom, left, and right field points. 4. Run automated threshold edge-detection to measure line width across 50 lines per site. | `Measured mean line width for 50 um targets must be within 50.0 ± 5.0 um across all 5 sites; resist profile edges must show zero observable scumming, residual unexposed bridging, or micro-tearing.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-1-3-02` | **Post-Exposure Bake (PEB) Thermal Uniformity and Hotplate Temperature Accuracy** | Multi-channel Surface Contact K-type Thermocouple Datalogger calibrated against NIST standard with ±0.1°C resolution | 1. Affix 5 calibrated surface thermocouples to a sacrificial 4-inch silicon wafer (center, north, south, east, west at 10mm from edge). 2. Set hotplate setpoint to 115.0°C and allow 30 minutes for thermal equilibrium. 3. Place instrumented wafer on hotplate vacuum chuck. 4. Log temperature data continuously for 300 seconds at 1 Hz. | `Steady-state temperature across all 5 monitoring channels must stabilize at 115.0 ± 1.0°C; maximum delta-T across the entire substrate plane must not exceed 1.5°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant nitrile outer gloves over inner disposable nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles and full-face polycarbonate shield, Flame-retardant, anti-static cleanroom lab coat or chemical apron, Closed-toe chemical-resistant footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with TMAH: Immediately flush with copious volumes of emergency shower water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated clothing; TMAH acts as a potent systemic neurotoxin and dermal paralytic. Eye contact: Irrigate eyes with isotonic saline or eyewash station water for 20 minutes with forced eyelid retraction; seek immediate emergency medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation must be conducted within a dedicated chemical wet bench or fume hood maintaining minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) with scrubbed exhaust to capture volatile organic solvents and alkaline vapors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate spent TMAH aqueous developer waste into dedicated polyethene alkaline waste carboys. Neutralize with dilute hydrochloric or citric acid to pH 6.0-9.0 in a dedicated effluent neutralization tank prior to industrial waste disposal; do NOT mix with organic solvent or acid-etch waste streams.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tetramethylammonium hydroxide (MF-319 Developer)** | `75-59-2` | VLSI / Electronic Grade | `2.4% (0.26N aqueous)` |
| **Shipley Microposit 1813 Photoresist (PGMEA solvent base)** | `108-65-6` | Semiconductor Grade | `70-85% PGMEA, 10-20% Novolac Resin, 1-10% Diazonaphthoquinone` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Resist Rinse & Surface Prep)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (MOS) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: HMDS vapor-primed, spin-coated Shipley 1813 (1.3 um nominal) on 100nm thermal oxide, soft-baked at 115°C for 60s, ambient cooled to 22°C.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully developed, DI-rinsed, N2 blow-dried patterned resist stencil on SiO2, free of developer residue, verified clean under optical metrology, ready for pre-BOE hard bake or wet oxide etching.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption from cleanroom ambient degrades developer profile, causing lateral resist adhesion failure, pinholing, and severe undercutting during the subsequent BOE 6:1 dip-etch.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Validation and dimensional buy-off for the I-line stepper exposure, post-exposure bake, and developer metrology package for Gen 1 macro-features, ensuring repeatable resist feature reproduction and surface integrity prior to wet oxide patterning.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `METROLOGY_CD_PROFILE_REPORT_GEN1.csv`
- [ ] `PEB_HOTPLATE_THERMAL_MAPPING_RUN01.pdf`
- [ ] `OPTICAL_INSPECTION_DEVELOPED_RESIST_5PTS.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-development critical dimension for 50um test geometry across 5 wafer sites** | `50.0 um` | ±5.0 um | Calibrated 100x optical metallurgical microscope edge-detection profile extraction |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-Exposure Bake hotplate surface temperature uniformity across 100mm substrate zone** | `115.0°C` | ±1.0°C | 5-point surface thermocouple array datalogging over 300s dwell time |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Residual unexposed photoresist film thickness in fully developed clear-field windows** | `0.0 nm` | +5.0 nm | Spectroscopic reflectometry / optical profilometer step-height measurement |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit requires all 5 die inspection fields to demonstrate clear trench opening with zero scumming, CD within 50.0 ± 5.0 um, thermal uniformity verified at 115.0 ± 1.0°C, and all metrology artifacts digitally signed and archived in the wafer run database.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse

**Module**: Wet Chemistry / Oxide Patterning  
**Technology Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 1)  
**Classification**: Safety Critical / Hydrofluoric Acid Process  

---

### 1. Process Workflow

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 1: Bath Setup & Surfactant    │
│  BOE 6:1 (40% NH4F : 49% HF) + 0.1%  │
│  Triton X-100 / Fluorad @ 25°C       │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 2: Immersion Dip-Etch         │
│  Thermally grown SiO2: 80-100 nm/min │
│  CVD / TEOS SiO2: 150-220 nm/min     │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 3: Cascade Dump Rinse         │
│  5 Cycles UPW (18.2 MOhm-cm)         │
│  Rinse bath cutoff > 16 MOhm-cm      │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                   │
                   ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Stage 4: Endpoint & Metrology       │
│  Hydrophobic dewetting check         │
│  Fluoride neutralization & dry       │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Required Chemical Formulations & Operating Parameters

* **BOE 6:1 Primary Etchant**:
  * **Composition**: $6\text{ parts } 40\% \text{ NH}_4\text{F} : 1\text{ part } 49\% \text{ HF}$.
  * **pH Target**: $\sim 4.5$ (buffered by $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to maintain constant fluoride ion activity).
  * **Operating Bath Temperature**: $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.
* **Surfactant / Wetting Spike**:
  * **Additive**: $0.1\% \text{ v/v}$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad.
  * **Function**: Lowers surface tension to suppress micro-bubble entrapment within high-aspect-ratio oxide contact windows and micro-trenches.
* **Pre-requisite Surface Preparation**:
  * Photoresist pattern primed via HMDS (Hexamethyldisilazane) vapor prime at $120^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain resist adhesion and prevent lateral peeling.
* **Cascade Rinse Fluid**:
  * Ultra-Pure Water (UPW), incoming resistivity $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **Safety Protocol & PPE Verification**:
   * Don full acid gear: chemical apron, sleeve guards, face shield, and heavy neoprene/nitrile over-gloves.
   * Verify that **Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%)** is unexpired and positioned immediately adjacent to the wet bench.
2. **Etch Bath Conditioning**:
   * In a dedicated fluoropolymer (PTFE/PFA) tank, verify BOE 6:1 solution is stabilized at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
   * Verify $0.1\%$ wetting agent (Triton X-100 or Fluorad) is fully dispersed without surface foam.
3. **Immersion Dip-Etch**:
   * Load HMDS-primed and patterned wafer cassette into the PTFE dipper arm.
   * Submerge into BOE 6:1 bath with gentle vertical reciprocal agitation.
   * **Etch Time Calculation**:
     * For **Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$**: Etch rate is $80\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($800\text{ to } 1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
     * For **CVD / TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$**: Etch rate is $150\text{ to } 220\text{ nm/min}$.
     * For **Native oxide clearing**: Etch duration is $10\text{ to } 15\text{ seconds}$.
4. **Cascade Dump Rinse Transfer**:
   * Quickly transfer cassette into the Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) tank within $<3\text{ seconds}$ to avoid air-drying or uncontrolled bevel etching.
   * Execute **5 complete dump-and-fill cycles** with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW.
   * Continue cascade overflow until effluent bath resistivity reads $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
5. **Drying & Hydrophobic Surface Check**:
   * Spin rinse dry (SRD) or pull wafer slowly for observation: bare silicon contact surfaces must display complete hydrophobic water-sheeting/dewetting.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Method / Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$) | $80 - 100\text{ nm/min}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Film Thickness Metrology |
| **CVD / TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $185\text{ nm/min}$ | $150 - 220\text{ nm/min}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Reflectometry |
| **Cascade Rinse Bath Resistivity** | $> 16.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | $\ge 16.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-situ Inline UPW Resistivity Sensor (Cell Constant $k=0.01$) |
| **Etch Selectivity ($\text{SiO}_2$ : Si)** | $> 100 : 1$ | Minimum $100:1$ | Cross-sectional Profilometry / Step Height Analysis |

---

### 5. Context Citations

* **[Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)]**:
  * 6:1 formulation ratio ($6\text{ parts } 40\% \text{ NH}_4\text{F} : 1\text{ part } 49\% \text{ HF}$).
  * Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate at $25^\circ\text{C}$ ($\sim 100\text{ nm/min}$ / $1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  * Addition of $0.1\%$ Triton X-100 / Fluorad wetting agent for trench bubble elimination.
  * HMDS vapor prime pre-treatment at $120^\circ\text{C}$.
  * Mandatory Calcium Gluconate safety protocol for HF exposure.
* **[Source: Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates]**:
  * Etch rates at $25^\circ\text{C}$: Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ ($80 - 100\text{ nm/min}$), CVD/TEOS $\text{SiO}_2$ ($150 - 220\text{ nm/min}$), and Native oxide ($10 - 15\text{ s}$).
  * Selectivity ratios: $\text{SiO}_2:\text{Si} > 100:1$; $\text{SiO}_2:\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4 > 20:1$.
  * Buffering chemistry maintaining $\text{pH} \sim 4.5$ and constant fluoride ion activity.
* **[Source: RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering]**:
  * Cascade dump rinse protocol: 5 dump cycles using $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW.
  * Effluent resistivity endpoint threshold ($> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
  * Hydrophobic surface dewetting endpoint indicator for exposed silicon oxide strip completion.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Bath temperature drift beyond ±0.5°C introduces unacceptable etch rate variation across the 180nm oxide hardmask, as BOE 6:1 Arrhenius kinetics shift etch rate by ~3 nm/min per °C. Furthermore, surfactant degradation and localized depletion in stagnant boundary layers will skew cross-wafer 3-sigma oxide thickness uniformity beyond ±2.5%. Constant recirculation, PTFE inline filtering (0.1 µm), and automated cascade dump rinse (QDR) trigger interfaces must be synchronized with wafer immersion timing.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm ground rules, capillary pinning of the etchant meniscus in micro-trenches causes incomplete oxide clear (micromasking) unless surface tension is lowered below 30 mN/m using an ultra-clean fluorosurfactant or non-ionic surfactant (e.g., 0.1% Triton X-100 or perfluoroalkyl sulfonate). In addition, excessive HMDS prime degradation or lack of post-exposure bake (PEB) hard-bake crosslinking can result in severe resist lift-off, lateral undercut, or mouse-bite defects due to hydrofluoric acid tunneling along the resist/SiO2 interface.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Pre-mixed semiconductor electronic grade (VLSI / SLSI Grade) BOE 6:1 with pre-formulated, low-foaming surfactant has high lead times and shelf-life constraints due to ammonium fluoride precipitation below 16°C and surfactant phase separation. On-site spiking of surfactant into pristine BOE requires validated ultra-pure surfactant stock to avoid introducing alkali metal cations (Na+, K+ < 1 ppb) into front-end DRAM gate-adjacent dielectric domains.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Cycle time from hard-bake completion through BOE immersion and quick-dump cascade rinsing directly governs front-end DRAM line yields. Unscheduled delays during cascade rinsing or nitrogen spin-dry lead to unmonitored lateral oxide erosion and resist lifting. Process recipes, bath life counters (in etched SiO2 area / cm²), and calcium gluconate safety readiness must be verified prior to lot release.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial HF tunneling causing catastrophic photoresist delamination, extreme isotropic undercut, and dimensional collapse of 180nm oxide openings.
1. Bubble entrapment and incomplete meniscus wetting within high-aspect features leading to partial oxide clearing and non-functional open contacts.
1. Fluoride salt crystallization (NH4F precipitation) or particulate re-deposition during insufficient cascade rinse overflow, inducing pinholes and dielectric breakdown.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-01` | **BOE 6:1 Thermal Oxide Etch Rate and Uniformity Validation** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (49-point wafer mapping, 3mm edge exclusion) and Constant Temperature Recirculating Quartz Bath with Inline Temperature Sensor. | 1. Immerse pilot wafer into surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 bath for precisely 30.0 seconds using automated PTFE dip-arm. 2. Rapidly transfer within <3 seconds to quick-dump rinse (QDR) tank and execute 5 rapid dump/fill cycles with 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW. 3. Complete cascade overflow rinse until tank resistivity reaches >=16.0 MOhm-cm. 4. Spin-rinse dry wafer under filtered N2 at 2200 RPM for 120 seconds. 5. Measure post-etch remaining oxide thickness across 49 points on spectroscopic ellipsometer. | `Thermal SiO2 etch rate must be between 95.0 nm/min and 105.0 nm/min (nominal 50.0 ± 2.5 nm removed in 30 seconds), with within-wafer non-uniformity (1-sigma / mean) <= 2.0% across 49 sites.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-02` | **Surfactant Wetting Meniscus and Resist Undercut SEM Inspection** | Top-down / Cross-Sectional Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscope (CD-SEM) and Optical Surface Defect Scanner. | 1. Perform 100% nominal clear dip-etch in surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 plus 10% controlled over-etch. 2. Cascade rinse in UPW until effluent resistivity reaches 17.5 MOhm-cm, followed by dry N2 bakeout. 3. Examine 10 cross-wafer dense trench sites under CD-SEM for residual oxide or footing. 4. Measure post-etch bottom CD and lateral resist undercut profile at 5 distinct array locations. | `Zero visible micromasking/un-etched oxide residue in trenches (10/10 sites clear); lateral undercut under photoresist <= 15.0 nm per side; zero evidence of resist edge curling, peeling, or pinhole peeling.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavyweight Neoprene / Butyl rubber chemical gauntlets (tested for HF permeation), Full-face transparent polycarbonate chemical splash shield over ANSI Z87.1 splash goggles, Acid-resistant DuPont Tychem / PVC chemical apron with full arm sleeves, Safety shoes with chemical-resistant neoprene over-boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Hydrofluoric acid exposure poses extreme systemic toxicity and deep bone-decalcification hazards. Immediate action required: In case of dermal contact, strip all contaminated clothing immediately under emergency safety shower; continuously flush skin with copious cold water for exactly 2 minutes; immediately massage unexpired 2.5% Calcium Gluconate topical gel into the affected area with gloved hands continuously until medical personnel arrive. Maintain dedicated calcium gluconate emergency stations adjacent to the wet bench. For eye contact, flush with sterile eyewash solution for 15 minutes and administer 1% calcium gluconate eye drops under medical direction. Transport victim immediately to hospital with HF safety declaration sheet.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous wet bench lip exhaust with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) connected directly to dedicated fluorinated acid exhaust scrubber system with continuous differential pressure interlock. If exhaust drop falls below 80 FPM, bench bath immersion actuators must fail-safe lift wafers out of chemicals and abort cycle.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent BOE and fluorinated rinse effluent must be segregated from general acid waste and plumbed directly to a specialized Fluoride Waste Neutralization (FWN) system. Treat effluent with calcium hydroxide (slaked lime, Ca(OH)2) or calcium chloride (CaCl2) to precipitate insoluble calcium fluoride (CaF2) cake; adjust final liquid supernatant pH to 6.5-8.5 prior to regulated discharge with fluoride concentration strictly monitored <= 10 ppm.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF)** | `7664-39-3` | VLSI / SEMI Tier 3 | `49% wt in aqueous solution (1 part in 6:1 BOE mix)` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (NH4F)** | `12125-01-8` | VLSI / SEMI Tier 3 | `40% wt in aqueous solution (6 parts in 6:1 BOE mix)` |
| **Triton X-100 (Surfactant / Octylphenol ethoxylate)** | `9002-93-1` | Electronic / High Purity (<5 ppb trace metals) | `0.1% wt spike in BOE solution` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic lithography resist surface with HMDS-primed thermal SiO2 bottom, completely dry, zero moisture condensation, post-hard-bake completed within <60 minutes.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Pristine etched silicon/oxide step surface; bare silicon regions fully hydrophobic (hydrogen-terminated, contact angle >75°), thoroughly dried without watermark rings or residual fluoride salts.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time prior to rinse/next step leads to atmospheric water-vapor native oxide regrowth on exposed silicon trenches, air particulate adhesion, and unchecked vapor-phase HF micro-etching along resist boundaries creating uncontrolled critical dimension swelling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful execution of surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 dip-etch recipe on 180nm DRAM oxide patterning layer, achieving controlled oxide clearance down to substrate with minimal lateral undercut, sub-2% etch uniformity, zero bubble-induced micromasking, and complete fluoride removal via cascade dump rinsing.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `BOE_6-1_EtchRate_Uniformity_Map.csv`
- [ ] `CrossSectional_Trench_CD_Undercut_SEM.tiff`
- [ ] `WetBench_CascadeRinse_Resistivity_Log.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Thermal SiO2 vertical etch rate in surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 at 25.0°C** | `100.0 nm/min` | ±5.0 nm/min | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry across 49 measurement points pre- and post-etch |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Lateral photoresist undercut per trench sidewall post 10% over-etch** | `12.0 nm` | <= 15.0 nm maximum | In-line CD-SEM cross-sectional / tilted high-resolution metrology |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Final stage cascade overflow dump rinse tank deionized water resistivity** | `18.0 MOhm-cm` | >= 16.5 MOhm-cm minimum threshold | Inline calibrated ultrapure water resistivity conductivity cell sensor |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher sign-off requires: (1) Processed wafer 49-point oxide etch rate confirms within 95-105 nm/min with <=2% non-uniformity; (2) CD-SEM confirms 100% open trenches with no micromasking residue and lateral undercut <=15 nm; (3) Cascade dump rinse logs confirm minimum effluent resistivity >=16.5 MOhm-cm before wafer spin-dry; (4) EHS checklist completed verifying zero HF leaks and unexpired calcium gluconate at the wet bench.
