# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Details
- **Title:** BOE 6:1 Stoichiometric Compounding & 0.1% Wetting Surfactant Dosing
- **Hierarchy:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > [Architecture & Integration] > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning [Chemical Processing] > HMDS Vapor Prime, Resist Patterning & Wet Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution [Wet Chemistry] > Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse [Wet Chemistry] > Surfactant-Spiked BOE 6:1 Bath Formulation, Bath Wetting & Thermal Stabilization [Wet Chemistry] > BOE 6:1 Chemical Compounding, Surfactant Wetting Dosing & Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration [Wet Chemistry] > BOE 6:1 Stoichiometric Compounding & 0.1% Wetting Surfactant Dosing [Wet Chemistry]
- **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type:** Buy / Formulate

---

## 1. Safety & PPE Pre-Requisites
> [!CAUTION]
> **Hydrofluoric Acid Hazard**: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) penetrates skin and deeply binds systemic calcium. An unexpired tube of **calcium gluconate gel** must be present within arm's reach at the wet bench before opening chemical containers. Operators must wear full acid-gear: fluoropolymer apron, heavy neoprene/Viton over-gloves, and a face shield.

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|             BOE 6:1 COMPOUNDING & SURFACTANT DOSING FLOW                     |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  [Step 1: Prep & Tare]           Clean fluoropolymer PVDF/PTFE vessel
         │
         ▼
  [Step 2: NH4F Addition]         Dispense 6 volumetric parts 40% NH4F
         │
         ▼
  [Step 3: HF Addition]           Dispense 1 volumetric part 49% HF into NH4F
         │
         ▼
  [Step 4: Surfactant Dosing]     Pipette 0.1% v/v Triton X-100 or Fluorad
         │
         ▼
  [Step 5: Homogenization]        PTFE impeller stir; equilibrate to 25°C
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Step 1: Labware Preparation and Safety Check
1. Ensure the dedicated laminar flow wet bench exhaust velocity is nominal.
2. Verify calcium gluconate gel availability and expiry.
3. Clean and inspect a dedicated acid-compatible fluoropolymer (PTFE/PVDF or PFA) mixing container; verify zero particulate contamination.

### Step 2: Volumetric Dispensing of Buffer (40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$)
1. Measure exactly **6 volumetric parts** of semiconductor-grade **40% Ammonium Fluoride ($\text{NH}_4\text{F}$)** solution (e.g., 600 mL).
2. Pour the measured $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ into the PTFE compounding vessel.

### Step 3: Stoichiometric Hydrofluoric Acid (49% HF) Addition
1. Measure exactly **1 volumetric part** of semiconductor-grade **49% Hydrofluoric Acid ($\text{HF}$)** solution (e.g., 100 mL).
2. Slowly decant the $49\%\ \text{HF}$ into the $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ solution under laminar exhaust to prevent local heating and splattering. Maintain the 6:1 volumetric ratio to buffer against HF depletion and lock bath pH.

### Step 4: Surfactant Dosing (0.1% Wetting Agent)
1. Using an acid-resistant micropipette, draw **0.1% by volume** of wetting surfactant (**Triton X-100** or **Fluorad**) (e.g., 0.70 mL for a 700 mL total compounding batch).
2. Dispense the wetting agent directly into the center of the liquid column to eliminate micro-trench bubble entrapment and lower surface tension.

### Step 5: Homogenization and Thermal Stabilization
1. Stir the solution using a high-purity PTFE magnetic stir bar or PTFE paddle for 3–5 minutes until the surfactant is completely dissolved without foaming.
2. Cover the bath with a fluoropolymer vapor-containment lid and allow the temperature to stabilize at **25°C** prior to wafer qualification.

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Tolerance / Range | Verification Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stoichiometric Volume Ratio** | **6:1** ($\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : $\text{HF}$) | $\pm 0.5\%$ by volume | Calibrated PFA graduated cylinder / mass balance |
| **Surfactant Concentration** | **0.1%** | $\pm 0.01\%$ v/v | Precision acid micropipette |
| **Bath Calibration Temperature** | **25°C** | $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ | Immersion fluoropolymer-sheathed PT100 RTD |
| **SiO₂ Etch Rate Baseline** | **100 nm/min** (1000 Å/min) | $\pm 5\%$ at 25°C | Pre/post spectroscopic ellipsometry on thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ test wafer |

---

## 4. Context References & Source Citations
- **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
  - Stoichiometry: *6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$*.
  - Etch rate: *Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at 25°C is approximately 100 nm/minute (1000 Å/min)*.
  - Wetting agent: *0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad added to eliminate bubble entrapment in micro-trenches*.
  - Safety protocol: *Hydrofluoric acid penetrates skin and binds calcium; calcium gluconate gel must be present at all times*.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Station exhaust and DI water loop (18.2 MOhm-cm, particle filter 0.1 um) must interlock prior to wafer boat immersion. Rinse cascade must terminate downstream acid carries before SC-2.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: BOE 6:1 (NH4F:HF) etch rate must be calibrated at 70-80 nm/min at 25°C. SC-1 (5:1:1 H2O:NH4OH:H2O2) must be maintained at 75°C +/- 2°C to eliminate light organics without pitting Si.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Electronic-grade semiconductor reagents (VLSI/MOS grade) must be procured from certified chemical distributors; technical-grade chemicals will induce metallic surface poisoning (Fe, Cu, Ni > 1e10 atoms/cm2).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 24-32 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Chemical cross-contamination or incomplete dump rinse leaves watermark defects and micro-masking during subsequent etch).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Watermark defect formation during static pull-out from hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic transition.
1. Exhaust face-velocity drop below 0.5 m/s causing acid vapor condensation on cleanroom tooling.
1. Over-etch in BOE undercut exceeding 50 nm, destroying contact via dimensional margins.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-1-2-2-01` | **Post-Clean Particle & Metallic Trace Contamination Assay** | Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner (KLA-Tencor / Surfscan) & TXRF Spectrometer | 1. Load unpatterned witness silicon wafer into darkfield laser scatterometer. 2. Scan complete surface for light point defects (LPD) at size bin >= 180 nm. 3. Perform Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) for trace Fe, Cu, Ni surface concentrations. | `LPD count (>= 180 nm) < 10 defects/wafer (Pass); Transition metals (Fe, Ni, Cu) < 5e10 atoms/cm2 (Pass).` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-1-2-2-02` | **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) Step Height & Lateral Undercut Profilometry** | Stylus Profilometer (Veeco Dektak XT) / Atomic Force Microscope (AFM) | 1. Zero stylus force baseline at 3 mg on planar SiO2 field. 2. Scan 200 um profile across etched contact window step at 20 um/s scan speed. 3. Record step height h_step and lateral undercut under resist margin. | `Etch depth matches target +/- 5% (Pass); lateral undercut <= 35 nm (Pass); surface roughness Ra < 0.5 nm (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty butyl/neoprene gloves (0.7 mm thickness, tested for HF permeation), Full-face polycarbonate splash shield over ANSI Z87.1 safety goggles, Acid-resistant chemical apron with sleeves (PVC/Neoprene), Acid gas vapor cartridge respirator (NIOSH approved for HF/HCl)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: MANDATORY ON-SITE ANTIDOTE: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%). In case of HF skin contact: Flush immediately under emergency drench shower for 2-3 minutes, then vigorously massage Calcium Gluconate Gel into affected skin continuously until emergency medical response arrives. Never apply standard burn creams.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated polypropylene wet bench with vertical laminar exhaust face velocity >= 0.55 m/s. Interlocked with wet acid scrubber.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate fluoride effluent. Neutralize with Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2). Verify pH 7.0-8.5 before drain discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF)** | `7664-39-3` | VLSI/MOS Electronic Grade (< 1 ppb metals) | `49% conc. or 1:50 DHF` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (NH4F)** | `12125-01-8` | Electronic Grade | `40% aq (for BOE 6:1 buffer)` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)** | `7722-84-1` | Electronic Grade (unstabilized) | `30% aq (for SC-1 & SC-2)` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)** | `7647-01-0` | Electronic Grade | `37% aq (for SC-2 clean)` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (NH4OH)** | `1336-21-6` | Electronic Grade | `29% aq (for SC-1 clean)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic with native chemical oxide (Tox ~1.0 nm) and organic particulates.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic H-terminated bare silicon (water contact angle > 75°), zero watermarks, Tox < 0.2 nm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native SiO2 spontaneously regrows in ambient air at ~0.1 nm/hr, degrading interface state density Dit and causing uncontrolled threshold voltage shift in downstream gate oxidation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of BOE 6:1 Stoichiometric Compounding & 0.1% Wetting Surfactant Dosing: Chemical cleaning and surface preparation verified with zero watermark defects, bare hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated silicon, and calibrated oxide etch rate.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Surface_particle_laser_scan_Surfscan.pdf`
- [ ] `Sessile_drop_contact_angle_measurement.png`
- [ ] `DHF_BOE_calibrated_etch_rate_sheet.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-DHF bare silicon water contact angle** | `>= 75.0 deg` | +/- 5.0 deg | Automated Sessile Drop Goniometer (DI water droplet) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Surface particulate defect density (> 0.1 um)** | `< 15 particles/wafer` | Max acceptable particle count on 100mm wafer | Darkfield Laser Surface Inspection (Surfscan) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Surface metallic impurity concentration (Fe, Ni, Cu)** | `< 1.0e10 atoms/cm²` | Max allowable contamination | Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer surface exhibits 100% uniform dewetting / hydrophobicity with zero visible drying marks under bright light; residual native oxide Tox < 0.2 nm confirmed by spectroscopic ellipsometry.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-WET-MET-004`
**Title:** Recirculating Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration & Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch-Rate Metrology  
**Node Path:** `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Architecture & Integration > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning > HMDS Vapor Prime, Resist Patterning & Wet Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution > Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse > Surfactant-Spiked BOE 6:1 Bath Formulation, Bath Wetting & Thermal Stabilization > BOE 6:1 Chemical Compounding, Surfactant Wetting Dosing & Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration > Recirculating Constant-Temperature Bath Calibration & Thermal SiO2 Etch-Rate Metrology`  
**Generation:** Gen 2 ($\mu\text{m}$) | **Action Type:** Make  
**Safety Protocol:** HF Emergency Protocol Active (Ensure Calcium Gluconate Gel is accessible and unexpired).

---

### 1. Process Overview & Calibration Setup

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Recirculation & Thermal Equilibration (25.0°C)          |
|    - Pump Rate: Recirculating PVDF/PTFE Bath                 |
|    - Temperature Target: 25.0°C (Stable within ±0.5°C)      |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Pre-Etch Ellipsometry Baseline                           |
|    - Measure initial thermal SiO2 film thickness (T1)       |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Timed Calibration Dip-Etch                               |
|    - 6:1 BOE (6 parts 40% NH4F : 1 part 49% HF)             |
|    - Surfactant: 0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad               |
|    - Duration: Exactly 60.0 seconds immersion               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. Quick Dump Rinse (QDR), Spin Dry & Post-Etch Metrology   |
|    - Measure remaining thermal SiO2 thickness (T2)          |
|    - Calculate Etch Rate: (T1 - T2) / 1.0 min               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **PPE & Workstation Verification:**
   - Don full acid PPE: chemical apron, heavy neoprene gloves, face shield, and chemical vapor respirator.
   - Verify the immediate presence of unexpired **Calcium Gluconate Gel** at the chemical wet bench.

2. **Constant-Temperature Recirculation Stabilization:**
   - Fill the recirculating chemical-duty bath with compounded **BOE 6:1** formulation (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$) spiked with **0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad** wetting agent.
   - Engage the recirculation loop to purge trapped micro-bubbles and achieve homogeneous mixture.
   - Set the bath temperature controller to **25.0°C**. Allow bath to recirculate until thermal equilibrium is attained and stabilizes within target tolerances.

3. **Pre-Etch Thickness Metrology:**
   - Load a clean monitor test wafer with a known thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ layer into the spectroscopic ellipsometer/reflectometer.
   - Map a 5-point thickness profile across the wafer surface and record average baseline thickness $T_1$ in nm (or Å).

4. **Calibration Immersion Etch:**
   - Transfer the monitor wafer using a PTFE carrier boat into the 25.0°C recirculating BOE 6:1 bath.
   - Immerse the wafer and agitate gently for exactly **60.0 seconds** (1.00 minute) under constant recirculation.

5. **Cascade Rinse & Decontamination:**
   - Immediately withdraw the wafer carrier and transfer directly into the Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) tank filled with deionized (DI) water to halt the etching reaction.
   - Run three consecutive dump cycles, followed by cascade overflow rinsing until resistivity reaches $> 18\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
   - Transfer to the spin rinse dryer (SRD) and cycle with warm filtered $\text{N}_2$.

6. **Post-Etch Metrology & Rate Computation:**
   - Measure the remaining oxide thickness $T_2$ across the same 5 measurement locations.
   - Calculate the etch rate:
     $$\text{Etch Rate} = \frac{T_1 - T_2}{1.0\ \text{min}}\ (\text{nm/min})$$
   - Confirm calculated rate aligns with baseline qualification values before releasing the bath to production wafer lots.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Recirculating Bath Temperature** | 25.0 | $\pm 0.5$ | °C | Calibrated In-situ Thermocouple / RTD Probe |
| **Thermally Grown $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | 100.0 | $\pm 5.0$ (approx. 1000 Å/min) | nm/min | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Reflectometry |
| **Wetting Agent Dosing** | 0.1 | Nominal | % vol/vol | Volumetric Dispense Sensor / Recipe Log |
| **$\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ Hard Mask Selectivity Loss Rate** | $< 0.5$ | Maximum allowable | nm/min | Comparative Ellipsometry Calibration |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Sources Cited

1. **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**
   - *Composition & Chemistry:* BOE 6:1 formulated with 6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ and 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$.
   - *Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate:* Approximately $100\ \text{nm/min}$ ($1000\ \text{\AA/min}$) at 25°C.
   - *Additives & Adhesion:* Inclusion of $0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad surfactant prevents bubble entrapment in micro-trenches; HMDS vapor prime executed at 120°C prior to resist coating.
   - *Safety Critical:* Mandatory continuous presence of calcium gluconate gel for HF exposure mitigation.
2. **Source: Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**
   - *Etch Mask Resistance:* Verified $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ etch rate $< 0.5\ \text{nm/min}$ in BOE.
3. **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**
   - *PID Thermal Tolerance Standards:* Temperature uniformity targets established to maintain thermal control within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal coupling between the recirculating bath's external heater/chiller loop and the internal PVDF/PFA bath immersion chamber exhibits significant thermal transport latency. The control loop must implement cascade PID tuning with Pt100 RTD feedback located directly inside the active chemical flow stream rather than the heat-exchanger reservoir, preventing steady-state temperature offsets greater than +/-0.1 deg C that would otherwise introduce uncorrectable etch-rate drift across multi-wafer batch runs.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: BOE 6:1 (34.6% NH4F : 6.8% HF) etch kinetics on high-density thermal SiO2 exhibit an Arrhenius activation energy of ~0.36 eV (etch rate ~68-72 nm/min at 25.0 deg C, shifting by ~1.8 nm/min per deg C). Precise baseline calibration requires running an ellipsometric 49-point thickness delta map before and after a tightly timed 120.0-second dip. Spectroscopic ellipsometry Psi/Delta optical model fitting (Cauchy model: n(lambda) = 1.457 at 632.8 nm, k = 0) must account for surfactant boundary layers to avoid systematic thickness measurement skew.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standard semiconductor-grade BOE 6:1 premix with trace non-ionic fluorosurfactant (e.g., NCW-1000 or Triton-type fluorinated surfactant at 100-200 ppm) exhibits tight supply constraints and strict shelf-life degradation due to NH3 outgassing and fluorosurfactant micelle precipitation. Chemical inventory must maintain certified UP-S/SEMI Grade 1 purity lots in sealed fluoropolymer drums with Certificate of Analysis tracking trace cations (Fe < 5 ppb, Na < 5 ppb) to prevent surface contamination.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal SiO2 etch-rate qualification is a critical-path gate milestone in the 180nm DRAM patterning sequence. Any delay in bath temperature stabilization (>45 min warm-up) or metrology turnaround directly impacts lot cycle time. Cross-functional buy-in requires automated data logging directly from the ellipsometer to the lot traveler to close out tool release within 1 shift without manual calculation errors.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal boundary layer gradient (>0.3 deg C) across the chemical bath cassette caused by localized recirculation stagnation or clogged spray-header nozzles, resulting in across-wafer etch non-uniformity exceeding 2.5%.
1. Evaporative loss of NH3 or HF due to improper lip-exhaust balancing (>120 LFPM), altering the 6:1 buffer ratio and shifting the active HF2- ion concentration, leading to uncontrolled etch rate acceleration or precipitation of ammonium fluosilicate crystals.
1. Post-etch carryover of residual fluoride into the quick-dump rinse (QDR) due to inadequate surfactant wetting release, causing uncontrolled micro-etching during transfer and catastrophic thinning of 180nm gate dielectric regions.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-1-2-3-01` | **Recirculating Constant-Temperature Bath 9-Point Thermal Uniformity & Stability Verification** | Calibrated NIST-traceable multi-channel Pt100 RTD data logger (accuracy +/-0.02 deg C), chemical-resistant PFA-sheathed thermal probe array, laminar flow wet bench exhaust monitor | 1. Immerse a 9-sensor PFA-sheathed RTD grid across the cassette volume (corners, edge midpoints, and bath center at 50mm immersion depth). 2. Log continuous temperature readings across all 9 channels at 1 Hz for 30 consecutive minutes. 3. Calculate spatial thermal uniformity: delta_T_spatial = T_max - T_min at any given timestamp. 4. Calculate temporal stability: delta_T_temporal = max(T) - min(T) across the 30-minute logging window for the center probe. | `Pass if bath center steady-state temperature is 25.00 +/- 0.10 deg C, spatial temperature delta across all 9 positions is <= 0.15 deg C, and temporal temperature fluctuation over 30 minutes is <= +/- 0.05 deg C. Fail if any probe exceeds 25.20 deg C or drifts > 0.05 deg C/min.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-1-2-3-02` | **Thermal SiO2 Etch-Rate and Across-Wafer Uniformity Metrology via Spectroscopic Ellipsometry** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 240-850 nm, micro-spot 100 um), automated vacuum-assisted wafer stage, automated QDR/SRD cascade rinse modules, cleanroom-rated stopwatch (+/-0.05 s) | 1. Perform pre-etch 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry scan (measure Psi/Delta, fit Cauchy model n=1.457, extract thickness d_initial and map uniformity). 2. Transfer monitor wafer in standard fluoropolymer cassette into stabilized BOE 6:1 bath; start precision timer upon complete subversion. 3. Maintain continuous 8.0 SLPM recirculation without mechanical agitation for exactly 120.0 seconds. 4. Rapidly transfer cassette to QDR (< 5 s transfer time) and execute 4-cycle dump-rinse sequence with UPW (resistivity >= 18.2 MOhm-cm). 5. Spin rinse dry (SRD) wafer under high-purity filtered N2 for 180 s at 2500 RPM. 6. Perform post-etch 49-point ellipsometry scan across identical physical coordinates. 7. Compute etch rate: ER = (mean(d_initial) - mean(d_final)) / 2.0 minutes. 8. Compute within-wafer non-uniformity: NU% = ((ER_max - ER_min) / (2 * ER_mean)) * 100%. | `Pass if mean thermal SiO2 etch rate is 70.0 +/- 3.0 nm/min (140.0 +/- 6.0 nm removed per 120 s) and 49-point within-wafer non-uniformity (NU%) is <= 1.50% with an ellipsometric fit goodness-of-fit (GOF) >= 0.990. Fail if etch rate falls outside 67.0-73.0 nm/min or NU% > 1.50%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavyweight butyl/neoprene outer acid gauntlets with rolled cuff (SEMI S2 compliant), Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield combined with ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash goggles, Acid-resistant heavy-gauge neoprene apron with fluid-barrier sleeves, Steel-toe chemically resistant boot covers / acid boots, Nitrile inner gloves (double gloving under acid gauntlets)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Immediately flush exposed area with copious cold water for exactly 2 minutes while shouting for emergency assistance. Immediately apply and vigorously massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate Gel into skin using gloved hands until medical personnel arrive; reapply every 10-15 minutes to sequester deep fluoride ion penetration and prevent systemic hypocalcemia and cardiac arrest. For ocular exposure, irrigate eyes continuously with sterile isotonic saline or 1.0% calcium gluconate eye wash for at least 15 minutes. Call emergency services immediately; state Hydrofluoric Acid exposure.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet chemical bench dedicated lip exhaust must maintain continuous face velocity between 100 and 120 LFPM across all slot intake openings. Exhaust plenum ducted to dedicated Acid/Fluoride scrubber with continuous pH monitoring and differential pressure interlock. If exhaust drop falls below 80 LFPM, automated wet bench interlock must disallow bath immersion arm activation and sound local audio-visual alarms.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent chemical effluent must be automatically drained to a dedicated Fluoride Industrial Waste Treatment (FIW) collection sump via double-contained PFA piping. Secondary neutralization requires stoichiometric dosing of Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) or Calcium Chloride (CaCl2) to precipitate insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) cake at pH 7.5 to 8.5, followed by coagulant/flocculant settling and slurry dewatering prior to municipal discharge compliance (dissolved F- < 10 ppm).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (BOE Component)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 1 / UP-S | `6.8 wt%` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (BOE Component)** | `12125-01-8` | SEMI Grade 1 / UP-S | `34.6 wt%` |
| **Fluorosurfactant (Perfluoroalkyl surfactant / ethoxylated alcohol additive)** | `65545-80-4` | Electronic Grade | `150 ppm (0.015 wt%)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic clean dry thermal SiO2 surface, zero organic residue, particulate count < 5 defects @ >= 0.2 um, post-clean surface verified dry without moisture condensation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Clean, particle-neutral, uniform oxide target surface with residual post-etch thermal oxide film (or bare hydrophobic Si interface with contact angle > 75 deg if etched to clear); dried under ultrapure N2, resistivity of final cascade rinse overflow >= 18.0 MOhm-cm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes airborne organic amine and hydrocarbon adsorption from cleanroom ambient onto the oxide surface, inducing localized wetting inhibition, pinholes, and micro-masking during the subsequent BOE dip-etch step, yielding catastrophic step-height variation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified constant-temperature recirculating BOE 6:1 bath operating within +/-0.05 deg C temporal and +/-0.15 deg C spatial limits at 25.00 deg C, validated with baseline thermal SiO2 etch rate of 70.0 +/- 3.0 nm/min and <= 1.50% within-wafer non-uniformity across 49 points on 150mm monitor wafers, ensuring process readiness for 180nm DRAM oxide patterning.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `REC_BATH_TEMP_STABILITY_30MIN_LOG.csv`
- [ ] `THERMAL_SIO2_49PT_ELLIPSOMETRY_ETCH_MAP.tiff`
- [ ] `BOE_6TO1_QUALIFICATION_SIGN_OFF_REPORT.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Recirculating bath chemical steady-state temperature stability over 30 minutes continuous operation** | `25.00 deg C` | +/- 0.05 deg C | Continuous 1 Hz NIST-traceable Pt100 RTD multi-channel data acquisition in active chemical stream |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Baseline thermal SiO2 etch rate in surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 at 25.00 deg C** | `70.0 nm/min` | +/- 3.0 nm/min | Pre/post etch 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometric film thickness delta over exactly 120.0 s immersion |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Across-wafer etch rate non-uniformity (NU%) across 49 measurement points on 150mm wafer** | `1.00 %` | <= 1.50 % | Calculated ((ER_max - ER_min) / (2 * ER_mean)) * 100% from automated 49-point polar map |

The control loop must implement cascade PID tuning with Pt100 RTD feedback located directly inside the active chemical flow stream rather than the heat-exchanger reservoir, preventing steady-state temperature offsets greater than +/-0.1 deg C that would otherwise introduce uncorrectable etch-rate drift across multi-wafer batch runs.

Precise baseline calibration requires running an ellipsometric 49-point thickness delta map before and after a tightly timed 120.0-second dip. Spectroscopic ellipsometry Psi/Delta optical model fitting (Cauchy model: n(lambda) = 1.457 at 632.8 nm, k = 0) must account for surfactant boundary layers to avoid systematic thickness measurement skew.

Chemical inventory must maintain certified UP-S/SEMI Grade 1 purity lots in sealed fluoropolymer drums with Certificate of Analysis tracking trace cations (Fe < 5 ppb, Na < 5 ppb) to prevent surface contamination.
critics.laya_pm: Thermal SiO2 etch-rate qualification is a critical-path gate milestone in the 180nm DRAM patterning sequence. Any delay in bath temperature stabilization (>45 min warm-up) or metrology turnaround directly impacts lot cycle time. Cross-functional buy-in requires automated data logging directly from the ellipsometer to the lot traveler to close out tool release within 1 shift without manual calculation errors.
critical_failure_modes: Thermal boundary layer gradient (>0.3 deg C) across the chemical bath cassette caused by localized recirculation stagnation or clogged spray-header nozzles, resulting in across-wafer etch non-uniformity exceeding 2.5%.

Evaporative loss of NH3 or HF due to improper lip-exhaust balancing (>120 LFPM), altering the 6:1 buffer ratio and shifting the active HF2- ion concentration, leading to uncontrolled etch rate acceleration or precipitation of ammonium fluosilicate crystals.

testcases.instrumentation: Calibrated NIST-traceable multi-channel Pt100 RTD data logger (accuracy +/-0.02 deg C), chemical-resistant PFA-sheathed thermal probe array, laminar flow wet bench exhaust monitor
testcases.pre_conditions: Recirculating bath filled to nominal weir level with 18.0 L of pre-mixed BOE 6:1 with surfactant. testcases.procedure: 1. Immerse a 9-sensor PFA-sheathed RTD grid across the cassette volume (corners, edge midpoints, and bath center at 50mm immersion depth). 2. Log continuous temperature readings across all 9 channels at 1 Hz for 30 consecutive minutes. 3. Calculate spatial thermal uniformity: delta_T_spatial = T_max - T_min at any given timestamp. 4. Calculate temporal stability: delta_T_temporal = max(T) - min(T) across the 30-minute logging window for the center probe.

testcases.instrumentation: Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 240-850 nm, micro-spot 100 um), automated vacuum-assisted wafer stage, automated QDR/SRD cascade rinse modules, cleanroom-rated stopwatch (+/-0.05 s)
testcases.pre_conditions: Thermal oxidation monitor wafer (150 mm p-type Si, 100.0 +/- 2.0 nm dry thermal SiO2 grown at 1000 deg C in 3-zone furnace with HCl clean). Wafer clean, dust-free, and measured via 49-point polar map on ellipsometer prior to etch. Bath verified at 25.00 +/- 0.05 deg C.
testcases.procedure: 1. Perform pre-etch 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry scan (measure Psi/Delta, fit Cauchy model n=1.457, extract thickness d_initial and map uniformity). 2. Transfer monitor wafer in standard fluoropolymer cassette into stabilized BOE 6:1 bath; start precision timer upon complete subversion. 3. Maintain continuous 8.0 SLPM recirculation without mechanical agitation for exactly 120.0 seconds. 4. Rapidly transfer cassette to QDR (< 5 s transfer time) and execute 4-cycle dump-rinse sequence with UPW (resistivity >= 18.2 MOhm-cm). 5. Spin rinse dry (SRD) wafer under high-purity filtered N2 for 180 s at 2500 RPM. 6. Perform post-etch 49-point ellipsometry scan across identical physical coordinates. 7. Compute etch rate: ER = (mean(d_initial) - mean(d_final)) / 2.0 minutes. 8. Compute within-wafer non-uniformity: NU% = ((ER_max - ER_min) / (2 * ER_mean)) * 100%.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass if mean thermal SiO2 etch rate is 70.0 +/- 3.0 nm/min (140.0 +/- 6.0 nm removed per 120 s) and 49-point within-wafer non-uniformity (NU%) is <= 1.50% with an ellipsometric fit goodness-of-fit (GOF) >= 0.990. Fail if etch rate falls outside 67.0-73.0 nm/min or NU% > 1.50%.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Document ID:** `SOP-WET-MET-004`  
**Classification:** Gen 1 (mm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip Architecture & Integration  
**Unit Process:** Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning  
**Task Title:** Thermal Stabilization Profiling, Contact Angle Surface Tension Metrology & Baseline Etch Rate Qualification

---

## 1. Process Workflow Overview

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│       Formulate       │
│   Surfactant-Spiked   │
│     BOE 6:1 Bath      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│        Thermal        │
│     Stabilization     │
│   Profiling at 25.0°C │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│    Contact Angle &    │
│    Surface Tension    │
│       Metrology       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Baseline Etch Rate   │
│   Qualification on    │
│     Thermal SiO2      │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            ▼
┌───────────◇───────────┐
│  Acceptance Criteria  │
│        Passed?        │
└─────┬───────────┬─────┘
   Yes│           │No
      ▼           ▼
┌───────────┐ ┌───────────────┐
│  Release  │ │ Quarantine &  │
│   Bath    │ │  Re-profile   │
└───────────┘ └───────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Safety & PPE Protocols

> [!CAUTION]
> **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) Contact Hazard:**
> HF penetrates skin deeply without immediate sensation of pain, dissociates, and chelates systemic calcium ions ($Ca^{2+}$).
> - **Mandatory PPE:** Acid-rated apron, full face shield, heavy neoprene/PVDF gloves over nitrile inner gloves.
> - **Emergency Response:** An unexpired tube of **calcium gluconate gel** must be present within arm's reach of the wet bench at all times prior to opening the chemical bath enclosure.

---

## 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

### Step 1: Chemical Bath Formulation & Wetting Verification
1. Ensure the bath vessel contains standard **BOE 6:1** formulated from:
   - **6 parts** $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ (Ammonium Fluoride)
   - **1 part** $49\%\ \text{HF}$ (Hydrofluoric Acid)
2. Verify the surfactant additive concentration:
   - Wetting agent: **$0.1\%$ Triton X-100** (or Fluorad) by volume to eliminate bubble entrapment in micro-trenches.
3. Verify bath pH stabilizes at $\mathbf{\sim 4.5}$ via constant fluoride ion activity.

### Step 2: Thermal Stabilization Profiling
1. Activate the recirculating immersion chiller/heater bath loop with inert PTFE/PVDF plumbing.
2. Monitor bath temperature using an acid-encapsulated RTD probe.
3. Profile and hold bath temperature at **$25^\circ\text{C}$** until thermal equilibrium is maintained within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across the tank profile for $\ge 30\text{ minutes}$.

### Step 3: Surface Tension & Contact Angle Metrology
1. Extract a $5.0\text{ mL}$ aliquot sample from the stabilized bath.
2. Load an HMDS-primed wafer test coupon ($120^\circ\text{C}$ vapor prime) into the automated optical goniometer.
3. Dispense a $5\ \mu\text{L}$ sessile droplet of the surfactant-spiked BOE solution onto the coupon.
4. Record baseline contact angle $\theta$ and verify rapid surface wetting with zero micro-bubble entrapment across the liquid-wafer interface.

### Step 4: Baseline Etch Rate Qualification Run
1. Select a prime monitor wafer with **thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$** (dry or wet oxide).
2. Measure initial oxide thickness ($T_0$) at 9 or 13 points using an optical ellipsometer/reflectometer ($n \approx 1.46$).
3. Immerse the test wafer into the $25^\circ\text{C}$ BOE 6:1 bath with gentle vertical agitation for a timed cycle of exactly **$60\text{ seconds}$** ($1.00\text{ min}$).
4. Immediately transfer into the dump rinser / cascade overflow rinse bath for a minimum $>5\text{-cycle}$ DI water rinse until effluent resistivity exceeds $18\ \text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$; spin-rinse-dry with filtered $\text{N}_2$.
5. Measure post-etch thickness ($T_1$) at the identical 9 or 13 points. Calculate the average etch rate:
   $$\text{Etch Rate} = \frac{T_0 - T_1}{1.0\ \text{min}}$$

---

## 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Measurement Method / Tooling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bath Temperature** | **$25.0^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$** | Inline PTFE-sheathed RTD temperature sensor |
| **Bath pH** | **$\text{pH } 4.5 \pm 0.2$** | Fluoride-resistant immersion pH probe |
| **Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | **$80\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$** ($800\text{ to } 1000\text{ \AA/min}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (pre/post-etch delta at $25^\circ\text{C}$) |
| **Etch Selectivity ($\text{SiO}_2 : \text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$)** | **$> 20 : 1$** ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4 \text{ etch rate} < 0.5\text{ nm/min}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry on LPCVD $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ coupon ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$) |

---

## 5. Source Citations & References

- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE):**
  - Formulation ratio: 6 parts $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part $49\%\ \text{HF}$.
  - Etch rate of thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ at $25^\circ\text{C} \approx 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  - Surfactant wetting spike: $0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad.
  - HMDS vapor prime pre-treatment condition: $120^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Safety requirement: Immediate availability of calcium gluconate gel.
- **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates:**
  - Buffering mechanism: $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ stabilizes fluoride ion activity and maintains solution $\text{pH } \sim 4.5$.
  - Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate window: $80\text{ to } 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($800\text{ to } 1000\text{ \AA/min}$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
  - Etch selectivity: $\text{SiO}_2 : \text{single-crystal Si} > 100:1$; $\text{SiO}_2 : \text{Si}_3\text{N}_4 > 20:1$.
- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks:**
  - LPCVD $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ baseline characteristics ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$).
  - Chemical resistance to BOE: Etch rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The wet bench recirculating immersion bath requires strict thermal stabilization decoupled from room ambient variations. Exothermic surfactant micellization and chemical dissociation in BOE (6:1 NH4F:HF) mandate dual-loop cascade PID control using a PFA-sheathed RTD immersed directly in the bath and an external heating/cooling jacket. Temperature drifts exceeding +/-0.2°C cause non-linear etch rate shifts of ~1.5% per °C, invalidating 180nm contact and node dielectric etch targets.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Surfactant addition (e.g., non-ionic perfluorinated or hydrocarbon surfactants at 100-500 ppm) reduces the liquid-air surface tension from ~72 mN/m down to <30 mN/m, lowering the contact angle on patterned hydrophobic photoresist sidewalls from >75° to <35°. This prevents micro-bubble pinning and pinhole formation in sub-micron vias. Baseline etch rate qualification must differentiate between densified thermal SiO2 (~100 nm/min at 21.0°C) and native/CVD oxide to establish tight lot-to-lot process predictability.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Pre-mixed semiconductor Grade BOE 6:1 (34.6% NH4F : 6.8% HF) with stabilized surfactant has limited shelf-life due to surfactant segregation and trace cation precipitation. Sourcing ultra-pure fluorosurfactants meeting VLSI/ULSI specs in domestic supply chains requires long-lead import logistics; on-site spiking requires gravimetric/micropipette dispensing validation under cleanroom Class 100 conditions.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal profiling and baseline qualification must fit within the critical wafer release window without delaying primary lot patterning. Ramping the bath to equilibrium takes up to 45 minutes; if metrology qualification is not cleared before resist stabilization expires, unetched lots risk adhesion degradation, track-induced footing, or post-bake contamination.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal gradient stratification in the stagnant regions of the bath exceeding 0.5°C, yielding radial oxide thickness non-uniformity across 150mm/200mm wafers.
1. Surfactant phase separation or surface foam generation blocking wetting into high-aspect-ratio oxide contact cuts, causing incomplete via opening.
1. Loss of volatile HF through aggressive exhaust draught altering the 6:1 molar ratio, leading to drift in baseline etch rate over cumulative bath lifetime.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-1-3-01` | **BOE Bath Thermal Stabilization & Multi-Point Temperature Uniformity Profile** | Calibrated NIST-traceable multi-channel Pt100 RTD array (9-point quartz jig, +/-0.03°C precision) and recirculating PFA bath controller | 1. Submerge 9-point RTD profiling jig across top, middle, and bottom spatial nodes of the 20L tank. 2. Log temperature at 1.0 Hz for 60 minutes after PID controller indicates steady-state. 3. Calculate mean steady-state temperature, maximum peak-to-peak delta across all nodes, and thermal drift over a continuous 30-minute logging window. | `Mean bath temperature must stay within 21.0°C +/- 0.2°C; spatial thermal non-uniformity across all 9 probe nodes must be <= 0.3°C; 30-minute drift rate must be < 0.1°C/hr.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-1-3-02` | **Contact Angle Wetting & Baseline Thermal Oxide Etch Rate Qualification** | Automated Optical Goniometer / Tensiometer (sessile drop method, +/-0.1° resolution) and Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 250-800 nm, +/-0.1 nm film thickness accuracy) | 1. Dispense 5 uL droplet of surfactant-spiked BOE onto patterned resist coupon and measure static contact angle at t=5s. 2. Measure pre-etch SiO2 thickness on monitor wafer at 49 points via spectroscopic ellipsometry. 3. Perform 60.0-second timed immersion etch of the monitor wafer in the BOE bath with gentle 0.5 Hz vertical agitating carrier. 4. Cascade dump rinse in UPW for 180s, spin-dry under N2, and measure post-etch SiO2 thickness at identical 49 points. | `Equilibrium contact angle on resist surface must be <= 35.0°; 6:1 BOE thermal oxide etch rate must measure between 95.0 nm/min and 105.0 nm/min at 21.0°C with within-wafer etch rate non-uniformity (1-sigma / mean) <= 2.0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full-face chemical splash shield combined with ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical goggles, Heavyweight fluoroelastomer (Neoprene/Viton laminate) chemical gloves over inner nitrile gloves, Full-coverage chemical-resistant apron and sleeves (Tychem or heavy-gauge PVC), Steel-toe boots with acid-resistant chemical overboots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Immediately flush skin exposure with emergency eyewash/deluge shower for 5 minutes. Continuously massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel into affected areas using gloved hands until medical personnel arrive. In case of ocular exposure, irrigate with sterile 1.0% calcium gluconate eye solution or saline for 15+ minutes. Administer 100% O2 if inhaled; call dedicated hazmat emergency response immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated acid wet bench exhaust plenum maintaining minimum face velocity of 100 to 120 FPM (0.5 to 0.6 m/s) with continuous differential pressure interlocks (< -0.25 in. w.g.) and toxic fluoride gas detection (HF threshold alarm set at 0.5 ppm).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated fluoride wastewater drainage line directed to specialized fluoride precipitation reactor. Neutralize with 10% calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry or calcium chloride (CaCl2) to precipitate insoluble CaF2 sludge (target pH 7.5 - 8.5, dissolved fluoride < 10 ppm) prior to municipal discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (BOE Component)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI | `6.8 wt%` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (BOE Component)** | `12125-01-8` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI | `34.6 wt%` |
| **Perfluorinated / Non-ionic Wetting Agent** | `29457-72-5` | Electronic / Analytical Grade | `0.025 wt% (250 ppm)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: HMDS vapor-primed, I-line/DUV patterned and hard-baked (115°C) photoresist over densified thermal SiO2, free from scumming and solvent residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Clean, hydrophilically/hydrophobically patterned cleared contact open oxide, rinsed to UPW resistivity > 17.8 MOhm-cm, spin-dried and moisture-free.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full metrological qualification of the surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 bath establishing thermal equilibrium at 21.0°C, verifying wetting contact angle <= 35.0° on photoresist, and baselining thermal oxide etch rate at 100.0 nm/min (+/-5.0 nm/min) with <2% 1-sigma across-wafer uniformity.

- [ ] `contact_angle_wetting_droplet_analysis.tiff`

| `ASSERT-02` | **Surfactant-mediated static contact angle on post-bake photoresist** | `30.0°` | <= 35.0° maximum limit | Automated sessile-drop goniometry optical tangent fit analysis |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Thermal SiO2 baseline etch rate and within-wafer etch uniformity** | `100.0 nm/min` | +/-5.0 nm/min, within-wafer non-uniformity (1-sigma) <= 2.0% | 49-point pre/post immersion spectroscopic ellipsometry on 150mm monitor wafer |

critics.systems_engineer: The wet bench recirculating immersion bath requires strict thermal stabilization decoupled from room ambient variations. Exothermic surfactant micellization and chemical dissociation in BOE (6:1 NH4F:HF) mandate dual-loop cascade PID control using a PFA-sheathed RTD immersed directly in the bath and an external heating/cooling jacket. Temperature drifts exceeding +/-0.2°C cause non-linear etch rate shifts of ~1.5% per °C, invalidating 180nm contact and node dielectric etch targets.
critics.domain_expert: Surfactant addition (e.g., non-ionic perfluorinated or hydrocarbon surfactants at 100-500 ppm) reduces the liquid-air surface tension from ~72 mN/m down to <30 mN/m, lowering the contact angle on patterned hydrophobic photoresist sidewalls from >75° to <35°. This prevents micro-bubble pinning and pinhole formation in sub-micron vias. Baseline etch rate qualification must differentiate between densified thermal SiO2 (~100 nm/min at 21.0°C) and native/CVD oxide to establish tight lot-to-lot process predictability.
critics.supply_chain: Pre-mixed semiconductor Grade BOE 6:1 (34.6% NH4F : 6.8% HF) with stabilized surfactant has limited shelf-life due to surfactant segregation and trace cation precipitation. Sourcing ultra-pure fluorosurfactants meeting VLSI/ULSI specs in domestic supply chains requires long-lead import logistics; on-site spiking requires gravimetric/micropipette dispensing validation under cleanroom Class 100 conditions.
critics.laya_pm: Thermal profiling and baseline qualification must fit within the critical wafer release window without delaying primary lot patterning. Ramping the bath to equilibrium takes up to 45 minutes; if metrology qualification is not cleared before resist stabilization expires, unetched lots risk adhesion degradation, track-induced footing, or post-bake contamination.
critical_failure_modes: Thermal gradient stratification in the stagnant regions of the bath exceeding 0.5°C, yielding radial oxide thickness non-uniformity across 150mm/200mm wafers.
Surfactant phase separation or surface foam generation blocking wetting into high-aspect-ratio oxide contact cuts, causing incomplete via opening.
Loss of volatile HF through aggressive exhaust draught altering the 6:1 molar ratio, leading to drift in baseline etch rate over cumulative bath lifetime.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Thermal Equilibrium Profiling & Recirculating Bath Temperature Mapping

**Scope:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) — Wet Chemical Processing Station  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Safety Caution:** Hydrofluoric acid penetrates skin and binds calcium; calcium gluconate gel must be present and inspected at the station at all times prior to operating the bath.

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Fill Bath with BOE   │
│   6:1 & 0.1% Wetting   │
│         Agent          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│        Initiate        │
│    Recirculation &     │
│      Heating Loop      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Deploy 5-Point PFA   │
│   Thermocouple Array   │◄─╮
└────────────┬───────────┘  │
             │              │
             ▼              │
┌────────────────────────┐  │
│     Log Real-Time      │  │
│    Thermal Gradient    │  │
│        Mapping         │  │
└────────────┬───────────┘  │
             │              │
             ▼              │
┌────────────◇───────────┐  │
│   Stable at 25.0°C ±   │  │
│         0.5°C?         │  │
└────────────◇───────────┘  │
             │              │
           No├──────────────┼──────────────╮Yes
             ▼              │              ▼
┌────────────────────────┐  │ ┌────────────────────────┐
│   Tune Recirculation   │  │ │  Qualify Bath Thermal  │
│        PID Loop        ├──╯ │      Equilibrium       │
└────────────────────────┘    └────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **Safety & Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Inspection**
   - Confirm availability and expiration of topically applied calcium gluconate antidote gel at the chemical wet bench.
   - Don acid-resistant gear: heavy neoprene/nitrile sleeves, chemical apron, face shield, and gauntlet gloves.

2. **Chemical Bath Charging & Wetting Agent Spiking**
   - Charge the recirculating fluoropolymer (PVDF/PFA) bath with standard BOE 6:1 solution (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$).
   - Spike the mixture with 0.1% wetting agent (Triton X-100 or Fluorad) to suppress micro-trench bubble entrapment and establish consistent surface wetting.

3. **Recirculation & Temperature Controller Activation**
   - Start the magnetic-drive chemical circulation pump to maintain steady chemical turnover through the inline filter.
   - Power on the bath immersion heat exchanger / recirculating chiller loop and program the digital PID controller setpoint to **25.0°C**.

4. **Multi-Point Temperature Sensor Grid Mapping**
   - Immerse a qualified 5-point PFA-encapsulated thermocouple profiling array into the active wafer immersion zone (measuring center, front, back, left, and right spatial locations).
   - Log multi-channel temperature data at 10-second intervals for a continuous 20-minute stabilization window.

5. **Thermal Equilibrium Mapping & PID Tuning**
   - Map spatial temperature variations across the active wafer cassette zone to verify elimination of localized convection dead spots.
   - Adjust PID loop proportional gain ($P$) and integral time ($I$) as necessary until the maximum delta between any two mapping nodes satisfies stability criteria.

6. **Equilibrium Sign-Off & Release for Etch Qualification**
   - Record spatial delta values and average steady-state temperature into the run log sheet.
   - Proceed to baseline oxide etch rate qualification.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Tolerance | Verified Context Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Steady-State Bath Temperature** | `25.0` | `±0.5` | `°C` |
| **Spatial Bath Temperature Uniformity** | `≤ 0.5` | Max across 300 mm cassette envelope | `°C` |
| **Wetting Agent Spiking Concentration** | `0.1` | `±0.01` | `% (vol/vol)` |
| **Baseline Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | `100` (equivalent to `1000 Å/min`) | `±5` | `nm/minute` |

---

### Context Citations

- **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
  - BOE 6:1 composition (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$).
  - Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ nominal etch rate baseline: 100 nm/minute (1000 Å/min) at 25°C.
  - Wetting agent addition: 0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad to eliminate micro-trench bubble entrapment.
  - Mandatory safety protocol: Calcium gluconate gel presence due to HF calcium-binding hazard.
- **Source: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
  - Closed-loop PID temperature uniformity tolerance of $\pm 0.5\text{°C}$ across processing regions.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal feedback loop dynamics in a fluoropolymer (PVDF/PTFE) recirculating chemical bath suffer from significant thermal lag due to low thermal conductivity of PFA immersion heater sheaths and in-line fluoropolymer heat exchangers. A classic single-point PID loop coupled with pump recirculation flow pulses creates standing thermal gradients between the weir overflow zone and the central wafer cassette pocket. Feedforward compensation linked to pump flow rate (min 15 LPM) and multi-point RTD sensing is strictly required to prevent localized hot spots that skew etch rate uniformity across 150mm/200mm wafers.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 NH4F:HF), the etch rate of thermal and CVD SiO2 exhibits an Arrhenius activation energy of approximately 0.32-0.36 eV, corresponding to ~1.8 nm/min per 1°C temperature variation near 25.0°C. If spatial temperature non-uniformity across the cassette exceeds ±0.2°C, downstream gate or isolation oxide thickness will exhibit severe within-wafer (WIW) and wafer-to-wafer (WTW) non-uniformity exceeding the 180nm node process budget. Surfactant dissolution and cloud-point segregation dynamics are also highly sensitive to localized micro-thermal fluctuations.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-pure PFA-encapsulated Class-A 4-wire Pt100 RTDs calibrated to NIST standards for corrosive HF/NH4F chemistry introduces extended procurement lead times (8-12 weeks) from specialized vendors. Local second-sourcing for chemical-resistant fluoropolymer thermal mapping rakes or jigs must be validated early, ensuring that mechanical fittings do not compromise cleanroom wet bench trace metal purity (Fe, Cu, Ni < 0.1 ppb).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal mapping and equilibrium qualification cannot be allowed to monopolize active wet bench capacity during prime fabrication shifts. Bath stabilization from ambient (20°C) to 25.0°C target must be automated during off-hours pre-conditioning cycles with telemetry logged to the fab SCADA system. Sign-off must be completed within a 4-hour qualification window prior to releasing the wet station for production lot processing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Spatial thermal channeling caused by unbaffled recirculation jets, inducing a >0.5°C temperature delta between bottom and top wafer slots in the cassette.
1. RTD sheath delamination or pinhole corrosion under concentrated HF exposure, causing sensor resistance drift and thermal runaway of the immersion heater.
1. Surfactant phase separation or foaming induced by localized overheating at heater sheath boundary layers above 30°C.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-1-3-1-01` | **Multi-Point Spatial Thermal Mapping Across Cassette Submersion Volume** | 9-point NIST-traceable PFA-encapsulated Class-A 4-wire Pt100 RTD array grid integrated into dummy 25-wafer PFA cassette jig, logged via calibrated Keysight DAQ970A data acquisition unit at 1 Hz sampling rate. | 1. Lower the 9-point RTD mapping jig into the active process vessel matching standard cassette immersion depth (bottom, center, top tiers across front, center, and back slot positions). 2. Record continuous temperature telemetry across all 9 channels for 30 minutes in steady-state recirculation mode. 3. Calculate instantaneous spatial maximum delta T (T_max - T_min) across all 9 probe positions at every 10-second interval. 4. Compute the 30-minute time-averaged spatial temperature standard deviation across all channels. | `Spatial temperature across all 9 positions must remain within 25.0°C ± 0.15°C absolute; maximum instantaneous spatial gradient between any two probe points must not exceed 0.20°C; spatial standard deviation (1-sigma) must be ≤ 0.05°C over the 30-minute logging window.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-1-3-1-02` | **Thermal Recovery and Transient Stability Following Cold Cassette Insertion** | Calibrated central PFA-sheathed RTD immersed in cassette slot 13; Keysight DAQ970A logging at 2 Hz; automated cassette lifter mechanism operating at 20 mm/s. | 1. Initiate high-speed thermal logging. 2. Submerge the ambient dummy cassette into the active bath at 20 mm/s to simulate standard production immersion loading. 3. Measure the maximum negative thermal dip upon immersion. 4. Monitor and log the recovery curve until the core bath temperature returns to and stabilizes within ±0.10°C of the 25.0°C setpoint. 5. Evaluate PID overshoot or ringing over an 8-minute observation window. | `Maximum immersion thermal transient dip must be ≤ 0.35°C; bath core temperature must fully recover to 25.0°C ± 0.10°C within ≤ 120 seconds post-immersion; transient overshoot after recovery must not exceed +0.10°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full chemical splash face shield meeting ANSI Z87.1 D3 over certified UVEX safety goggles, Heavyweight 22-mil butyl or neoprene chemical-resistant gloves over secondary nitrile inner gloves, PFA/Neoprene full-body acid apron with integrated sleeves and sealed wrist cuffs, Steel-toe chemical boots with acid-resistant gaiters, Calibrated ambient wireless HF gas sensor badge (set to 0.5 ppm TWA threshold)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Immediately remove all contaminated clothing while flushing exposed skin under emergency safety shower for minimum 5 minutes. Apply 2.5% Calcium Gluconate topical gel continuously with gloved hands, rubbing vigorously into the affected zone until medical personnel take over. For ocular exposure, flush eyes at emergency eye-wash station for 15 minutes with sterile saline or isotonic water, then instill sterile 1% calcium gluconate eye drops. Do not apply calcium gluconate gel to eyes. Administer oxygen if vapors are inhaled; call emergency hazmat response immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous lip exhaust on wet bench lip slots operating at face velocity of 0.5 to 0.7 m/s (100-140 FPM) connected to dedicated fluoropolymer-lined acidic wet scrubber ducting. Interlocked differential pressure sensor (threshold minimum 200 Pa negative pressure) cuts power to immersion heaters and circulation pumps upon exhaust failure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent or overflow BOE chemistry is gravity-drained via dedicated PVDF double-contained piping to the fluoride waste neutralization system. Automated stoichiometric dosing of 20-30% Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry precipitates fluoride as insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) cake at pH 8.5-9.5, followed by coagulant/polymer dosing, filter pressing, and clarifier effluent discharge with residual fluoride < 10 ppm.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Fluoride** | `12125-01-8` | SEMI Grade 4 (UP-S) | `34.0% - 35.0% w/w (in 6:1 mix)` |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 4 (UP-S) | `6.8% - 7.1% w/w (in 6:1 mix)` |
| **Non-ionic Perfluorinated Alkyl Surfactant** | `29457-72-5` | Electronic Grade / Trace Metal < 1 ppb | `100 - 250 ppm` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-lithography hardbaked patterned photoresist (IX845 or equivalent) on thermally grown silicon dioxide (100 nm ± 5 nm), free of organic residue (DI rinse > 18.0 MOhm-cm, spin-dried), surface hydrophilicity verified.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Thermally stabilized BOE 6:1 bath verified at 25.0°C ± 0.15°C with steady-state recirculating flow ready for lot immersion; wafers exiting this step undergo immediate DI cascade dump rinse with completely dewetted hydrophobic bare silicon contact openings.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in cleanroom air leads to airborne moisture absorption by the patterned resist, causing photoresist lifting/undercutting during BOE immersion and airborne airborne amine/volatile organic adsorption that alters the local surface wetting angle.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full empirical thermal equilibrium profiling and 9-point spatial temperature mapping of the surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 recirculating bath, demonstrating spatial and temporal isothermality within ±0.15°C at 25.0°C and transient recovery within 120 seconds post-cassette loading.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `BOE_Recirc_Bath_9Point_Thermal_Map_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `BOE_Thermal_Transient_Cassette_Recovery_Telemetry.csv`
- [ ] `PID_Loop_AutoTuning_Flow_Decoupling_Matrix.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Steady-state spatial temperature uniformity across the 9 cassette measuring nodes in active recirculation** | `25.00°C` | ±0.15°C | Multi-channel 9-point Class-A Pt100 RTD logging via Keysight DAQ970A averaged over 30 minutes at 1 Hz |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum thermal transient recovery time following immersion of ambient dummy cassette** | `90 seconds` | ≤ 120 seconds | Direct time measurement from minimum negative deflection point to return within ±0.10°C band of 25.00°C setpoint |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Temporal temperature stability (drift) at central slot location over continuous 2-hour idle recirculation** | `0.00°C drift` | ±0.05°C peak-to-peak | Continuous RTD telemetry extraction and linear regression drift calculation over 7200 seconds |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 9 spatial mapping points must demonstrate mean temperatures within 24.85°C to 25.15°C with no single point exceeding a 0.20°C delta relative to bath average, transient cassette load recovery must complete in under 120 seconds, and dual-technician signoff must verify zero chemical leakage and calibrated RTD verification certificates.

testcases.title: Thermal Recovery and Transient Stability Following Cold Cassette Insertion
testcases.instrumentation: Calibrated central PFA-sheathed RTD immersed in cassette slot 13; Keysight DAQ970A logging at 2 Hz; automated cassette lifter mechanism operating at 20 mm/s.
testcases.pre_conditions: Bath at verified steady-state thermal equilibrium (25.00°C ± 0.05°C); 25-wafer production-equivalent blank silicon dummy cassette conditioned at ambient cleanroom temperature (20.5°C ± 0.5°C).
testcases.procedure:
1. Initiate high-speed thermal logging.
2. Submerge the ambient dummy cassette into the active bath at 20 mm/s to simulate standard production immersion loading.
3. Measure the maximum negative thermal dip upon immersion.
4. Monitor and log the recovery curve until the core bath temperature returns to and stabilizes within ±0.10°C of the 25.0°C setpoint.
5. Evaluate PID overshoot or ringing over an 8-minute observation window.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Maximum immersion thermal transient dip must be ≤ 0.35°C; bath core temperature must fully recover to 25.0°C ± 0.10°C within ≤ 120 seconds post-immersion; transient overshoot after recovery must not exceed +0.10°C.

ppe_required: Full chemical splash face shield meeting ANSI Z87.1 D3 over certified UVEX safety goggles
Heavyweight 22-mil butyl or neoprene chemical-resistant gloves over secondary nitrile inner gloves
PFA/Neoprene full-body acid apron with integrated sleeves and sealed wrist cuffs
Steel-toe chemical boots with acid-resistant gaiters
Calibrated ambient wireless HF gas sensor badge (set to 0.5 ppm TWA threshold)
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Immediately remove all contaminated clothing while flushing exposed skin under emergency safety shower for minimum 5 minutes. Apply 2.5% Calcium Gluconate topical gel continuously with gloved hands, rubbing vigorously into the affected zone until medical personnel take over. For ocular exposure, flush eyes at emergency eye-wash station for 15 minutes with sterile saline or isotonic water, then instill sterile 1% calcium gluconate eye drops. Do not apply calcium gluconate gel to eyes. Administer oxygen if vapors are inhaled; call emergency hazmat response immediately.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous lip exhaust on wet bench lip slots operating at face velocity of 0.5 to 0.7 m/s (100-140 FPM) connected to dedicated fluoropolymer-lined acidic wet scrubber ducting. Interlocked differential pressure sensor (threshold minimum 200 Pa negative pressure) cuts power to immersion heaters and circulation pumps upon exhaust failure.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent or overflow BOE chemistry is gravity-drained via dedicated PVDF double-contained piping to the fluoride waste neutralization system. Automated stoichiometric dosing of 20-30% Calcium Hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) slurry precipitates fluoride as insoluble Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) cake at pH 8.5-9.5, followed by coagulant/polymer dosing, filter pressing, and clarifier effluent discharge with residual fluoride < 10 ppm.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Post-lithography hardbaked patterned photoresist (IX845 or equivalent) on thermally grown silicon dioxide (100 nm ± 5 nm), free of organic residue (DI rinse > 18.0 MOhm-cm, spin-dried), surface hydrophilicity verified.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Thermally stabilized BOE 6:1 bath verified at 25.0°C ± 0.15°C with steady-state recirculating flow ready for lot immersion; wafers exiting this step undergo immediate DI cascade dump rinse with completely dewetted hydrophobic bare silicon contact openings.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Exceeding queue time in cleanroom air leads to airborne moisture absorption by the patterned resist, causing photoresist lifting/undercutting during BOE immersion and airborne airborne amine/volatile organic adsorption that alters the local surface wetting angle.

expected_result.summary: Full empirical thermal equilibrium profiling and 9-point spatial temperature mapping of the surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 recirculating bath, demonstrating spatial and temporal isothermality within ±0.15°C at 25.0°C and transient recovery within 120 seconds post-cassette loading.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Steady-state spatial temperature uniformity across the 9 cassette measuring nodes in active recirculation
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-channel 9-point Class-A Pt100 RTD logging via Keysight DAQ970A averaged over 30 minutes at 1 Hz

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Maximum thermal transient recovery time following immersion of ambient dummy cassette
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Direct time measurement from minimum negative deflection point to return within ±0.10°C band of 25.00°C setpoint

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Temporal temperature stability (drift) at central slot location over continuous 2-hour idle recirculation
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Continuous RTD telemetry extraction and linear regression drift calculation over 7200 seconds

expected_result.signoff_criteria: All 9 spatial mapping points must demonstrate mean temperatures within 24.85°C to 25.15°C with no single point exceeding a 0.20°C delta relative to bath average, transient cassette load recovery must complete in under 120 seconds, and dual-technician signoff must verify zero chemical leakage and calibrated RTD verification certificates.
