nodes.sop_content:
### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

#### **Title:** Post-Etch Rapid Cascade Quench, Spin-Rinse Dry (SRD) & Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Inspection
**Process Step:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Metrology  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Buy / Execution

---

### Process Workflow Diagram

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Etch Bath Exit (BOE 6:1 Dip at 25°C)        │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │ Rapid Transfer (< 5 s)
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Multi-Stage Cascade Overflow DI Water Rinse │
│  (Resistivity Recovery to 18 MΩ·cm)          │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │ Nitrogen Purge & Transfer
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Spin-Rinse Dry (SRD)                        │
│  (4,000 RPM Spin Cycle, N2 Blanket Dry)      │
└──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                       │ Dry Transfer
                       ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Metrology        │
│  (Film Thickness & Refractive Index n)       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Emergency Safety & Rapid Transfer Setup**:
   - Verify that Calcium Gluconate antidote gel is physically stocked and accessible at the wet bench before wafer extraction.
   - Maintain the upstream BOE (6:1) bath temperature at $25^\circ\text{C}$.

2. **Rapid Cascade Overflow Quench**:
   - Immediately extract the wafer cassette from the BOE 6:1 solution upon completion of the timed etch step.
   - Transfer and plunge the cassette into Stage 1 of the deionized (DI) water cascade overflow rinse bath within $\le 5\text{ seconds}$ to arrest chemical etching.
   - Submerge sequentially across cascade stages under continuous bottom-up overflow until DI water effluent resistivity recovers to baseline ($\ge 18\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$), flushing all residual fluorides, $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$, and wetting agent surfactant.

3. **Spin-Rinse Dry (SRD) Execution**:
   - Transfer rinsed wafers into the automated Spin-Rinse Dryer chamber under filtered nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) purge.
   - Execute the spin-dry recipe: ramp to $4,000\text{ RPM}$ for $30\text{ seconds}$ with simultaneous high-purity heated $\text{N}_2$ purge to eliminate surface water droplets, micro-trench entrapment, and edge-bead dry spots without mechanical water spotting.

4. **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Inspection**:
   - Transfer dry wafers to the automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometer loading stage.
   - Configure measurement recipe for multi-layer dielectric modeling on Si substrate across the visible wavelength range (centered at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$).
   - Measure 5-point/9-point across-wafer test sites targeting remaining dielectric/hard mask thickness and refractive index.
   - Verify that the hard mask or remaining oxide target thickness conforms strictly within tolerance before releasing the lot to downstream resist strip or metallization.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric & Tolerance | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cascade Quench Transfer Latency** | $\le 5.0$ | $\text{s}$ | Automated wet bench robotic arm / PLC timer |
| **SRD Spin Drying Speed & Duration** | $4,000 \pm 10$ at $30 \pm 1$ | $\text{RPM}$ / $\text{s}$ | SRD Optical Tachometer & Controller Log |
| **Silicon Nitride Film Refractive Index ($n$)** | $2.00 \pm 0.02$ (at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$) | Dimensionless | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer |
| **Oxide Etch Step Rate Uniformity Reference** | $100 \pm 5$ ($1000 \pm 50\text{ \AA/min}$) | $\text{nm/min}$ | Pre/Post Ellipsometric Step-Height Delta at $25^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 3. Literature Context Citations

- **[Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)]**:
  - Etch rate of thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is approximately $100\text{ nm/minute}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  - BOE consists of 6 parts $40\%\text{ NH}_4\text{F}$ and 1 part $49\%\text{ HF}$ with wetting agent ($0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad); Calcium Gluconate gel mandate for HF exposure safety.
- **[Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming]**:
  - Mechanical rotation dynamics and standard recipe execution: spin cycle at $4,000\text{ RPM}$ for $30\text{ seconds}$ with ramp rate up to $10,000\text{ RPM/s}$.
- **[Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks]**:
  - Silicon Nitride hard mask film characteristics: refractive index $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$; high resistance to BOE ($< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ etch rate).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Cascade quench bath transfer must occur in under 3 seconds post-dip etch to avoid runaway exothermic boundary-layer etching, yet automated mechanical or manual jig handling must not splash residual HF/NH4F chemistry onto unetched resist boundaries or spin-rinse dry (SRD) rotor bearings.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Directly post-BOE 6:1 etch, the open silicon oxide interface reaches hydrogen termination (Si-H) or residual fluorinated intermediate species; incomplete cascade DI water flushing (resistivity < 18.0 MOhm*cm) causes residual fluoride salt crystallization upon nitrogen spin-drying, severely distorting spectroscopic ellipsometry psi and delta polarimetric fits across the 350-800nm spectrum.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Spectroscopic ellipsometers with high-precision micro-spot goniometers are expensive capital assets; for Gen 1 open-source DRAM prototyping, custom broadband xenon/halogen reflectometer stages or refurbished multi-wavelength ellipsometer heads (e.g., J.A. Woollam or Rudolph legacy units) require standardized optical calibration wafers (100nm thermal SiO2 on Si) to verify cross-lab baseline repeatability.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Cycle time must balance thorough cascade rinsing (>3 turnover cycles) against strict queue time limits before atmospheric native oxide regrows or airborne organic contaminants foul the freshly etched gate/isolation oxide step, stalling the daily batch yield.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Water spotting and micro-droplet dry-down stains on patterned oxide windows caused by inadequate SRD purge pressure or unbalanced rotor RPM, generating artificial phase shifts in ellipsometry.
1. Unquenched BOE drag-out into the primary quench cell causing localized over-etching and undercut of S1813 photoresist features exceeding the 100-micron Gen 1 tolerance envelope.
1. Uncontrolled native oxide regrow (Si-O bond reformation) and organic adsorption due to exceeding post-rinse queue time before spectroscopic ellipsometric inspection, leading to false film thickness overestimation.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-2-3-01` | **Post-Quench Rinse Effluent Resistivity and SRD Surface Dryness Inspection** | In-line Ultra-pure DI Water Resistivity Probe (0.01 uS/cm precision), High-Purity N2 Purge Spin-Rinse Dryer (SRD) Tachometer, High-Intensity Darkfield Inspection Lamp (532nm LED) | 1. Submerge wafer carrier into Stage 1 dump rinser for 30s quick-dump cycle. 2. Cascade through Stage 2 and Stage 3 overflow rinse tanks until effluent resistivity meter stabilizes. 3. Transfer wafer immediately to Spin-Rinse Dryer rotor. 4. Execute spin recipe: Rinse cycle at 800 RPM with DI spray for 60s, followed by dry spin at 2800 RPM under 40 PSI filtered N2 purge for 120s. 5. Unload wafer in ISO 5 clean bench and examine front surface under darkfield collimated green LED illumination at 45-degree incidence. | `Cascade effluent resistivity must read >= 18.0 MOhm*cm at 25 deg C prior to SRD transfer; visual darkfield inspection must reveal zero drying water-marks, residual salt haze, or droplet streaks across the active die area.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-2-3-02` | **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Film Thickness and Optical Parameter Validation** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 370 nm - 1000 nm, 70-degree angle of incidence, 100-micron microspot optics) | 1. Mount wafer on vacuum chuck and align optical beam to central unmasked oxide test pad and 4 peripheral quadrant pads (5-point map). 2. Acquire polarimetric raw data (Psi and Delta spectra) from 400 nm to 800 nm. 3. Fit acquired spectra using a standard Cauchy/Sellmeier SiO2 on Si optical model. 4. Record mean remaining oxide thickness (T_ox), refractive index (n at 632.8 nm), and Mean Squared Error (MSE) of fit across all 5 test sites. | `Remaining oxide thickness target within target recipe specifications (+/- 2.5 nm); refractive index n = 1.457 +/- 0.005 at 632.8 nm; regression fit quality MSE <= 2.5 across all 5 measurement sites.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavyweight butyl/neoprene chemical aprons and sleeves, Fluoroelastomer / Neoprene dual-layer gloves over nitrile examination gloves, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1, Closed-toe chemical-resistant neoprene boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calgonate 2.5% Calcium Gluconate Gel must be present within arm's reach of the rinse station. In case of skin contact with quench tank fluid, strip contaminated clothing immediately, flush with copious cold water for 60 seconds, and vigorously massage calcium gluconate gel into affected skin continuously until emergency medical responders arrive. For eye exposure, flush with isotonic sterile eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet bench cascade tanks and SRD exhaust ports must connect to a continuous acid scrubbed exhaust system maintaining a minimum slot capture face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s), monitored by differential pressure interlocks.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Stage 1 dump-rinse drag-out effluent must be routed directly to the centralized fluoride waste treatment stream (FWT) with calcium chloride (CaCl2) or lime slurry precipitation for CaF2 sludge removal, never discharged into general acid/neutralization drains.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (trace carryover)** | `7664-39-3` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `< 1.0% in primary quench bath` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (trace carryover)** | `12125-01-8` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `< 5.0% in primary quench bath` |
| **Deionized Water (Cascade Rinse)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor UPW Grade Type E-1 | `> 99.99%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (SRD Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) 99.999% | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Partially etched patterned thermal/PECVD silicon dioxide submerged in BOE 6:1 with active chemical etch boundary layer.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic/hydrophilic mixed pattern, decontaminated, ultra-dry, particulate-free oxide surface with stable hydrogen passivation ready for metrology.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide re-growth (> 0.5 nm) in ambient cleanroom air coupled with airborne molecular organic contamination (AMOC) altering refractive index fits and falsifying post-etch thickness metrology.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful termination of BOE 6:1 chemical reaction via sub-3s rapid DI cascade quenching, complete salt decontamination to 18 MOhm*cm resistivity, streak-free centrifugal N2 drying, and spectroscopic ellipsometry multi-point thickness mapping confirming target etch stop parameters without pattern degradation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-2-3_Rinse_Conductivity_Log.csv`
- [ ] `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-2-3_Ellipsometry_5Point_Map.pdf`
- [ ] `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-2-3_Darkfield_Surface_Inspection.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-BOE-QUENCH-01` | **Cascade rinse bath final effluent resistivity reaches deionized equilibrium** | `18.2 MOhm*cm` | +/- 0.2 MOhm*cm | In-situ calibrated resistivity probe at Stage 3 overflow weir |
| `ASSERT-BOE-QUENCH-02` | **Remaining targeted oxide thickness verified post-etch and dry** | `50.0 nm` | +/- 2.5 nm across 5-point wafer map | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Cauchy model fit (MSE < 2.5) across 370-1000 nm |
| `ASSERT-BOE-QUENCH-03` | **Post-SRD frontside surface residual macro/micro particulate density** | `0 defects` | < 3 defects (> 1.0 um) across entire active substrate | High-intensity darkfield glancing-incidence optical inspection |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer passes 5-point spectroscopic ellipsometry with MSE <= 2.5 within 30 minutes of SRD cycle completion, darkfield imaging verifies zero water spotting or fluoride precipitation residue, and all rinse logs confirm effluent resistivity >= 18.0 MOhm*cm.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-MET-BOE-001
**Title:** Multi-Stage Cascade Overflow Rinse and Resist Adhesion Metrology  
**Context:** DRAM Foundation VN — 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 1)  
**Process Stage:** Wet Chemistry / Metrology post-BOE 6:1 SiO₂ Patterning  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This SOP defines the post-etch multi-stage cascade overflow rinse protocol to quench Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) reactions, remove ionic fluoride/ammonium residues, prevent photoresist lifting, and measure post-rinse resist adhesion and clean endpoint integrity.

---

### 2. Safety, PPE & Equipment Pre-checks
> [!CAUTION]
> **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) Hazard:** HF penetrates skin deeply and dissociated fluoride ions bind serum calcium. **Calcium gluconate gel** must be present at the wet bench workstation at all times.

- **PPE:** Full acid apron, face shield over safety glasses, heavy PVDF/Neoprene acid gloves over nitrile inner gloves.
- **Rinse Tank:** Multi-stage cascade overflow bath constructed from PVDF/PTFE supplied with continuous 18.2 MΩ·cm Ultra-Pure Water (UPW).
- **Drainage:** Dedicated acid waste neutralization line (AWN).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+-----------------------+     +-----------------------+     +------------------------+
| Stage 1: Quick Quench | --> | Stage 2: Intermediate | --> | Stage 3: High Purity   |
| Primary Dump Rinse    |     | Cascade Rinse Tank    |     | Overflow Rinse Tank    |
| (5 dump cycles)       |     | (Resistivity monitor) |     | (>16-18.2 MOhm-cm UPW) |
+-----------------------+     +-----------------------+     +------------------------+
                                                                         |
                                                                         v
                                                            +------------------------+
                                                            | Surface Dewet Check &  |
                                                            | CD-SEM Resist Adhesion |
                                                            +------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Initial Quench & Primary Cascade Dump Rinse
1. Immediately transfer the wafer carrier from the BOE 6:1 bath into the primary quick-dump rinse (QDR) stage within **< 3 seconds** to halt SiO₂ etching (~80–100 nm/min thermal oxide rate).
2. Execute **5 cycles** of fill-and-dump with 18.2 MΩ·cm UPW at ambient temperature (22°C–25°C).

#### Step 2: Multi-Stage Cascade Overflow Immersion
1. Submerge the wafer cassette into Stage 2 cascade overflow rinse tank (counter-current UPW flow).
2. Monitor in-line effluent conductivity/resistivity sensor. Rinse continuously until resistivity recovers to **> 16.0 MΩ·cm**.
3. Move carrier to Stage 3 final overflow tank for **60 seconds** under constant UPW laminar overflow to flush residual surfactant (Triton X-100 / Fluorad) and ammonium ions (NH₄⁺).

#### Step 3: Spin-Rinse-Dry (SRD)
1. Transfer wafer boat to automated Spin-Rinse-Dry (SRD) tool.
2. Run baseline dry recipe: low-speed rinse, followed by high-speed spin drying under hot, filtered dry nitrogen ($N_2$) blanket.

#### Step 4: Photoresist Adhesion & Etch Profile Metrology
1. **Dewetting / Clearing Check:** Inspect etched open oxide patterns for complete clearing (hydrophobic transition check on open silicon areas).
2. **Optical Inspection (Macro/Micro):** Inspect wafer under brightfield/darkfield illumination at 50×–1000× magnification across 5 points (Center, North, South, East, West) for resist peeling, blistering, or undercut lifting caused by chemical intrusion or HMDS prime failure.
3. **CD-SEM Adhesion & Profile Verification:** Measure critical dimension (CD) and photoresist footing/undercut in dense feature arrays (180nm pitch).

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter | Target Specification | Measurement Method | Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Final Rinse Water Resistivity** | $\ge 16.0$ | In-line resistivity probe (Stage 3 overflow bath) | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ |
| **Cascade Dump Rinse Cycles** | $5$ | Automated cycle counter / QDR controller | $\text{cycles}$ |
| **Photoresist Peeling / Lifting Defect Density** | $0$ (Zero delamination at trench/contact edges) | High-resolution Optical / Darkfield Inspection | $\text{defects/cm}^2$ |
| **SiO₂ Etch Endpoint Uniformity (Thermal Oxide)** | $80 - 100$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (remaining oxide thickness vs. time) | $\text{nm/min}$ |

---

### 5. Context Citations
- **Formulation, Safety & Surfactants:** *Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)* — BOE 6:1 (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$), 100 nm/min thermal oxide etch rate at 25°C, 0.1% surfactant additive, HMDS vapor prime at 120°C for resist adhesion, and mandatory calcium gluconate safety requirements.
- **Rinse Protocol & Resistivity Endpoint:** *Source: RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering* — Cascade dump rinse baseline using 5 cycles with 18.2 MΩ·cm UPW until bath resistivity exceeds 16 MΩ·cm; hydrophobic dewetting verification.
- **Selectivity & Etch Mechanics:** *Source: Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates* — Thermal oxide etch rate envelope of 80–100 nm/min at 25°C, $\text{SiO}_2$ to Si selectivity > 100:1, and deep dermal HF penetration hazards.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Cascade overflow rinse must decouple mechanical fluid shear from chemical diffusion at Gen 1 scales (100 µm features). Turbulent DI water introduction directly onto patterned Shipley 1813 creates catastrophic boundary-layer peel forces. The dump-and-overflow cycle requires an integrated in-line resistivity probe (<0.5 cm standoff from wafer weir) to detect ionic depletion from BOE fluoride salts before wafer transfer, ensuring DI water recovery reaches >16 MOhm-cm without manual handling latency.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Following surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 immersion, capillary drag along etched SiO2 sidewalls promotes lateral resist lifting if interfacial surface energy shifts abruptly. Resist adhesion metrology must verify zero edge delamination, zero blistering, and intact footings using optical brightfield/darkfield and critical dimension (CD) inspection. Furthermore, incomplete cascade rinsing traps ammonium fluoride crystals at the resist/oxide triple point, yielding micro-masking defects in downstream gate dielectric processing.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-pure water (UPW) generation in decentralized/garage cleanroom environments faces severe throughput bottlenecks; a 3-stage cascade rinse consuming >5 L/min of 18.2 MOhm-cm water demands high-recovery modular RO/EDI skids. Sourcing certified semiconductor-grade HF/NH4F compatible PVDF/PTFE weir tanks and sub-micron N2 spray guns requires secondary sourcing channels to avoid lead times exceeding 8 weeks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Balancing wafer throughput against resist undercut risk is paramount. A prolonged cascade rinse (>5 minutes) degrades unbaked photoresist structural integrity, whereas an abbreviated cycle leaves fluoride residue that violates the post-etch queue-time envelope for furnace growth. The operational workflow must constrain wafer transfer from BOE bath to final dry within 360 seconds while establishing reproducible resistivity logs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial photoresist peeling and line collapse caused by hydrodynamic fluid shear or surface-tension-induced capillary forces during stage-1 cascade overflow rinse.
1. Fluoride salt precipitation and ammonium fluosilicate micro-crystallization on patterned active areas due to inadequate cascade dilution stages or stagnant boundary layers.
1. Lateral resist lifting and under-film etching exceeding ±5 µm tolerance resulting from surfactant entrapment at the SiO2/S1813 interface.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-01` | **Cascade Overflow Rinse Ionic Cleansing and Resist Mechanical Integrity Test** | In-line immersion resistivity probe (PTFE-sheathed, 0.01 cell constant), calibrated brightfield/darkfield metallurgical microscope with 10x Plan Achromat objective (NA 0.25) and CMOS digital reticle camera. | 1. Submerge etched wafer into Stage 1 overflow tank operating at 2.0 L/min DI water flow for 60 seconds. 2. Index wafer to Stage 2 and Stage 3 overflow tanks for 60 seconds each with counter-current UPW flow until the Stage 3 weir sensor stabilizes. 3. Record final weir DI water resistivity. 4. Transfer wafer to spin-rinse/dry station or perform filtered N2 blow-dry at 1.5 bar with 45-degree incidence angle. 5. Inspect 9 standardized grid coordinates across the wafer surface under 100x magnification to evaluate photoresist boundary edges and calculate pattern lifting area. | `Final overflow weir resistivity must reach ≥ 16.0 MOhm-cm within 180 seconds. Total photoresist pattern delamination or edge peel must be 0.0% across all 9 inspection fields, with zero visible ammonium fluosilicate crystalline residues at 100x magnification.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-02` | **Resist Adhesion Tape/Shear Robustness and Undercut Width Metrology** | Optical inspection microscope with calibrated digital micrometer reticle (sub-micron resolution), ASTM D3359 cross-hatch cutter / precision scribe with compliant Kapton pressure-sensitive adhesion tape (1.0 N/cm peel rating). | 1. Position wafer under optical microscope and measure lateral resist footing undercut along 5 distinct 100 µm wide oxide test structures. 2. Apply standardized pressure-sensitive tape across designated peripheral non-active test structures, applying uniform roller pressure of 200 kPa. 3. Peel tape smoothly at a 90-degree angle within 5 seconds. 4. Re-examine the test structure grid under brightfield/darkfield illumination. 5. Calculate percentage of lifted resist area and quantify lateral footing delta. | `Zero photoresist removal (Classification 5B per ASTM D3359 standard) across the tested peripheral array. Lateral undercut at the resist-SiO2 interface must not exceed 0.8 µm from the patterned mask edge.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl rubber gloves over nitrile inner gloves, Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield with chin guard, Chemical-resistant neoprene/PVDF apron and sleeves, Closed-toe chemical-resistant safety boots, Continuous personal HF gas / fluoride badge monitor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium gluconate gel (2.5%) must be immediately accessible within 3 meters of the wet bench. In case of skin exposure, flush with copious water for 1 minute, immediately massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into affected area until pain subsides, and seek emergency medical evaluation. In case of eye contact, flush with isotonic saline or eyewash solution for 15 minutes and call for medical transport.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet process station dedicated lip exhaust and rear-slotted exhaust maintaining a minimum capture velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) across the entire open weir surface, ducted to an acid-fume scrubber with caustic scrubbing liquor.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Cascade rinse effluent containing fluoride carryover must be routed to a dedicated fluorochemical waste drain. Neutralize in a retention tank using aqueous calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) or calcium chloride (CaCl2) to precipitate insoluble calcium fluoride (CaF2), adjusting pH to 6.5-8.5 prior to clarifier discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (trace carryover in rinse effluent)** | `7664-39-3` | VLSI/Semi Grade | `< 0.5% in rinse water` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (trace carryover in rinse effluent)** | `12125-01-8` | VLSI/Semi Grade | `< 2.0% in rinse water` |
| **Deionized Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | Type 1 Semiconductor Grade (> 18.0 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Etched SiO2 pattern wet with residual surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 solution; photoresist hydrated but intact.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fluoride-free, fully dried hydrophilic/hydrophobic differentiated Si/SiO2 surface with adhered S1813 resist, free of ionic salts.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive ambient air exposure causes atmospheric airborne hydrocarbon chemisorption onto exposed silicon windows and spontaneous native oxide regrow (> 0.5 nm), degrading subsequent metallization/doping interface resistance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful execution of the 3-stage cascade overflow rinse achieving full removal of residual BOE salts, confirmed by rinse effluent resistivity recovery to ≥ 16 MOhm-cm, with zero photoresist delamination, zero blistering, and undercut limited to < 0.8 µm.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `cascade_rinse_resistivity_telemetry.csv`
- [ ] `resist_adhesion_post_rinse_inspection.tiff`
- [ ] `boe_rinse_metrology_signoff_report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-TC-BOE-01` | **Stage 3 overflow cascade rinse water resistivity recovery** | `16.5` | ±0.5 MOhm-cm | Calibrated in-line PTFE immersion conductivity/resistivity sensor logged at 1 Hz |
| `ASSERT-TC-BOE-02` | **Photoresist film delamination across active pattern inspection sites** | `0.0` | +0.0% | Automated 100x optical brightfield digital image thresholding across 9 wafer zones |
| `ASSERT-TC-BOE-03` | **Maximum lateral resist undercut footing width** | `0.6` | ±0.2 µm | High-magnification calibrated optical reticle microscope measurement |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer passes 100% of 9-point optical pattern retention criteria with zero edge lifting, cascade bath weir resistivity reaches ≥ 16.0 MOhm-cm within 180 seconds of rinse initiation, and wafer is N2-dried and stowed into dry nitrogen box within the 30-minute queue-time window.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Multi-Stage Cascade Overflow Rinse Recipe Execution & DI Water Effluent Resistivity Monitoring

- **Node ID**: `node-wet-rinse-cascade-boe-gen2`
- **Level**: Leaf SOP (Gen 2: $\mu\text{m}$ / 180nm Node Pre-Capacitor & Active Dielectric Clean)
- **Action Type**: Make
- **Discipline**: Wet Chemistry / Surface Preparation & Contamination Metrology

---

### 1. Process Architecture & Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  BOE 6:1 Chemical Dip  │
│          Tank          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │Carrier Transfer <= 5s
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Stage 1: Quench &    │
│     Rough Cascade      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │Counter-Current Overflow
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        Stage 2:        │
│  Intermediate Cascade  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │Upstream Fresh UPW
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Stage 3: Final     │
│    Resistivity Cell    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │Effluent Probe >= 18.0 MOhm.cm
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│        Nitrogen        │
│   Marangoni/SRD Dry    │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Pre-Operational Baseline Verification & Safety Check**:
   - Confirm safety emergency station: [calcium gluconate gel](docs/context.yaml) must be unexpired and present within direct reach of the bench due to hydrofluoric acid ($HF$) toxicity.
   - Verify that incoming Ultra-Pure Deionized Water (UPDI) into Stage 3 shows an inlet resistivity of $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25.0^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Ensure constant counter-current weir overflow cascade from Stage 3 $\rightarrow$ Stage 2 $\rightarrow$ Stage 1 with bottom UPW injection at a flow rate of $12.0 \pm 1.0\text{ L/min}$.

2. **Cassette Unload & Transfer-to-Quench**:
   - Immediately upon completion of the timed Buffered Oxide Etch ($6:1\text{ NH}_4\text{F}:\text{HF}$ with $0.1\%$ wetting agent at $25^\circ\text{C}$, nominal etch rate $\sim 100\text{ nm/min}$ on thermal $\text{SiO}_2$), lift the Teflon wafer boat from the etch vessel.
   - Transfer wafer carrier into **Stage 1 (Rough Quench Tank)** within $\le 5.0\text{ seconds}$ to prevent uncontrolled airborne micro-etching and resist peeling.

3. **Multi-Stage Cascade Overflow Progression**:
   - **Stage 1 (Rapid Quench & Heavy Ionic Displacement)**: Submerge and oscillate vertically for $45\text{ s}$ to strip bulk viscous fluoride salts ($[\text{NH}_4]^+$, $[\text{HF}_2]^-$) and surfactant residues.
   - **Stage 2 (Intermediate Cascade Dilution)**: Advance carrier to Stage 2 with laminar overflow for $60\text{ s}$. Counter-current effluent washes away trapped micro-droplets from patterned micro-trenches.
   - **Stage 3 (Precision Final Clean & In-Situ Effluent Monitoring)**: Seat carrier into Stage 3 directly upstream of the fresh UPW supply nozzles. Run overflow rinsing while continuous resistivity data logging is active.

4. **In-Line Resistivity Endpoint & Unload**:
   - Monitor the in-line effluent coaxial conductivity/resistivity sensor downstream of Stage 3.
   - Continue overflow until the cell effluent recovers from ionic dip back to $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ (normalized to $25^\circ\text{C}$) and maintains stability for $\ge 30\text{ consecutive seconds}$.
   - Actuate pneumatic lift to extract the boat slowly under an ultra-pure filtered $N_2$ curtain into the Spin-Rinse Dryer (SRD) or Marangoni drying module.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Gate Limit | Measurement Method / Sensor |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Effluent Rinse Endpoint Resistivity** | $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ (stabilized $\ge 30\text{ s}$) | In-line temperature-compensated Pt/Toroidal cell probe at Stage 3 overflow drain |
| **Bath Operating Temperature** | $25.0^\circ\text{C}$ | $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ | Dual-redundant calibrated PT100 RTD in cascade tank manifold |
| **Wet Transfer Delay (Etch $\rightarrow$ Quench)** | $3.0\text{ s}$ | $\le 5.0\text{ s}$ maximum | Automated wet-bench robotic arm transfer timer |
| **Counter-Current UPW Volumetric Flow** | $12.0\text{ L/min}$ | $11.0 - 13.0\text{ L/min}$ | PFA ultrasonic transit-time liquid flowmeter |

---

### 4. Context Literature & Citations

1. **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
   - Chemical composition: $6\text{ parts } 40\%\text{ NH}_4\text{F}$ and $1\text{ part } 49\%\text{ HF}$.
   - Physical rates: Thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate at $25^\circ\text{C} \approx 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
   - Boundary controls: Constant pH maintenance, $0.1\%$ wetting agent (Triton X-100 or Fluorad) micro-trench displacement, and strict presence of calcium gluconate antidote gel.
2. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - Geometrical context: Transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, bitline contact interface, stacked capacitor over bitline (COB). Contaminant-free surfaces required to preserve dielectric integrity and retain cell leakage targets $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
3. **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**:
   - Mask selectivity: Stoichiometric $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ hard masks exhibit etch rates $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ in BOE, serving as chemical barriers during patterned dielectric oxide clearing.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Multi-stage cascade overflow rinsing must decouple wet bench hydrodynamic residence time from inline resistivity cell response delay. The downstream cell probe has an intrinsic 4-8 second transit lag; if resistivity endpoint gating triggers prematurely before boundary layer diffusion clears stagnant liquid pockets inside high-aspect-ratio wafer cassette slots, residual NH4F/HF dragout will carry over into subsequent drying stages, causing micro-corrosion and water mark defectivity.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Following surfactant-spiked BOE 6:1 oxide etch, the wafer surface exhibits mixed wettability (hydrophobic bare silicon or poly-Si exposed regions alongside hydrophilic residual oxide and fluorinated photoresist sidewalls). A minimum 3-stage cascade counter-current flow is required to displace fluorosurfactant micelles that adhere electrostatically to the photoresist. Effluent resistivity monitoring must recover to >= 18.0 MOhm-cm at 25°C with a stable plateau (drho/dt < 0.02 MOhm-cm/min) to guarantee sub-ppb ionic fluoride contamination.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-Pure Water (UPW) consumption in continuous overflow cascade tanks can exceed 15-20 L/min per weir. Without an automated quick-dump-rinse (QDR) pre-rinse or closed-loop proportional solenoid throttle governed by effluent resistivity thresholds, fab UPW polish loop polishers (mixed-bed deionizer resin beds) risk premature ionic saturation and high operational costs for DRAM Foundation VN Gen 1 pilot lines.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Rinse cycle duration directly impacts wet bench lot throughput. Cycle times exceeding 180 seconds bottle up the critical litho-etch-strip loop. Robust inline resistivity endpoint detection must replace fixed conservative timer schedules, shaving 45 seconds per wafer boat while securing unambiguous automated electronic batch record sign-off.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Stagnant chemical boundary layer entrapment within wafer-to-wafer pitch gaps (< 4.76 mm) leading to localized continuous oxide undercutting post-etch
1. Surfactant redeposition and drying-induced Marangoni ring/water mark formation across critical DRAM cell array patterns
1. Effluent resistivity sensor probe polarization or bio-fouling leading to false endpoint declaration and fluoride carryover into the drying chamber

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-1-01` | **Cascade Overflow Rinse Effluent Resistivity Recovery and Endpoint Gating Verification** | Inline temperature-compensated Thornton 0.01 cm^-1 cell constant resistivity sensor (Mettler Toledo M800 transmitter), PTFE flow-through cell at Stage 3 overflow weir, calibrated to ASTM D1125 at 25.0°C +/- 0.1°C. | 1. Submerge cassette into Stage 1 overflow weir; maintain continuous UPW upflow at 15 L/min for 45 s. 2. Index cassette to Stage 2 for 45 s. 3. Transfer cassette to Stage 3 final overflow weir equipped with inline resistivity probe. 4. Log resistivity data every 100 ms via automated SCADA DAQ. 5. Monitor resistivity transient from initial dip up to recovery threshold. 6. Assert steady-state resistivity and stability criteria for a continuous 30-second window prior to unlatching cassette lift. | `Effluent resistivity must reach >= 18.0 MOhm-cm within <= 120.0 seconds of Stage 3 immersion, with resistivity drift rate |drho/dt| <= 0.02 MOhm-cm/min sustained over 30 consecutive seconds.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-1-02` | **Post-Rinse Residual Fluoride Ion Chromatographic Extraction Metrology** | Dionex ICS-5000+ Ion Chromatography (IC) system with AS11-HC analytical column, UPW surface extraction bag/cell apparatus with Class 1 cleanroom sealed environment. | 1. Sample 3 sacrificial wafers from lot (slot 1, slot 13, slot 25). 2. Perform whole-wafer surface leaching using 10.0 mL of 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW sealed inside ultra-clean PTFE bag at 80°C for 30 minutes. 3. Decant leachate directly into pre-cleaned IC vial. 4. Inject 25 uL sample into Dionex IC system calibrated with 0.01 to 10 ppb F- analytical standards. 5. Quantify total extractable ionic fluoride areal density in ng/cm^2. | `Total surface ionic fluoride concentration must be <= 0.05 ng/cm^2 across all sampled slots; slot-to-slot non-uniformity (3-sigma) must not exceed 10%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavyweight fluoroelastomer/butyl rubber chemical apron (ASTM F739 tested), Nitrile inner gloves (6 mil) under heavy neoprene/butyl composite outer gauntlets (14 mil), Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield combined with ANSI Z87.1 certified splash goggles, Polypropylene chemical-resistant safety boots with steel toe and non-slip acid-resistant soles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium gluconate gel (2.5% USP) must be immediately accessible within 10 feet of the wet bench. In case of skin exposure to rinse effluent with suspected HF carryover, immediately strip contaminated clothing, flush affected area with copiously flowing water for 2 minutes, and massage calcium gluconate gel continuously into the skin until medical personnel arrive. For ocular contact, flush with sterile isotonic saline or eye wash for 15 minutes and seek emergency medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous lip exhaust slots along overflow weir edges maintaining capture face velocity of 0.5 to 0.7 m/s (100-140 FPM), connected to dedicated acid-scrubber exhaust header negative pressure interlocked at -125 Pa.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Stage 1 and Stage 2 concentrated overflow dumps route to dedicated HF-bearing industrial waste line for calcium fluoride (CaF2) precipitation dosing with hydrated lime (Ca(OH)2). Stage 3 high-purity effluent (> 16 MOhm-cm) is automatically diverted via 3-way pneumatic PTFE valve to the fab UPW reclaim loop.

| **Hydrofluoric Acid (trace carryover in rinse effluent)** | `7664-39-3` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI-C12) | `< 0.1 wt% (effluent carryover)` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (trace carryover in rinse effluent)** | `12125-01-8` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI-C12) | `< 0.5 wt% (effluent carryover)` |
| **Ultra-Pure Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM D5127 Type E-1.2 | `> 99.9999 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `20 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched pattern with surfactant-coated photoresist mask and exposed hydrophilic SiO2 or hydrophobic Si surface wet with residual BOE 6:1 solution.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Pristine, particle-free, deionized water-rinsed surface devoid of ionic fluorides and surfactant residues, fully prepared for Marangoni/IPA or spin-rinse drying.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes airborne boron/phosphorus and organic amine sorption onto moist hydrophilic surfaces, localized photoresist swelling, and irreversible staining/haze from evaporated HF droplets producing localized etch pitting.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete, automated execution of a 3-stage cascade overflow rinse protocol following BOE 6:1 dip-etch, verified by continuous real-time effluent resistivity recovery to >= 18.0 MOhm-cm and validated trace ionic fluoride surface contamination below 0.05 ng/cm^2.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CASCADE_RINSE_RESISTIVITY_LOG_TC22231.csv`
- [ ] `RINSE_ENDPOINT_METROLOGY_REPORT_TC22231.pdf`
- [ ] `SURFACE_EXTRACT_ION_CHROMATOGRAPHY_RUN_TC22231.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-01` | **Stage 3 overflow weir effluent resistivity at 25°C reaches baseline specification** | `18.10 MOhm-cm` | +0.10 / -0.10 MOhm-cm | Automated Thornton inline conductivity/resistivity sensor datalogger at Stage 3 weir exit |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total rinse effluent clearing time from Stage 1 immersion to Stage 3 qualification** | `120.0 seconds` | +15.0 / -10.0 seconds | Wet bench PLC sequence execution timer synced with resistivity threshold trigger |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-rinse whole-wafer surface residual fluoride ion concentration** | `0.030 ng/cm^2` | +0.020 / -0.015 ng/cm^2 | Ion chromatography (IC) analysis of thermal UPW extraction leachate from lot witness wafers |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Oxide Step-Height & Etch Uniformity Verification

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure specifies the metrological inspection protocol for verifying thermal silicon dioxide ($\text{SiO}_2$) step-height, residual film thickness, and etch uniformity following Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) immersion on 180nm generation DRAM wafers using Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (SE).

---

### 2. Metrology Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Wafer Load &      │
│       Alignment       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Spectroscopic     │
│     Ellipsometry      │
│      Calibration      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Post-BOE Oxide     │
│      Thickness &      │
│  Step-Height Mapping  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     Uniformity &      │
│      Selectivity      │
│      Calculation      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────◇───────────┐
│   Pass Acceptance     │
│       Criteria?       │
│                       │
└───────────◇───────────┘
            │
            ├────────────────────────────╮
         Yes│                            │No
            ▼                            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────────┐
│  Lot Release to Gate  │    │  Trigger OOC Hold &   │
│     Stack / LOCOS     │    │  Etch Recalibration   │
└───────────────────────┘    └───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Tool Initialization & Reference Calibration**:
   - Power on the spectroscopic ellipsometer light source (Xe arc lamp / broadband source, wavelength range: $250\text{ nm} - 850\text{ nm}$).
   - Perform system baseline calibration using an industry-certified calibration standard (native oxide on Si wafer). Verify baseline refractive index of the Si reference standard.
2. **Wafer Loading & Pattern Alignment**:
   - Transfer the post-BOE etched, cascade-overflow-rinsed, and spin-dried 180nm DRAM wafer onto the automated vacuum chuck.
   - Execute optical pattern recognition (PR) alignment targeting the 180nm DRAM cell array scribe-line metrology test pads (adjacent to the 180nm gate access channel $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ active areas).
3. **Multi-Point Ellipsometric Acquisition**:
   - Collect ellipsometric parameters $(\Psi, \Delta)$ across standard multi-point inspection patterns (minimum 49-point wafer map with 3 mm edge exclusion) at angles of incidence $\theta = 65^\circ, 70^\circ, 75^\circ$.
   - Acquire spectra on both etched $\text{SiO}_2$ recess regions and adjacent $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ hard mask reference features.
4. **Dispersion Modeling & Step-Height Extraction**:
   - Apply a robust optical dispersion model:
     - **$\text{SiO}_2$ Layer**: Cauchy model or Sellmeier dispersion with nominal refractive index target $n \approx 1.46$ at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$.
     - **$\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ Hard Mask**: Amorphous dielectric model target $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$.
   - Fit experimental $(\Psi, \Delta)$ curves to extract remaining oxide thickness $t_{\text{ox}}$ and calculate step-height differential $\Delta h = t_{\text{ox, pre}} - t_{\text{ox, post}}$.
5. **Etch Rate & Within-Wafer (WIW) Uniformity Determination**:
   - Compute the experimental etch rate:
     $$\text{Etch Rate} = \frac{\Delta h}{t_{\text{etch}}} \quad [\text{nm/min}]$$
   - Calculate Within-Wafer (WIW) etch non-uniformity:
     $$\text{Non-Uniformity (\%)} = \frac{t_{\text{max}} - t_{\text{min}}}{2 \times t_{\text{mean}}} \times 100\%$$
   - Calculate hard mask selectivity ratio $S = \text{Etch Rate}_{\text{SiO}_2} / \text{Etch Rate}_{\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4}$.
6. **Pass/Fail Disposition**:
   - If all criteria meet specifications, release the lot to downstream processing (stacked capacitor / gate stack dielectric formation).
   - If parameters violate acceptance limits, flag an Out-of-Control (OOC) hold, inspect for micro-trench bubble entrapment or bath depletion, and alert chemical processing engineers.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                            ┌──────────────────────────┐
                            │░░                        │
  WIW Non-Uniformity Max (%)┤░░                        │
                            │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                   │
       BOE Bath Temp (deg C)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                   │
Si3N4 Mask Loss Max (nm/min)┤▓                         │
                            │▓                         │
 BOE SiO2 Etch Rate (nm/min)┤██████████████████████████│
                            │██████████████████████████│
                            └┬─────┬──────┬─────┬─────┬┘
                             0    25     50    75   100 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target | Tolerance / Specification Limit | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Thermally Grown $\text{SiO}_2$ Etch Rate** | $100$ | $100 \pm 5$ ($1000 \pm 50$) | $\text{nm/min}$ ($\text{\AA/min}$) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Timed Dip |
| **$\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ Mask Etch Loss Rate** | $< 0.5$ | $\le 0.5$ | $\text{nm/min}$ | SE Thin Film Fit ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$) |
| **Within-Wafer (WIW) Etch Non-Uniformity** | $\le 2.5$ | $\le 3.0$ | $\%$ ($1\sigma$) | 49-point SE Map Analysis |
| **Etch Bath Temperature** | $25.0$ | $25.0 \pm 0.5$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | In-situ Thermocouple Sensor |

---

### 5. Context Literature Citations
* **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
  - Formulated as $6:1$ ratio of $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ to $49\%\ \text{HF}$.
  - Established thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate baseline of $\sim 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$. Constant pH maintenance ensures uniform dissolution.
* **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**:
  - Dense amorphous hard mask film characterized by refractive index $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$.
  - Confirmed etch resistance to BOE with hard mask removal rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$, ensuring high etch selectivity ($> 200:1$) over $\text{SiO}_2$.
* **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Contextual integration for 180nm unit cell geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ access transistor channels) where precise oxide recess step-heights govern dielectric barrier formation and bitline contact plug clearance.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Optical spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) provides non-destructive, sub-angstrom film thickness and refractive index extraction, but extracting step-height post-BOE requires dedicated open-frame test macro pads (minimum 80x80 um spot clearance) to decouple bulk unetched thermal/CVD SiO2 thickness from etched trench recess. Automated coordinate registration must synchronize with the wafer notch aligner to eliminate spot overlap on photoresist sidewalls, which causes beam scattering, depolarisation spikes, and spurious optical fitting convergence.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Modeling patterned or partially etched wet oxide surfaces requires rigorous dispersion formulation. A standard single-layer Cauchy or Sellmeier model fails if surface microroughness (RMS > 1.5 nm) or chemical sub-stoichiometric fluorinated oxy-hydride transition layers exist post-BOE rinse. The metrology recipe must incorporate an effective medium approximation (Bruggeman EMA, 50% void / 50% SiO2) top layer to maintain Goodness of Fit (GoF > 0.985) and decouple interfacial roughness from actual etched step-height.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring production-grade spectroscopic ellipsometry tool time or capital acquisition (e.g., J.A. Woollam M-2000 or KLA ASET series) entails lead times of 16-24 weeks and high cleanroom bay installation costs. NIST-traceable thermal SiO2 reference calibration standards (certified 25 nm, 100 nm, 500 nm wafer standards) must be budgeted and maintained under scheduled recalibration contracts to prevent tool-to-tool optical drift across foundry lot signoffs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology queue times represent a primary bottleneck directly preceding photoresist stripping. A 49-point wafer mapping scan takes approximately 4 to 6 minutes per wafer; high-density lot sampling will throttle the wet bench throughput if queue-time constraints to resist strip/bake are tight. A hybrid 9-point monitor for inline pilot wafers and 49-point mapping for qualification lots balances cycle-time budgets without sacrificing cross-wafer uniformity traceability.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Optical beam spot clipping on patterned photoresist step boundaries, introducing polarization depolarization (> 5%) and erroneous step-height divergence > 15 nm.
1. Dispersion parameter correlation between film thickness (d) and refractive index (n) at thin oxide regimes (< 10 nm), yielding false over-etch calculations due to unconstrained Cauchy model fitting.
1. Native oxide regrowing and atmospheric organic airborne molecular contamination (AMC) accumulating during extended Q-time delays, skewing measured etch depth by +0.5 to +1.2 nm.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-2-01` | **Dual-Site Absolute Oxide Step-Height & Etch Depth Verification** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (Rotating Compensator Ellipsometer, spectral range 245-1000 nm, focused micro-spot 50x50 um, integrated high-precision motorized XY stage) | 1. Align wafer notch and load wafer onto vacuum chuck at 21.0 ± 0.5 °C. 2. Navigate micro-spot beam to unetched oxide test macro pad (80x80 um, PR-protected). 3. Acquire Psi and Delta spectra across 245-1000 nm at 65, 70, and 75 degree incident angles. 4. Fit unetched SiO2 thickness using standard Sellmeier dispersion model. 5. Move stage to adjacent open-window etched oxide macro pad (80x80 um). 6. Acquire spectral polarization data and fit remaining SiO2 thickness with Bruggeman EMA surface roughness model. 7. Compute step-height as: h_step = d_unetched - d_etched. | `Goodness of Fit (GoF) >= 0.990 on both sites; calculated step-height h_step matches target etch recipe depth within ±3.0 nm (e.g., target 120.0 nm step requires measured 117.0 nm to 123.0 nm); polarization depolarization < 2.0%.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-2-02` | **49-Point Full-Wafer Etch Uniformity & Radial Non-Uniformity Verification** | Automated Production Spectroscopic Ellipsometer with 200mm wafer handler and automated pattern recognition vision system | 1. Load wafer automatically from FOUP/cassette to vacuum stage. 2. Execute automated pattern recognition on global fiducials to establish zero-offset coordinates. 3. System sequentially measures 49 predefined test sites distributed across concentric radial zones (center, 30 mm, 60 mm, 90 mm radius). 4. For each site, record remaining oxide thickness (d_i) and GoF. 5. - **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Class 1 laser / UV broadband optical tool with interlocked enclosure. critics.systems_engineer: Optical spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) provides non-destructive, sub-angstrom film thickness and refractive index extraction, but extracting step-height post-BOE requires dedicated open-frame test macro pads (minimum 80x80 um spot clearance) to decouple bulk unetched thermal/CVD SiO2 thickness from etched trench recess. Automated coordinate registration must synchronize with the wafer notch aligner to eliminate spot overlap on photoresist sidewalls, which causes beam scattering, depolarisation spikes, and spurious optical fitting convergence.
critics.domain_expert: Modeling patterned or partially etched wet oxide surfaces requires rigorous dispersion formulation. A standard single-layer Cauchy or Sellmeier model fails if surface microroughness (RMS > 1.5 nm) or chemical sub-stoichiometric fluorinated oxy-hydride transition layers exist post-BOE rinse. The metrology recipe must incorporate an effective medium approximation (Bruggeman EMA, 50% void / 50% SiO2) top layer to maintain Goodness of Fit (GoF > 0.985) and decouple interfacial roughness from actual etched step-height.
critics.supply_chain: Procuring production-grade spectroscopic ellipsometry tool time or capital acquisition (e.g., J.A. Woollam M-2000 or KLA ASET series) entails lead times of 16-24 weeks and high cleanroom bay installation costs. NIST-traceable thermal SiO2 reference calibration standards (certified 25 nm, 100 nm, 500 nm wafer standards) must be budgeted and maintained under scheduled recalibration contracts to prevent tool-to-tool optical drift across foundry lot signoffs.
critics.laya_pm: Metrology queue times represent a primary bottleneck directly preceding photoresist stripping. A 49-point wafer mapping scan takes approximately 4 to 6 minutes per wafer; high-density lot sampling will throttle the wet bench throughput if queue-time constraints to resist strip/bake are tight. A hybrid 9-point monitor for inline pilot wafers and 49-point mapping for qualification lots balances cycle-time budgets without sacrificing cross-wafer uniformity traceability.
critical_failure_modes: Optical beam spot clipping on patterned photoresist step boundaries, introducing polarization depolarization (> 5%) and erroneous step-height divergence > 15 nm.
Dispersion parameter correlation between film thickness (d) and refractive index (n) at thin oxide regimes (< 10 nm), yielding false over-etch calculations due to unconstrained Cauchy model fitting.
Native oxide regrowing and atmospheric organic airborne molecular contamination (AMC) accumulating during extended Q-time delays, skewing measured etch depth by +0.5 to +1.2 nm.

nodes.label: Post-BOE Photoresist Undercut & Adhesion Interface Metrology via CD-SEM
nodes.sop_content:
# SOP: Post-BOE Photoresist Undercut & Adhesion Interface Metrology via CD-SEM

**Hierarchy Level:** Gen 2 (µm) | Metrology  
**Module Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning > Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse > Multi-Stage Cascade Overflow Rinse and Resist Adhesion Metrology  
**Action Type:** Make / Metrology Characterization  

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Wafer Vacuum Mount &  │
│       Load Lock        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Low-kV Beam Setup &   │
│   Focus Calibration    │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Resist Profile &    │
│     Pitch Top-Down     │
│       Inspection       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Tilted Stage      │
│       Undercut &       │
│      Delamination      │
│       Metrology        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Acceptance Gate &    │
│   Recipe Disposition   │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Handling & Chamber Loading:**
   - Retrieve the processed wafer immediately following the cascade DI overflow rinse and complete drying cycle.
   - Verify that the dehydration and HMDS silylation steps were executed prior to coating to ensure resist adhesion integrity.
   - Transfer the 100mm wafer onto the CD-SEM load-lock stage using cleanroom vacuum wands; pump down the chamber to standard vacuum operating pressure ($< 1 \times 10^{-4}\text{ Pa}$).

2. **Beam Setup & Anti-Charging Calibration:**
   - Configure electron gun parameters for non-destructive organic photoresist inspection:
     - Accelerating voltage: $0.8\text{ kV} - 1.2\text{ kV}$ (low landing energy to prevent Shipley 1813 film shrinkage or burning).
     - Probe current: $\le 10\text{ pA}$.
   - Auto-calibrate astigmatism and focus on a non-critical peripheral alignment mark.

3. **Top-Down Critical Dimension (CD) & Alignment Inspection:**
   - Translate stage to the target Gen 2 test array and alignment fiducials across 5-point inspection sites (Center, North, South, East, West).
   - Capture top-down secondary electron (SE) images to verify feature pitch and lateral overlay alignment against pre-etch reticle layout.
   - Measure residual photoresist mask width and inspect for gross film peel-off or lifting at line-ends.

4. **Tilted Stage Interface & Undercut Measurement:**
   - Tilt the eucentric SEM stage to $30^\circ - 45^\circ$ along the cleaved cross-section or line edge trench to expose the $\text{SiO}_2$/photoresist boundary.
   - Measure the lateral undercut profile beneath the Shipley 1813 resist footing generated by isotropic BOE etching ($100\text{ nm/min}$ nominal oxide etch rate).
   - Evaluate the methyl-siloxane adhesion footprint to confirm absence of acid penetration/trenching or resist delamination notches.

5. **Data Logging & Wafer Unload:**
   - Record measured CD line width, lateral undercut ratio, and remaining resist thickness across all test sites.
   - Vent the load-lock chamber with dry $\text{N}_2$ and transfer the wafer to the next photoresist strip or oxide inspection station.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter / Target Metric | Acceptance Criteria Target Value | Physical Units | Tolerance / Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Resist Film Thickness** | `1.30` | $\mu\text{m}$ | $\pm 15\text{ nm}$ across 100mm wafer |
| **Gen 2 Alignment Overlay** | $\le 5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | Upper specification limit ($\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$) |
| **Lateral Oxide Undercut Rate** | `100` | $\text{nm/minute}$ | $\pm 10\text{ nm/minute}$ (referenced to $1000\text{ \AA/min}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$) |
| **Resist Interfacial Delamination** | `0` (Zero peel-off / no footing lift) | $\mu\text{m}$ | Continuous methyl-siloxane bonded boundary |

---

### Literature Context Citations

- **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE):**
  - *Etch Kinetics & Formulation:* BOE (6:1) consists of 6 parts $40\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{F}$ and 1 part $49\%\ \text{HF}$, exhibiting a thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate of approximately $100\text{ nm/minute}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$. Constant pH and uniform etch rates are maintained via buffer equilibrium.
  - *Wetting & Interface Protection:* Wetting agent ($0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad) eliminates micro-trench bubble entrapment; HMDS vapor priming is required at $120^\circ\text{C}$ to prevent resist adhesion failure and peel-off during acid exposure.
- **Source: Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming:**
  - *Film Uniformity & Profile:* Shipley 1813 spin-coated at $4000\text{ RPM}$ delivers $1.30\ \mu\text{m} \pm 15\text{ nm}$ uniform film across 100mm wafers.
  - *Surface Chemistry:* Reactively silylates hydrophilic silanol ($-\text{Si-OH}$) into hydrophobic methyl-siloxane ($-\text{Si-O-Si(CH}_3)_3$) bonds, ensuring resistance against isotropic under-etch lifting.
- **Source: Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018):**
  - *Process Alignment & Film Geometry:* Gen 2 lithography alignment tolerance targets $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ with Shipley 1813 resist (~$1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ nominal thickness).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-BOE metrology via CD-SEM introduces high electrostatic discharge (ESD) and local e-beam charge accumulation risks on insulating SiO2 structures, which can distort secondary electron line-scan profiles and yield false critical dimension (CD) measurements. Low accelerating voltage (0.8-1.2 kV) with beam current <= 10 pA must be integrated into the automated recipe, coupled with active wafer de-charging or tilt-beam imaging (5-15 deg) to accurately resolve retrograde photoresist footing versus genuine isotropic oxide undercutting without inducing severe hydrocarbon polymerization/carbon deposition along measured feature sidewalls.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In Gen 1 (mm/sub-mm test structures targeting scaled 180nm nodes), wet isotropic BOE 6:1 etches thermally grown or CVD SiO2 uniformly at ~100 nm/min, yielding an intrinsic 1:1 lateral-to-vertical undercut ratio. If HMDS vapor prime adhesion was suboptimal or cascade rinsing failed to quench HF instantaneously, capillary stress and lateral boundary peeling will manifest as catastrophic resist lifting exceeding 2.0x oxide thickness. CD-SEM line-scan algorithm thresholds (50% threshold vs maximum slope derivative) must be calibrated against cross-sectional FIB-SEM to differentiate resist profile retraction from buried oxide cavity boundaries under top-down illumination.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dedicated in-line CD-SEM tools (e.g., Hitachi S-9380 or Applied Materials NanoSEM) have extremely high capital depreciation and require specialized single-wafer load locks. For open-source lab environments without dedicated fab CD-SEM clusters, contingency protocols using standard analytical FE-SEM equipped with calibrated tilted stages and low-vacuum/charge-compensation modes must be qualified to prevent operational bottlenecks caused by proprietary SEM downtime or delayed calibration standard tip replacements.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput directly bottlenecks wet bench cycle time. If wafers linger prior to CD-SEM inspection, residual fluoride trace contamination or ambient moisture uptake will degrade resist integrity prior to strip. The inspection loop must be limited to 5 site-measurements per wafer across 3 die locations within 30 minutes of cascade rinse dry, ensuring rapid go/no-go gating for the subsequent photoresist ash/strip sequence without stalling the front-end lot flow.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Electron beam-induced photoresist shrinkage and carbon contamination during repeated high-magnification CD-SEM beam rastering, distorting apparent undercut dimension by >15%.
1. Severe surface charging on un-cleared dielectric field regions causing spatial beam deflection, image astigmatism, and catastrophic line-scan edge-detection algorithm failure.
1. Capillary force-induced photoresist pattern collapse and unpeeling at wet rinse drying stage misinterpreted as excessive chemical undercut.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-3-01` | **Top-Down Low-Voltage CD-SEM Undercut & Bias Evaluation** | In-line Low-Voltage Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscope (CD-SEM, Hitachi S-9220/S-9380 equivalent) with 800V extraction potential, calibrated magnification standard (NIST-traceable 100nm pitch grating) | 1. Load wafer into CD-SEM chamber; align wafer using global optical fiducial crosshairs. 2. Navigate to primary 1.0 mm test grating structures at center, mid-radius, and edge dies (5 points total). 3. Set beam acceleration to 0.8 kV, beam current to 8 pA, working distance to 3.0 mm. 4. Acquire secondary electron top-down image at 50,000x magnification across 5 distinct line-space pairs. 5. Execute automated threshold edge-detection algorithm: extract top resist width (CD_top) and bottom oxide foot width (CD_bottom). 6. Calculate lateral undercut delta = (CD_top - CD_bottom) / 2. | `Lateral undercut per edge must be <= 1.15x nominal vertical oxide etch depth (target <= 115 nm for 100 nm vertical etched step); edge roughness 3-sigma variation < 15 nm across all 5 die locations. Complete absence of resist delamination/peeling.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-3-02` | **Tilted-Beam Multi-Angle Resist-Oxide Adhesion Interface Profilometry** | Field Emission SEM (FE-SEM) equipped with a 5-axis eucentric motorized tilt stage (-5 to +45 deg tilt) and high-resolution through-the-lens secondary electron (SE) detector | 1. Position stage at wafer center test pattern array. 2. Tilt specimen stage to 15.0 deg tilt angle relative to electron optical axis while tracking eucentric height. 3. Adjust dynamic focus and stigmation at 1.0 kV accelerating voltage to resolve the three-dimensional photoresist foot interface. 4. Measure physical contact angle and gap distance between the bottom edge of Shipley 1813 resist and the underlying SiO2 interface. 5. Inspect resist anchor perimeter over a 100 um continuous line length for micro-buckling, notch cavities, or interfacial blistering. | `Resist-to-oxide adhesion interface gap must be 0.0 nm (no interfacial delamination or lifting visible at 80,000x resolution); resist sidewall profile slope must maintain >= 75 degrees; zero micro-voids or peeling notches detected over 100 um line scan.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-absorbing safety glasses with side shields, Electrostatic discharge (ESD) cleanroom coat and conductive heel straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For nitrogen asphyxiation hazard in confined equipment service chase: Immediately move victim to fresh air; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing has stopped; summon emergency medical services. For minor IPA eye/skin contact: Flush affected area with clean DI water eye-wash or wash station for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: High-vacuum turbomolecular pumping system backed by dry scroll pump; vacuum exhaust routed directly to dedicated cleanroom facility house tool exhaust (>= 15 SCFM negative pressure ducting) to prevent VOC or dry nitrogen buildup in operating bay.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: No active chemical wet waste generated at CD-SEM tool. Pre-cleaned IPA lint-free wipe consumables must be disposed of in designated sealed flammable/hazardous solid waste receptacles.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Ultra-High Purity 99.999% for SEM vent cycles)** | `7727-37-9` | UHP Grade 5.0 | `>= 99.999%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Analytical chamber wipe solvent)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly cascade-rinsed and spin-dried hydrophobic/hydrophilic patterned SiO2/Si substrate with intact Shipley 1813 photoresist mask; zero droplet stain residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electron-beam evaluated wafer surface ready for plasma photoresist strip/ash; localized inspection sites subjected to < 10 pA dose with negligible hydrocarbon deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air Q-time (> 30 min) causes atmospheric moisture absorption and airborne organosilicon contamination along exposed BOE undercut trenches, inducing resist footprint relaxation and invalidating post-etch CD metrology repeatability.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable CD-SEM metrology characterization confirming isotropic wet oxide undercut conforms strictly to BOE 6:1 kinetic specifications (1:1 aspect ratio relative to etch depth) with robust photoresist-to-oxide adhesion interface and complete absence of pattern delamination.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `METROLOGY_CD_SEM_UNDERCUT_RUN_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `CD_SEM_INTERFACIAL_INSPECTION_DOSSIER.pdf`
- [ ] `CALIBRATED_LINE_SCAN_TOP_DOWN_IMAGES.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean lateral isotropic oxide undercut per side does not exceed calibrated vertical etch target + tolerance limit** | `100.0 nm` | +/- 15.0 nm | 5-point automated secondary electron line-scan edge-detection algorithm via CD-SEM |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Interfacial photoresist delamination/foot separation along the SiO2 boundary must be zero across all evaluated structures** | `0.0 nm` | + 0.0 nm | 15-degree tilted-stage high-magnification FE-SEM inspection at 80,000x |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal acceptance requires five-point CD-SEM undercut average within 100 +/- 15 nm, zero visible resist lifting across 100% of tested die line-space arrays, and engineering signoff appended to METROLOGY_CD_SEM_UNDERCUT_RUN_DATA.csv prior to releasing lot to downstream dry oxygen plasma photoresist strip.

testcases.instrumentation: In-line Low-Voltage Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscope (CD-SEM, Hitachi S-9220/S-9380 equivalent) with 800V extraction potential, calibrated magnification standard (NIST-traceable 100nm pitch grating)
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer has completed BOE 6:1 timed etch, 5-stage cascade DI overflow rinse (resistivity > 18.0 MOhm-cm), and spin-rinse dry; surface inspected for gross peeling under optical dark-field microscopy; load-lock vacuum <= 5e-6 Torr.
testcases.procedure: 1. Load wafer into CD-SEM chamber; align wafer using global optical fiducial crosshairs. 2. Navigate to primary 1.0 mm test grating structures at center, mid-radius, and edge dies (5 points total). 3. Set beam acceleration to 0.8 kV, beam current to 8 pA, working distance to 3.0 mm. 4. Acquire secondary electron top-down image at 50,000x magnification across 5 distinct line-space pairs. 5. Execute automated threshold edge-detection algorithm: extract top resist width (CD_top) and bottom oxide foot width (CD_bottom). 6. Calculate lateral undercut delta = (CD_top - CD_bottom) / 2.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Lateral undercut per edge must be <= 1.15x nominal vertical oxide etch depth (target <= 115 nm for 100 nm vertical etched step); edge roughness 3-sigma variation < 15 nm across all 5 die locations. Complete absence of resist delamination/peeling.

testcases.title: Tilted-Beam Multi-Angle Resist-Oxide Adhesion Interface Profilometry
testcases.instrumentation: Field Emission SEM (FE-SEM) equipped with a 5-axis eucentric motorized tilt stage (-5 to +45 deg tilt) and high-resolution through-the-lens secondary electron (SE) detector
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer successfully cleared TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-2-3-3-01 top-down screening; vacuum chamber pressure <= 1e-6 Torr; stage tilt calibration verified at 0 deg baseline.
testcases.procedure: 1. Position stage at wafer center test pattern array. 2. Tilt specimen stage to 15.0 deg tilt angle relative to electron optical axis while tracking eucentric height. 3. Adjust dynamic focus and stigmation at 1.0 kV accelerating voltage to resolve the three-dimensional photoresist foot interface. 4. Measure physical contact angle and gap distance between the bottom edge of Shipley 1813 resist and the underlying SiO2 interface. 5. Inspect resist anchor perimeter over a 100 um continuous line length for micro-buckling, notch cavities, or interfacial blistering.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Resist-to-oxide adhesion interface gap must be 0.0 nm (no interfacial delamination or lifting visible at 80,000x resolution); resist sidewall profile slope must maintain >= 75 degrees; zero micro-voids or peeling notches detected over 100 um line scan.

ppe_required: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-absorbing safety glasses with side shields
Electrostatic discharge (ESD) cleanroom coat and conductive heel straps

cas_chemicals.name: Compressed Nitrogen (Ultra-High Purity 99.999% for SEM vent cycles)

ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For nitrogen asphyxiation hazard in confined equipment service chase: Immediately move victim to fresh air; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing has stopped; summon emergency medical services. For minor IPA eye/skin contact: Flush affected area with clean DI water eye-wash or wash station for 15 minutes.
