nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Calibration Standard Step-Height Verification & Stylus Tracking Setup

**Node & Architecture:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Process Level:** Gen 2 ($\mu$m) | Metrology  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180NM-CAL-002`

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Mount Calibration    │
│    Standard & Level    │
│         Stage          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Configure Stylus    │
│    Force & Tracking    │
│         Speed          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Execute Reference    │
│       Step Scan        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Cross-Check Metric &  │
│  Alignment Tolerance   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Mounting & Stage Leveling:**
   - Secure the certified reference step-height calibration standard onto the contact profilometer vacuum chuck or macroscopic stage.
   - Use the optical alignment camera to level the standard, ensuring the scan vector is perpendicular ($90^\circ \pm 0.5^\circ$) to the calibration ridge edge.
   - Align stage coordinates ensuring feature positioning conforms within Gen 2 alignment limits.

2. **Stylus Parameter & Tracking Setup:**
   - Initialize stylus contact tracking with a low tracking force ($\le 15\text{ mg}$) to prevent ridge gouging or standard degradation.
   - Set scan profile length ($L \ge 200\,\mu\text{m}$) across the reference step edge with a scan speed $\le 10\,\mu\text{m/s}$.
   - Ensure the stylus tracking filter is configured to isolate low-frequency topography from high-frequency acoustic/environmental noise.

3. **Calibration Scan Execution:**
   - Execute five ($5$) consecutive forward and reverse profile runs across the certified step boundary.
   - Acquire trace profiles and perform baseline two-point linear tilt subtraction across planar reference flatlands on both sides of the step.

4. **Cross-Check & Tool Calibration Factor Calculation:**
   - Compute mean step-height $H_{\text{meas}}$ and standard deviation $\sigma_H$.
   - Calculate instrument calibration correction factor $C_f = H_{\text{nominal}} / H_{\text{meas}}$.
   - Update profilometer acquisition software calibration matrix prior to wafer oxide step-height (BOE 6:1 post-etch) profiling.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                     Metrology Calibration & Baseline Metric References
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░          │
     Gate Ox Ref (nm)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░          │
                     │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒          │
   EOT Stack Ref (nm)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒          │
Resist Thick Ref (um)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                        │
                     │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                        │
 Gen 2 Align Tol (um)┤█████████████████████████████████│
                     │█████████████████████████████████│
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0.0     1.2     2.5     3.8    5.0 
```

| Metric ID | Parameter | Nominal / Target Spec | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-MET-01** | Stage Lateral Alignment Tolerance | $\pm 5\,\mu\text{m}$ | Optical stage encoder / reticle crosshair check |
| **AC-MET-02** | Photoresist Step Reference Thickness | $1.3\,\mu\text{m}$ (Nominal Shipley 1813 baseline) | Profilometric step profile check across resist edge |
| **AC-MET-03** | Gate Dielectric Equivalent Target Reference | $3.5\,\text{ nm}$ | Baseline instrument vertical sensitivity validation |
| **AC-MET-04** | Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT) Capacitor Reference | $3\text{ to }4\,\text{ nm}$ | Calibration linearity check across thin-film domain |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Citations

1. **Alignment Tolerance & Resist Thickness Reference:**
   - *Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)*:
     - *"Alignment tolerance at Gen 1 is $\pm 100\text{ microns}$ ($0.1\text{ mm}$), improving to $\pm 5\text{ microns}$ in Gen 2."*
     - *"Photoresist: Shipley 1813 spin-coated at 4000 RPM yields $\sim 1.3\text{ micron}$ thickness."*
2. **Dielectric Thickness & Channel Geometry Limits:**
   - *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*:
     - *"Gate dielectric is thermally grown silicon dioxide ($\text{SiO}_2$) at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness."*
     - *"Stacked capacitors (Crown or Cylinder type) utilize silicon nitride ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$) or tantalum pentoxide ($\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$) high-k dielectrics with equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) around $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$."*
3. **Channel Dimensions:**
   - *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*:
     - Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Linear stage Abbe errors and mechanical compliance in the custom Gen 1 4040 aluminum/MGN12H profilometer drive can introduce tilt and apparent curvature when scanning calibration standards. Mechanical isolation pads (sorbothane/neoprene) must decouple ambient vibrations >30 Hz, and closed-loop linear optical/magnetic encoders must verify scan velocity uniformity to prevent artificial baseline slopes or distorted step-height readings.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating stylus tracking dynamics requires balancing stylus force (target 5-15 mg) against stylus tip radius (typically 2.0 to 12.5 um) to avoid plastic deformation or scratching of soft gold/aluminum calibration standards or post-etch photoresist/oxide steps. The step-height standard (nominal 100 nm to 1000 nm calibrated range traceable to NIST/PTB) must undergo leveling (two-point linear baseline subtraction) to differentiate true vertical step height from sample wedge tilt.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Certified NIST-traceable step-height standards (such as VLSI Standards / Applied Physics silicon step standards with certified SiO2 on Si steps) have long lead times and require strict calibration certificates. High-purity isopropyl alcohol and dry nitrogen guns for non-contact blow-off cleaning must be kept in stock to prevent organic deposition on certified step trenches without introducing abrasive damage.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration and baseline verification are gating steps for the entire post-BOE oxide etch qualification pipeline. Delays in standard certification or unverified stylus tracking will bottleneck oxide etch rate determination, stall photoresist selectivity measurements, and introduce systematic errors into subsequent gate dielectric integration cycles.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Excessive stylus tracking force causing permanent plastic scratching or micro-grooving across the calibration step standard, permanently invalidating its certified step height.
1. Mechanical stage vibration or pitch/yaw errors exceeding baseline noise tolerances, leading to step-height measurement errors greater than +/- 2% of the certified calibration value.
1. Organic contamination or particulate deposition at the standard step edge producing false edge peak transients and distorted leveling baseline calculations.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-2-1-01` | **NIST-Traceable Step-Height Calibration Standard Accuracy & Linearity Verification** | Contact Profilometer (stylus radius 2.5 um, calibrated force 10 mg), NIST-traceable SiO2/Si calibration standard (certified step height 180.0 nm +/- 1.0 nm), active vibration isolation table. | 1. Mount certified 180.0 nm step standard on profilometer vacuum chuck. 2. Align scan trajectory orthogonal to step edge (+/- 0.5 degrees). 3. Set scan length to 1000 um, scan speed to 20 um/s, stylus force to 10 mg. 4. Execute 5 independent scans across the calibrated step trench. 5. Perform baseline tilt leveling using reference flat zones on both sides of the step. 6. Compute mean step height and standard deviation across all 5 scans. | `Mean measured step height must be 180.0 nm +/- 3.0 nm (within +/- 1.67% of certified value); 1-sigma repeatability across 5 scans must be <= 1.5 nm.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-2-1-02` | **Stylus Dynamic Tracking Force & Baseline Noise Level Cross-Check** | Contact Profilometer, precision quartz optical flat (surface roughness Ra < 0.5 nm), analytical micro-balance / calibrated load cell sensor. | 1. Position stylus over quartz optical flat. 2. Set nominal stylus force to 10.0 mg and calibrate via internal sensor/counterweight mechanism. 3. Lower stylus onto surface and record static vertical baseline noise for 30 seconds with stage stationary. 4. Run dynamic scan of 2000 um length at 25 um/s across optical flat. 5. Verify absence of stylus bounce, resonance oscillation, or surface scoring using post-scan 100x optical microscope inspection. | `Static baseline noise floor must have Rq <= 0.8 nm; dynamic scan profile Ra must be <= 1.2 nm without resonant ringing or cyclic ripple; post-scan optical inspection must show 0 visible scratch tracks on the quartz reference flat.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Cleanroom ESD coat / antistatic smock
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin or eye contact with IPA rinse solvent, flush immediately with copious amounts of clean deionized water for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, remove affected person to fresh air. If irritation or dizziness persists, seek medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted within laminar flow cleanroom hood or cleanroom environment with HEPA filtration (minimum 0.45 m/s face velocity) and local solvent exhaust snorkel for IPA wipe preparation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and IPA rinses must be collected in closed, grounded, flame-resistant flammable solvent waste containers labeled with CAS 67-63-0; do not dispose down acid or standard aqueous drains.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Cleanroom Grade (>= 99.8%) | `100%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Compressed)** | `7727-37-9` | High Purity Clean Dry Nitrogen (Grade 5.0, 99.999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched and cascade-rinsed wafer with patterned SiO2 features, blown dry with filtered N2, free of liquid droplets or residual BOE acid film.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated contact profilometer verified with NIST step standard; ready for production wafer micro-trench and oxide step-height acquisition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding clean air queue time causes airborne particulate and hydrocarbon deposition onto wafer and standard surfaces, producing false step-height spikes, stylus dragging, and calibration drift.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration and dynamic tracking qualification of the contact profilometer using a certified NIST-traceable step-height standard, establishing verified vertical measurement accuracy, noise floor compliance, and non-destructive stylus force settings for post-BOE oxide step-height metrology.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CAL_STEP_VERIFICATION_CERT_TC_2_2_3_2_1.pdf`
- [ ] `PROFILOMETER_NOISE_FLOOR_AND_REPEATABILITY_RAW.csv`
- [ ] `STANDARD_SURFACE_POST_CAL_OPTICAL_INSPECTION.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Calibrated step-height measurement deviation from certified NIST reference standard value** | `180.0 nm` | +/- 3.0 nm | 5-point leveled step-height profilometry line scan across certified standard |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Static profilometer baseline root-mean-square vertical noise floor (Rq)** | `0.5 nm` | <= 0.8 nm | 30-second stationary stylus vertical position data sampling at 100 Hz on quartz optical flat |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Stylus applied tracking force repeatability and accuracy** | `10.0 mg` | +/- 1.0 mg | Precision micro-force calibration gauge measurement prior to scan cycle |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Five consecutive step-height measurements of the certified 180.0 nm standard yield a mean value between 177.0 nm and 183.0 nm with standard deviation <= 1.5 nm, baseline noise floor Rq <= 0.8 nm, and optical microscopy confirming zero surface scratching or residue on the standard.

Set scan length to 1000 um, scan speed to 20 um/s, stylus force to 10 mg. 4. Execute 5 independent scans across the calibrated step trench. 5. testcases.title: Stylus Dynamic Tracking Force & Baseline Noise Level Cross-Check
testcases.instrumentation: Contact Profilometer, precision quartz optical flat (surface roughness Ra < 0.5 nm), analytical micro-balance / calibrated load cell sensor.
testcases.pre_conditions: Quartz optical flat cleaned with VLSI-grade IPA and dried with filtered N2; profilometer acoustic hood closed; environmental baseline vibration < 0.05 um/s RMS.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-180NM-042`
**Title:** Patterned Oxide Micro-Trench Stylus Profilometry Scan Execution  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Metrology > Contact Profilometer Oxide Step-Height Verification  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Stage Vacuum &     │
│  Leveling Cross-Check  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Stylus Tip & Scan    │
│    Parameters Setup    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Micro-Trench Profile  │
│       Traversal        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Baseline Leveling &   │
│      Step-Height       │
│       Extraction       │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Loading & Chuck Vacuum Lock:**
   - Transfer the post-BOE patterned wafer onto the profilometer motorized vacuum chuck.
   - Engage chuck vacuum (> 80 kPa) and verify wafer planarity under the integrated high-magnification optical alignment camera.
2. **Alignment & Calibration Standard Verification:**
   - Perform an initial cross-check scan across an on-stage certified calibration step standard to ensure the LVDT/optical deflection sensor operates with linearity within certified tolerances before wafer measurement.
   - Align the optics to the patterned micro-trench test structure array adjacent to the memory cell array block.
3. **Scan Recipe Configuration:**
   - Configure stylus scan parameters:
     - Scan length: $50\text{ }\mu\text{m} - 100\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ orthogonal to the etched micro-trench lines.
     - Stylus tracking force: $\le 1.0\text{ mg}$ (to prevent resist gouging or scratching).
     - Scan speed: $2.0\text{ }\mu\text{m/s}$ to ensure high lateral spatial point density.
4. **Scan Execution & Profile Acquisition:**
   - Lower the diamond stylus tip onto the unetched reference plateau at least $10\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ prior to the trench edge.
   - Execute the forward profilometer scan across the patterned oxide trench into the etched recess and out onto the opposite reference plane.
5. **Data Post-Processing & Step-Height Determination:**
   - Apply two-point linear tilt subtraction leveling using the unetched reference planes.
   - Measure the vertical step height ($\Delta Z$) between the baseline plateau and the flat bottom of the micro-trench.
   - Compute the thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ wet etch depth and correlate against the target BOE 6:1 etch duration.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Tolerance | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Profilometer Etch Rate Verification** | $100$ (equivalent to $1000\text{ \AA/min}$) | $\pm 5$ | $\text{nm/minute}$ | Contact Profilometer $\Delta Z$ / Dip-etch run time |
| **BOE 6:1 Process Bath Temperature** | $25.0$ | $\pm 0.5$ | $^{\circ}\text{C}$ | In-situ bath temperature thermocouple |
| **Prior HMDS Vapor Prime Temperature** | $120$ | $\pm 2$ | $^{\circ}\text{C}$ | Integrated oven chamber pyrometer / thermocouple |
| **Thin Gate Oxide Baseline Thickness Reference** | $3.5$ | $\pm 0.2$ | $\text{nm}$ | Ellipsometric cross-check / dry oxidation baseline |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context Citations

- **Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE):**
  - Chemical composition: $6\text{ parts } 40\%\text{ NH}_4\text{F} : 1\text{ part } 49\%\text{ HF}$.
  - Etch rate of thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$: approximately $100\text{ nm/minute}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  - Surface prep & adhesion: HMDS (Hexamethyldisilazane) vapor prime executed at $120^{\circ}\text{C}$ prior to resist coating.
  - Wetting agent addition ($0.1\%\text{ Triton X-100 or Fluorad}$) required to suppress bubble entrapment within micro-trenches.
  - Safety protocol: Immediate availability of calcium gluconate gel for dermal HF exposure.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - Gate dielectric baseline physical thickness: $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown at $850^{\circ}\text{C} - 900^{\circ}\text{C}$ dry oxidation.
  - Architecture: 1T1C stacked capacitor with minimum capacitance target of $25 - 30\text{ fF/cell}$ ($28\text{ fF}$ target).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Contact stylus profilometry imposes physical shear forces on micro-patterned trench edges. At Gen 1 (mm-scale chip with micro-trench features), if photoresist is retained as the step masking baseline, stylus loading forces exceeding 5 mg (approx. 49 uN) with a 2.0 um diamond tip radius risk mechanical furrowing or plastic deformation of Shipley 1813 resist, yielding artificially deep step-height readings. A calibrated tracking force of 1.0 to 2.5 mg and a scan speed below 20 um/s must be hard-coded into the scan recipe to prevent transducer feedback oscillations and tip flight across steep 90-degree oxide sidewalls.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: BOE 6:1 isotropic wet etching produces a characteristic lateral undercut beneath the resist mask with an approximate 1:1 aspect ratio relative to vertical oxide thickness (approx. 200 nm to 500 nm depending on wet etch target). Stylus profilometry cannot profile retrograde or vertical undercut profiles due to tip cone-angle limits (typically 45 to 60 degrees). profilometry data must be paired with optical spectroscopic ellipsometry Psi/Delta measurements on open unpatterned test pads (100 um x 100 um) to decouple residual thin film oxide thickness from mechanical step-height discontinuities, verifying clear trench bottoms down to the silicon substrate.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Diamond stylus tips (2 um or 5 um radius, 60-degree cone angle) for contact profilometers (e.g., Ambios XP-2, Veeco Dektak, or KLA Tencor series) represent a single-point failure with lead times of 8-12 weeks in Vietnam. High-precision step-height calibration standards (e.g., VLSI Standards 88 nm or 180 nm certified SiO2/Si pitch gratings) must be stored in dry N2 desiccators; chipping the stylus tip during manual wafer alignment aborts Gen 1 metrology validation for weeks unless secondary acoustic-enclosure optical non-contact profilers or AFM probes are stocked.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Profilometer scans run sequentially across multiple wafer sites (5-point mapping: center, top, bottom, left, right). At scan lengths of 500 um to 1 mm at 15 um/s, each profile trace requires ~60 seconds plus stage repositioning. Cycle time per wafer will exceed 25 minutes if automated wafer mapping recipes are not written. To stay within Gen 1 prototype schedule, limit early test wafer validation to a 3-point cross-wafer scan (center, notch-side, flat-side) before release to downstream photoresist strip and furnace diffusion.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Photoresist furrowing and plastic gouging by excessive stylus contact force (>5 mg), generating artifact peaks and false step-height measurements exceeding 50 nm deviation.
1. Acoustic and vibrational coupling from cleanroom air handling units (AHU) or fume hoods causing high-frequency vertical noise floor > 3.0 nm RMS, masking micro-trench floor topography.
1. Chipped or contaminated diamond stylus tip collecting sticky resist debris during scanning, leading to tip broadening, loss of lateral resolution, and rounded step transitions.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-2-2-01` | **Contact Stylus Profilometer Trench Depth and Oxide Step-Height Verification** | Calibrated Contact Stylus Profilometer (KLA Tencor Alpha-Step D-500 / Veeco Dektak 150 or equivalent) equipped with 2.0 um radius diamond tip, 60-degree cone angle, isolated on an active pneumatic vibration isolation table under acoustic enclosure. | 1. Mount wafer onto motorized vacuum chuck and initiate wafer vacuum (> 60 kPa). 2. Align the optical camera to locate the center die micro-trench test structure (100 um wide trench flanked by oxide/resist mesa). 3. Set profilometer recipe: Scan length = 600 um, Stylus stylus force = 1.5 mg (14.7 uN), Scan speed = 15 um/s, Data sampling rate = 200 Hz (0.075 um sampling interval). 4. Lower stylus gently onto the unetched oxide/resist mesa 100 um prior to trench edge. 5. Execute traverse scan across the micro-trench floor and onto the opposite mesa. 6. Level baseline using two-point cursor planarization across the top mesa surfaces. 7. Place measurement cursors R (reference) on top mesa and M (measure) on the trench floor minimum flat zone over a 30 um averaging window. | `Measured vertical oxide step height must measure between 170.0 nm and 190.0 nm (Target 180.0 nm ± 10.0 nm nominal etch target), with trench floor roughness Rq < 1.2 nm RMS and sidewall transition width < 8.0 um.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-2-2-02` | **Stylus Profilometry Noise Floor and Repeatability Verification on Bare Silicon Trench Floor** | Contact Stylus Profilometer with integrated LVDT transducer, 2.0 um diamond stylus, calibrated against NIST-traceable standard. | 1. Position stylus on flat, etched silicon trench floor of the center test coupon. 2. Set scan length to 100 um with stylus tracking force of 1.0 mg, traverse speed 10 um/s. 3. Execute 5 consecutive repeat scans along the identical traverse track without translating the X-Y stage. 4. Extract 1D vertical profile Z(x) for each run into raw ASCII format. 5. Compute the standard deviation of step height and root-mean-square roughness (Rq) across the 5 iterations. | `Peak-to-peak system noise floor Z_noise must be <= 1.0 nm; 1-sigma repeatability of measured step height across 5 repeat traces must be <= 1.5 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 / ISO 5 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (double-gloved), Polypropylene cleanroom coat and hood, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses, Static-dissipative cleanroom booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with trace solvent residues, flush immediately with copious cleanroom DI water for at least 15 minutes. In case of mechanical pinch or eye strain from optical aligner, rest eyes and seek first-aid review. Note: Though metrology is non-chemical, verify wafer has completed acid neutralization; if residual HF/BOE odor or droplets are detected, evacuate area and apply 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel to skin contact points immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted in Class 100 / ISO 5 laminar air flow cleanroom bay with downflow air velocity 0.45 m/s ± 0.05 m/s. Profilometer stage localized under mini-environment enclosure with HEPA filtration.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA cleanroom wipes disposed of in sealed, static-dissipative solvent waste bins connected to house solvent exhaust; dry nitrogen vented through general cleanroom return plenums.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, rinse/wipe solvent for stage/wafer backside)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / SLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 blow-off)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 (UHP) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `6 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic silicon trench floor (bare Si exposed by complete BOE 6:1 wet etch) bounded by hydrophilic thermal oxide / photoresist mesa sidewalls, thoroughly dried via N2 spin-rinse.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Profiled wafer with confirmed oxide step height, dry and unmarred, ready for automated photoresist wet strip (piranha/organic solvent) or dry O2 plasma ashing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient cleanroom air promotes native oxide growth (> 0.6 nm within 60 minutes) and airborne molecular contamination (AMC, hydrocarbons/siloxanes) on bare silicon floors, altering post-strip ellipsometric baselines and contaminating subsequent thermal/LPCVD furnace tubes.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable completion of Gen 1 contact stylus profilometry across patterned oxide micro-trenches, yielding accurate step-height confirmation of the BOE 6:1 etch process, qualifying trench cleanout down to silicon, and confirming negligible resist scratching or mechanical degradation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `micro_trench_stylus_step_height_center_die.csv`
- [ ] `profilometer_wafer_5point_cross_section_report.pdf`
- [ ] `trench_sidewall_profile_overlay_raw.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Center-die oxide step height verifies complete BOE wet etching to targeted depth** | `180.0 nm` | ±10.0 nm | Two-cursor baseline-subtracted vertical step calculation over 30 um averaging window on KLA/Veeco profilometer trace |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Trench floor roughness confirms clean oxide removal without pitted silicon damage** | `0.85 nm RMS` | < 1.50 nm RMS | 1D profile surface roughness Rq calculation over 50 um flat trench floor segment |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Cross-wafer 5-point etch uniformity confirms uniform boundary-layer dissolution** | `3.5 %` | <= 5.0 % | Percent non-uniformity calculation: [(Max Step - Min Step) / (2 * Mean Step)] * 100 across 5 wafer sites |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher executes automated or manual 5-point stylus profilometry scan; all 5 points show step heights within 170.0 - 190.0 nm with no furrowing on adjacent resist surfaces, trench floor Rq < 1.5 nm RMS, and CSV scan profiles are cryptographically hashed and uploaded to DRAM Foundation VN run archive.

```text
│  Etch-Rate Profiling  │
│  & Cross-Correlation  │
│      Calculation      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│      Acceptance       │
│    Verification &     │
│       Pass/Fail       │
│      Disposition      │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

## 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Safety & Substrate Staging**:
   - Ensure cleanroom personnel safety protocols are verified prior to wafer handling. Note: Hydrofluoric acid penetrates skin and binds calcium; calcium gluconate gel must be present at all times.
   - Stage post-BOE etched and rinsed 180nm DRAM patterned wafers at the metrology station (25°C ambient temperature control).

2. **Stylus Profilometer Step-Height Extraction**:
   - Mount the wafer onto the vacuum chuck of the contact profilometer and align fiducials to the patterned oxide micro-trench test structures.
   - Perform a linear stylus scan across the etched SiO2 step edge (crossing from the unetched mask/reference region into the cleared micro-trench).
   - Level the raw scan baseline, extract the step-height profile ($\Delta z_{\text{profile}}$), and record the physical trench step height in nm (or Å).

3. **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Metrology**:
   - Transfer the wafer to the spectroscopic ellipsometer vacuum stage.
   - Perform optical measurements at $\lambda = 632.8\text{ nm}$ across test monitor pads:
     - Measure remaining oxide thickness ($T_{\text{rem}}$) in etched regions.
     - Measure hard mask / reference film refractive index ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ for $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$) and unetched initial oxide thickness ($T_{\text{init}}$).
   - Fit $\Psi$ and $\Delta$ spectra to extract optical thickness values.

4. **Etch-Rate Profiling & Dual-Tool Cross-Correlation**:
   - Calculate mechanical etch rate:
     $$\text{Etch Rate}_{\text{prof}} = \frac{\Delta z_{\text{profile}}}{t_{\text{etch}}}$$
   - Calculate optical etch rate:
     $$\text{Etch Rate}_{\text{ellip}} = \frac{T_{\text{init}} - T_{\text{rem}}}{t_{\text{etch}}}$$
   - Correlate the profilometer physical step-height measurement directly against optical thickness difference $(\Delta T_{\text{ellip}} = T_{\text{init}} - T_{\text{rem}})$. Verify differential offset ($\delta = |\Delta z_{\text{profile}} - \Delta T_{\text{ellip}}|$) to ensure no resist footing, trench micro-loading, or over-etch artifacts skew profilometric data.

5. **Data Logging & Run Disposition**:
   - Log profilometer profiles, refractive indices, and extracted etch rates into the run tracking database.
   - If acceptance criteria match nominal baseline rates, pass the lot to subsequent stacked capacitor/contact integration modules.

---

## 3. Verified Source Citations

- **Etch Chemistry, Rates & Safety**: *Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*
  - BOE 6:1 (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$).
  - Etch rate of thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is approximately $100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  - Calcium gluconate gel safety requirement for HF exposure.
- **Hard Mask Optical & Etch Characteristics**: *Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks*
  - Silicon Nitride ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$) refractive index $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$.
  - $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ etch rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ in BOE.
- **Device Topology Context**: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*
  - 180nm architecture cell geometry (access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, stacked capacitor layout).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Discrepancies between tactile contact stylus profilometry and spectroscopic/null ellipsometry arise from mechanical deformation of soft photoresist sidewalls by the stylus tip (2-5 µm diamond radius at 1-5 mg force) versus optical model assumptions (effective medium approximation, refractive index Cauchy/Sellmeier model n=1.46 for thermally grown SiO2). A rigorous dual-modality calibration loop must establish baseline offset matrices across test dies before committing full lot wafer runs.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Capillary meniscus entrapment during post-BOE rinsing and native oxide regrowth (~0.5-1.0 nm within 30 min ambient air) distorts thin-film Delta/Psi ellipsometric readings in etched Si micro-trenches. Contact step-height extraction across PR-to-oxide versus oxide-to-bare-Si must account for PR swelling or partial dissolution if solvent stripping occurs asynchronously.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Certified VLSI or NIST-traceable step-height standards (e.g., 100 nm and 500 nm SiO2/Si steps) have 6-8 week recalibration lead times and steep international customs hurdles. The garage lab must maintain secondary in-house quartz step artifacts cross-verified against primary ellipsometry baselines to avoid line stoppages.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput must balance the Gen 1 loose macroscopic overlay constraints (±100 µm) with run-to-run cycle time. Stylus scan rastering across 9-point wafer maps takes 25 minutes per wafer; dual-point optical ellipsometry correlation must serve as a high-speed proxy gating wet-bench release within a 45-minute shift window.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Profilometer stylus tip dragging or scratching unstripped Shipley 1813 photoresist creating artificial step gouges (>15 nm artifact error).
1. Ellipsometric model convergence breakdown due to spatial beam spot overhang across micro-trench sidewalls causing depolarized signal scattering.
1. Native oxide regrowing on bare silicon floor prior to ellipsometric measurement, falsely suppressing calculated etch depth and nominal BOE etch rate by 5-10%.

Extract step height (Z_step) via valley-to-plateau mean step algorithm and calculate etch rate: ER = (Z_initial - Z_remaining) / t_etch or Z_step / t_etch. | `Measured step height Z_step matches nominal target within ±5.0% across all 5 dice; intra-wafer etch uniformity 1-sigma < 3.5%; no mechanical gouge marks exceeding 5 nm Ra on silicon baseline.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-2-3-02` | **Ellipsometric Delta-Psi Oxide Film Cross-Correlation and Residual Verification** | Variable Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometer / Laser Null Ellipsometer (HeNe 632.8 nm, 70° angle of incidence, 1 mm focused spot size) | 1. Acquire reference Psi and Delta on unetched field oxide region to establish pre-etch baseline oxide thickness. 2. Translate stage to the 2 mm x 2 mm open etched metrology pad. 3. Acquire Psi and Delta at 70° incidence over 5 acquisitions with signal-to-noise ratio > 40 dB. 4. Fit measured spectra using Cauchy dispersion model to extract residual oxide film thickness (d_residual). 5. Compute optical step height Delta_d = d_field - d_residual. 6. Cross-correlate optical Delta_d against mechanical step-height Z_step from TC-01. | `Absolute delta |Z_step (profilometer) - Delta_d (ellipsometer)| <= 3.0 nm; goodness of fit Mean Squared Error (MSE) < 2.5; residual oxide thickness in fully cleared trench < 1.0 nm (native oxide floor).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/laser safety goggles (rated OD 5+ at 632.8 nm), Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, powder-free, 6 mil), ESD-safe anti-static cleanroom smock and conductive heel grounders
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For chemical splash/contact during chuck wipe-down: Flush affected eyes or skin with flowing tap water for 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, move subject immediately to fresh air. For potential trace HF residue from incomplete cascade rinse: Apply 2.5% calcium gluconate gel immediately to exposed dermal areas and seek prompt medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Metrology bench must operate under localized laminar flow hood (ISO Class 5 air velocity 0.45 m/s ± 20%) equipped with HEPA filtration to eliminate airborne particulate settling on optical and mechanical scan tracks. Solvent cleaning venting minimum 50 FPM face velocity.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA-wetted cleanroom wipers must be disposed of in dedicated hazardous solvent waste bins with airtight self-closing lids. No corrosive wet chemicals are dispensed directly at the metrology station.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for Chuck & Stage Cleaning** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / MOS) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DI Rinse Standard)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (>18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly rinsed (DI >18 MOhm-cm) and N2 blow-dried wafer, hydrophilic in cleared micro-trenches (native Si / OH-terminated) and hydrophobic on Shipley 1813 resist mask.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized, non-destructively probed oxide step-height profiles; pristine, dust-free surface vacuum-sealed or transferred directly to photoresist strip bench.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding 30 minutes in ambient atmosphere allows 0.8-1.5 nm uncontrolled native oxide growth and airborne organic hydrocarbon contamination, causing false residual film readings on ellipsometry and subsequent resist-strip wet-chemical wetting failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful dual-modality metrological quantification of BOE 6:1 etched SiO2 step heights and etch rate across 5 standard die points, showing sub-3 nm correlation between contact profilometry and spectroscopic ellipsometry.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `step_height_profilometry_raw_profiles.csv`
- [ ] `ellipsometry_psi_delta_dispersion_fits.pdf`
- [ ] `dual_modality_etch_rate_correlation_matrix.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| `ASSERT-01` | **BOE 6:1 SiO2 etch rate extracted from step-height profilometry** | `1.80 nm/s` | ±0.15 nm/s | Linear regression of 5-point profilometric step height divided by calibrated etch time |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Optical & SEM Micro-Trench Defect Inspection for Lateral Undercutting & Resist Peeling

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180-BOE-006`  
**Subsystem / Workstream:** Metrology & Defect Inspection (180nm Open-Source DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type:** Buy / Infeed Metrology Tooling  

---

## 1. Inspection Process Workflow

```text
┌─────────────────────────┐
│      Wafer Infeed:      │
│  Post-BOE Dip & Rinse   │
└────────────┬────────────┘
             ▼
┌─────────────────────────┐
│  Optical Brightfield /  │
│  Darkfield Inspection   │
└────────────┬────────────┘
             ▼
┌────────────◇────────────┐
│    Resist Peeling or    │
│        Lifting?         │
└──────┬────────────┬─────┘
    Yes│          No│
       ▼            ▼
┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────┐
│ Flag Adhesion│ │   CD-SEM Micro-Trench   │
│ Failure/Hold │ │        Metrology        │
└──────────────┘ └────────────┬────────────┘
                              ▼
                 ┌─────────────────────────┐
                 │  Measure Lateral Etch   │
                 │  Undercut & Trench CD   │
                 └────────────┬────────────┘
                              ▼
                 ┌────────────◇────────────┐
                 │   Undercut Within Spec  │
                 │       (≤ 100 nm)?       │
                 └──────┬────────────┬─────┘
                    Pass│        Fail│
                        ▼            ▼
                 ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐
                 │  Pass Lot to │ │ Hold Lot for │
                 │ Step-Height/ │ │ Etch / HMDS  │
                 │ Ellipsometry │ │ Recipe Audit │
                 └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

### Step 1: Automated Wafer Handling & Optical Macroscopic Screening
1. Transfer post-cascade-rinsed and spin-dried wafers to the automated optical inspection (AOI) cassette stage.
2. Perform automated wafer surface scanning using dual-mode Brightfield/Darkfield optical microscopy at $5\times$ to $50\times$ optical magnification.
3. Inspect patterned photoresist edges across a standard 9-point/49-point array for macroscopic fringe delamination, bubble-induced resist peeling, or blistering along oxide micro-trench borders.

### Step 2: Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscopy (CD-SEM) Alignment
1. Load passed optical wafers into the ultra-high-vacuum load lock of the CD-SEM ($P < 1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Torr}$).
2. Set beam acceleration voltage to low landing energy ($E_{\text{beam}} = 500\text{ eV} - 1.0\text{ keV}$) and beam current ($I_{\text{beam}} \le 10\text{ pA}$) to eliminate electron-beam shrinkage or charging on the $1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ thick photoresist layer.
3. Auto-align to fiducial alignment marks targeting the 180nm unit cell array (transistor channel geometry: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, sharing bitline contacts).

### Step 3: Lateral Undercut & Micro-Trench Measurement
1. Drive beam to designated micro-trench test structures across 9 monitoring sites (center, mid-radius, edge exclusion $\ge 3\text{ mm}$).
2. Acquire high-magnification secondary electron (SE) micrographs ($50,000\times - 150,000\times$) at standard $0^\circ$ normal incidence and $45^\circ$ tilted stage view.
3. Compute lateral undercut ($\delta_{\text{undercut}}$) by measuring the difference between the photoresist bottom opening width and the etched $\text{SiO}_2$ trench top opening width:
   $$\delta_{\text{undercut}} = \frac{W_{\text{trench, top}} - W_{\text{resist, bottom}}}{2}$$
4. Verify micro-trench bottom clearing to confirm absence of trapped-bubble pinning or surfactant residues.

### Step 4: Disposition & Downstream Hand-off
1. If any site displays resist edge lifting $> 0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ or lateral undercut exceeding wet etch limits, route wafer to resist strip, surface de-contamination, and rework loop.
2. If all points pass, release wafer to downstream mechanical profilometry and spectroscopic ellipsometry metrology.

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Inspection Metric | Target Spec & Limit | Measurement Method / Tool | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Resist Interface Peeling / Delamination** | **$0\text{ defects}$** (Zero observable lifting at resist-$\text{SiO}_2$ boundary) | Automated Optical Brightfield / Darkfield ($20\times/50\times$) | Defect count / wafer |
| **Lateral Wet Etch Undercut ($\delta_{\text{undercut}}$)** | **$\le 100\text{ nm}$** per edge (Isotropic profile commensurate with $100\text{ nm/min}$ BOE rate) | In-line CD-SEM ($E_{\text{beam}} \le 1.0\text{ keV}$, tilted SE mode) | Nanometers ($\text{nm}$) |
| **Photoresist Film Integrity (Thickness Retained)** | **$1300\text{ nm} \pm 2\text{ nm}$** (No chemical erosion from BOE bath) | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Reflectometry (Cauchy/Sellmeier model) | Nanometers ($\text{nm}$) / Micrometers ($\mu\text{m}$) |
| **Trench Bubble Pinning / Micro-masking** | **$0\text{ occurrences}$** (Complete micro-trench clearing via surfactant spike) | CD-SEM Defect Review ($> 50,000\times$) | Defect count / field |

---

## 4. Literature & Context Citations

* **Source 1: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
  * Etch rate of thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ in BOE 6:1 at $25^\circ\text{C}$ is $\approx 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$).
  * Photoresist adhesion requires $120^\circ\text{C}$ HMDS vapor prime; addition of $0.1\%$ wetting agent (Triton X-100 or Fluorad) is required to eliminate micro-trench bubble entrapment and micro-masking defects.
* **Source 2: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
  * Precision verification of the $1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ photoresist film within $\pm 2\text{ nm}$ using Cauchy/Sellmeier optical models ($\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$) and 9-point/49-point wafer mapping to track radial variations.
* **Source 3: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  * Unit cell geometry baselines: Transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, ensuring micro-trench opening tolerances protect active cell pitch and bitline contacts.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-BOE inspection must establish clean metrology handoffs between wet chemical etch benches and downstream high-vacuum strip/implant chambers. Lateral undercutting and photoresist peeling directly degrade critical dimension (CD) budgeting, causing parasitic capacitive variation in DRAM bitlines. Without rigorous optical screening prior to SEM inspection, micro-delaminated Shipley 1813 fragments risk outgassing or particle shedding inside ultra-high vacuum (UHV) SEM chambers, compromising system availability.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Isotropic wet etching with BOE 6:1 inherently produces lateral undercut beneath the patterned Shipley 1813 mask roughly equal to the vertical oxide etch depth (lateral etch ratio ~1.0:1.0). Inadequate HMDS vapor priming or surfactant depletion in BOE leads to boundary layer capillary intrusion, causing severe interfacial resist peeling and excessive undercut (>1.5x etch depth). Optical brightfield/darkfield and calibrated low-kV field emission SEM (FESEM) cross-sections are vital to verify the structural integrity of the resist-oxide anchor boundary without electron-beam charging distortion.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Shipley 1813 resist, Microposit MF-319 developer, and electronic-grade BOE (buffered oxide etch 6:1 with surfactant) require stringent batch traceability and controlled temperature storage (2-8°C for photoresists). Relying on external or boutique analytical SEM centers introduces turnaround latency; local high-resolution metallurgical optical microscopes equipped with calibrated reticles must be used as primary screening filters to conserve paid SEM beam hours.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Gen 1 (mm) execution tolerates coarser absolute features, but resist peeling at the micro-trench perimeter creates fatal yield loss via pinhole short circuits and gate oxide leakage. Inspection protocols must enforce a go/no-go gating rubric within 15 minutes of cascade rinse/spin-dry to prevent photoresist re-hydration and ensure immediate rework stripping if undercutting exceeds baseline specifications.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Interfacial photoresist peeling and delamination along trench perimeters due to insufficient HMDS priming or high capillary peel stresses during BOE dip-etch.
1. Excessive isotropic lateral undercutting (>1.25x oxide etch thickness) causing collapse or pinch-off of adjacent DRAM micro-trench oxide barrier walls.
1. Photoresist carbonization and surface degradation under uncalibrated high-energy SEM electron-beam irradiation, invalidating trench profile metrology.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-3-01` | **Brightfield/Darkfield Optical Micro-Trench Perimeter Delamination & Peeling Inspection** | Calibrated Epifluorescence / Metallurgical Optical Microscope (50x/100x Plan Fluor objectives, 0.90 NA, darkfield/brightfield switchable, digital CMOS camera with sub-micron stage micrometer calibration) | 1. Mount patterned wafer onto the microscope vacuum chuck and align wafer flat/notch. 2. Calibrate optical reticle across a 100 um certified reference target. 3. Traverse to 9 standard die sites across the wafer (center, 4 inner radius, 4 outer radius). 4. Switch to darkfield illumination at 50x magnification to screen for fringe scattering, bright halo anomalies, or detached resist flakes along micro-trench edges. 5. Switch to brightfield illumination at 100x magnification, capture 2048x1536 high-contrast TIFF images, and measure resist footing fringe width using calibrated line-width tool. | `Zero visible resist peeling or boundary fraying observed across 100% of inspected fields; boundary fringe displacement indicating interfacial fluid ingress must be < 0.20 um.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-3-02` | **Low-kV In-Lens FESEM Lateral Undercut & Trench Wall Profile Metrology** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FESEM) operated at low landing energy (0.8 kV to 1.2 kV, probe current < 50 pA) with through-the-lens secondary electron (TLD-SE) detector to prevent resist charging. | 1. Load cleaved cross-section coupon into load-lock and pump to < 5e-5 mbar before chamber transfer. 2. Establish working distance at 3.0 mm to 4.0 mm, landing energy at 1.0 kV. 3. Locate target micro-trench fiducial cross-sections across center and edge coupons. 4. Acquire cross-sectional micrograph at 50,000x magnification using fast scan accumulation (line integration = 16) to prevent electron beam resist shrinkage. 5. Measure horizontal lateral undercut distance (L_undercut) beneath the resist ledge and vertical oxide etch depth (D_oxide). 6. Compute undercut ratio R = L_undercut / D_oxide. | `Lateral undercut distance L_undercut <= 1.15x vertical oxide step height (R <= 1.15); resist sidewall contact angle must remain intact without cantilever lift-off (> 75 degrees).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Double nitrile gloves (VWR / Ansell TouchNTuff, outer 8-mil, inner 4-mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles and full-face polycarbonate shield, Acid-resistant heavy-duty neoprene or fluoroelastomer apron during handling of wet-processed cassettes, Cleanroom-compatible ESD chemical-resistant lab coat and closed-toe cleanroom boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Although inspection is dry, wafers carry risk of latent acid transfer: 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel must be maintained at the inspection station. For suspected HF contact: immediately strip PPE, rinse with cold running water for 2 minutes, liberally massage Calcium Gluconate gel into skin continuously, and seek immediate emergency medical care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Optical inspection bench must be equipped with localized mini-environment HEPA filtration (Class 100/ISO 5 downflow hood) and laminar exhaust to capture solvent vapors and particulate shedding. SEM dry turbo pump exhaust must be vented directly to certified house toxic/acid scrubber exhaust lines.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Wafers exhibiting resist peeling or test coupons must be discarded in dedicated fluoropolymer acid-compatible solid waste containers. Spent rinse wipes and inspection wipes are treated as hazardous toxic solid waste; liquid neutralization requires calcium carbonate/slaked lime slurry for any fluorinated effluents.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (trace residual on unwashed carriers)** | `7664-39-3` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `0.1% to 1.0% aqueous residual` |
| **Shipley Microposit S1813 Photoresist (solidified film on wafer)** | `Proprietary Mixture` | Semiconductor Grade | `100% solid film (~1.3 um thickness)` |
| **Hexamethyldisilazane (HMDS bonded residue)** | `999-97-3` | Semiconductor Grade | `Monolayer (< 1%)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic silicon oxide surface patterned with post-baked Shipley 1813 photoresist, completely rinsed in DI cascade dump rinser and spin-dried under 0.2 um filtered N2.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Verified intact photoresist mask and etched micro-trenches, desiccated and ready for downstream dry photoresist strip (O2 plasma ash) or buffered wet strip without organic/fluoride residue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption (moisture uptake causing photoresist swelling, amine uptake neutralizer contamination, and native oxide re-growth on exposed silicon trench floors).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable Definition of Done for post-BOE micro-trench metrology: Complete optical multi-die defect map and high-resolution SEM cross-sectional verification demonstrating uniform oxide trench opening, absence of interfacial resist lift-off, and strictly bounded isotropic undercutting conforming to Gen 1 DRAM tolerances.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DEFECT_MAP_OPTICAL_INSPECTION_TC2233.pdf`
- [ ] `MICRO_TRENCH_UNDERCUT_METROLOGY_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `SEM_CROSS_SECTION_PROFILE_IMAGE_SET.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum lateral resist undercut (L_undercut) relative to nominal oxide trench boundary** | `0.35 um` | +/- 0.05 um | Calibrated in-lens cross-sectional FESEM line metrology at 50,000x magnification |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Photoresist boundary peeling / interfacial delamination failure rate across inspected dies** | `0.0%` | +0.0% (Zero Tolerance) | Optical darkfield/brightfield 100x automated surface inspection across 9 designated die locations |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit signoff requires 100% optical inspection pass across all 9 sample sites with zero peeling defects, SEM verification of lateral undercut within <= 0.40 um absolute limit, and completed dual-engineer signoff recorded in the DRAM Foundation VN laboratory information system.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Multi-Point Brightfield/Darkfield Optical Inspection for Resist Delamination & Peeling

**Task Hierarchy:** DRAM Foundation VN > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) SiO2 Patterning > HMDS Vapor Prime, Resist Patterning & Wet Oxide Dip-Etch Recipe Execution > Surfactant-Spike BOE 6:1 Dip-Etch Recipe Execution & Cascade Rinse > Post-Etch Micro-Trench Inspection, Oxide Step-Height Profilometry & Ellipsometric Metrology > Optical & SEM Micro-Trench Defect Inspection for Lateral Undercutting & Resist Peeling > Automated Multi-Point Brightfield/Darkfield Optical Inspection for Resist Delamination & Peeling  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Action Type:** Buy (Commercial Automated Inspection Station & Optics)

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Stage Calibration &   │
│     Origin Zeroing     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Wafer Vacuum Chuck &  │
│      Multi-Point       │
│   Coordinate Mapping   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Brightfield       │
│   Metrology: Focus &   │
│  Contrast Calibration  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Darkfield Optical    │
│      Inspection:       │
│       High-Angle       │
│       Scattering       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Polarization /     │
│     Reflectometric     │
│     Residual Check     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Automated Defect    │
│  Tagging & Pass/Fail   │
│     Classification     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **System Initialization & Stage Calibration:**
   - Power on the automated optical inspection (AOI) tool and initialize the motorized X-Y-Z macroscopic stage.
   - Verify stage repeatability and alignment tolerance within the **±5 µm** Gen 2 specification using the reference grid target.
   - Configure optics using a **10x Plan Achromat objective (NA 0.25)** for micron-scale trench resolution.

2. **Wafer Loading & Multi-Point Coordinate Mapping:**
   - Load the post-etch wafer onto the vacuum chuck after the DI cascade rinse and dry step.
   - Select either an automated **9-point** or **49-point wafer mapping** routine to comprehensively track radial film variations across the substrate.
   - Align wafer notch/flat and zero the coordinate system.

3. **Multi-Point Brightfield Optical Inspection:**
   - Under coaxial brightfield illumination, execute autofocus at each mapped inspection site across the wafer.
   - Inspect trench edges and oxide step features for broad-area blistering, pattern shifting, or gross resist loss.
   - Capture reference images across the 9 or 49 points to verify planar resist profile across the 1.3 µm nominal film.

4. **Multi-Point Darkfield Optical Inspection:**
   - Switch to high-angle darkfield illumination mode at the identical coordinate sites.
   - Detect non-specular light scattering caused by lifted resist sidewalls, micro-flaking, lateral undercutting fringes, or delaminated edge boundaries.
   - Flag any site exhibiting anomalous high-contrast darkfield flare along trench perimeters.

5. **Spectroscopic / Reflectometric Film Confirmation & Lot Disposition:**
   - Perform spot spectroscopic reflectometry at the mapped target sites.
   - Apply Cauchy/Sellmeier dispersion modeling to measure photoresist residual thickness relative to the **1.3 µm** nominal thickness target.
   - If delamination or edge peeling exceeds defect thresholds at any coordinate, isolate the wafer, halt downstream processing, and flag upstream HMDS vapor prime (120°C) and surfactant-spike BOE (6:1) dip-etch steps for recipe verification.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric / Specification | Tolerance | Units | Verification Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage Alignment Tolerance (Gen 2)** | `5` | `±5` | `µm` | Motorized optical stage encoder / fiducial reference |
| **Nominal Photoresist Thickness** | `1.3` | `±0.002` (±2 nm) | `µm` | Spectroscopic ellipsometry / reflectometry |
| **Wafer Mapping Grid Density** | `9` or `49` | `Exact integer` | `points` | Automated inspection recipe coordinate map |
| **Optical Objective Resolution** | `10` (NA: `0.25`) | Nominal fixed | `x` (magnification) | 10x Plan Achromat objective |

---

### Context Citations

- **Alignment & Optics:** *Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)* — Gen 2 alignment tolerance specified at **±5 microns**, microscope objective utilizing **10x Plan Achromat (NA 0.25)**, and photoresist thickness baseline of **~1.3 micron** (Shipley 1813 at 4000 RPM).
- **Film Metrology & Mapping:** *Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology* — Automated **9-point or 49-point wafer mapping** to evaluate radial non-uniformity; Cauchy/Sellmeier dispersion models parameterizing $n(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$; photoresist film thickness precision verified within **±2 nm** (0.002 µm) at the nominal **1.3 µm** layer.
- **Process Context & Adhesion Baseline:** *Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)* — Adhesion failure / resist delamination prevention via prior **HMDS vapor prime at 120°C** before BOE 6:1 dip etching.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automating multi-point brightfield and darkfield inspection requires rigorous hardware-software synchronization between the motorized X-Y-Z piezo stage and optical illumination switching. Darkfield scatterometry detects subtle fringe scattering caused by sub-micron photoresist edge lifting that brightfield reflection misses due to low numerical aperture contrast. However, optical inspection throughput drops exponentially if focus-tracking (Z-height laser autofocus) drifts across wafer bow (>30 um) induced by post-thermal oxidation stress.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Surfactant-spiked BOE (6:1 NH4F:HF) reduces surface tension to ~30 mN/m, enhancing wetting in high-aspect micro-trenches, but residual fluorinated surfactant or inadequate cascade rinsing causes capillary peeling at the hydrophobic Si/SiO2 interface. Brightfield imaging captures catastrophic macro-delamination (>5 um blister blisters), whereas darkfield scattering uniquely catches Rayleigh and Mie scattering from micro-blisters (<1 um) and lateral undercutting before the resist collapses during spin drying.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Automated dual-mode brightfield/darkfield microscopes with certified sub-micron laser autofocus stages (such as Olympus/Evident MX series or Nikon Eclipse LV/NW systems) face long procurement lead times (24-36 weeks) and high capital expenditure. In an open-source fab context, retrofitting existing upright compound optical microscopes with an off-the-shelf high-precision automated motorized XY stage, ring darkfield LED illuminator, and high-speed USB3 CMOS camera provides a viable, low-cost fallback.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Inspection of resist integrity after wet BOE dip-etch directly gates the subsequent photoresist strip and ion implantation or thermal diffusion steps. If delamination escapes detection here, severe pattern bridging, punch-through, or over-etched SiO2 isolation trenches will scrap entire DRAM wafer lots. A strict gate of <15 minutes queue time to inspect all 49 sample points per wafer must be enforced to avoid bottlenecking downstream batch processing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Darkfield scatter saturation caused by dried DI water residue or airborne airborne particulate contamination misidentified as resist edge lifting, triggering false lot rejects.
1. Autofocus failure over etched SiO2/Si step boundaries leading to out-of-focus image capture and undetected micro-channel resist delamination (<500 nm).
1. Delayed inspection exceeding queue time, causing unrinsed trace BOE/surfactant moisture inside micro-trenches to continue lateral oxide etching and severe pattern detachment.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-3-1-01` | **Automated 49-Point Brightfield/Darkfield Resist Peeling & Delamination Inspection** | Automated Metrology Microscope (Nikon/Olympus compatible) with 50x/0.80 NA BD Objective, High-Resolution 20MP CMOS Monochrome Sensor, Closed-Loop Laser Autofocus (±0.1 um Z-resolution), and Motorized XY Scanning Stage (±0.5 um repeatability). | 1. Load wafer onto motorized vacuum chuck and execute automated 3-point wafer centering and fiducial notch alignment. 2. Initialize standard 49-point polar mapping grid across the 150mm/200mm wafer surface (edge exclusion: 3 mm). 3. For each test die location: actuate laser autofocus to locate resist surface plane at nominal Z-height. 4. Capture Brightfield image at 50x magnification (exposure 15 ms, coaxial LED illumination) to detect gross delamination and macro-pattern loss. 5. Switch illumination filter turret to Darkfield mode (external ring illumination, 45-degree angle of incidence, exposure 65 ms) to capture scatter from micro-trenches, edge lifting, and lateral undercutting. 6. Execute automated threshold segmentation algorithm (Otsu method) calculating darkfield scatter intensity area ratio and perimeter fringe discontinuity. 7. Log coordinates, darkfield defect count, and image artifacts to metrology database. | `Pass: Zero (0) brightfield gross peeling defects (>2 um width) across all 49 points; Darkfield scatter area ratio at trench edges must not exceed 0.8% of patterned perimeter. Edge-lifting/delamination count = 0 per wafer.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-3-1-02` | **Lateral Undercut & Edge-Lifting Profilometry Correlation Metrology** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer / High-Resolution Optical Step-Height Profilometer integrated with co-axial darkfield defect review camera. | 1. Navigate XY stage to designated lithographic test crosshairs in Die (0,0), Die (R/2, 0), and Die (R-3mm, 0). 2. Acquire calibrated 100x Darkfield optical micrograph with lateral spatial resolution of 0.24 um/pixel. 3. Extract gray-level intensity profile orthogonal to the photoresist-to-etched oxide transition line. 4. Measure the lateral width of the high-scattering halo (denoting resist overhang / lateral undercutting). 5. Align spectroscopic reflectometer/profilometer beam (spot size 30 um) over adjacent open etched window and intact resist step to verify remaining oxide thickness and resist step height. | `Pass: High-scattering halo (lateral undercutting/peeling) must be <= 180 nm across all tested zones. Measured photoresist step height must equal 1.30 um ± 0.05 um with no swelling or thinning indicative of chemical attack.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, 6 mil minimum), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative cleanroom smock, hood, and conductive shoe covers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Although this is an optical inspection station, wafers arrive directly from BOE wet bench. Calgonate (2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel) must be present in the inspection bay. In case of suspected chemical skin contact from unwashed wafer edges: flush with cold DI water for 5 minutes, immediately massage calcium gluconate gel continuously into affected skin, and seek emergency medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operated under HEPA-filtered laminar flow cleanroom bench (ISO Class 5 / Class 100) with air velocity 0.45 m/s ± 20%. Microscope vacuum chuck exhaust vented to toxic/solvent house exhaust to prevent trace vapor recirculation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Wafers exhibiting chemical residue or contamination must be transferred using dedicated PTFE vacuum wands into an acid-compatible dump rinse tank; inspection wipe waste disposed of in designated hazardous cleanroom solid waste containers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 gas purge)** | `7727-37-9` | VLSI / Electronic Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Residual Hydrofluoric Acid (trace carryover hazard)** | `7664-39-3` | Trace contaminant monitoring | `< 1 ppm (trace)` |
| **Residual Ammonium Fluoride (trace carryover hazard)** | `12125-01-8` | Trace contaminant monitoring | `< 1 ppm (trace)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic patterned silicon trench bottom with hydrophilic thermal SiO2 sidewalls; cleanroom air-dried photoresist (Shipley 1813 or equivalent) intact on mesa structures.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Optically verified defect-free patterned photoresist/SiO2 surface, inspected and cleared for downstream photoresist strip or oxide verification metrology.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time in ambient cleanroom air promotes airborne amine absorption, moisture condensation in micro-trenches causing capillary stress, and latent lateral resist detachment, invalidating subsequent wet-strip selectivity and metallization.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full wafer multi-point automated brightfield/darkfield optical inspection map and defect log confirming zero photoresist peeling, blistering, or catastrophic delamination, with lateral undercutting strictly confined within 180nm DRAM design rules across all 49 mapped points.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `49_point_optical_inspection_defect_map.csv`
- [ ] `brightfield_darkfield_delamination_inspection_report.pdf`
- [ ] `high_res_trench_darkfield_scatter_composites.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Gross resist peeling/delamination defect count across 49-point wafer survey** | `0` | +0 defects | Automated Brightfield Optical Inspection (50x, Otsu morphological defect segmentation) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum lateral darkfield fringe scattering width (lateral undercut/edge lift)** | `180 nm` | +20 nm / -50 nm | Calibrated Darkfield Scatterometric Optical Intensity Profile across Test Vernier Trenches |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Z-autofocus repeatability across 49 mapping points on warped substrate** | `0.10 um` | ± 0.05 um | Closed-loop optical piezo laser autofocus sensor log verification |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher verifies 100% completion of 49-point inspection with zero brightfield peeling defects detected, maximum darkfield lateral undercutting <= 200 nm, and signed electronic lot traveler attached to brightfield_darkfield_delamination_inspection_report.pdf.

Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE) (Semiconductor Chemical Processing Handbook)

critics.systems_engineer: Automating multi-point brightfield and darkfield inspection requires rigorous hardware-software synchronization between the motorized X-Y-Z piezo stage and optical illumination switching. Darkfield scatterometry detects subtle fringe scattering caused by sub-micron photoresist edge lifting that brightfield reflection misses due to low numerical aperture contrast. However, optical inspection throughput drops exponentially if focus-tracking (Z-height laser autofocus) drifts across wafer bow (>30 um) induced by post-thermal oxidation stress.
critics.domain_expert: Surfactant-spiked BOE (6:1 NH4F:HF) reduces surface tension to ~30 mN/m, enhancing wetting in high-aspect micro-trenches, but residual fluorinated surfactant or inadequate cascade rinsing causes capillary peeling at the hydrophobic Si/SiO2 interface. Brightfield imaging captures catastrophic macro-delamination (>5 um blister blisters), whereas darkfield scattering uniquely catches Rayleigh and Mie scattering from micro-blisters (<1 um) and lateral undercutting before the resist collapses during spin drying.
critics.supply_chain: Automated dual-mode brightfield/darkfield microscopes with certified sub-micron laser autofocus stages (such as Olympus/Evident MX series or Nikon Eclipse LV/NW systems) face long procurement lead times (24-36 weeks) and high capital expenditure. In an open-source fab context, retrofitting existing upright compound optical microscopes with an off-the-shelf high-precision automated motorized XY stage, ring darkfield LED illuminator, and high-speed USB3 CMOS camera provides a viable, low-cost fallback.
critics.laya_pm: Inspection of resist integrity after wet BOE dip-etch directly gates the subsequent photoresist strip and ion implantation or thermal diffusion steps. If delamination escapes detection here, severe pattern bridging, punch-through, or over-etched SiO2 isolation trenches will scrap entire DRAM wafer lots. A strict gate of <15 minutes queue time to inspect all 49 sample points per wafer must be enforced to avoid bottlenecking downstream batch processing.
critical_failure_modes: Darkfield scatter saturation caused by dried DI water residue or airborne airborne particulate contamination misidentified as resist edge lifting, triggering false lot rejects.
Autofocus failure over etched SiO2/Si step boundaries leading to out-of-focus image capture and undetected micro-channel resist delamination (<500 nm).
Delayed inspection exceeding queue time, causing unrinsed trace BOE/surfactant moisture inside micro-trenches to continue lateral oxide etching and severe pattern detachment.

testcases.title: Automated 49-Point Brightfield/Darkfield Resist Peeling & Delamination Inspection
testcases.instrumentation: Automated Metrology Microscope (Nikon/Olympus compatible) with 50x/0.80 NA BD Objective, High-Resolution 20MP CMOS Monochrome Sensor, Closed-Loop Laser Autofocus (±0.1 um Z-resolution), and Motorized XY Scanning Stage (±0.5 um repeatability).
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer has completed BOE 6:1 dip-etch, 5-stage dump cascade DI rinse (resistivity > 18.0 MOhm*cm), and N2 spin-dry. Wafer vacuum chucked under class 100 laminar flow hood.
testcases.procedure:
1. Load wafer onto motorized vacuum chuck and execute automated 3-point wafer centering and fiducial notch alignment.
2. Initialize standard 49-point polar mapping grid across the 150mm/200mm wafer surface (edge exclusion: 3 mm).
3. For each test die location: actuate laser autofocus to locate resist surface plane at nominal Z-height.
4. Capture Brightfield image at 50x magnification (exposure 15 ms, coaxial LED illumination) to detect gross delamination and macro-pattern loss.
5. Switch illumination filter turret to Darkfield mode (external ring illumination, 45-degree angle of incidence, exposure 65 ms) to capture scatter from micro-trenches, edge lifting, and lateral undercutting.
6. Execute automated threshold segmentation algorithm (Otsu method) calculating darkfield scatter intensity area ratio and perimeter fringe discontinuity.
7. Log coordinates, darkfield defect count, and image artifacts to metrology database.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass: Zero (0) brightfield gross peeling defects (>2 um width) across all 49 points; Darkfield scatter area ratio at trench edges must not exceed 0.8% of patterned perimeter. Edge-lifting/delamination count = 0 per wafer.

testcases.title: Lateral Undercut & Edge-Lifting Profilometry Correlation Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Spectroscopic Ellipsometer / High-Resolution Optical Step-Height Profilometer integrated with co-axial darkfield defect review camera.
testcases.pre_conditions: TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-2-2-3-3-1-01 completed; wafer identified with target test vernier structures in Center, Mid-Radius, and Edge zones.
testcases.procedure:
1. Navigate XY stage to designated lithographic test crosshairs in Die (0,0), Die (R/2, 0), and Die (R-3mm, 0).
2. Acquire calibrated 100x Darkfield optical micrograph with lateral spatial resolution of 0.24 um/pixel.
3. Extract gray-level intensity profile orthogonal to the photoresist-to-etched oxide transition line.
4. Measure the lateral width of the high-scattering halo (denoting resist overhang / lateral undercutting).
5. Align spectroscopic reflectometer/profilometer beam (spot size 30 um) over adjacent open etched window and intact resist step to verify remaining oxide thickness and resist step height.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Pass: High-scattering halo (lateral undercutting/peeling) must be <= 180 nm across all tested zones. Measured photoresist step height must equal 1.30 um ± 0.05 um with no swelling or thinning indicative of chemical attack.

ppe_required: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, 6 mil minimum)
ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields
Static-dissipative cleanroom smock, hood, and conductive shoe covers
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Although this is an optical inspection station, wafers arrive directly from BOE wet bench. Calgonate (2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel) must be present in the inspection bay. In case of suspected chemical skin contact from unwashed wafer edges: flush with cold DI water for 5 minutes, immediately massage calcium gluconate gel continuously into affected skin, and seek emergency medical attention.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Operated under HEPA-filtered laminar flow cleanroom bench (ISO Class 5 / Class 100) with air velocity 0.45 m/s ± 20%. Microscope vacuum chuck exhaust vented to toxic/solvent house exhaust to prevent trace vapor recirculation.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Wafers exhibiting chemical residue or contamination must be transferred using dedicated PTFE vacuum wands into an acid-compatible dump rinse tank; inspection wipe waste disposed of in designated hazardous cleanroom solid waste containers.

q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Optically verified defect-free patterned photoresist/SiO2 surface, inspected and cleared for downstream photoresist strip or oxide verification metrology.
