critics.systems_engineer: Contact stylus profilometry across patterned oxide steps introduces physical shear and local surface contact pressure (>10 MPa with sub-micron tip radius) that can dislodge or delaminate vulnerable 180nm photoresist sidewalls if scanned prior to PR strip, or induce micro-scratching on bare Si if contact force exceeds 2 mg (19.6 uN). The recipe must explicitly decouple scan speed (<= 10 um/s), stylus radius (2.0 um tip), and tracking force (1.5 mg) to prevent dynamic flight over steep BOE vertical step transitions.
critics.domain_expert: At 180nm DRAM node oxide thicknesses (~300 nm to 500 nm field/isolation oxide), acoustic noise floor and sample leveling (Wedge Error / tilt) dominate step-height errors. Two-point baseline leveling across at least 50 um of unetched SiO2 terrace before and after the trench is required to isolate true BOE step height from wafer bow. Furthermore, stylus scan lines must be aligned perpendicular (90 +/- 2 deg) to the DRAM cell trench orientation using the integrated optical split-field microscope to avoid measuring hypotenuse scan artifacts.
critics.supply_chain: Diamond-tipped styli (2.0 um radius, 60-degree cone angle) have standard tool lifespans of 1,200 to 1,500 scans before tip flattening or chipping occurs. In-house replacement diamond styli from vendors like KLA-Tencor or Bruker face an 8-to-12-week procurement lead time in Southeast Asia. A standard calibration step-height reference standard (VLSI Standards 480 nm certified SiO2/Si pitch) must be scanned every 50 runs to qualify tip integrity without expending production dummy wafers.
critics.laya_pm: Multi-site wafer runs (9-point layout matching the sheet resistance and lithography grid) consume ~4.5 minutes per site including auto-focus, leveling, and optical alignment, totaling ~42 minutes per wafer. If cycle time exceeds 45 minutes, it breaks the inline metrology takt time for the BOE wet bench batch release. Stylus recipe length must be restricted to 200 um per trace with 10 um/s velocity to maintain takt time compliance.
critical_failure_modes: Tip chipping or blunting yielding artificial sidewall broadening and negative step-height offset (> 5% error vs. spectroscopic ellipsometry reference).
Stylus tip gouging or scratching into unannealed silicon substrate in deep BOE-etched trenches due to excessive stylus downforce (> 3.0 mg).
Wafer vacuum chuck distortion or particulate contamination causing localized tilt that exceeds the software leveling range (+/- 2 um over 200 um scan length).

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-STYLUS-GEN2-001`  
**Title:** Stylus Profilometer Calibration and Stylus Force/Scan Speed Recipe Parameterization  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Process Node / Architecture:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Tool Setup & Stage   │
│        Leveling        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Stylus Calibration   │
│   on Certified Step    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Parameterize Force &  │
│       Scan Speed       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Multi-Site Wafer    │
│      Verification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
Establish a reproducible calibration and scan recipe for contact stylus profilometry on patterned oxide trenches (post-Buffered Oxide Etch, BOE 6:1) and interconnect steps. Ensure stylus tracking fidelity without plowing soft films (such as Shipley 1813 photoresist) or chipping brittle dielectric/metal edges.

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Check and Environmental Isolation:**
   - Verify acoustic enclosure doors are sealed and pneumatic anti-vibration table pressure is normalized.
   - Clean the vacuum stage using high-purity filtered N2 and cleanroom wiper.

2. **Stage Alignment & Baseline Calibration:**
   - Mount a certified step-height calibration standard onto the stage.
   - Engage optical alignment camera; align standard alignment marks with the stage translation axis within the Gen 2 macroscopic alignment tolerance of **$\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$**.
   - Perform a reference scan across the certified step to verify Z-sensor linearity and calibrate the vertical piezo/LVDT gain.

3. **Stylus Force Recipe Parameterization:**
   - Select diamond stylus tip radius ($2.0\ \mu\text{m}$ or $5.0\ \mu\text{m}$, 60° cone).
   - Set contact stylus force appropriately low ($1\ \text{mg}$ to $5\ \text{mg}$ / $\sim 10\ \mu\text{N}$ to $50\ \mu\text{N}$) to avoid plastic deformation or surface scratching on soft Shipley 1813 photoresist layers ($1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ nominal thickness).
   - Inspect test scan path under high-magnification optical camera to confirm zero visible tip-drag furrows or resist deformation.

4. **Scan Speed and Spatial Sampling Configuration:**
   - Set scan profile length across the target trench/feature (e.g., $100\ \mu\text{m}$ to $500\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Set scan speed between $10\ \mu\text{m/s}$ and $20\ \mu\text{m/s}$ to ensure the tip maintains contact without bouncing or ringing over high-aspect vertical sidewalls.
   - Configure data sampling frequency $\ge 100\ \text{Hz}$ to achieve horizontal point density $< 0.2\ \mu\text{m/point}$.

5. **Multi-Site Post-BOE Trench Run Execution:**
   - Load the post-BOE 6:1 patterned wafer onto the chuck and engage vacuum hold-down.
   - Align wafer die coordinate system within the **$\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$** Gen 2 tolerance.
   - Execute the 5-point multi-site wafer recipe (Center, Top, Bottom, Left, Right).
   - Apply automated two-point leveling / baseline tilt subtraction to extract step heights across the oxide trenches and verify uniformity against metal-1 nominal step heights ($350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Tolerance | Detection / Metrology Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stage & Pattern Alignment** | $\le 5$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ | Optical cross-hair coordinate alignment (Gen 2 alignment budget) |
| **Photoresist Film Integrity (No Plowing)** | $1.3$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | $\pm 0.05\ \mu\text{m}$ | Post-scan profile baseline check & optical inspection for zero gouging |
| **Step-Height Measurement Repeatability** | $350$ | $\text{nm}$ | $\pm 5\%$ ($\pm 17.5\ \text{nm}$) | 5-run repeated scan on nominal M1/step features |

---

### 4. Verified Literature References

1. **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018):**
   - *Gen 2 Alignment Budget:* Alignment tolerance baseline of $\pm 5\ \mu\text{m}$ for Gen 2 photolithography and metrology registration.
   - *Photoresist Specification:* Shipley 1813 spin-coated at 4000 RPM yields $\sim 1.3\ \mu\text{m}$ thickness with soft bake at 115°C for 60 seconds; guides stylus force limits to prevent scratch indentation.
2. **Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects:**
   - *Film Thickness & Step Reference:* Metal-1 interconnect thickness target of $350\ \text{nm} \pm 5\%$ used to benchmark profilometer step-height vertical scale accuracy.
3. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
   - Transistor channel length $L = 180\ \text{nm}$, bitline contact shared geometry, establishing lateral dimension scaling constraints for sub-micron/micron metrology.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The integration between the Gen 1 extruded aluminum 4040 stage structure, linear guides (MGN12H), and the contact stylus transducer introduces low-frequency structural resonance and Abbe offset errors during scan transitions. If stepper motor microstepping (1/16) generates harmonics matching the cantilever mechanical resonance (~120 Hz to 350 Hz), vertical displacement tracking will exhibit severe noise artifacts (>15 nm RMS). The mechanical stage must be decoupled with sorbothane isolation pads, and stylus tracking speed must be throttled to prevent dynamic overshoot across the steep vertical BOE trench sidewall.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating stylus force is paramount for patterned Shipley 1813 photoresist over wet-etched SiO2. Excessive stylus tracking force (>5 mg / ~50 uN) will plastically gouge the post-bake soft photoresist step edges (nominal thickness ~1.3 um), falsely measuring trench depths and contaminating the diamond stylus tip with polymer debris. Conversely, insufficient stylus force (<0.5 mg / ~5 uN) causes tip hydroplaning/skating and transient decoupling at high scan speeds (>20 um/s) when dropping into sharp 100 nm to 500 nm wet-etched SiO2 trenches. The scan speed recipe must be strictly parameterized between 5 to 15 um/s with stylus force maintained at 1.5 to 3.0 mg (15 to 30 uN).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Certified VLSI/NIST-traceable step-height standards (e.g., nominal 100 nm and 1000 nm SiO2 on Si steps) require lead times of 8 to 12 weeks and specialized handling. In-house fabricated step standards lack certified secondary calibration, introducing systematic offset risk across wafer lots. Diamond styli (2.0 um to 5.0 um tip radius, 60-degree cone) are fragile single-source consumables susceptible to catastrophic chipping upon unbuffered wafer edge contact or abrupt stage homing errors, necessitating at least 2 replacement styli in local buffer inventory.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration and recipe parameterization define the metrology baseline for all downstream BOE wet-etch depth uniformity gates. Failure to complete this task within the allocated shift creates a critical bottleneck for post-etch strip and gate oxide growth. Operating researchers must lock calibration profiles against standard reference artifacts before scanning operational production wafers to prevent invalidating entire multi-site wafer runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Photoresist plastic deformation or furrowing caused by excessive stylus contact force (>50 uN) leading to erroneous step-height measurements and diamond tip polymer contamination.
1. Stylus tip flight/decoupling over sharp etched steps caused by excessive lateral scan velocity (>20 um/s) combined with under-damped cantilever tracking response.
1. Calibration curve drift and vertical non-linearity resulting from thermal expansion of the uncalibrated LVDT/optical sensor and un-isolated environmental acoustic vibrations (>30 Hz).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-2-1-01` | **NIST-Traceable Step-Height Calibration & Vertical Linearity Verification** | Contact Stylus Profilometer (LVDT/optical detection, 2.0 um diamond stylus tip radius), NIST-traceable step-height calibration standard (nominal 1000 nm SiO2/Si step, certified standard deviation <= 1.5 nm), Class 1000 cleanroom isolation table. | 1. Mount certified 1000 nm step-height standard on vacuum chuck and engage vacuum clamp. 2. Position stylus 100 um upstream of reference step. 3. Configure scan recipe: scan length = 400 um, scan speed = 10 um/s, stylus tracking force = 2.0 mg (19.6 uN), sampling frequency = 100 Hz. 4. Execute 5 consecutive automated profile scans across the calibrated step. 5. Apply ISO 5436-1 step-height leveling algorithm across lower and upper reference planes. 6. Calculate mean step height (H_meas), calibration gain factor (K_cal = H_nominal / H_meas), and repeatability standard deviation (sigma). | `Measured mean step height must match certified 1000 nm standard within +/- 1.0% (990 nm <= H_meas <= 1010 nm); 5-run measurement repeatability standard deviation sigma <= 3.0 nm; baseline noise on flat reference plane <= 2.5 nm RMS.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-2-1-02` | **Stylus Force & Scan Speed Recipe Parameterization on Shipley 1813 / SiO2 BOE Trench** | Contact Stylus Profilometer with adjustable tracking force mechanism (0.5 to 10 mg), Optical Inspection Microscope (100x Nomarski DIC), Test wafer with Shipley 1813 photoresist patterns post-BOE wet etch (nominal trench depth ~500 nm SiO2, PR thickness ~1.3 um). | 1. Load test wafer containing 50 um wide BOE-etched SiO2 test trenches with soft-baked/hard-baked Shipley 1813 mask intact. 2. Execute a matrix of scans varying stylus force (1.0 mg, 2.0 mg, 3.5 mg, 5.0 mg) across three scan speeds (5 um/s, 10 um/s, 25 um/s) across adjacent identical trench structures. 3. Record profile traces, step transition slope fidelity, and trailing edge oscillation. 4. Unload wafer and perform 100x DIC optical inspection along the stylus scan tracks to verify absence of plastic furrowing or scratch gouging on the resist surface. 5. Identify the operational envelope where vertical tracking error is minimized without mechanical indentation. | `Zero visible plastic deformation, scratch lines, or resist furrowing visible under 100x DIC optical inspection; step transition profile shows clean single-peak derivative with zero tip flight ringing/overshoot (>10 nm); step height repeatability between 5 um/s and 10 um/s recipes matches within +/- 2.0 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, Full cleanroom ESD smock, hairnet, and cleanroom booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye exposure to IPA cleaning solvent, flush immediately with copious clean water or eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, move individual to fresh cleanroom air supply. For mechanical pinch injuries from linear translation stage, disengage emergency stop and evaluate for localized trauma.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted in standard laminar flow hood or Class 1000 cleanroom ambient. IPA lens/stage wipe cleaning conducted under localized bench exhaust or solvent-rated fume extraction mini-hood (face velocity >= 0.5 m/s).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA-wetted cleanroom wipes (polyester/cellulose) must be disposed of in a dedicated, sealed, flame-resistant solvent waste bin. Solid hazardous waste collected and processed through certified cleanroom solvent incineration channels. No liquid chemical discharge to municipal sewer.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade (0.1 um filtered) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Compressed Dry Nitrogen (N2)** | `7727-37-9` | High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly rinsed (DI water resistivity 18.2 MOhm*cm) and spin-dried wafer patterned with Shipley 1813 resist over BOE 6:1 wet-etched SiO2 steps; surface clean, free of particulate contamination (>0.5 um), unstripped resist intact.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Profilometry-characterized patterned wafer, zero stylus scratch marks or diamond tip debris on active die regions; purged under dry N2 flow ready for photoresist strip and spectroscopic ellipsometry cross-correlation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended atmospheric air exposure (>60 minutes) leads to airborne organic hydrocarbon adsorption and airborne particulate accumulation in etched micro-trenches, altering apparent step height by >5 nm and causing diamond stylus tip snagging or resist adhesion degradation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration of the contact stylus profilometer vertical displacement transducer using certified NIST-traceable standards, alongside the formal parameterization and signoff of the stylus force (2.0 mg / 19.6 uN) and scan velocity (10.0 um/s) recipe optimized for wet-etched SiO2/Shipley 1813 microstructures without resist scratching or tip decoupling.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CALIBRATION_REPORT_STYLUS_1000NM_NIST.pdf`
- [ ] `RECIPE_PARAMETERIZATION_FORCE_SPEED_MATRIX.csv`
- [ ] `POST_ETCH_TRENCH_PROFILE_RAW_SCANS.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Vertical step-height calibration accuracy against certified 1000 nm standard** | `1000.0 nm` | +/- 10.0 nm (+/- 1.0%) | ISO 5436-1 standard step leveling algorithm across 5 repeated scans using calibrated profilometer software |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Scan baseline RMS noise floor under operational vibration isolation** | `1.8 nm RMS` | <= 2.5 nm RMS | Root-mean-square roughness evaluation (Rq) across a 200 um polished bare Si reference flat with stage running at 10 um/s |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Shipley 1813 photoresist mechanical indentation depth along scan path** | `0.0 nm` | <= 1.0 nm (undetectable via optical DIC/profilometry re-scan) | Orthogonal re-scan across previous scan path at 0.5 mg tracking force combined with 100x Nomarski DIC optical microscopy |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Profilometer vertical calibration factor confirmed within 1.000 +/- 0.010 with 5-run standard deviation <= 3.0 nm; optimal recipe locked at 2.0 mg tracking force and 10 um/s scan speed; zero physical scratch tracks detected on resist test structures; calibration certificate signed and uploaded to DRAM Foundation VN metrology repository.

testcases.title: NIST-Traceable Step-Height Calibration & Vertical Linearity Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Contact Stylus Profilometer (LVDT/optical detection, 2.0 um diamond stylus tip radius), NIST-traceable step-height calibration standard (nominal 1000 nm SiO2/Si step, certified standard deviation <= 1.5 nm), Class 1000 cleanroom isolation table.
testcases.pre_conditions: Profilometer seated on active pneumatic or sorbothane vibration isolation table; ambient temperature stabilized at 21.0 +/- 0.5 deg C; diamond stylus inspected under optical microscope (50x) confirming zero resist contamination or edge chipping; calibration standard cleaned with clean dry nitrogen (CDA/N2 blow).
testcases.procedure:
1. Mount certified 1000 nm step-height standard on vacuum chuck and engage vacuum clamp.
2. Position stylus 100 um upstream of reference step.
3. Configure scan recipe: scan length = 400 um, scan speed = 10 um/s, stylus tracking force = 2.0 mg (19.6 uN), sampling frequency = 100 Hz.
4. Execute 5 consecutive automated profile scans across the calibrated step.
5. Apply ISO 5436-1 step-height leveling algorithm across lower and upper reference planes.
6. Calculate mean step height (H_meas), calibration gain factor (K_cal = H_nominal / H_meas), and repeatability standard deviation (sigma).
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Measured mean step height must match certified 1000 nm standard within +/- 1.0% (990 nm <= H_meas <= 1010 nm); 5-run measurement repeatability standard deviation sigma <= 3.0 nm; baseline noise on flat reference plane <= 2.5 nm RMS.

testcases.title: Stylus Force & Scan Speed Recipe Parameterization on Shipley 1813 / SiO2 BOE Trench
testcases.instrumentation: Contact Stylus Profilometer with adjustable tracking force mechanism (0.5 to 10 mg), Optical Inspection Microscope (100x Nomarski DIC), Test wafer with Shipley 1813 photoresist patterns post-BOE wet etch (nominal trench depth ~500 nm SiO2, PR thickness ~1.3 um).
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer thoroughly DI-water rinsed, spin-dried, and inspected for resist delamination; profilometer vertical calibration locked via TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-2-1-01.
testcases.procedure:
1. Load test wafer containing 50 um wide BOE-etched SiO2 test trenches with soft-baked/hard-baked Shipley 1813 mask intact.
2. Execute a matrix of scans varying stylus force (1.0 mg, 2.0 mg, 3.5 mg, 5.0 mg) across three scan speeds (5 um/s, 10 um/s, 25 um/s) across adjacent identical trench structures.
3. Record profile traces, step transition slope fidelity, and trailing edge oscillation.
4. Unload wafer and perform 100x DIC optical inspection along the stylus scan tracks to verify absence of plastic furrowing or scratch gouging on the resist surface.
5. Identify the operational envelope where vertical tracking error is minimized without mechanical indentation.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Zero visible plastic deformation, scratch lines, or resist furrowing visible under 100x DIC optical inspection; step transition profile shows clean single-peak derivative with zero tip flight ringing/overshoot (>10 nm); step height repeatability between 5 um/s and 10 um/s recipes matches within +/- 2.0 nm.

ppe_required: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, ESD-safe)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses
Full cleanroom ESD smock, hairnet, and cleanroom booties
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For skin or eye exposure to IPA cleaning solvent, flush immediately with copious clean water or eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, move individual to fresh cleanroom air supply. ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: IPA-wetted cleanroom wipes (polyester/cellulose) must be disposed of in a dedicated, sealed, flame-resistant solvent waste bin. # Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Info
- **Title**: Multi-Site 9-Point Radial Wafer Coordinate Mapping and Automated Scan Run
- **Context Path**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) $\text{SiO}_2$ Patterning [Chemical Processing] > Post-Etch Spectroscopic Ellipsometry & Profilometry Metrology Inspection [Metrology] > Stylus Profilometry Step-Height & Etch Trench Uniformity Characterization [Metrology] > Post-BOE Etch Trench Step-Height Profilometry Recipe Setup and Scan Execution [Metrology] > Post-BOE Trench Stylus Profilometry Scan Recipe Configuration and Multi-Site Wafer Run [Metrology] > Multi-Site 9-Point Radial Wafer Coordinate Mapping and Automated Scan Run [Metrology]
- **Generation**: Gen 2 ($\mu\text{m}$)
- **Action Type**: Make

---

## 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the wafer coordinate mapping and automated multi-site scanning protocol for post-Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) $\text{SiO}_2$ pattern characterization. It establishes an automated 9-point radial inspection routine across the wafer to evaluate step heights, trench profiles, and radial film thickness/etch non-uniformity across the DRAM cell integration topology.

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

### Step 1: Substrate Loading & Vacuum Chucking
1. Retrieve the post-BOE 180nm DRAM wafer from the cleanroom transport pod using Teflon-coated vacuum wands.
2. Center the wafer on the automated stage chuck with primary wafer notch/flat aligned to standard orientation ($0^\circ$).
3. Engage the chuck vacuum and verify solid chuck vacuum hold prior to scan head motion.

### Step 2: Global Coordinate Alignment & Deskew
1. Initiate the optical vision system to detect the wafer center $(X=0, Y=0)$ and notch/fiducial markers.
2. Perform automated two-point or three-point rotational deskew across pattern alignment fiducials to eliminate angular misalignment ($\theta$).
3. Establish global origin reference $(0, 0)$ aligned to the center die.

### Step 3: 9-Point Radial Coordinate Grid Programming
1. Program the automated coordinate recipe to execute a standard 9-point mapping pattern:
   - **Site 1**: Center die $(0, 0)$.
   - **Sites 2–5 (Inner Ring / Mid-Radius)**: 4 orthogonal points at radius $R_1$ (e.g., $(0, +R_1)$, $(+R_1, 0)$, $(0, -R_1)$, $(-R_1, 0)$).
   - **Sites 6–9 (Outer Ring / Edge)**: 4 orthogonal or interleaved points at radius $R_2$ positioned within the edge exclusion boundary.
2. Define the local scan track at each site, aligning the measurement vector perpendicular to the BOE-patterned $\text{SiO}_2$ trench edge.

### Step 4: Automated Scan Execution & Surface Profiling
1. Initiate the automated batch sequence for the 9 mapped sites.
2. At each site:
   - Perform automated autofocus and local pattern recognition to locate the target step-height feature.
   - Gently lower the stylus/optical probe into measurement position and execute the traverse scan across the patterned trench.
   - Record vertical displacement/film profile data.
3. Automatically retract the probe to safe transit clearance height before traversing to the subsequent programmed coordinate.

### Step 5: Data Extraction, Non-Uniformity Mapping & Unloading
1. Calculate step heights, remaining oxide thickness, and etch depths across all 9 measured locations.
2. Compile radial non-uniformity profiles and evaluate measurement dispersion.
3. Move stage to the load/unload position, disengage vacuum chuck, and return the wafer to the carrier lot.

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Specification | Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Measurement Gauge Repeatability (CV)** | $\text{CV} < 1.0\%$ across 9-point mapping | $\%$ (Coefficient of Variation) |
| **Dielectric Gate Oxide Baseline Precision** | Sub-Angstrom precision within $\pm 0.05$ | $\text{nm}$ |
| **Photoresist Mask Baseline Measurement Tolerance** | Within $\pm 2$ (nominal thickness $\sim 1.3$) | $\text{nm}$ ($\mu\text{m}$) |
| **Coordinate Mapping Coverage** | Complete execution of 9/9 radial wafer sites | Points / Sites |

---

## 4. Context References & Literature Citations

1. **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
   - *Automated 9-Point Wafer Mapping*: Tracks radial film non-uniformity across spin coating, furnace, and etching runs.
   - *Measurement Precision*: Dry gate oxide ($3.5\text{ nm}$) measured with sub-Angstrom precision ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$); photoresist ($1.3\ \mu\text{m}$) measured within $\pm 2\text{ nm}$.
2. **Four-Point Collinear Probe Metrology for Semiconductor Sheet Resistance**:
   - *Gauge Repeatability & Reproducibility (R&R)*: Must maintain measurement coefficient of variation $\text{CV} < 1.0\%$ across 9-point wafer mapping.
3. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - Context for the underlying 180nm unit cell geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$) and stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) architectures requiring tight step-height and dielectric layer planarization control.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated 9-point radial coordinates (Center, ±r/2, ±r with 3mm edge exclusion on 150mm/200mm wafers) must integrate automated pattern recognition (die-to-die alignment) to eliminate manual theta-rotation error. Stylus force must be calibrated dynamically to 0.05 mN to prevent photoresist micro-plowing or scribe-line tear-out across peripheral test structures, while stage translation speeds must maintain vibration damping below 0.2 nm RMS to guarantee Gauge R&R measurement CV < 1.0%.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Stylus tip convolution artifacts (typically using a 2.0 um diamond stylus with a 60-degree cone) will artificially round vertical sidewalls of anisotropic BOE-etched SiO2 trenches. The mapping routine must enforce baseline leveling against adjacent bare silicon field references and account for lateral step distortion. Furthermore, cross-correlation with post-etch spectroscopic ellipsometry (Psi/Delta Cauchy model extraction) is mandatory to verify that measured step height reflects true SiO2 film removal without under-etch or excessive isotropic undercut.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Diamond-tipped styli are single-source consumables prone to tip chipping, tip flattening, and carbonaceous residue build-up during automated multi-site wafer runs. A secondary source for calibrated 2.0 um/60° styli and VLSI standard quartz step-height calibration masters (certified to ±0.5 nm NIST traceability) must be qualified to prevent metrology cell down-time during high-throughput Gen 1 pilot runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Automated 9-point execution per wafer must complete within a 6-minute cycle-time envelope to prevent wafer queuing bottlenecks ahead of post-etch photoresist strip. Automated CSV/recipe handshakes between the profilometer host PC and the manufacturing execution system (MES) must auto-abort the run if optical pattern alignment fails consecutively on 2 sites.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Photoresist indentation and trench edge gouging caused by uncalibrated stylus over-force (>0.15 mN), yielding artificial step-height under-reporting and defect generation.
1. Theta-skew and stage coordinate drift leading to stylus landing on active DRAM array structures rather than dedicated scribe-line metrology trenches.
1. Airborne organic and particulate contamination on wafer surfaces during prolonged stage mapping, causing baseline distortion and spurious vertical step jumps (>5 nm).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-2-2-01` | **Automated 9-Point Radial Step-Height Repeatability and Gauge R&R Validation** | Automated Contact Stylus Profilometer (KLA Tencor P-7 / Ambios XP-200 equivalent) equipped with 2.0 um 60° diamond stylus, isolation table, and automated theta-alignment stage. | 1. Execute automated Chuck Vacuum and optical theta fine-alignment using wafer notch and alignment fiducials. 2. Load automated 9-point radial recipe: scan length = 500 um, scan speed = 20 um/s, stylus tracking force = 0.05 mN (0.5 mg), sampling frequency = 200 Hz. 3. Perform automated scan sequence across sites 1 through 9. 4. Auto-level baseline using two 50 um reference zones flanking the etch trench. 5. Repeat 9-point sequence for 5 consecutive loading/unloading cycles to collect 45 measurement points. | `Repeatability coefficient of variation (CV = std_dev / mean) across 5 consecutive runs on all 9 sites must be < 1.0%; static step height measurement across all 9 sites must match nominal etch target within ±3.0%.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-2-2-02` | **Multi-Site 9-Point Radial Etch Uniformity and Across-Wafer Variation Profile** | Automated Stylus Profilometer cross-referenced with Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam M-2000DI or equivalent, 193-1690 nm spectral range). | 1. Execute automated 9-point profilometry recipe recording trench step height h_step(i) for sites i = 1..9. 2. Transfer wafer to spectroscopic ellipsometer and measure remaining oxide thickness d_ox(i) in adjacent unmasked test pads at identical 9 radial coordinates using Cauchy model fit (MSE < 2.5). 3. Calculate total initial oxide thickness d_initial(i) = h_step(i) + d_ox(i). 4. Calculate across-wafer etch non-uniformity percentage NU = [(Max(h_step) - Min(h_step)) / (2 * Mean(h_step))] * 100. | `Across-wafer non-uniformity NU <= 2.5%; absolute delta between profilometric step-height and ellipsometric differential oxide thickness |h_step(i) - (d_initial(i) - d_ox(i))| <= 2.0 nm for all 9 measurement sites.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 nitrile cleanroom gloves (double-gloved), Standard ESD-safe cleanroom bunny suit with face mask, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye contact with IPA: Flush with copious amounts of clean deionized water for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of concentrated solvent vapors: Remove personnel to fresh air immediately; supply oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted inside cleanroom ISO Class 5 laminar flow hood; tool exhaust connected to general cleanroom house VOC/solvent exhaust duct maintaining static pressure of -0.2 to -0.5 in. w.g.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA wipes and lint-free cleaning swabs disposed of in certified airtight flammable solid solvent waste bins for dedicated thermal incineration. No aqueous acid or chemical drain connections required during physical metrology operation.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA - lens and chuck cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 - stage floating and blow-off)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-BOE patterned wafer with active patterned photoresist on silicon dioxide; DI water rinsed to 18 MOhm-cm resistivity, spin-dried under UHP N2; hydrophobic exposed Si trench bottom with hydrophilic patterned oxide surface.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Scanned wafer with uncompromised photoresist integrity, zero stylus gouge debris, clean bare silicon trench floors ready for immediate automated oxygen plasma photoresist ashing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time promotes ambient airborne molecular organic contamination (AMC) adsorption and native oxide regrowth (~0.2-0.5 nm) on exposed trench Si, impeding subsequent downstream dry etch/ashing and causing stylus tip contamination.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful automated 9-point radial profilometry scan across full wafer diameter validating post-BOE SiO2 trench step heights, ensuring cross-wafer etch uniformity within Gen 1 DRAM process specifications and Gauge R&R repeatability CV < 1.0% with zero surface gouging.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PROFILOMETRY_9PT_RAW_SCAN_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `WAFER_RADIAL_UNIFORMITY_HEATMAP_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `STYLUS_SURFACE_TRACE_HIGH_RES.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Measurement repeatability coefficient of variation across 9-point radial wafer map** | `0.75%` | < 1.0% | Gauge R&R statistical evaluation across 5 sequential automated 9-point wafer recipe passes |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-BOE trench step-height radial non-uniformity across 9 measurement sites** | `1.8%` | <= 2.5% | Calculated via (Max_Step - Min_Step) / (2 * Mean_Step) * 100 on 9 radial coordinates |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum stylus measurement indentation depth on unbaked photoresist mask edges** | `0.0 nm` | < 0.5 nm | Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) trace audit across stylus-scanned scribe-line test trench |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 9 radial sites successfully scanned without stage collision or pattern loss; raw CSV and processed PDF reports automatically archived to MES repository; ASSERT-01 through ASSERT-03 confirmed within tolerances; formal metrology engineer signoff executed in wafer lot routing card.

```text
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Acceptance Gate &    │
│    SPC Disposition     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

### Step 1: Pre-Scan Reference Standard Verification
1. Load certified calibration reference standard onto stylus profilometer vacuum chuck.
2. Execute calibration scan across certified step standard. Verify vertical displacement accuracy and linearity against standard limits prior to production wafer loading.
3. Clean profilometer diamond stylus tip with automated solvent brush cycle to eliminate organic particulates.

### Step 2: Multi-Site Wafer Loading & Recipe Execution
1. Load 180nm post-BOE etched wafer onto vacuum stage; confirm vacuum seal ($> 80\text{ kPa}$).
2. Load automated pattern recognition recipe targeting the 180nm isolation/dielectric test trenches adjacent to cell layout structures (cell access channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
3. Execute automated 49-point wafer map scan tracking radial distribution from center to edge. Stylus traverses across unetched hard mask reference planes ($\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ hard mask with nominal refractive index $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$) into the BOE-etched trench bottoms.

### Step 3: Raw Profile Baseline Levelling & Step-Height Extraction
1. Apply 2-point linear baseline subtraction across the hard mask shoulders on each side of the trench to correct stage tilt.
2. Place reference cursor band $R$ on unetched surface shoulder and measurement cursor band $M$ across the central 50% bottom plane of the etched trench floor.
3. Extract step height $H_i = \bar{Z}_R - \bar{Z}_M$ for each site $i \in [1, 49]$.

### Step 4: Radial Uniformity Computation & Outlier Screening
1. Compute mean etch trench depth ($\bar{H}$), standard deviation ($\sigma$), and percent radial non-uniformity across all 49 measurement sites:
   $$\text{Non-Uniformity (\%)} = \frac{H_{\max} - H_{\min}}{2 \times \bar{H}} \times 100\%$$
2. Cross-verify profilometry step-height profiles against post-etch spectroscopic reflectometry/ellipsometry thickness measurements for the remaining thermal oxide / pad oxide.

### Step 5: Disposition & Metrology Data Logging
1. Transfer extracted 49-point profile dataset into the Fab Statistical Process Control (SPC) database.
2. Flag any wafer exceeding within-wafer non-uniformity thresholds for review by the Etch Engineering module.

---

| **Ellipsometry Reference Precision** | 0.00 | $\le \pm 0.05$ | nm | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry Context |
| **Target Critical Feature Channel Length ($L$)** | 180 | $180 \pm 10$ | nm | 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology Context |

## 4. Cited Literature References
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Access transistor dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$), folded bitline cell layout geometry, and dielectric layer integration.
- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks:** Refractive index validation ($n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$) and high etch resistance against BOE (etch rate $< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$) enabling stable profilometric top-reference planes.
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology:** Automated 49-point wafer mapping methodology for tracking radial film non-uniformity and sub-Angstrom optical measurement precision ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-BOE stylus profilometry relies on direct mechanical contact, introducing potential stylus tip convolution and micro-scratching on soft photoresist masks or unannealed oxide films; contact stylus loading force must be constrained to <= 1.0 mg to prevent permanent plastic deformation while scanning across high-aspect trench edges.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Accurate step-height extraction for 180nm DRAM isolation and gate oxide patterns requires baseline leveling with dual-cursor algorithms over at least 50 um flat plateau regions to decouple wafer bow/warp from true chemical wet-etch step depth, followed by validation against an ISO/NIST-traceable certified step standard.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Certified VLSI or NIST-traceable step height calibration standards (e.g., nominal 100 nm and 500 nm SiO2/Si steps) along with diamond stylus replacement tips (2.0 um radius) require strict single-vendor sourcing with 8-12 week lead times; lack of backup standards risks complete metrology line suspension.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Multi-site wafer scanning across 9 sites per 150mm/200mm wafer increases total metrology overhead by up to 45 minutes per lot; automated recipe execution, multi-point coordinate mapping, and instantaneous sigma calculation are mandatory to prevent metrology lot queuing bottlenecks.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Tip chipping or blunting causing severe lateral broadening, false step-height rounding, and baseline drift exceeding +/- 15 nm.
1. Excessive stylus contact force (> 3.0 mg) causing photoresist gouging and particle generation across active device areas.
1. Uncompensated wafer tilt and vacuum chuck micro-particulates inducing artificial step-height variance > 10% across wafer diameter.

### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Node Title:** Etch Depth Profile Extraction, Radial Non-Uniformity Mapping, and Cross-Metrology Correlation  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1) $\text{SiO}_2$ Patterning > Post-Etch Spectroscopic Ellipsometry & Profilometry Metrology Inspection > Stylus Profilometry Step-Height & Etch Trench Uniformity Characterization > Post-BOE Etch Trench Step-Height Profilometry Recipe Setup and Scan Execution > Etch Depth Profile Extraction, Radial Non-Uniformity Mapping, and Cross-Metrology Correlation  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type:** Buy (Metrology Hardware COTS)

---

#### 1. Metrology Architecture & Workflow

```text
│      Step Height       │    │       Thickness        │
```

---

#### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

##### Step 1: Pre-Etch Baseline Optical Data Extraction
1. Load the pre-etch Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (SE) wafer map database.
2. Verify pre-etch film thickness data acquired via Cauchy dispersion modeling ($n(\lambda), k(\lambda)$) across the standard automated **9-point radial map** or **49-point wafer map**.
3. Ensure dry thermal oxide baseline measurement uncertainty meets precision specs ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$).

##### Step 2: Stylus Profilometry Step-Height Profile Extraction
1. Mount the post-BOE etched and solvent-stripped wafer onto the vacuum chuck of the stylus profilometer.
2. Execute line scans across etched $\text{SiO}_2$ step edges at established radial coordinates ($r = 0\text{ mm}$ [center], $r = 25\text{ mm}$, $r = 50\text{ mm}$, and $r = 70\text{ mm}$ [edge]).
3. Apply standard two-point baseline leveling across the unetched oxide terrace and calculate physical trench depth $d_{\text{stylus}}(r)$ at each radial point.

##### Step 3: Post-Etch Optical Thickness & Etch Delta Calculation
1. Transfer wafer to the Spectroscopic Ellipsometry stage and align wafer notch/flat.
2. Measure remaining oxide thickness $t_{\text{post}}(r)$ across the identical coordinates ($r = 0, 25, 50, 70\text{ mm}$) using Fresnel reflection coefficient polarization ratios:
   $$\rho = \frac{r_p}{r_s} = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$$
3. Compute the optical etch depth delta:
   $$\Delta t_{\text{SE}}(r) = t_{\text{pre}}(r) - t_{\text{post}}(r)$$

##### Step 4: Cross-Metrology Correlation & Calibration
1. Compute the cross-metrology discrepancy at each site:
   $$\delta_{\text{metrology}}(r) = \left| d_{\text{stylus}}(r) - \Delta t_{\text{SE}}(r) \right|$$
2. Confirm correlation alignment against the nominal thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ BOE 6:1 etch rate ($80\text{ nm/min}$ to $100\text{ nm/min}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$).
3. If discrepancy exceeds acceptance threshold, recalibrate the optical Cauchy model refractive index parameters against the physical stylus step reference.

##### Step 5: Radial Non-Uniformity Mapping
1. Calculate the wafer-level radial non-uniformity percentage ($NU_{\%}$) using the min-max metric:
   $$NU_{\%} = \frac{d_{\max} - d_{\min}}{2 \times d_{\text{avg}}} \times 100\%$$
2. Log full 9-point/49-point depth profile and generate the radial trend plot.

#### 5. Local Literature Citations
* **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**: Polarization principle $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \exp(i\Delta)$, Cauchy dispersion parameterization $n(\lambda), k(\lambda)$, gate oxide measurement precision ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$), photoresist thickness tracking ($\pm 2\text{ nm}$), and automated 9-point/49-point wafer mapping.
* **Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 & 7:1) Silicon Dioxide Wet Etch Rates**: $6:1$ ratio of $40\%\text{ NH}_4\text{F} : 49\%\text{ HF}$ maintaining $\text{pH} \approx 4.5$, thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate of $80\text{ nm/min}$ to $100\text{ nm/min}$ ($800\text{ to } 1000\text{ \AA/min}$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$, and high selectivity ($> 100:1$ over Si).
* **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**: Nominal etch rate confirmation ($100\text{ nm/min}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$), bubble mitigation with wetting agents, and HF safety protocols.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Cross-metrology alignment between contact stylus profilometry and non-destructive spectroscopic ellipsometry requires rigid spatial coordinates matching lithography test keys. Stylus tip drag (radius 2.0 um, stylus force >= 3 mg) risks soft-mask/photoresist edge plastic deformation or micro-scratching on active DRAM isolation oxide regions, inducing systematic step-height offsets compared to optical phase shifts (Psi, Delta) extracted via Cauchy/Sellmeier models. Automated fiducial registration must map 49-point polar coordinates (r, theta) across the 150mm/200mm wafer with sub-micron repeatable chuck staging.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Radial etch non-uniformity during isotropic Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE 6:1 NH4F:HF) is predominantly governed by boundary-layer mass-transport limitations, meniscus surface-tension pinning, and fluid vortex dynamics during static/agitated immersion. Ellipsometry derives unetched field SiO2 remaining thickness via optical model fitting (assuming n=1.46 at 632.8 nm), whereas stylus profilometry measures physical topological step height between photoresist/unmasked oxide and etched trenches. Accurate correlation demands subtracting residual photoresist thickness measured prior to resist strip, or profilometer validation performed strictly post-resist ash/piranha clean.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Diamond stylus tips (2 um radius) degrade via tip-rounding and particulate chipping when profiling sharp oxide steps, requiring scheduled cantilever compliance calibration and qualification against NIST-traceable step-height standards (VLSI Standards 180nm/500nm). High-purity calibration wafer availability and spare stylus sensor heads represent a single-point failure for continuous in-line metrology loops in Gen 1 pilot fab lines.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Dual-tool wafer mapping across 49 die locations introduces an 18-minute metrology bottleneck per wafer if stylus scan speeds are set below 20 um/s to suppress vibrational bounce. We must freeze a 9-point radial benchmark protocol for standard line monitoring, expanding to full 49-point cross-metrology correlation only during initial BOE bath qualification and etch rate recalibration cycles.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Photoresist sidewall rounding or mechanical gouging under high stylus tip tracking force, generating false step-height inflation or trench depth underestimation.
1. Optical dispersion model mismatch in spectroscopic ellipsometry caused by etch-induced surface microroughness (RMS > 1.5 nm) or fluoropolymer/fluorosilicate residual film on etched SiO2 trench bottoms, skewing delta-psi phase regressions.
1. Spatial registration drift (> 50 um) between optical ellipsometer spot center (approx. 25-50 um beam waist) and stylus physical scan line, sampling disparate process topography across radial gradient zones.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-3-01` | **49-Point Radial Etch Depth Profilometry and Non-Uniformity Extraction** | KLA Tencor Alpha-Step D-600 Stylus Profilometer with 2.0 um diamond stylus tip and automated wafer chuck | 1. Load wafer onto automated vacuum chuck and align primary flat/notch to 0 degrees. 2. Calibrate stylus force to exactly 1.5 mg and set scan speed to 20 um/s over a 500 um scan length across predefined metrology test keys (100 um wide oxide trenches). 3. Execute programmed 49-point polar mapping pattern spanning center (r=0 mm) to edge (r=70 mm on 150mm wafer). 4. Perform baseline leveling on unetched oxide plateau and extract step height (delta-Z) for each location. 5. Compute mean etch depth (D_mean), standard deviation (sigma), and wafer radial non-uniformity percentage: NU (%) = [(D_max - D_min) / (2 * D_mean)] * 100. | `Target etch depth = 180.0 nm; Absolute allowable range: 171.0 nm to 189.0 nm (±5.0%). Wafer radial non-uniformity NU <= 3.5% across all 49 measured sites. Stylus scan profile must exhibit zero stick-slip noise (Ra on unetched plateau < 0.8 nm).` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-3-02` | **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry vs. Stylus Profilometry Cross-Metrology Correlation** | J.A. Woollam M-2000 Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (245-1000 nm spectral range, 70-degree angle of incidence) and KLA Tencor Alpha-Step D-600 | 1. Mount wafer onto M-2000 vacuum stage with identical coordinate origin. 2. Measure remaining oxide thickness in broad unmasked etch pads adjacent to the profilometer test keys across the identical 49 die locations. 3. Apply Cauchy dielectric dispersion model (An=1.457, Bn=0.0035, Cn=0.00013) to solve for remaining thickness (T_post). 4. Calculate optical etch depth: D_optical = T_pre - T_post. 5. Perform linear regression and residual error analysis: Residual_i = |D_optical,i - D_stylus,i|. 6. Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient R^2 across all 49 data points. | `Pearson correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.985. Mean absolute residual deviation between optical depth and stylus step height <= 2.5 nm across all sites. No individual site residual to exceed 4.0 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: 14-mil butyl/neoprene blend chemical gloves over nitrile inner gloves, ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash face shield with indirect-vent goggles, Chemical-resistant PTFE/acid apron with heat-sealed seams, Full-coverage cleanroom bunny suit with chemically impervious arm gauntlets
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with HF/BOE residues: Immediately rinse under emergency deluge shower for 15 seconds, strip all contaminated garments, and massage Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%) into affected tissue until medical emergency services arrive. For eye exposure: Flush continuously at eye wash station for 15 minutes using sterile 1.0% calcium gluconate eye wash or isotonic saline. Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh uncontaminated air, administer 100% humidified medical oxygen, and immediately dispatch emergency response.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet chemical etch and strip benches must maintain dedicated acid exhaust with face velocity of 100 to 120 FPM (0.51 to 0.61 m/s) at sash opening, interlocked with differential pressure sensors (Magnehelic delta-P >= 0.75 in w.g.) tied into wet bench auto-abort circuits. Metrology tools operate in Class 100 cleanroom air laminar flow hoods with 0.45 m/s downflow velocity.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Fluoride-bearing etch rinse effluent routed to dedicated Fluoride Waste Treatment (FWT) line for calcium fluoride precipitation via hydrated lime Ca(OH)2 addition, targeting effluent F- < 10 ppm. Never combine HF waste with general acid-waste neutralization (AWN) streams due to calcium scale clogging and exothermic off-gassing risks.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (component of BOE 6:1)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 4 (UP-S) | `6.8 wt%` |
| **Ammonium Fluoride (component of BOE 6:1)** | `12125-01-8` | SEMI Grade 4 (UP-S) | `34.6 wt%` |
| **Sulfuric Acid (Piranha Clean pre-metrology)** | `7664-93-9` | SEMI Grade 3 | `96.0 wt%` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (Piranha Clean pre-metrology)** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Grade 3 | `30.0 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic/partially hydrophilic patterned thermal/CVD SiO2 wafer exiting BOE etch bath, DI rinse resistivity >= 18.0 MOhm-cm, spin-rinse dry verified with particle count delta < 10 at 0.2 um.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Passivated, fully characterized oxide step-height profiles free of mechanical stylus marks, verified hydrocarbon-free under optical inspection, ready for polysilicon gate deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes uncontrolled native oxide regowth (0.2-0.5 nm) in opened silicon/poly trenches, ambient airborne molecular organic contamination (AMC/siloxanes) altering ellipsometer optical models, and atmospheric moisture absorption inducing surface charging during profilometry.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full radial etch depth extraction and cross-metrology correlation successfully achieved across the 150mm wafer. Stylus profilometer 49-point topology maps demonstrate nominal 180nm etch depth within ±3.5% wafer non-uniformity. Spectroscopic ellipsometry regression shows R^2 >= 0.985 agreement with mechanical step heights, proving valid Cauchy optical modeling and establishing rigorous line process control.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Megasonic Bath & Solvent Degreasing Protocol for Etch Depth Profile Extraction, Radial Non-Uniformity Mapping, and Cross-Metrology Correlation

---

### Process Flow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Solvent Degreasing   │
│  Tank: Acetone / IPA  │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Megasonic Acoustic   │
│       Agitation       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│   DI Water Cascade    │
│    Overflow Rinse     │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│  Surface Preparation  │
│    & Profilometry     │
│       Scanning        │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│     Radial Map &      │
│     Ellipsometry      │
│      Correlation      │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Safety & Wet Bench Preparation**:
   - Verify secondary containment and exhaust airflow at the solvent clean bench.
   - Confirm safety readiness: Ensure hydrofluoric acid emergency protocols are intact following prior BOE handling (calcium gluconate gel must be present and verified on-site).

2. **Solvent Immersion & Megasonic Degreasing**:
   - Immerse post-etch wafer substrate into electronic-grade solvent tank (Acetone followed by Isopropanol) to strip organic residues, photoresist edge beads, and surfactant traces left from buffered etching (e.g., 0.1% Triton X-100 or Fluorad wetting agents).
   - Engage the megasonic acoustic transducer array to dislodge submicron particulate entrapment and particulate debris from etched micro-trenches without damaging fragile topography.

3. **DI Water Cascade Rinse & Spin Rinse Drying (SRD)**:
   - Transfer wafer carrier rapidly to the deionized (DI) water quick-dump/cascade overflow rinse tank until resistivity reaches > 18 MΩ·cm.
   - Execute filtered high-purity $N_2$ spin-rinse drying cycle to eliminate liquid water marks prior to mechanical contact.

4. **Metrology Alignment & Stylus Profilometry Step-Height Scan**:
   - Transfer the dry, degreased wafer to the stylus profilometer staging chuck.
   - Execute mechanical step-height profiling along etched oxide trench boundaries down to the underlying mask/substrate baseline (referencing BOE thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ nominal etch rate baseline of $\sim 100\text{ nm/min}$ / $1000\text{ \AA/min}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$).

5. **Wafer-Level Radial Non-Uniformity Mapping & Ellipsometry Correlation**:
   - Execute programmed 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping scan to quantify radial step-height variations from wafer center to edge.
   - Transfer wafer to spectroscopic ellipsometer to perform cross-metrology correlation (evaluating $\Psi$ and $\Delta$ across optical models such as Cauchy or Sellmeier parameterizations against physical stylus step-height values).

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target & Tolerance | Context / Method Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Profilometry Step-Height Precision (Photoresist Reference Layer)** | $\pm 2\text{ nm}$ | Stylus scan correlated with spectroscopic ellipsometry photoresist thickness baseline ($1.3\text{ }\mu\text{m}$) |
| **Thin Dielectric Metrology Precision (Ellipsometry Correlation)** | $\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$ | Optical measurement of ultra-thin dry oxide films ($3.5\text{ nm}$) |
| **Wet Bench Temperature Stability** | $25^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ | BOE 6:1 thermal oxide etch rate reference condition ($\sim 100\text{ nm/min}$) |
| **Radial Mapping Grid Coverage** | Standard 9-point or 49-point automated pattern | Radial distribution mapping across wafer diameter |

---

### Cited Literature References

1. **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
   - Established BOE 6:1 (6 parts 40% $\text{NH}_4\text{F}$ : 1 part 49% $\text{HF}$) baseline thermal $\text{SiO}_2$ etch rate of $\sim 100\text{ nm/min}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Addressed wetting agent residue cleanup ($0.1\%$ Triton X-100 or Fluorad) and required safety presence of calcium gluconate gel.
2. **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**:
   - Established cross-metrology correlation equations ($\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$), Cauchy/Sellmeier dispersion modeling, precision targets ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$ for $3.5\text{ nm}$ oxide; $\pm 2\text{ nm}$ for $1.3\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ photoresist), and automated 9-point or 49-point radial wafer mapping protocols.
3. **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**:
   - Baseline selectivity verification for underlying or adjacent $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ stop/mask layers with index $n = 2.00 \pm 0.02$ at $632.8\text{ nm}$ and high chemical resistance ($< 0.5\text{ nm/min}$ in BOE).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-BOE patterned wafers retain fluorocarbon polymers, micro-bubble surfactants (Triton X-100/Fluorad residues), and trace ammonium fluoride crystals inside high-aspect-ratio 180nm trenches. Integrating solvent degreasing (NMP/Acetone/IPA) with a 1 MHz megasonic bath removes these particulates without mechanical cavitation damage to fragile patterned oxide sidewalls, ensuring clean baseline contact for stylus profilometry and spectroscopic ellipsometry cross-correlation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Acoustic streaming dissipation in standard ultrasonic tanks (<100 kHz) causes severe cavitation pitting and pattern collapse in sub-micron SiO2 features. Operating strictly at 0.95-1.05 MHz megasonic agitation with a power density limit of <= 1.5 W/cm2 provides laminar acoustic boundary layer thinning (~0.2 um) enabling total solvent solvating of organic residues and surfactant monolayers while preventing transient acoustic cavitation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade solvent mixtures (VLSI / SEMI Grade 1 NMP, Acetone, and IPA) and megasonic-rated quartz immersion tanks must be qualified for high chemical purity (trace metal < 1 ppb, particle count < 10 particles/mL at >= 0.2 um). Supply chain shortages of ultra-pure IPA or fluoropolymer carrier cassettes require strict closed-loop bath filtration (0.05 um PTFE recirculating filter) to maintain bath life beyond 48 operational hours.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Executing this wet degreasing step directly links wet chemical etching to physical and optical metrology. Uncontrolled bath temperature or uncalibrated immersion duration will create wafer-to-wafer cycle time drift and bottleneck profilometry recipe queues. Clean validation gate ensures that subsequent radial uniformity mapping across 200mm wafers operates on particle-free substrates.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Megasonic transducer power spike (> 2.0 W/cm2) triggering structural delamination or chipping of micro-patterned oxide trench edges prior to stylus contact.
1. Solvent dry-stain and micro-precipitation during rapid acetone-to-IPA transfer, depositing insoluble organic halos inside etch trenches that distort stylus step-height measurement by > 15 nm.
1. Incomplete megasonic acoustic coupling due to degas failure in the bath, leaving bubble entrapment in 180nm deep features and shielding local etch residues from dissolution.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-3-1-01` | **Post-Solvent Degreasing Surface Residue & Organic Particle Density Verification** | Laser Surface Particle Scanner / Defect Inspection System (KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP2 or equivalent calibrated down to 60 nm) | 1. Load dried 200mm wafer onto automated laser inspection stage under class 1 laminar flow hood. 2. Calibrate edge exclusion zone to 3.0 mm. 3. Execute full-wafer dark-field laser scattering scan with sensitivity threshold set to >= 0.1 um particle size. 4. Extract total particle count, spatial particle coordinate map, and cluster distribution across center, middle, and edge radial zones. 5. Cross-reference defect coordinates against unpatterned reference die. | `Total added particle count (>= 0.1 um) across entire 200mm wafer surface must be <= 15 particles (< 0.05 particles/cm2), with zero localized particle clusters or residue halos detected inside patterned trench inspection cells.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-3-1-02` | **Megasonic Cavitation Integrity and Oxide Step-Height Preservation Test** | High-Resolution Stylus Profilometer (Bruker DektakXT or KLA Alpha-Step D-600 with 2 um radius diamond stylus, 1.0 mg stylus tracking force) | 1. Position cleaned wafer on vacuum chuck and align 5 reference coordinate dies across wafer radius (center, +/- 45mm, +/- 90mm). 2. Perform 500 um line scans across 180nm BOE etch trench step features at 10 um/s scan rate and 0.02 um lateral sampling resolution. 3. Extract baseline oxide step height, trench bottom surface roughness (Ra), and trench sidewall edge sharpness profile. 4. Compare post-megasonic step height against pre-degreasing ellipsometric film thickness differential measurements. | `Trench bottom surface roughness Ra must be <= 0.8 nm; step-height measurement repeatability across 3 consecutive scans at each site must show standard deviation sigma <= 0.5 nm; cross-correlation delta between stylus step-height and spectroscopic ellipsometry thickness delta must be <= 1.5 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant double-layer nitrile over fluoropolymer (Silver Shield/4H) inner gloves, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1, Acid/solvent-resistant flame-retardant cleanroom apron, Vapor-tight chemical safety goggles, Static-dissipative cleanroom safety boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For solvent inhalation: Evacuate victim immediately to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored. For skin contact with NMP/Acetone/IPA: Flush immediately with copious flowing water for a minimum of 15 minutes while removing contaminated clothing. In the event of secondary or residual HF contact (post-BOE transfer error): Immediately flush affected skin for 2 minutes, then massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel continuously into exposed area until medical emergency personnel arrive. For eye exposure: Irrigate eyes at eyewash station for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek urgent ophthalmological evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated explosive-proof solvent wet bench with constant face velocity between 0.45 m/s and 0.55 m/s (90 to 110 fpm). Continuous volatile organic compound (VOC) vapor extraction to dedicated VOC central scrubber exhaust ducting. Real-time infrared LEL (Lower Explosive Limit) detection sensors set to alarm at 10% LEL and trip automatic bath fire-suppression (CO2/N2 purge) at 25% LEL.

critics.systems_engineer: Post-BOE patterned wafers retain fluorocarbon polymers, micro-bubble surfactants (Triton X-100/Fluorad residues), and trace ammonium fluoride crystals inside high-aspect-ratio 180nm trenches. Integrating solvent degreasing (NMP/Acetone/IPA) with a 1 MHz megasonic bath removes these particulates without mechanical cavitation damage to fragile patterned oxide sidewalls, ensuring clean baseline contact for stylus profilometry and spectroscopic ellipsometry cross-correlation.
critics.domain_expert: Acoustic streaming dissipation in standard ultrasonic tanks (<100 kHz) causes severe cavitation pitting and pattern collapse in sub-micron SiO2 features. Operating strictly at 0.95-1.05 MHz megasonic agitation with a power density limit of <= 1.5 W/cm2 provides laminar acoustic boundary layer thinning (~0.2 um) enabling total solvent solvating of organic residues and surfactant monolayers while preventing transient acoustic cavitation.
critics.supply_chain: Electronic-grade solvent mixtures (VLSI / SEMI Grade 1 NMP, Acetone, and IPA) and megasonic-rated quartz immersion tanks must be qualified for high chemical purity (trace metal < 1 ppb, particle count < 10 particles/mL at >= 0.2 um). Supply chain shortages of ultra-pure IPA or fluoropolymer carrier cassettes require strict closed-loop bath filtration (0.05 um PTFE recirculating filter) to maintain bath life beyond 48 operational hours.
critics.laya_pm: Executing this wet degreasing step directly links wet chemical etching to physical and optical metrology. Uncontrolled bath temperature or uncalibrated immersion duration will create wafer-to-wafer cycle time drift and bottleneck profilometry recipe queues. Clean validation gate ensures that subsequent radial uniformity mapping across 200mm wafers operates on particle-free substrates.
critical_failure_modes: Megasonic transducer power spike (> 2.0 W/cm2) triggering structural delamination or chipping of micro-patterned oxide trench edges prior to stylus contact.
Solvent dry-stain and micro-precipitation during rapid acetone-to-IPA transfer, depositing insoluble organic halos inside etch trenches that distort stylus step-height measurement by > 15 nm.
Incomplete megasonic acoustic coupling due to degas failure in the bath, leaving bubble entrapment in 180nm deep features and shielding local etch residues from dissolution.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): PTFE Acid Immersion Cassette & Neutralizer for Etch Depth Profile Extraction, Radial Non-Uniformity Mapping, and Cross-Metrology Correlation

**Discipline / Category**: Safety Infrastructure  
**Target Generation**: Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type**: Buy

---

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / ISO Class 6 laminar flow bench, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (acid/solvent exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Substrate Fixturing
- Mount substrate securely onto vacuum chuck stage and align mechanical/optical fiducials.
- Zero baseline instruments and establish background electrical/chemical noise floor.

### 3. Recipe Execution & Parameter Control
- Execute process sequence according to verified engineering specifications.
- Monitor thermal, optical, or chemical rate transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Acceptance
- Perform quantitative verification using 4-Point Probe / Ellipsometer / Fume Hood Interlock.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The mechanical tolerance and thermal dissipation profile of the virgin PTFE acid immersion cassette must withstand rapid thermal cycling from room temperature up to 130°C during exothermic acid contact without dimensional warping (>0.1 mm distortion) or wafer pocket pinching. Cassette design must provide uniform laminar fluid flow between wafer slots to prevent stagnant boundary layers that skew subsequent post-etch radial non-uniformity mapping and profilometry correlation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-purity virgin PTFE (fluoropolymer) cassettes must exhibit zero extractable trace metal ions (<0.1 ppb Fe, Cu, Ni, Ca) and zero fluoropolymer particulate shedding into aggressive oxidizer baths. Chemical neutralization tanks must feature automated pH-monitored exotherm moderation using diluted sodium bicarbonate or potassium hydroxide slurries with high-volume N2 sparging to prevent thermal runaway and effervescence carryover.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Virgin PTFE semiconductor-grade 100mm/150mm cassette carriers and high-capacity polyolefin/PTFE neutralizer rinse baths must be procured from qualified cleanroom equipment fabricators (e.g., Entegris or certified custom fluoropolymer CNC specialists) with certified USP Class VI / SEMI F57 extraction documentation to circumvent lead times exceeding 12 weeks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Safety infrastructure must be validated, leak-tested, and fully integrated into wet-bench bay exhausts before running wet chemical oxide profiling wafers; incomplete neutralizer hookup or cassette dimension non-conformance will halt subsequent step-height stylus profilometry milestones across the Gen 1 DRAM front-end run.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal expansion creep or thermal shock warping of the PTFE cassette causing edge-contact stress, wafer breakage, or micro-scratching across active 180nm DRAM test structures.
1. Inadequate fluid drain and rinse clearance between cassette teeth causing chemical hang-up and localized over-etching, skewing radial step-height profiling.
1. Violent exothermic boil-over or gas entrapment in the neutralizer station during high-concentration acid neutralization, leading to localized containment breach and operator acid splash hazard.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-3-2-01` | **PTFE Cassette Thermal Shock and Slot Dimensional Stability Verification** | Mitutoyo Digimatic Calipers, Keyence Optical Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM), Controlled Hot Acid Bath (130°C), Ultra-pure DI Water Quench Tank | 1. Submerge empty PTFE cassette into a heated bath at 130°C +/- 2°C for 30 minutes. 2. Rapidly transfer cassette within 5 seconds into 20°C DI water bath and soak for 10 minutes. 3. Repeat thermal shock cycle 5 times. 4. Blow dry with high-purity filtered N2 and stabilize at 21.0°C for 2 hours. 5. Measure slot pitch, pocket spacing, and planar orthogonality across 25 slots using optical CMM. | `Slot pitch dimensional deviation <= 0.05 mm across all 25 slots; maximum cassette frame warpage <= 0.10 mm; zero structural micro-cracking or plastic deformation.` |
| `TC-BOE-OXIDE-ETCH-3-3-2-3-2-02` | **Immersion Neutralizer Effervescence and Thermal Exotherm Quench Capacity** | Submersible PTFE-jacketed thermocouple array (4 probes), In-line High-accuracy pH meter (0.01 pH resolution), Flow-controlled N2 sparger system | 1. Introduce 500 mL of concentrated acid solution into the active neutralization tank over a 60-second metered dispensing cycle. 2. Log peak temperature across all 4 submerged thermocouple probes at 1 Hz sampling rate. 3. Monitor pH inflection curve until solution stabilizes. 4. Inspect visual containment splash guards for liquid aerosol carryover. 5. Measure final neutralized effluent pH after 5 minutes of automated mixing. | `Maximum transient peak exotherm temperature <= 45.0°C; final neutralized effluent pH stabilized within 6.5 to 8.5 within 300 seconds; zero liquid aerosol escape outside perimeter lip-exhaust zone.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl/neoprene multi-layer acid gloves (tested against concentrated H2SO4/HF/H2O2), Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield with wrap-around side guards, Acid-resistant heavy-duty vinyl/PTFE apron with sleeve guards, Closed-toe cleanroom safety boots with chemical-resistant overshoes, Cleanroom Class 100 chemical-resistant coverall and nitrile under-gloves
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Immediate immersion eyewash/safety shower within 10 seconds (max 5 meters away). For skin contact: strip all contaminated clothing immediately, flush skin under continuous deluge water for minimum 15 minutes. For accidental HF trace exposure, massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel continuously into affected skin until medical personnel arrive. Call emergency response immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Wet bench dedicated acid scrubber exhaust with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) at full sash opening; equipped with continuous differential pressure sensor and audio-visual low-flow alarm interlocking chemical dispense solenoids.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent chemical streams must undergo controlled automated batch neutralization with temperature feedback control and active continuous N2 bubbling; pH must equilibrate to 6.5 - 8.5 before discharge to the facility Industrial Waste Neutralization (IWN) system.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sulfuric Acid** | `7664-93-9` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI Tier 3 / Cleanroom Class) | `96.0% - 98.0% w/w` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | Electronic Grade (SEMI Tier 3 / Cleanroom Class) | `30.0% - 32.0% w/w` |
| **Sodium Bicarbonate** | `144-55-8` | Reagent Grade / Industrial Neutralization Grade | `10.0% w/v aqueous solution` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-strip clean wafer surface with chemical native oxide or partially etched thermal/TEOS oxide, free of gross organic photoresist residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Neutralized, ultra-pure DI water rinsed (resistivity >= 18.2 MOhm*cm) and spin-rinse dried wafer surface ready for step-height stylus profilometry without salt precipitates.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes airborne organic volatile airborne particulate adsorption and uneven native oxide regrowth (>1.5 nm) skewing sub-nanometer stylus step-height profiling accuracy and radial non-uniformity mapping.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical and operational qualification of the PTFE acid immersion cassette and automated neutralization bath, validating thermal/mechanical slot pitch stability, extractable trace metal purity, and exotherm-controlled effluent neutralization to support precise post-etch step-height stylus profilometry.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ptfe_cassette_thermal_cmm_dimension_report.pdf`
- [ ] `acid_neutralizer_exotherm_ph_characterization.csv`
- [ ] `ptfe_carrier_trace_metal_icpms_certificate.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum cassette wafer slot pitch distortion post-thermal cycling** | `0.02 mm` | <= 0.05 mm | High-magnification optical coordinate measuring machine (CMM) inspection across all 25 slots |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Neutralizer bath effluent temperature surge during maximum acid charge** | `35.0 °C` | <= 45.0 °C | Multi-channel calibrated submerged thermocouple logging during continuous 500 mL acid introduction |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Final neutralized effluent pH before drainage transfer** | `7.20` | +/- 0.80 pH units | Calibrated dual-electrode semiconductor-grade pH probe logging |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 25 slots of the virgin PTFE cassette demonstrate pitch deviation <= 0.05 mm without pocket binding; neutralization bath maintains peak exotherm <= 45.0°C with effluent stabilized between pH 6.5 and 8.5; zero safety trip/interlock faults verified by Lead Cleanroom EHS Engineer and Process Metrology Lead.
