# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Megasonic Transducer Acoustic Power Density Calibration

**Task Title:** Megasonic Transducer Acoustic Power Density Calibration  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > Standard RCA-1 & RCA-2 Wafer Cleaning Line [Chemical Processing] > RCA-1 / DHF Oxide Strip / RCA-2 Wet Sequence Execution [Wet Chemistry] > RCA Chemical Bath Preparation & Megasonic Tank Qualification [Wet Chemistry] > Megasonic Transducer Acoustic Power Density Calibration [Wet Chemistry]  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 2 (180nm / $\mu\text{m}$)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Workflow

In 180nm DRAM fabrication featuring high-aspect-ratio stacked capacitors (Crown/Cylinder topologies with sub-400 nm pitch), megasonic agitation provides acoustic microstreaming essential for removing sub-micron particulates during RCA-1/RCA-2 cleaning. Over-power acoustic transients induce mechanical cavitation damage that fractures delicate crown structures, while under-power yields incomplete particle removal. This calibration routine benchmarks and normalizes the piezoelectric transducer array power output across the entire active liquid immersion plane.

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│  Tank Inspection &   │
│     DIW Degas        │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│   Piezo Hydrophone   │
│   Grid Positioning   │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│  RF Generator Power  │
│     Step Mapping     │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│  Uniformity Check &  │
│   Tool Certification │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Safety Interlock & Bath Degas Verification:**
   - Confirm bath overflow recirculation is active with fresh Ultra-Pure Deionized Water (UPW/DIW).
   - Ensure the integrated in-line degassing unit reduces dissolved oxygen ($O_2$) content below cavitation-nucleation saturation limits to prevent erratic bubble scattering.
   - Verify tank grounding and RF shielding integrity.

2. **Hydrophone Calibration Grid Setup:**
   - Mount a calibrated calibrated piezoelectric needle hydrophone (piezo-ceramic sensor) onto an automated 3-axis ($X$-$Y$-$Z$) immersion scanner stage.
   - Position the sensor tip at the wafer-plane active region (nominally $30 \pm 1\text{ mm}$ above the quartz/sapphire transducer window face).
   - Initialize scanning boundaries matching the wafer carrier immersion footprint.

3. **RF Generator Frequency & Tuning Matching:**
   - Power on the megasonic RF generator ($0.8 - 1.0\text{ MHz}$ nominal operational band).
   - Engage auto-tuning circuit and confirm reflected power ($P_{\text{refl}}$) is minimized relative to forward power ($P_{\text{fwd}}$) into the piezoelectric array.

4. **Multi-Point Acoustic Power Density Mapping:**
   - Execute a 25-point spatial raster across the horizontal wafer-exposure plane at low forward power setting ($20\%$).
   - Record root-mean-square acoustic pressure ($P_{\text{rms}}$) and calculate acoustic power density:
     $$I_{\text{ac}} = \frac{P_{\text{rms}}^2}{\rho c} \quad (\text{W/cm}^2)$$
     *(where $\rho$ is DIW fluid density and $c$ is the acoustic speed of sound in water).*
   - Increment RF power across operating steps ($40\%$, $60\%$, $80\%$, $100\%$) and document linearity curves.

5. **Uniformity Calculation & Drift Analysis:**
   - Calculate within-bath acoustic power density non-uniformity:
     $$\text{Non-Uniformity (\%)} = \left(\frac{I_{\text{max}} - I_{\text{min}}}{2 \times I_{\text{mean}}}\right) \times 100$$
   - Check for transducer element dead spots or focal hot spots exceeding safe thresholds.
   - Save calibration profiles to the wet-bench process controller and log qualification status.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance Band | Measurement Method / Tooling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Acoustic Power Density ($I_{\text{ac}}$)** | $1.20\text{ W/cm}^2$ | $\pm 0.10\text{ W/cm}^2$ | Calibrated Immersion Hydrophone Probe |
| **Planar Acoustic Power Non-Uniformity** | $\le 5.0\%$ | Upper specification limit | 25-Point Immersion Grid Raster Scan |
| **RF Generator Reflected Power Ratio ($P_{\text{refl}} / P_{\text{fwd}}$)** | $\le 2.0\%$ | Max allowable impedance mismatch | In-Line Directional RF Wattmeter / Generator Telemetry |
| **Acoustic Drift over 30-min Continuous Run** | $\le \pm 1.5\%$ | Peak-to-peak deviation | Continuous Stationary Center-Point Hydrophone Monitor |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

* **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]:**
  - High-aspect-ratio stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) structures erected via tungsten plug (W-plug) require strictly calibrated megasonic acoustic density limits to eliminate particle contamination while preventing mechanical shear collapse or pattern peeling across dense memory arrays.
* **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]:**
  - Highlights tight cell geometry with wordline and bitline pitch at approximately $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$ and ultra-thin gate dielectric (~$3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness), underscoring the requirement for uniform megasonic power distribution to prevent localized gate or dielectric fracture during RCA chemical bath processing.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Megasonic power calibration directly influences acoustic streaming boundary layer thinning versus cavitation-induced physical damage. The primary systems vulnerability is spatial acoustic standing-wave non-uniformity across the immersion tank, generating localized hot-spots that degrade sub-micron polysilicon or gate oxide structures while leaving stagnant dead zones under-cleaned.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Operating in the 0.8 MHz to 1.5 MHz regime requires strict power density regulation between 1.0 and 2.5 W/cm2. Excessive acoustic power causes transient cavitation and surface pitting, whereas insufficient power fails to overcome particle-to-substrate Van der Waals and electrostatic double-layer forces in RCA-1 (SC-1) alkaline solutions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement of calibrated piezoelectric quartz/PZT transducer plates, impedance-matched RF generators, and hydrophone acoustic sensors faces vendor lead times exceeding 12 to 16 weeks; secondary sourcing of chemical-resistant PFA tank liners and immersible wireless cavitation probes is essential to avoid cleanroom qualification halts.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The calibration schedule must tightly synchronize with initial RCA chemical bath fill cycles. Uncalibrated transducer run-in risks damaging preliminary 180nm pilot wafers; hydrophone spatial mapping must execute within an allocated 48-hour preventive maintenance and qualification window.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Piezoelectric crystal delamination or decoupling from the tank bottom leading to severe acoustic power loss and non-uniform particle removal.
1. Transient acoustic cavitation hot-spots causing mechanical micro-fractures, pattern collapse, and gate edge erosion on 180nm features.
1. RF generator impedance mismatch causing thermal runaway in the megasonic transducer housing and subsequent bath temperature instability.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-2-1-2-01` | **Acoustic Power Density and Transducer Uniformity Hydrophone Mapping** | Submersible calibrated piezoelectric hydrophone (0.5-2.0 MHz range) mounted on automated 3-axis XYZ stage, digital storage oscilloscope, and RF wattmeter. | 1. Position hydrophone 10 mm above transducer array surface at 25 grid points across wafer exposure plane. 2. Activate megasonic generator at nominal setpoint (e.g., 1.5 W/cm2, 1.0 MHz). 3. Record peak-to-peak voltage on oscilloscope and compute acoustic pressure (kPa) and acoustic power density (W/cm2). 4. Traverse across full bath volume to detect standing-wave nodes and antinodes. | `Acoustic power density must read 1.50 ± 0.15 W/cm2 across the central 300 mm zone; acoustic field spatial non-uniformity must be <= 5.0% across all 25 measurement points.` |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-2-1-2-02` | **Acoustic Cavitation Damage and Pinhole Qualification on Thin Oxide Monitor Wafers** | Brightfield wafer inspection tool (particle detection down to 0.18 um), ellipsometer, optical microscope, and aluminum foil cavitation witness sheet. | 1. Immerse bare aluminum witness foil for 30 seconds to map physical erosion pitting pattern. 2. Immerse 10nm SiO2 monitor wafers for 10 minutes under 100% duty cycle megasonic agitation. 3. Rinse in QDR, spin-dry under N2, and inspect wafer surface for pinhole generation, pitting, and defect adder counts. | `Aluminum foil test must exhibit uniform micro-perforation density without concentrated tearing (>1 mm); wafer inspection must confirm zero oxide pinholes and delta particle count <= 5 adders at >= 180nm threshold.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant neoprene apron and sleeves, Heavy-duty butyl gloves over inner nitrile gloves, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield with ANSI Z87.1 safety glasses, Class 100 cleanroom-compatible chemical splash boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush with sterile saline/water for minimum 20 minutes under eye-wash station. Skin contact: Drench under emergency shower; for HF exposure, immediately massage Calcium Gluconate 2.5% gel into skin until pain ceases. Seek emergency medical attention immediately for all vapor inhalation or chemical splashes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous wet bench exhaust with face velocity maintained at 0.5 ± 0.1 m/s (100 FPM); automated pressure-differential interlock configured to trip RF generator power if exhaust plenum flow drops below 80% nominal threshold.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Ammoniacal and peroxide overflow streams segregated into dedicated alkaline waste drain line; automated dosing with sulfuric acid (H2SO4) and sodium bisulfite for peroxide quench and pH neutralization (6.5 to 8.5) prior to final wastewater discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Grade 5 (UP-S) | `28.0 - 30.0% NH3 basis` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Grade 5 (UP-S) | `30.0 - 32.0% aqueous solution` |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 4 | `0.5% (DHF pre-clean)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic Si-H terminated surface following dilute HF (DHF) oxide strip or native oxide bearing post-ash surface.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Clean, chemically passivated hydrophilic chemical oxide surface (0.8 - 1.2 nm SiOx) free of organic films and particle contaminants.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive native oxide regrowth, airborne molecular organic (AMC) contamination, and unmitigated airborne particle adhesion leading to gate dielectric breakdown and contact resistance shifts (rho_c > 1.0 x 10^-6 Ohm*cm2).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full qualification and acoustic mapping of the megasonic cleaning tank demonstrating stable acoustic power density, controlled cavitation, uniform acoustic field, and sub-180nm particle removal efficiency without substrate or gate pattern degradation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `megasonic_acoustic_field_calibration_map.csv`
- [ ] `transducer_power_density_qualification_report.pdf`
- [ ] `cavitation_foil_and_oxide_pinhole_inspection.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Acoustic power density at wafer cleaning plane** | `1.50 W/cm2` | ±0.10 W/cm2 | Submersible hydrophone measurement at 25 grid points across wafer carrier zone |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Acoustic field spatial non-uniformity across tank active volume** | `3.5%` | <= 5.0% | Spatial standard deviation divided by mean of 25-point hydrophone matrix |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Silicon dioxide monitor wafer pinhole defect density post-exposure** | `0.0 defects/cm2` | 0.0 defects/cm2 (zero tolerance at >= 180nm) | Brightfield dark-field laser scattering wafer defect inspection |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal sign-off requires hydrophone spatial non-uniformity <= 5.0%, stable RF reflected power < 2.0% over a 60-minute continuous run, and zero defect/pitting adders detected on two consecutive 200mm monitor wafers, countersigned by the Wet Chemistry Domain Expert and Lead Systems Engineer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Bath Particle Clearance & Surface Cleanliness Metrology Qualification

**Document ID:** `SOP-WET-MET-180NM-002`  
**Classification:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM Architecture  
**Process Line:** Standard RCA-1 & RCA-2 Wafer Cleaning Line [Chemical Processing]  
**Sub-Process:** RCA-1 / DHF Oxide Strip / RCA-2 Wet Sequence Execution > Bath Particle Clearance & Surface Cleanliness Metrology Qualification  
**Action Type:** Buy (Procured Wet Bench / Metrology Tooling Verification)

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the step-by-step qualification protocol for liquid particle counts in RCA chemical baths, intermediate rinse tank water purity, and post-strip surface cleanliness metrology. This verification ensures that incoming substrate cleanliness conforms to the stringent interface integrity required for 180nm DRAM stacked-capacitor (COB) plug fabrication and thin gate/ONO dielectric layers.

---

### 2. Verified Literature & Context Citations
* **RCA Chemical Bath Conditions & Rinsing:** RCA-1 (`5:1:1` $\text{DI}:\text{NH}_4\text{OH}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) maintained at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}80^\circ\text{C}$ for $10\text{--}15\text{ min}$; intermediate dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for $3\text{ minutes}$; dilute HF dip ($1:50\text{ HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$) for $15\text{--}30\text{ seconds}$; RCA-2 (`6:1:1` $\text{DI}:\text{HCl}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}80^\circ\text{C}$ for $10\text{ minutes}$; final high-purity $\text{N}_2$ blow-dry (*Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure*).
* **Oxide Etch Rate Baseline:** Thermal oxide removal reference rate using buffered chemistries is approximately $100\text{ nm/minute}$ ($1000\text{ \AA/min}$) at $25^\circ\text{C}$ (*Source: Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)*).
* **DRAM Cell Topology & Impact:** 180nm stacked capacitor node features access transistor gate length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, with capacitance budget $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$ and target leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ (*Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Step 1: Inline Liquid Particle Counter (LPC) Sampling       |
  |         (RCA-1 bath & 18.2 MOhm-cm Quick Dump Rinse tank)   |
  +------------------------------+------------------------------+
                                 |
                                 v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Step 2: DHF Oxide Strip Hydrophobic Wetting Qualification   |
  |         (1:50 HF:H2O for 15-30 s, contact angle inspection) |
  +------------------------------+------------------------------+
                                 |
                                 v
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
  | Step 3: Laser Surface Particle Scanning (LSPS) Run          |
  |         (Unpatterned monitor wafer post RCA-2 & N2 dry)     |
  +-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Inline Liquid Particle Counter (LPC) & Resistivity Check
1. Engage the chemical bath recirculating pump and continuous megasonic filtration module.
2. Verify that the intermediate and final rinse tank DI water supplies meet the online resistivity threshold of $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ before loading monitor wafers.
3. Draw an automated 100 mL sample using an inline LPC configured for chemical baths. Ensure background bath counts stabilize under continuous recirculation before introducing qualification wafers.

#### Step 2: Dilute HF (DHF) Oxide Strip & Surface Hydrophobicity Check
1. Immerse a test monitor wafer in the pre-cleaned RCA-1 tank at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}80^\circ\text{C}$ for $10\text{--}15\text{ minutes}$, followed by a $3\text{ minute}$ dump rinse in $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ DI water.
2. Transfer monitor to the $1:50\text{ HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ bath for $15\text{--}30\text{ seconds}$ to strip the chemical/native oxide film.
3. Confirm complete transition from hydrophilic to hydrophobic behavior (sheeting water break / dewetting across the full active wafer face).
4. Rinse immediately in the dump rinse tank for $3\text{ minutes}$.

#### Step 3: RCA-2 Metallic Clearance & Final Dry Run
1. Transfer the hydrophobic monitor wafer into the RCA-2 bath (`6:1:1` $\text{DI}:\text{HCl}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) maintained at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}80^\circ\text{C}$ for $10\text{ minutes}$.
2. Perform final $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ cascade DI water rinse and complete high-purity dry nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) blow-dry.

#### Step 4: Surface Cleanliness Metrology Scan
1. Transfer dry monitor wafer directly to the cleanroom Laser Surface Particle Scanner (LSPS).
2. Measure light point defect (LPD) additions across the surface (binning particles $\ge 180\text{ nm}$ corresponding to critical dimension $L = 180\text{ nm}$).
3. Log results into the Statistical Process Control (SPC) system to qualify the bath for production lot release.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Physical Units | Verification Method | Literature Source Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Intermediate Rinse DI Water Resistivity** | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | Inline Conductivity/Resistivity Probe | Standard RCA Wafer Clean Procedure |
| **RCA-1 (SC-1) Bath Temperature Range** | $70\text{ -- }80$ | ${^\circ}\text{C}$ | Integrated Bath Resistance Temperature Detector (RTD) | Standard RCA Wafer Clean Procedure |
| **DHF Exposure Duration** | $15\text{ -- }30$ | $\text{seconds}$ | Automated Wet Bench Robotic Immersion Timer | Standard RCA Wafer Clean Procedure |
| **Critical Defect Size Metrology Threshold** | $\ge 180$ | $\text{nm}$ | Laser Surface Particle Scanner (Channel Binning) | 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology ($L = 180\text{ nm}$) |

---

### 5. Safety & Spill Control
* Hydrofluoric acid ($1:50\text{ HF}$) poses critical safety hazards; calcium gluconate antidote gel must be verified at the bench inspection station before commencing any bath qualification.
* PPE requirements: Acid-rated neoprene apron, heavy-duty face shield, and chemical-resistant sleeves/gloves during bath sampling.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In a Gen 1 garage/pilot fab baseline, qualifying bath particle clearance and surface cleanliness without an in-line laser surface scanning inspection system (such as KLA-Tencor Surfscan) creates an observability bottleneck. Relying solely on optical darkfield inspection (NA 0.25) or liquid optical particle counters (OPCs) introduces a blind spot for sub-micron (<0.5 um) defect adders before gate oxidation or contact lithography. The fluidic recirculation loop must guarantee laminar bath replenishment at >3 turnovers per hour through 0.1 um PTFE filters while damping megasonic transducer acoustic streaming cavitation to prevent micro-bubble entrapment and redeposition.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: RCA-1 (NH4OH:H2O2:DIW) operates via controlled surface micro-etching (~0.5 nm/min) and concurrent electrostatic particle repulsion governed by Zeta potential. At pH 9-10, both bare/chemically-oxidized silicon surfaces and standard silica/organic particles maintain negative zeta potentials, preventing redeposition. However, if ammonium hydroxide evaporates preferentially during 70-80°C operations without auto-spiking replenishment, bath pH drops below 8.2, collapsing the electrostatic double layer and causing catastrophic redeposition of particle clusters directly onto active DRAM transistor gate areas.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade (SEMI Tier 1 / VLSI grade) H2O2, NH4OH, and HCl reagents are challenging to secure for open-source and pilot fabrication lines in developing regions such as Vietnam. Reagent purity variations (technical vs. semiconductor grade) introduce heavy trace metal contaminants (Fe, Cu, Al > 10 ppb) and particulate counts > 100 particles/mL at 0.5 um directly into the bath. Sourcing PVDF/PTFE chemical bath tanks, megasonic quartz arrays, and electronic-grade point-of-use PTFE filter cartridges (0.1 um absolute) requires 12 to 16 weeks lead time and certified chemical compatibility documentation.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Executing metrology qualification on Gen 1 manual wet benches without automated cassette transfer introduces severe human-induced variability. Operators transferring wafer boats manually between megasonic RCA baths, dump rinsers, and spin-rinse dryers (SRD) risk bath sloshing, fluid surface meniscus contamination, and unmonitored queue times exceeding the 30-minute threshold. The milestone must gate subsequent gate dielectric growth behind automated statistical process control (SPC) charts demonstrating 3 consecutive runs below the particle adder threshold.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Zeta potential reversal and particulate redeposition induced by ammonia depletion and bath pH drift below 8.5 during megasonic processing.
1. Megasonic transducer localized acoustic cavitation pitting and hot-spot wafer surface erosion causing macroscopic gate dielectric pinholes.
1. Meniscus-drag particle recontamination during manual wafer extraction from stagnant bath surface boundaries prior to quick-dump rinsing.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-2-1-3-01` | **Bath Liquid Particle Clearance Rate Qualification** | Liquid Optical Particle Counter (OPC, 0.1 um sensitivity, calibrated for corrosive chemistry) connected to PTFE bath sampling port; calibrated pH meter with chemical-resistant glass electrode. | 1. Spike the chemical bath with 1.0 mL of certified 1.0 um silica sphere calibration suspension to simulate a high particulate excursion (> 10,000 particles/mL). 2. Initiate continuous megasonic agitation at 1.0 MHz (75W forward power) and active bath filtration loop at 5.5 L/min. 3. Sample bath fluid via OPC every 2 minutes for a total duration of 30 minutes. 4. Continuously log particle concentrations across channel bins >= 0.2 um, >= 0.5 um, and >= 1.0 um. 5. Measure and record bath pH at t=0, t=15, and t=30 minutes. | `Bath particle clearance must achieve >= 99.0% particle count reduction within 20 minutes of filtration/megasonics (particulate count <= 10 particles/mL at >= 0.5 um). Bath pH must remain >= 9.2 throughout the 30-minute run.` |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-2-1-3-02` | **Post-Clean Wafer Surface Cleanliness & Defect Adder Qualification** | High-resolution optical darkfield wafer inspection system (Plan Achromat 10x/20x objective, darkfield ring illuminator, calibrated image analysis software) and spectroscopic ellipsometer. | 1. Load the three mapped pilot wafers into a virgin PTFE carrier cassette. 2. Submerge cassette into the qualified RCA-1 bath (70°C, 1.0 MHz megasonics active) for 10 minutes. 3. Immediately transfer cassette within 5 seconds to QDR (Quick Dump Rinse) tank; execute 4 dump-fill cycles with 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW. 4. Transfer to Spin-Rinse Dryer (SRD) and dry with heated semiconductor-grade N2 at 2500 RPM for 180 seconds. 5. Re-scan wafers under darkfield optical inspection, registering coordinate-matched defect adders. 6. Measure chemical native oxide thickness across 9 points per wafer via spectroscopic ellipsometry. | `Average net particle adders across the 3 wafers must be <= 5 adders/wafer at >= 1.0 um; chemical oxide thickness must measure 0.8 nm to 1.2 nm with 1-sigma spatial uniformity across wafer < 5%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant neoprene/butyl apron with full sleeve coverage, Heavy-duty butyl/Viton overgloves worn over double nitrile exam gloves, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield with ANSI Z87.1 certified safety goggles underneath, Acid/alkali-resistant steel-toe rubber chemical boots with pant legs draped externally
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin exposure: Flush immediately with emergency safety shower for minimum 15 minutes while removing contaminated PPE and clothing; seek immediate medical attention. For eye splash: Irrigate open eyelids with emergency eyewash for minimum 20 minutes continuously; transport to ophthalmology emergency center immediately. For inhalation of NH3 or HCl vapors: Immediately remove victim to fresh uncontaminated air, administer humidified medical oxygen if breathing is labored, do not induce vomiting if ingested; rinse mouth thoroughly with copious water.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous wet bench chemical exhaust maintaining minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) across sash opening with dedicated differential pressure sensor (< -0.25 inches water column relative to room). Ammonia/alkali exhaust routed to wet chemical acid/base counter-current packed bed scrubber; dedicated explosion-proof exhaust fans with dual-sensor airflow alarms.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: RCA-1 (alkaline/peroxide) and RCA-2 (acidic) effluents must be segregated into distinct drain lines to prevent violent exothermic gas evolution. RCA-1 waste transferred to a vented peroxide-decomposition holding tank, decomposed via low-concentration sodium metabisulfite or catalytic carbon bed until H2O2 < 5 ppm, followed by automated dual-stage acid/base neutralization to pH 6.5 - 8.5 before discharge to industrial wastewater treatment.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-received or post-ash silicon surface with variable organic residue, uncontrolled ambient native oxide (0.5 - 2.5 nm), and airborne particulate contamination.

critics.systems_engineer: In a Gen 1 garage/pilot fab baseline, qualifying bath particle clearance and surface cleanliness without an in-line laser surface scanning inspection system (such as KLA-Tencor Surfscan) creates an observability bottleneck. Relying solely on optical darkfield inspection (NA 0.25) or liquid optical particle counters (OPCs) introduces a blind spot for sub-micron (<0.5 um) defect adders before gate oxidation or contact lithography. The fluidic recirculation loop must guarantee laminar bath replenishment at >3 turnovers per hour through 0.1 um PTFE filters while damping megasonic transducer acoustic streaming cavitation to prevent micro-bubble entrapment and redeposition.
critics.domain_expert: RCA-1 (NH4OH:H2O2:DIW) operates via controlled surface micro-etching (~0.5 nm/min) and concurrent electrostatic particle repulsion governed by Zeta potential. At pH 9-10, both bare/chemically-oxidized silicon surfaces and standard silica/organic particles maintain negative zeta potentials, preventing redeposition. However, if ammonium hydroxide evaporates preferentially during 70-80°C operations without auto-spiking replenishment, bath pH drops below 8.2, collapsing the electrostatic double layer and causing catastrophic redeposition of particle clusters directly onto active DRAM transistor gate areas.
critics.supply_chain: Electronic-grade (SEMI Tier 1 / VLSI grade) H2O2, NH4OH, and HCl reagents are challenging to secure for open-source and pilot fabrication lines in developing regions such as Vietnam. Reagent purity variations (technical vs. semiconductor grade) introduce heavy trace metal contaminants (Fe, Cu, Al > 10 ppb) and particulate counts > 100 particles/mL at 0.5 um directly into the bath. Sourcing PVDF/PTFE chemical bath tanks, megasonic quartz arrays, and electronic-grade point-of-use PTFE filter cartridges (0.1 um absolute) requires 12 to 16 weeks lead time and certified chemical compatibility documentation.
critics.laya_pm: Executing metrology qualification on Gen 1 manual wet benches without automated cassette transfer introduces severe human-induced variability. Operators transferring wafer boats manually between megasonic RCA baths, dump rinsers, and spin-rinse dryers (SRD) risk bath sloshing, fluid surface meniscus contamination, and unmonitored queue times exceeding the 30-minute threshold. The milestone must gate subsequent gate dielectric growth behind automated statistical process control (SPC) charts demonstrating 3 consecutive runs below the particle adder threshold.
critical_failure_modes: Zeta potential reversal and particulate redeposition induced by ammonia depletion and bath pH drift below 8.5 during megasonic processing.
Megasonic transducer localized acoustic cavitation pitting and hot-spot wafer surface erosion causing macroscopic gate dielectric pinholes.
Meniscus-drag particle recontamination during manual wafer extraction from stagnant bath surface boundaries prior to quick-dump rinsing.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Sequential SC-1 / DHF 50:1 Strip / SC-2 Wet Clean & Marangoni Dry

**Document ID:** `SOP-WET-180NM-RCA-001`  
**Node Level:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Standard RCA-1 & RCA-2 Wafer Cleaning Line > Wet Chemistry  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
│                        │
│  SC-1 Alkaline Clean   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘

┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Dump Rinse UPW     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     DHF 50:1 Strip     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Dump Rinse UPW     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │

┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  SC-2 Acid Desorption  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Overflow Rinse 18.2   │
│        MOhm-cm         │
│                        │

             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Marangoni Dry      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Station Inspection & Preparation**:
   - Verify all baths are filled with ultra-pure water (UPW) with resistivity at $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
   - Ensure cleanroom exhaust and heated bath recirculators are functional.

2. **SC-1 (Standard Clean 1 / RCA-1) Alkaline Organic & Particle Strip**:
   - **Bath Formulation**: $5\text{ parts UPW/DI H}_2\text{O} : 1\text{ part } 29\%\text{ NH}_4\text{OH} : 1\text{ part } 30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$.
   - **Bath Temperature**: Maintain at $70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$.
   - **Immersion Time**: $10 - 15\text{ minutes}$.
   - **Mechanism**: Oxidizes trace organics, light metals, and continuously removes surface particulate contamination via silicon micro-etch/regrowth.

3. **Intermediate Dump Rinse 1**:
   - Transfer wafer carrier immediately into the quick-dump rinse (QDR) bath.
   - Rinse using $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for $3\text{ minutes}$ to eliminate residual ammonium hydroxide.

4. **Dilute HF (DHF 50:1) Native Oxide Strip**:
   - **Bath Formulation**: $50\text{ parts UPW/H}_2\text{O} : 1\text{ part } 49\%\text{ HF}$ (or $1:50\text{ HF}:\text{H}_2\text{O}$).
   - **Bath Temperature**: Ambient ($20^\circ\text{C} - 25^\circ\text{C}$).
   - **Immersion Time**: $15 - 30\text{ seconds}$.
   - **Surface Observation**: Strip native oxide until the wafer surface undergoes complete transition from hydrophilic to hydrophobic (beading off bare silicon without wetting).

5. **Intermediate Dump Rinse 2**:
   - Perform quick dump rinse using $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW for $3\text{ minutes}$ until cascade effluent resistivity recovers.

6. **SC-2 (Standard Clean 2 / RCA-2) Acid Desorption**:
   - **Bath Formulation**: $6\text{ parts UPW/DI H}_2\text{O} : 1\text{ part } 37\%\text{ HCl} : 1\text{ part } 30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$.
   - **Bath Temperature**: Maintain at $75^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$ (operational window $70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$).
   - **Immersion Time**: $10\text{ minutes}$.
   - **Mechanism**: Desorbs and complexes alkali ions ($\text{Na}^+$, $\text{K}^+$) and transition/heavy metal impurities ($\text{Fe}$, $\text{Cu}$, $\text{Ni}$, $\text{Au}$) into soluble metal-chloride compounds.

7. **Final Overflow Rinse & Marangoni Dry**:
   - Transfer wafers to overflow rinse tank charged with continuous $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW until bath reaches baseline resistivity.
   - Transfer to drying module: Apply filtered $\text{N}_2$ Marangoni drying (or high-purity $\text{N}_2$ blow-dry / IPA vapor dry) at controlled withdrawal velocity to ensure particle- and watermark-free hydrophobic/hydrophilic boundary drying.

---

```text
               │███████████████████████████████████████│
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
               0.0      18.8     37.5      56.2    75.0
```

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| **UPW Rinse Effluent Resistivity** | `18.2` | $\ge 18.0$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-line conductivity/resistivity sensor |
| **SC-1 Bath Operating Temperature** | `75.0` | $70.0 - 80.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Integrated bath RTD / Thermocouple |
| **SC-2 Bath Operating Temperature** | `75.0` | $\pm 2.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Integrated bath RTD / Thermocouple |
| **DHF 50:1 Immersion Duration** | `22.5` | $15.0 - 30.0$ | $\text{s}$ | Automated wet bench immersion timer |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **`RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering`**:
  - SC-2 chemistry formulation ($6:1:1\text{ UPW}:\text{HCl}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$), bath temperature ($75^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$), immersion time ($10\text{ min}$), removal of alkali ($\text{Na}^+, \text{K}^+$) and transition metals ($\text{Fe}, \text{Cu}, \text{Ni}, \text{Au}$), and filtered $\text{N}_2$ Marangoni drying.
- **`Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure`**:
  - SC-1 chemistry formulation ($5:1:1\text{ DI H}_2\text{O}:\text{NH}_4\text{OH}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$), thermal window ($70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$), immersion ($10 - 15\text{ min}$), intermediate dump rinse ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ for $3\text{ min}$), and 1:50 HF dip ($15 - 30\text{ s}$) inducing hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic surface transition.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The sequential wet bench integration introduces inter-bath cross-contamination risks and carrier drag-out dynamics. Specifically, drag-out of NH4OH/H2O2 alkaline traces into the acidic DHF bath can alter etching uniformity and bath pH, while drag-out of F- ions into SC-2 risks precipitation of insoluble metal fluorides. Quick Dump Rinsers (QDR) with resistivity triggers (>= 18.0 MOhm-cm) and continuous bath replenishment/dosing systems must be synchronized to prevent bath starvation and maintain delta-T within +/- 1.5 deg C across standard quartz/PVDF vessels.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In a 180nm DRAM process, native oxide strip via 50:1 DHF leaves a bare hydrophobic silicon surface terminated with Si-H bonds, which is exceptionally prone to trace airborne organic re-adsorption and noble metal (Cu, Au) galvanic displacement plating. The subsequent SC-2 bath (6:1:1 UPW:HCl:H2O2) must re-grow a chemical passivating oxide (0.8-1.2 nm) while desorbing Fe, Cu, and Ni ionic complexes without micro-roughening the silicon lattice (keeping delta-Rq < 0.05 nm). The Marangoni dry phase must balance isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor concentration and wafer pull velocity (1-2 mm/s) to eliminate watermarks on patterned topography without organic residue staining.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade chemicals (SEMI Tier 3/Grade 5 or VLSI/UP-S grade: < 0.1 ppb metal trace contamination) are critical for gate dielectric pre-cleans in open-source DRAM manufacturing. Sourcing 49% semiconductor HF, 29% semiconductor NH4OH, and electronic H2O2 locally in Vietnam requires stringent batch qualification and pre-shipment ICP-MS certificates, as industrial or lab reagent grades (> 10 ppb Fe/Cu) will poison gate oxide integrity and DRAM cell retention times.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Execution schedule must tightly couple the wet clean sequence with downstream thermal gate oxidation (E1-OX-180). Exceeding Q-time boundaries (<= 60 min cleanroom air exposure) will cause uncontrolled, non-stoichiometric native oxide regrowth, forcing wafer scrap and chemical bath requalification. Chemical consumption and neutralization duty cycles must be aligned with fab wastewater treatment limits (fluoride precipitating capacity and neutralization sump turnover).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Watermark defect formation during Marangoni dry due to inadequate IPA/N2 gradient or uneven pull velocity over hydrophobic/hydrophilic boundary interfaces.
1. Noble metal galvanic displacement plating during 50:1 DHF strip leading to gate leakage and premature gate oxide breakdown (TDDB degradation).
1. Surface micro-roughening and silicon pitting caused by peroxide depletion or NH4OH/H2O2 ratio imbalance in SC-1.

Perform initial surface particle map and AFM roughness scan on prime monitor wafer before processing. 2. Execute wet clean recipe with verified bath concentrations (SC-1 5:1:1 at 75C for 10 min; DHF 50:1 at 22C for 30 s; SC-2 6:1:1 at 75C for 10 min; Marangoni dry at 1.5 mm/s). 3. Transfer wafer immediately under laminar flow to laser surface scanner; scan total particle counts >= 0.18 um across active wafer area (3mm edge exclusion). 4. Perform 5-point AFM scan (center, top, bottom, left, right) over 1 um x 1 um areas to extract average surface roughness Rq. | `Total surface adder particles (>= 0.18 um): <= 15 defects per 200mm wafer (< 0.05 defects/cm2). Average surface roughness delta-Rq: <= 0.05 nm relative to baseline incoming wafer; zero cluster watermarks detected.` |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-2-2-02` | **Metallic Contamination and Native Oxide Removal / Chemical Re-growth Profiling** | Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) spectrometer and spectroscopic ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam M-2000 equivalent). | 1. Measure wafer at 9 discrete radial points using spectroscopic ellipsometer immediately post-Marangoni dry to determine chemical oxide thickness and index of refraction. 2. Load monitor wafer into TXRF chamber under clean vacuum; acquire grazing-incidence fluorescence spectra at 5 distinct surface sites for critical transition and alkali metals (Fe, Cu, Ni, Na). 3. Calculate surface atomic concentration in atoms/cm2. | `Surface metal contamination for Fe, Cu, Ni: <= 5.0E+09 atoms/cm2 each. Na/K contamination: <= 1.0E+10 atoms/cm2. Post-SC-2 protective chemical oxide thickness: 0.9 nm to 1.3 nm with thickness non-uniformity (1-sigma) < 3.0%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full-face splash shield (ANSI Z87.1 approved) with chemical splash goggles, Heavy-duty butyl or neoprene chemical aprons and chemical sleeves, Triple-layer glove system: inner nitrile, mid-layer 15-mil nitrile, outer heavy-gauge butyl/Viton gloves (checked for pinhole leaks), Steel-toe chemical-resistant neoprene boots with splash guards, Type B/E chemical vapor respirator or positive-pressure cleanroom airline hood during bath charging/maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium gluconate gel (2.5%) must be immediately accessible within 10 feet of the wet bench. In case of HF skin exposure: immediately strip contaminated clothing, flush continuously with cold water for 2-3 minutes, then vigorously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into the affected area with fresh gloves continuously until medical assistance arrives. For eye splash: flush at emergency eyewash station with isotonic saline or copious UPW for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open. Seek emergency medical attention immediately for all chemical exposures.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated dual-channel polypropylene exhaust plenum: Acid-waste exhaust (dedicated scrubbed acid duct line maintaining >= 150 FPM face velocity at bench lip, static pressure -1.2 to -1.5 in. w.g.) strictly segregated from alkaline/ammonia exhaust (separate wet scrubber) to prevent volatile ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) salt deposition and duct clogging. Continuous laminar cleanroom downflow (0.45 m/s) with real-time Magnehelic differential pressure interlocks.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated drain lines: 1. Fluoride/HF waste routed to dedicated calcium chloride (CaCl2) precipitation tank to form insoluble CaF2 cake (< 10 ppm discharge limit). 2. Acid/Base general effluent directed to automated two-stage neutralization sump (dosing 10N NaOH and 10N H2SO4) monitoring pH between 6.5 and 8.5 before civil discharge. 3. IPA Marangoni exhaust/condensate routed to solvent drain with automated flame arrester.

| **Hydrochloric Acid (Electronic Grade)** | `7647-01-0` | SEMI Tier 3 / VLSI Grade | `37% wt stock aqueous solution` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (Electronic Grade)** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Tier 3 / VLSI Grade | `28-30% NH3 wt stock solution` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (Electronic Grade)** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Tier 3 / VLSI Grade (stabilized, low carbon) | `30% wt stock aqueous solution` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA, Semiconductor Grade)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Tier 3 / Electronic Grade | `99.9% wt anhydrous (for Marangoni dry vapor)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic or contaminated native oxide surface containing ambient airborne particulates, hydrocarbons, and residual post-litho/ash organic residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Passivated, pristine, chemically grown stoichiometric protective oxide layer (1.0 +/- 0.2 nm) free of organic films, particles, and watermark rings, hydrophobic-to-hydrophilic converted.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding queue time prior to thermal gate oxidation results in uncontrolled ambient native oxide regrowth with non-uniform stoichiometry and boron/phosphorus segregation, causing severe gate threshold voltage (Vth) shifts, gate dielectric breakdown degradation, and unrecoverable DRAM storage cell retention failure.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful delivery of a validated, particle-free (< 0.05 defects/cm2 at >= 0.18 um), metal-desorbed (< 5.0E+09 atoms/cm2 for Fe, Cu, Ni), watermark-free wafer surface with a uniform 1.1 nm chemical passivating oxide, ready for high-reliability gate oxide furnace insertion.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RCA_WET_CLEAN_PARTICLE_DEFECT_MAP_LOT01.tiff`
- [ ] `RCA_TXRF_METAL_CONTAMINATION_SPECTRUM_LOT01.csv`
- [ ] `RCA_PROCESS_RUN_AND_QTIME_SIGNOFF_REPORT_LOT01.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Surface particle defect density (adder count >= 0.18 um)** | `0.03 defects/cm2` | <= 0.05 defects/cm2 | Full-wafer laser darkfield light scattering inspection (SP2 equivalent) with 3mm edge exclusion |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Critical transition metal contamination level (Fe, Cu, Ni)** | `2.0E+09 atoms/cm2` | <= 5.0E+09 atoms/cm2 | Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) 5-point radial sampling |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-SC-2 chemical passivating oxide thickness** | `1.10 nm` | +/- 0.15 nm (uniformity 1-sigma < 3%) | Multi-angle spectroscopic ellipsometry 9-point surface profile |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All quantitative assertions (ASSERT-01 through ASSERT-03) verified within numerical tolerance on test monitors, zero watermark defect clusters verified via darkfield inspection, and wafer lot successfully docked into N2-purged FOUP/storage pod within 60 minutes of Marangoni cycle completion.

critics.systems_engineer: The sequential wet bench integration introduces inter-bath cross-contamination risks and carrier drag-out dynamics. Specifically, drag-out of NH4OH/H2O2 alkaline traces into the acidic DHF bath can alter etching uniformity and bath pH, while drag-out of F- ions into SC-2 risks precipitation of insoluble metal fluorides. Quick Dump Rinsers (QDR) with resistivity triggers (>= 18.0 MOhm-cm) and continuous bath replenishment/dosing systems must be synchronized to prevent bath starvation and maintain delta-T within +/- 1.5 deg C across standard quartz/PVDF vessels.
critics.domain_expert: In a 180nm DRAM process, native oxide strip via 50:1 DHF leaves a bare hydrophobic silicon surface terminated with Si-H bonds, which is exceptionally prone to trace airborne organic re-adsorption and noble metal (Cu, Au) galvanic displacement plating. The subsequent SC-2 bath (6:1:1 UPW:HCl:H2O2) must re-grow a chemical passivating oxide (0.8-1.2 nm) while desorbing Fe, Cu, and Ni ionic complexes without micro-roughening the silicon lattice (keeping delta-Rq < 0.05 nm). The Marangoni dry phase must balance isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor concentration and wafer pull velocity (1-2 mm/s) to eliminate watermarks on patterned topography without organic residue staining.
critics.supply_chain: Electronic-grade chemicals (SEMI Tier 3/Grade 5 or VLSI/UP-S grade: < 0.1 ppb metal trace contamination) are critical for gate dielectric pre-cleans in open-source DRAM manufacturing. Sourcing 49% semiconductor HF, 29% semiconductor NH4OH, and electronic H2O2 locally in Vietnam requires stringent batch qualification and pre-shipment ICP-MS certificates, as industrial or lab reagent grades (> 10 ppb Fe/Cu) will poison gate oxide integrity and DRAM cell retention times.
critics.laya_pm: Execution schedule must tightly couple the wet clean sequence with downstream thermal gate oxidation (E1-OX-180). Exceeding Q-time boundaries (<= 60 min cleanroom air exposure) will cause uncontrolled, non-stoichiometric native oxide regrowth, forcing wafer scrap and chemical bath requalification. Chemical consumption and neutralization duty cycles must be aligned with fab wastewater treatment limits (fluoride precipitating capacity and neutralization sump turnover).
critical_failure_modes: Watermark defect formation during Marangoni dry due to inadequate IPA/N2 gradient or uneven pull velocity over hydrophobic/hydrophilic boundary interfaces.
Noble metal galvanic displacement plating during 50:1 DHF strip leading to gate leakage and premature gate oxide breakdown (TDDB degradation).
Surface micro-roughening and silicon pitting caused by peroxide depletion or NH4OH/H2O2 ratio imbalance in SC-1.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Identification
- **Title**: Bath Chemistry Preparation & Bath Conditioning for SC-1, DHF 50:1, and SC-2
- **Subsystem**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Standard RCA-1 & RCA-2 Wafer Cleaning Line > Wet Chemistry
- **Action Type**: Make
- **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)

---

## 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     PPE & Chemical     │
│  Safety Verification   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  SC-1 Make-Up: 5:1:1   │
│     DIW:NH4OH:H2O2     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   DHF Make-Up: 50:1    │
│       DIW:HF 49%       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  SC-2 Make-Up: 6:1:1   │
│      DIW:HCl:H2O2      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Thermal Conditioning  │
│    70-80C & In-line    │
│   Temp Verification    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Bath Ready for Wafer  │
│     Lot Execution      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

### Step 1: Pre-Operational Safety & Station Check
1. Don acid/chemical personal protective equipment (PPE): chemical apron, heavy neoprene/nitrile sleeves and gloves, and full face shield.
2. Verify that **calcium gluconate gel** is present and unexpired within arm's reach of the wet bench.
3. Confirm operational exhaust face velocity and ensure the dump rinse tank supply has a minimum resistivity of $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.

### Step 2: SC-1 (RCA-1) Bath Preparation
1. Dispense **5 parts** Ultra-Pure Deionized Water ($\text{DI H}_2\text{O}$) into the quartz/PTFE bath tank.
2. Add **1 part** Ammonium Hydroxide ($29\%\text{ NH}_4\text{OH}$) slowly to the DI water.
3. Add **1 part** Hydrogen Peroxide ($30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$) to complete the $5:1:1$ ratio.
4. Activate the bath immersion heater and set temperature controller to **$70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$**.
5. Allow thermal and chemical equilibrium to stabilize before immersion (target processing window: 10–15 minutes per batch).

### Step 3: DHF 50:1 Oxide Strip Bath Preparation
1. Ensure the ambient bath tank is constructed of HF-compatible fluoropolymer (PVDF/PTFE).
2. Measure and charge **50 parts** Ultra-Pure Deionized Water ($\text{DI H}_2\text{O}$).
3. Carefully meter in **1 part** Hydrofluoric Acid ($49\%\text{ HF}$) under continuous laminar exhaust to produce the dilute $50:1$ ($\text{H}_2\text{O}:\text{HF}$) solution.
4. Maintain the DHF bath at ambient cleanroom temperature ($20^\circ\text{C} - 25^\circ\text{C}$); verify bath uniformity prior to running 15–30 second native oxide stripping dips.

### Step 4: SC-2 (RCA-2) Bath Preparation
1. Charge the designated SC-2 quartz tank with **6 parts** Ultra-Pure Deionized Water ($\text{DI H}_2\text{O}$).
2. Add **1 part** Hydrochloric Acid ($37\%\text{ HCl}$) slowly into the DI water.
3. Add **1 part** Hydrogen Peroxide ($30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$) to obtain the $6:1:1$ volumetric ratio.
4. Engage the immersion heater, ramping the solution to **$70^\circ\text{C} - 80^\circ\text{C}$**.
5. Maintain constant temperature conditioning for at least 10 minutes prior to wafer lot introduction.

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                    │░░░░░░░░░                         │
DI Rinse Resistivity┤░░░░░░░░░                         │

                    │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
      SC-1 Bath Temp┤██████████████████████████████████│
                    │██████████████████████████████████│
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                    0.0    18.8     37.5    56.2   75.0 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Unit | Measurement Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SC-1 Bath Operating Temperature** | $70.0 - 80.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | In-situ PFA-sheathed RTD temperature sensor |
| **SC-2 Bath Operating Temperature** | $70.0 - 80.0$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | In-situ PFA-sheathed RTD temperature sensor |
| **Intermediate Rinse Water Quality** | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-line resistivity cell sensor |
| **DHF Volumetric Mixing Ratio** | $50:1\ (\pm 1\%)$ | Ratio ($\text{H}_2\text{O}:\text{HF}$) | Automated flow injection metering dispense counter |

---

## 4. Context References & Source Citations
- **Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**:
  - SC-1 volumetric formulation ($5\text{ DI H}_2\text{O} : 1\text{ NH}_4\text{OH } [29\%] : 1\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2\ [30\%]$) and bath thermal setpoint ($70^\circ\text{C}-80^\circ\text{C}$, 10–15 min).
  - DHF dilution ratio ($50:1\ \text{H}_2\text{O}:\text{HF}$) and native oxide strip duration (15–30 s).
  - SC-2 volumetric formulation ($6\text{ DI H}_2\text{O} : 1\text{ HCl } [37\%] : 1\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2\ [30\%]$) and operating thermal setpoint ($70^\circ\text{C}-80^\circ\text{C}$, 10 min).
  - Rinse line resistivity requirement ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
- **Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE)**:
  - Personal safety mandate: mandatory presence of topical calcium gluconate gel for all hydrofluoric acid handling and bath make-up.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Bath life and spike chemistry addition dynamics are uncoupled in open recirculating quartz tanks; accelerated thermal decomposition of H2O2 in alkaline SC-1 (75°C) alters the NH4OH:H2O2 ratio rapidly, leading to silicon surface micro-roughness (haze) and uncontrolled native oxide regrowth if spiking intervals and megasonic power density (>0.8 W/cm²) are not closed-loop regulated.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: DHF 50:1 etch rate on thermal vs native oxide must be calibrated at 21.5°C ± 0.5°C; improper bath conditioning or organic surfactant carryover into the HF module causes localized hydrophobic pinning, incomplete oxide stripping, and subsequent transition-metal precipitation (Fe/Cu) directly onto bare dangling silicon bonds prior to SC-2 passivation.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade UPW (18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C with TOC < 2 ppb) and SEMI Tier 4 / Grade 5 bulk chemicals (NH4OH, H2O2, HCl, HF) have stringent shelf-life stability and container leaching vulnerabilities; uncertified local blending of 49% semiconductor HF or stabilized peroxide risks introducing sub-ppm aluminum and calcium contaminants that exhaust SC-2 chelating capacity prematurely.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Sequential execution timing without automated inter-tank Q-time alarms risks wafer stalling in unconditioned ambient hoods; bath turn-up must strictly enforce a 30-minute thermal/chemical stabilization window and qualification coupons before production wafer lots enter the line to avoid scrap cascades.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Thermal runaway or severe peroxide decomposition in SC-1 resulting in caustic ammonia outgassing, high bath pH drift (>10.5), and severe silicon pitting (>0.3 nm RMS surface roughness degradation).
1. Fluoride cross-contamination or chemical drag-out into downstream SC-2 bath causing fluorosilicate etching of quartz bath heaters and catastrophic gate-oxide pinhole formation.
1. Inadequate DHF bath degas conditioning leaving dissolved O2 > 15 ppb, causing galvanic micro-corrosion and water-mark ring defects during Marangoni dry.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-2-2-1-01` | **SC-1 Chemical Ratio and Thermal Homogeneity Bath Qualification** | Near-Infrared (NIR) inline chemical concentration monitor, calibrated 4-channel Teflon-sheathed RTD temperature profiler, and Metrohm automated titrator | 1. Measure steady-state bath temperature across 5 geometric immersion nodes (4 corners and center) at 75°C setpoint. 2. Extract three 20 mL bath aliquots at t=0, t=30, and t=60 minutes. 3. Perform potentiometric neutralization titration with 0.1 N HCl for NH4OH and ceric sulfate redox titration for H2O2 concentration. | `Temperature uniformity across all 5 nodes must be 75.0°C ± 1.5°C; NH4OH concentration must be 4.8 wt% ± 0.4 wt%; H2O2 concentration must be 4.3 wt% ± 0.3 wt% across 60 minutes.` |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-2-2-1-02` | **DHF 50:1 Oxide Etch Rate and Hydrophobic Contact Angle Verification** | Woollam M-2000 Spectroscopic Ellipsometer, Kruss Mobile Surface Analyzer (Drop Shape Analyzer), and 4-point probe resistivity meter | 1. Measure baseline SiO2 thickness at 49 points on wafer. 2. Immerse thermal oxide monitor wafer into DHF 50:1 for exactly 60 seconds with continuous N2 bubbling. 3. Quick-dump rinse in 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW for 3 cycles and N2 blow dry. 4. Re-measure post-etch oxide thickness at 49 points. 5. Immerse bare Si monitor wafer for 30 seconds to strip native oxide, dry, and dispense 2 uL UPW droplet to measure static sessile water contact angle. | `Thermal SiO2 etch rate must be 4.5 nm/min to 5.5 nm/min with across-wafer etch uniformity 3-sigma < 3.0%; post-strip bare Si static water contact angle must be >= 72.0 degrees.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical splash apron and jacket constructed of heavy-duty Neoprene/Butyl elastomer, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1 combined with chemical splash goggles, Heavyweight 22-mil Butyl gloves over Nitrile inner gloves with regular pinhole testing, Chemical-resistant safety boots with steel toe and Metatarsal guard, Emergency personal HF response pouch containing unopened 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF exposure: Immediately flood exposed skin with emergency tepid water for 2 minutes while alerting cleanroom staff. Continuously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into the affected area until medical personnel arrive; if splashed in eyes, irrigate with sterile 1% calcium gluconate eye wash or isotonic saline for 15 minutes. For NH4OH/HCl acid/base splashes: Drench shower for minimum 15 minutes, remove contaminated PPE, and seek emergency pulmonary and ophthalmic triage.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated acid and caustic wet bench exhaust plenum operating at -0.25 inches water column face velocity with laminar lip exhaust >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) across all open tank lips; acid scrubbers (packed tower water scrubber) for HF/HCl and caustic scrubbers (H2SO4 wash stage) for NH3 to avoid ammonium salt duct plugging.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated drain plumbing: Fluoride waste streams (DHF 50:1 and DHF rinses) piped strictly to dedicated Fluoride Waste Treatment (FWT) for calcium fluoride (CaF2) precipitation using lime slurry/CaCl2. SC-1 and SC-2 dumps directed to General Acid/Base Neutralization (AWN) system using 2-stage automated sulfuric acid and sodium hydroxide pH correction to 6.5 - 8.5 before POTW discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 4 | `49.0% - 50.0% w/w` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (NH4OH)** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Grade 5 | `28.0% - 30.0% w/w as NH3` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Grade 5 | `30.0% - 32.0% w/w` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)** | `7647-01-0` | SEMI Grade 5 | `36.5% - 38.0% w/w` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dirty as-received silicon substrate with atmospheric airborne molecular contamination (AMC), native oxide (1.2-1.8 nm), and trace organic/metallic surface residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Atomically smooth, metal-depleted (<1e10 atoms/cm² Fe/Cu/Ni), chemical oxide-passivated (0.8-1.0 nm SC-2 hydrophilic oxide layer) silicon surface.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to cleanroom ambient air beyond 30 minutes induces uncontrolled native oxide growth with volatile organic hydrocarbon uptake and atmospheric boron/phosphorus moisture absorption, causing threshold voltage instability, high interface trap density (Dit > 1e11 eV^-1 cm^-2), and gate dielectric breakdown failure.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Demonstrated full operational conditioning, chemical stoichiometric stability, and qualification of sequential SC-1 (5:1:1), DHF (50:1), and SC-2 (6:1:1) wet bench baths with validated cleaning efficiency, surface micro-roughness preservation, native oxide stripping, and chemical oxide regrowth ready for gate oxide furnace processing.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `rca_bath_conditioning_qualification_log.csv`
- [ ] `dhf_etch_uniformity_and_ellipsometry_report.pdf`
- [ ] `post_clean_afm_haze_defects_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-SC-1 Megasonic clean surface particle removal efficiency (PRE) for Si3N4/SiO2 particles >= 0.18 um** | `98.5%` | +1.5%, -0.5% | KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP2 unpatterned wafer surface defect inspection before and after clean |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-SC-2 surface transition metal contamination density (sum of Fe, Ni, Cu, Zn)** | `5.0e9 atoms/cm2` | <= 1.0e10 atoms/cm2 maximum limit | Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry with Vapor Phase Decomposition (VPD-ICP-MS) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-clean surface roughness RMS increment on bare silicon active area** | `0.12 nm` | +0.03 nm max delta from incoming baseline | Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) 2um x 2um non-contact tapping mode scan |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Engineering signoff granted only when automated bath titrations across 3 consecutive 1-hour cycles match stoichiometric limits, 150mm monitor wafers demonstrate PRE >= 98.0%, post-clean VPD-ICP-MS certifies heavy metal contamination < 1e10 atoms/cm², and static contact angle after DHF validates complete native oxide strip with zero water marks upon Marangoni dry.
citations: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure (Kern, W. - RCA Review & Semiconductor Cleaning Science)
Silicon Dioxide Etching with Buffered Oxide Etch (BOE) (Semiconductor Chemical Processing Handbook)
Photoresist Spin Coating Dynamics and HMDS Vapor Priming (Madou - Fundamentals of Microfabrication)

critics.systems_engineer: Bath life and spike chemistry addition dynamics are uncoupled in open recirculating quartz tanks; accelerated thermal decomposition of H2O2 in alkaline SC-1 (75°C) alters the NH4OH:H2O2 ratio rapidly, leading to silicon surface micro-roughness (haze) and uncontrolled native oxide regrowth if spiking intervals and megasonic power density (>0.8 W/cm²) are not closed-loop regulated.
critics.domain_expert: DHF 50:1 etch rate on thermal vs native oxide must be calibrated at 21.5°C ± 0.5°C; improper bath conditioning or organic surfactant carryover into the HF module causes localized hydrophobic pinning, incomplete oxide stripping, and subsequent transition-metal precipitation (Fe/Cu) directly onto bare dangling silicon bonds prior to SC-2 passivation.
critics.supply_chain: Electronic-grade UPW (18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C with TOC < 2 ppb) and SEMI Tier 4 / Grade 5 bulk chemicals (NH4OH, H2O2, HCl, HF) have stringent shelf-life stability and container leaching vulnerabilities; uncertified local blending of 49% semiconductor HF or stabilized peroxide risks introducing sub-ppm aluminum and calcium contaminants that exhaust SC-2 chelating capacity prematurely.
critics.laya_pm: Sequential execution timing without automated inter-tank Q-time alarms risks wafer stalling in unconditioned ambient hoods; bath turn-up must strictly enforce a 30-minute thermal/chemical stabilization window and qualification coupons before production wafer lots enter the line to avoid scrap cascades.
critical_failure_modes: Thermal runaway or severe peroxide decomposition in SC-1 resulting in caustic ammonia outgassing, high bath pH drift (>10.5), and severe silicon pitting (>0.3 nm RMS surface roughness degradation).
Fluoride cross-contamination or chemical drag-out into downstream SC-2 bath causing fluorosilicate etching of quartz bath heaters and catastrophic gate-oxide pinhole formation.
Inadequate DHF bath degas conditioning leaving dissolved O2 > 15 ppb, causing galvanic micro-corrosion and water-mark ring defects during Marangoni dry.

testcases.title: SC-1 Chemical Ratio and Thermal Homogeneity Bath Qualification
testcases.instrumentation: Near-Infrared (NIR) inline chemical concentration monitor, calibrated 4-channel Teflon-sheathed RTD temperature profiler, and Metrohm automated titrator
testcases.pre_conditions: Recirculation filtration active at 15 LPM through 0.05 um PTFE filter; megasonic transducer set to standby; bath filled with 5:1:1 UPW:NH4OH(29%):H2O2(30%) and conditioned for 30 minutes.
testcases.procedure: 1. Measure steady-state bath temperature across 5 geometric immersion nodes (4 corners and center) at 75°C setpoint. 2. Extract three 20 mL bath aliquots at t=0, t=30, and t=60 minutes. 3. Perform potentiometric neutralization titration with 0.1 N HCl for NH4OH and ceric sulfate redox titration for H2O2 concentration.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Temperature uniformity across all 5 nodes must be 75.0°C ± 1.5°C; NH4OH concentration must be 4.8 wt% ± 0.4 wt%; H2O2 concentration must be 4.3 wt% ± 0.3 wt% across 60 minutes.

testcases.title: DHF 50:1 Oxide Etch Rate and Hydrophobic Contact Angle Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Woollam M-2000 Spectroscopic Ellipsometer, Kruss Mobile Surface Analyzer (Drop Shape Analyzer), and 4-point probe resistivity meter
testcases.pre_conditions: PVDF bath filled with 50:1 UPW:HF (49%) maintained at 21.0°C ± 0.5°C; 150mm prime Si qualification wafer with 100 nm thermally grown SiO2 ready.
testcases.procedure: 1. Measure baseline SiO2 thickness at 49 points on wafer. 2. Immerse thermal oxide monitor wafer into DHF 50:1 for exactly 60 seconds with continuous N2 bubbling. 3. Quick-dump rinse in 18.2 MOhm-cm UPW for 3 cycles and N2 blow dry. 4. Re-measure post-etch oxide thickness at 49 points. 5. Immerse bare Si monitor wafer for 30 seconds to strip native oxide, dry, and dispense 2 uL UPW droplet to measure static sessile water contact angle.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Thermal SiO2 etch rate must be 4.5 nm/min to 5.5 nm/min with across-wafer etch uniformity 3-sigma < 3.0%; post-strip bare Si static water contact angle must be >= 72.0 degrees.

ppe_required: Chemical splash apron and jacket constructed of heavy-duty Neoprene/Butyl elastomer
Full-face polycarbonate splash shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1 combined with chemical splash goggles
Heavyweight 22-mil Butyl gloves over Nitrile inner gloves with regular pinhole testing
Chemical-resistant safety boots with steel toe and Metatarsal guard
Emergency personal HF response pouch containing unopened 2.5% Calcium Gluconate gel
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For HF exposure: Immediately flood exposed skin with emergency tepid water for 2 minutes while alerting cleanroom staff. Continuously massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into the affected area until medical personnel arrive; if splashed in eyes, irrigate with sterile 1% calcium gluconate eye wash or isotonic saline for 15 minutes. For NH4OH/HCl acid/base splashes: Drench shower for minimum 15 minutes, remove contaminated PPE, and seek emergency pulmonary and ophthalmic triage.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Dedicated acid and caustic wet bench exhaust plenum operating at -0.25 inches water column face velocity with laminar lip exhaust >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) across all open tank lips; acid scrubbers (packed tower water scrubber) for HF/HCl and caustic scrubbers (H2SO4 wash stage) for NH3 to avoid ammonium salt duct plugging.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Segregated drain plumbing: Fluoride waste streams (DHF 50:1 and DHF rinses) piped strictly to dedicated Fluoride Waste Treatment (FWT) for calcium fluoride (CaF2) precipitation using lime slurry/CaCl2. SC-1 and SC-2 dumps directed to General Acid/Base Neutralization (AWN) system using 2-stage automated sulfuric acid and sodium hydroxide pH correction to 6.5 - 8.5 before POTW discharge.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Dirty as-received silicon substrate with atmospheric airborne molecular contamination (AMC), native oxide (1.2-1.8 nm), and trace organic/metallic surface residues.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Atomically smooth, metal-depleted (<1e10 atoms/cm² Fe/Cu/Ni), chemical oxide-passivated (0.8-1.0 nm SC-2 hydrophilic oxide layer) silicon surface.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excessive exposure to cleanroom ambient air beyond 30 minutes induces uncontrolled native oxide growth with volatile organic hydrocarbon uptake and atmospheric boron/phosphorus moisture absorption, causing threshold voltage instability, high interface trap density (Dit > 1e11 eV^-1 cm^-2), and gate dielectric breakdown failure.

expected_result.summary: Demonstrated full operational conditioning, chemical stoichiometric stability, and qualification of sequential SC-1 (5:1:1), DHF (50:1), and SC-2 (6:1:1) wet bench baths with validated cleaning efficiency, surface micro-roughness preservation, native oxide stripping, and chemical oxide regrowth ready for gate oxide furnace processing.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-SC-1 Megasonic clean surface particle removal efficiency (PRE) for Si3N4/SiO2 particles >= 0.18 um
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP2 unpatterned wafer surface defect inspection before and after clean

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-SC-2 surface transition metal contamination density (sum of Fe, Ni, Cu, Zn)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry with Vapor Phase Decomposition (VPD-ICP-MS)

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Post-clean surface roughness RMS increment on bare silicon active area
quantitative_assertions.tolerance: +0.03 nm max delta from incoming baseline
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) 2um x 2um non-contact tapping mode scan

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Engineering signoff granted only when automated bath titrations across 3 consecutive 1-hour cycles match stoichiometric limits, 150mm monitor wafers demonstrate PRE >= 98.0%, post-clean VPD-ICP-MS certifies heavy metal contamination < 1e10 atoms/cm², and static contact angle after DHF validates complete native oxide strip with zero water marks upon Marangoni dry.
