# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Post-RCA Surface Defect Density Inspection & Darkfield Haze Mapping

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180-042`  
**Classification:** Metrology / Inspection Line  
**Target Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Process Step:** Post-RCA Surface Defect Density Inspection & Darkfield Haze Mapping  
**Action Type:** Buy (Commercial Laser Surface Particle Counter / Darkfield Inspection Metrology System)  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)

---

## 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure specifies the automated laser surface darkfield inspection and haze mapping for wafers exiting the RCA-1 / RCA-2 wafer cleaning line prior to critical high-temperature thermal steps (e.g., dry gate oxidation, polysilicon/high-k deposition). It qualifies surface cleanliness, particle defect count/density, and micro-roughness (haze) across 150mm/200mm silicon substrates.

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+-----------------------+     +------------------------+     +------------------------+
| 1. Wafer Loading &    | --> | 2. Recipe & Laser      | --> | 3. High-Gain Darkfield |
|    Cassette Placement |     |    Alignment (P/S-Pol) |     |    Surface Scanning    |
+-----------------------+     +------------------------+     +------------------------+
                                                                          |
                                                                          v
+-----------------------+     +------------------------+     +------------------------+
| 6. Clean Unload &     | <-- | 5. Pass/Fail Decision  | <-- | 4. Micro-Roughness     |
|    FOUP Routing       |     |    & Map Classification|     |    (Haze) Integration  |
+-----------------------+     +------------------------+     +------------------------+
```

### Step 1: Substrate Reception & Pre-Check
- Transfer the wafer cassette directly from the RCA final high-purity $\text{N}_2$ blow-dry / spin-rinse-dry station into the automated wafer-loader SMIF/cassette stage.
- Ensure the wafer surface is protected from airborne particulate contamination (ISO Class 1 mini-environment, laminar flow velocity $0.45 \pm 0.05\text{ m/s}$).

### Step 2: Recipe Selection & Optics Configuration
- Load recipe `REC-180DRAM-POSTRCA-HAZE`.
- Set laser beam incidence to grazing angle with darkfield collection optics configured for bare silicon / chemical native oxide surfaces.
- Select dual optical channels:
  - **Narrow Darkfield (NDF):** High sensitivity for isolated point defects and small particulate scattering.
  - **Wide Darkfield (WDF):** Optimized for low-frequency surface scatter and background darkfield haze.

### Step 3: Darkfield Particle & Surface Defect Scanning
- Clamp substrate electrostatically or via backside vacuum chuck with peripheral edge exclusion $\le 3.0\text{ mm}$.
- Initiate spiral/helical surface raster scan using solid-state laser source ($\lambda \sim 488\text{ nm}$ or $355\text{ nm}$ UV).
- Map coordinates $(X, Y)$ and cross-sectional scattering intensities for all detected surface anomalies down to threshold bin ($\ge 180\text{ nm}$ localized light scatterers - LLS).

### Step 4: Darkfield Haze Extraction & Surface Uniformity Mapping
- Integrate wide-angle darkfield scatter signals across wafer sub-apertures to extract average background haze in parts per million ($\text{ppm}$) relative to incident beam intensity.
- Detect localized haze anomalies indicating micro-roughness, chemical residue stains, or non-uniform native oxide regrowth following the HF dip/SC-2 clean.

### Step 5: Disposition & Pass/Fail Classification
- Correlate coordinates against DRAM unit cell critical pitch ($360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$ bitline/wordline pitch limits) to identify killer defects.
- Classify wafer disposition based on defect density limits and haze bounds. 
- Flag flagged wafers for rework (repeat SC-1/SC-2) if organic residue or particle clustering is identified.

### Step 6: Wafer Unload & Logging
- Return qualified wafers to clean transfer pods/cassettes and route to next process module (Gate Oxidation Furnace).
- Export wafer inspection defect map file (`.001` / KLARF standard) to the fab defect tracking database.

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Tolerance / Limit | Measurement Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Defect Particle Threshold Size** | $\ge 180$ | $\text{nm}$ | Equivalent Polystyrene Latex (PSL) sphere diameter | Darkfield Laser Scatter Channel |
| **Surface Defect Density ($D_0$)** | $\le 0.05$ | $\text{defects/cm}^2$ | Max threshold ($\ge 180\text{ nm}$ particle bin) | Automated Defect Coordinate Map |
| **Wafer Edge Exclusion Margin** | $3.0$ | $\text{mm}$ | $\pm 0.2\text{ mm}$ edge zone | Optical Chuck Edge Sensor |
| **Average Darkfield Background Haze** | $\le 0.15$ | $\text{ppm}$ | Maximum scatter over incident beam | Wide Darkfield Photodetector Array |

---

## 4. Context References & Literature Citations

- **Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**
  - Chemical sequence: RCA-1 ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}80^\circ\text{C}$), intermediate $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ DI rinse, 1:50 $\text{HF}$ dip ($15\text{--}30\text{ s}$), RCA-2 ($\text{HCl}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2:\text{H}_2\text{O}$ at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}80^\circ\text{C}$), and final high-purity $\text{N}_2$ blow-dry. 
  - Justifies post-clean metrology to verify the complete removal of organic surface films, particulate contaminants, and metallic ionic traces.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Unit cell access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$. Constrains the minimum optical inspection defect sensitivity limit to $\le 180\text{ nm}$ to detect killer particles before channel lithography and capacitor formation.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - Critical bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$, gate dielectric physical thickness of $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ grown at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$. Emphasizes that surface micro-roughness and darkfield haze must remain tightly bounded to avoid gate oxide breakdown and dielectric degradation.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-RCA defect metrology must cleanly decouple surface particulate counts from sub-surface micro-roughness haze. At 180nm DRAM ground rules, integrating darkfield laser scattering (405nm/488nm) requires strict baseline calibration against reference PSL spheres. Without dynamic optical thresholding between wide-angle (haze) and narrow-angle (discrete particle) collectors, background scatter from chemical oxide regrowth will skew Light Point Defect (LPD) sizing by over 25%, producing phantom defect escalations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Standard RCA-1 (SC-1: NH4OH/H2O2) strip followed by RCA-2 (SC-2: HCl/H2O2) and HF-last leaves either a chemical passivated oxide (~0.8-1.2 nm) or an H-terminated hydrophobic silicon surface. If darkfield inspection is performed on hydrophobic surfaces, airborne molecular contamination (AMC) and moisture condensation induce rapid micro-droplet nucleations, manifesting as false 'haze clouds' across the wafer periphery. The metrology recipe must specify laser incident angle, polarization (p-polarized vs s-polarized), and explicit haze gain calibration in ppm.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Dedicated bare-wafer defect inspection tools (e.g., KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP1/SP2 class) face long lead times and high refurbishment costs in Vietnam. The metrology pipeline must maintain backward compatibility with dual-purpose automated optical/confocal inspection systems or multi-point spectroscopic reflectometers outfitted with darkfield scattering channels, using certified 80nm-300nm NIST-traceable polystyrene latex (PSL) calibration standards sourced from regional secondary vendors.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Inspection throughput must not throttle the critical post-clean furnace queue time (Q-time). At a target run rate of 25 wafers/hour, 100% surface inspection with full darkfield haze mapping must execute within <= 90 seconds per 150mm/200mm wafer. If defect density fails, automated rework triggers back to SC-1/SC-2 must occur within a deterministic 15-minute operational window to prevent irreversible gate oxide integrity degradation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Queue-time breach leading to uncontrolled native oxide growth and airborne organic adsorption, which degrades gate oxide dielectric breakdown voltage (Vbd) and retention time.
1. Misclassification of micro-roughness haze as discrete LPDs due to PMT sensor drift or uncalibrated background scatter from trace chemical residues.
1. Wafer backside particle transfer during end-effector vacuum handling on the metrology stage, causing front-side focal plane distortion in subsequent lithography steps.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-3-3-2-01` | **Full-Wafer Laser Darkfield Particle Density (LPD) Qualification** | Automated Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner (405 nm / 488 nm solid-state laser, dual narrow/wide collector PMTs, NIST PSL calibrated) | 1. Load 150mm RCA-cleaned wafer onto vacuum chuck using backside-only ceramic end-effector. 2. Align notch/flat to 0-degree reference. 3. Execute spiral laser scan across 100% wafer surface with a 3mm edge exclusion. 4. Collect narrow-angle scatter signals and bin detected LPDs into size channels: 100-150nm, 150-200nm, and >200nm. 5. Generate coordinate defect map and compute total defect density per cm^2. | `Total Defect Density (LPD >= 120 nm) <= 0.15 defects/cm^2 across usable wafer area; zero killer defects (> 1.0 um) in active array area; edge-exclusion zone <= 3.0 mm.` |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-3-3-2-02` | **Surface Darkfield Haze Mapping and Chemical Oxide Uniformity Check** | Multi-channel Darkfield Surface Profiler & Haze Metrology Tool with Wide-Angle PMT Detector and integrated 49-point Spectroscopic Ellipsometer | 1. Position wafer in measurement chamber under 0.05 um filtered clean dry air (CDA). 2. Initiate wide-angle scatter scan at 50 um raster pitch to record raw surface scatter intensity. 3. Normalize intensity against incident beam to construct full-wafer haze map in parts-per-million (ppm). 4. Measure chemical oxide thickness at 49 points via spectroscopic ellipsometry (Delta/Psi fit with Cauchy model). 5. Correlate radial haze distribution with chemical oxide thickness variance. | `Average surface darkfield haze <= 0.12 ppm; maximum local haze peak <= 0.35 ppm; 49-point chemical oxide thickness within 1.05 nm ± 0.15 nm with 1-sigma non-uniformity < 2.5%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10 cleanroom compatible nitrile gloves (double-gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified laser safety goggles rated for 405nm/488nm OD > 6, Full static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and boot covers, Antistatic ESD-safe wrist strap or footwear grounder
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with IPA solvent, flush thoroughly with copious running water for 15 minutes. For accidental eye exposure to laser reflection, shut down beam interlock immediately, keep victim upright and eyes shielded, and seek immediate ophthalmological evaluation. In case of inhalation of trace organic solvent vapors, remove victim to fresh cleanroom air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Metrology chamber equipped with dedicated Class 1 laminar flow hood with HEPA/ULPA filtration (0.1 um capture efficiency >= 99.9999%); tool internal exhaust flow maintained at >= 15 m^3/hr to evacuate trace solvent vapors from stage cleaning.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes must be collected in closed, fire-resistant, grounded stainless-steel solvent disposal bins for segregation into organic flammable chemical waste streams. No direct drain discharge permitted.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Cleanroom Wipe Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 / Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (Ultrapure)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type E-1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly rinsed and dried Si (100) bare wafer post-RCA-1/RCA-2 sequence, exhibiting a pristine hydrophilic passivated chemical oxide (~1.0 nm) free of macroscopic liquid streaks.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Particle-inspected, qualified Si surface with verified low-defect baseline and mapped haze profile, maintained under sealed N2 environment prior to gate oxidation or dry dielectric furnace deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Airborne organic volatile condensation (AMC) and uncontrolled parasitic native oxide formation causing unrecoverable gate dielectric interface trap states (Dit), pinhole formation, and gate dielectric breakdown failure.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Demonstrated full-wafer surface qualification showing defect density <= 0.15 defects/cm^2 for particles >= 120 nm and mean darkfield haze <= 0.12 ppm, verifying that the RCA clean line meets 180nm DRAM gate oxidation standards without vacuum-chuck or handling contamination.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RCA_MET_LPD_KLARF_MAP_001.csv`
- [ ] `RCA_SURFACE_HAZE_SPECTRUM_REPORT_001.pdf`
- [ ] `RCA_WAFER_DEFECT_DENSITY_HEATMAP_001.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Average surface particle density for sizes >= 120nm must not exceed baseline threshold** | `0.15 defects/cm^2` | +0.02 defects/cm^2 | Automated Darkfield Laser Scanning Inspection (KLA/Surfscan KLARF coordinate analysis) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Mean surface background darkfield haze over active wafer diameter** | `0.12 ppm` | ±0.03 ppm | Calibrated wide-angle photomultiplier tube (PMT) scatterometer integral |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-RCA chemical oxide passivation thickness across 49-point wafer mapping** | `1.05 nm` | ±0.15 nm | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Psi/Delta optical modeling fit (Cauchy model) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Wafer lot exhibits zero killer defects (> 1.0 um) in active memory cell fields, meets ASSERT-01, ASSERT-02, and ASSERT-03 with 100% compliance, and is sealed in an N2 purged FOUP within the 30-minute cleanroom air Q-time limit.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Automated Goniometric Sessile Drop Contact Angle Passivation Profiling

### 1. Scope & Objective
This Standard Operating Procedure defines the protocol for automated goniometric sessile drop contact angle metrology on 180nm DRAM fabrication silicon substrates. The primary objective is to verify surface passivation uniformity, native oxide stripping completion, and transition between hydrophilic and hydrophobic states following the Standard RCA-1, intermediate HF dip (1:50 $\text{HF:H}_2\text{O}$), and RCA-2 cleaning sequences.

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Pre-Clean / Post-HF   │
│        Surface         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Automated Dispense:   │
│    18.2 MOhm-cm DI     │
│   Water Sessile Drop   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Side-View High-Speed  │
│    Optical Capture     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Baseline &       │
│     Young-Laplace      │
│        Fitting         │
│└───────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Multi-Point       │
│  Passivation Mapping   │
│    & Outlier Check     │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Substrate Handling & Chamber Conditioning**:
   - Transfer wafer from the cleaning line under high-purity $\text{N}_2$ environment directly to the automated goniometer stage to prevent airborne organic hydrocarbon adsorption or uncontrolled native oxide re-growth.
   - Maintain metrology chamber ambient at $21.0 \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ and relative humidity at $45 \pm 3\%$.

2. **Liquid Delivery System Priming**:
   - Purge automated micro-syringe line with ultra-pure deionized (DI) water exhibiting an electrical resistivity of $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
   - Ensure the dispensing tip is free of micro-bubbles and external wetting.

3. **Automated Wafer Mapping & Motion Setup**:
   - Load wafer recipe configured with standard radial tracking coordinates (utilizing standard automated 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping grid across center, mid-radius, and edge exclusion zones).
   - Align chuck zero coordinates to wafer notch/flat.

4. **Sessile Droplet Deposition**:
   - At each programmed inspection site, dispense a calibrated sessile micro-droplet ($2.0 \pm 0.2\ \mu\text{L}$) of $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ DI water at a controlled dosing rate ($1.0\ \mu\text{L/s}$).
   - Retract dosing needle vertically with zero vibration to avoid droplet sloshing or baseline distortion.

5. **Image Acquisition & Drop Profile Extraction**:
   - Capture side-view telecentric images within $2.0\text{ seconds}$ post-deposition using high-resolution digital optics with diffuse backlighting.
   - Automatically determine the substrate baseline and fit droplet tangent angles via Young-Laplace / polynomial circle fitting algorithms on both left ($\theta_L$) and right ($\theta_R$) contact contact interfaces.

6. **Passivation Profiling & Automated Run Validation**:
   - Average both angles: $\theta = \frac{\theta_L + \theta_R}{2}$.
   - Classify surface state: Hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated passivated surface ($>70^\circ$, typical for post-1:50 HF etch) vs. Hydrophilic chemical oxide / clean surface ($<10^\circ$, post-RCA-1 / RCA-2).
   - If contact angle deviation indicates incomplete native oxide strip or organic patch contamination, trigger an automated hold flag for engineering review.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Parameter | Target Metric / Value | Physical Units | Tolerance / Requirement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **DI Water Probe Resistivity** | $\ge 18.2$ | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | Minimum absolute resistivity threshold |
| **Wafer Mapping Grid Resolution** | $9\text{ or }49$ | points / wafer | Automated multi-point radial mapping |
| **HF Strip Contact Angle (Hydrophobic)** | $> 70$ | degrees ($^\circ$) | Minimum post-1:50 HF oxide strip passivation angle |
| **Post-RCA Surface Wetting (Hydrophilic)**| $< 10$ | degrees ($^\circ$) | Maximum post-SC-1 / SC-2 residual oxide contact angle |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure**
  - *Intermediate Rinse*: Dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for 3 minutes.
  - *Hydrofluoric Dip*: 1:50 $\text{HF:H}_2\text{O}$ dip for 15–30 seconds to strip native oxide; surface transitions from hydrophilic to hydrophobic.
  - *RCA-1 & RCA-2 Chemistry*: RCA-1 (5:1:1 $\text{H}_2\text{O}:\text{NH}_4\text{OH}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{–}80^\circ\text{C}$) and RCA-2 (6:1:1 $\text{H}_2\text{O}:\text{HCl}:\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{–}80^\circ\text{C}$) generating ultra-clean hydrophilic chemical oxide interfaces.
- **Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**
  - *Wafer Mapping*: Automated 9-point or 49-point wafer mapping tracks radial film non-uniformity across spin coating and furnace runs.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Substrate Criticality*: Gate and capacitor stack interfaces require stringent contamination control at $L = 180\text{ nm}$ transistor and dielectric integration nodes.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated sessile drop goniometry requires tight closed-loop synchronization between the micro-dispensing piezo/solenoid syringe, the 3-axis motorized wafer stage, and the high-speed telecentric CMOS imaging system. Vibration coupling from cleanroom air-handling or stage movement during droplet detachment causes droplet oscillation and contact line pinning distortions, corrupting the Young-Laplace numerical fitting if droplet settling time (typically 500 ms to 1 s) is not strictly regulated prior to optical acquisition.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm DRAM processing following dilute HF (DHF) etch and RCA-2 cleaning, silicon surface passivation shifts dramatically from hydrophilic Si-OH (silanol groups) to hydrophobic Si-H (hydride-terminated) bonds. Contact angle metrology must differentiate native chemical oxide re-growth and airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) adsorption from true hydride coverage, necessitating ultra-pure DI water (18.2 MOhm-cm, TOC < 2 ppb) to prevent spurious surfactant-induced contact angle depression below the required 75-85 deg threshold for fully stripped Si surfaces.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-purity dispensing consumables—specifically hydrophobic fluoropolymer-coated needle tips (30-34 gauge) and automated deionized water micro-syringes—face tight vendor lead times and contamination risks if standard laboratory-grade parts are substituted. Dual-sourcing of calibrated optical contact angle calibration standards (quartz optical reticles with lithographically defined droplet arcs) is required to ensure tool-to-tool matching across pilot and production lines.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Cycle time overhead must remain under 3.5 minutes for a full 9-point radial wafer map. Automated droplet suction/wicking must be integrated to prevent water pooling on prime production wafers, or non-destructive sacrificial test sites on wafer edge exclusion zones must be formally designated so that water droplet residue and micro-droplet drying watermarks (silica dissolution stains) do not degrade active 180nm memory array yield.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Evaporative volume reduction and contact line recession during prolonged optical exposure altering baseline contact angle (> 3 deg deviation within 5 seconds)
1. Airborne hydrocarbon/VOC contamination on hydrophobic Si-H surface during atmospheric queue time causing premature contact angle degradation prior to furnace loading
1. Dispensing needle clogging or wetting hysteresis causing non-axisymmetric droplet detachment and failure of the Young-Laplace circle/ellipse fitting algorithm

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-3-3-3-01` | **Automated 9-Point Radial Sessile Drop Contact Angle Hydrophobicity Verification** | Automated Optical Goniometer with high-speed CMOS camera (>= 60 fps), telecentric lens, vibration isolation table, motorized X-Y-theta wafer chuck, and automated micro-dispenser with 32G hydrophobic needle | 1. Load wafer onto motorized vacuum chuck and initiate automated recipe 'RCA_PASS_9PT'. 2. Align wafer notch to 0 deg and index to 9 standardized test coordinates (center, 4 points at r=35mm, 4 points at r=65mm). 3. At each coordinate, dispense a sessile drop of 1.50 +/- 0.10 uL UPW at a dispensing rate of 0.5 uL/s from a height of 1.0 mm above wafer surface. 4. Allow droplet to stabilize for 800 ms. 5. Capture 30 frames over 500 ms under collimated backlight. 6. Execute automated Young-Laplace baseline and contour fitting to extract left and right contact angles. 7. Wick droplet via automated vacuum aspiration nozzle prior to stage stepping. | `Mean water contact angle across all 9 points must be >= 78.0 deg with within-wafer standard deviation (1-sigma) <= 2.5 deg. Left-right angle symmetry difference must be <= 1.5 deg for all points.` |
| `TC-RCA-CLEAN-PROCESS-3-3-3-02` | **Post-Clean Hydrophilic Silicon Oxide Baseline and Passivation Uniformity Verification** | Automated Optical Goniometer with motorized stage and 0.05 uL resolution micro-dosing pump; Class 1 clean bench optical enclosure | 1. Mount hydrophilic control wafer onto goniometer chuck. 2. Position automated dispensing tip at center (0,0) and 4 orthogonal points at r=50mm. 3. Dispense a calibrated 1.00 uL UPW droplet at each position. 4. Record dynamic spreading and equilibrium contact angle using automated baseline edge-detection software within 1.0 s of substrate contact. 5. Compute mean surface energy and contact angle. | `Equilibrium contact angle must be < 5.0 deg (complete hydrophilic wetting of chemical oxide) across all 5 measurement sites, confirming absence of organic contamination or partial de-wetting patches.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles, Class 100 antistatic cleanroom gown with hood and face mask, ESD-safe safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For UPW: Non-hazardous; in case of cleanroom slips or spills, isolate area and wipe immediately. For IPA contact: Flush skin or eyes with eyewash station water for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of IPA vapors, move personnel to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Tool must be housed under a laminar downflow HEPA/ULPA hood (face velocity 0.45 m/s +/- 0.05 m/s) with localized mini-environment exhaust for volatile cleaning solvent vapor removal.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Aspirated water droplet effluent is routed to the facility industrial waste drain (IWD). IPA cleaning wipes must be disposed of in designated sealed solvent-waste containers and processed as hazardous flammable solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ultra-Pure Deionized Water (UPW)** | `7732-18-5` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI C35, 18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |
| **Isopropanol (for needle/stage calibration cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 5 (VLSI/MOS) | `>= 99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophobic hydride-terminated (Si-H) post-DHF rinse/dry or completely hydrophilic silanol-terminated (Si-OH) post-RCA-2 oxide passivated.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Verified passivated silicon substrate ready for immediate gate oxidation or thin-film dielectric deposition, free of micro-droplet residue.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding atmospheric Q-time results in uncontrolled native oxide re-growth (0.2-0.5 nm) and airborne volatile organic carbon (VOC) physisorption, degrading gate dielectric breakdown voltage (V_bd) and inducing threshold voltage (V_th) shifts in 180nm DRAM pass transistors.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full automated sessile drop contact angle characterization confirming complete, uniform surface passivation across 150mm production wafers, establishing quantitative compliance for post-clean hydrophobicity before gate dielectric growth.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WAF-180DRAM-RCA-PASSIVATION-MAP.csv`
- [ ] `GONIOMETRIC_DROP_CONTOUR_ANALYSIS.tiff`
- [ ] `METROLOGY_SIGNOFF_REPORT_PASSIVATION.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Average water contact angle across 9-point radial map on DHF-last treated wafer** | `80.5` | +/- 3.5 deg | Automated Young-Laplace optical edge-fitting algorithm on telecentric goniometric drop image |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Within-wafer contact angle non-uniformity across radial 9-point sites** | `2.1` | <= 3.0 % | Relative standard deviation ((sigma / mean) * 100) of the 9 measured coordinates |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Aspirated droplet residual watermark contamination at metrology sites** | `0` | <= 2 particles at >= 0.2 um bin size | Post-inspection dark-field laser scattering wafer defect inspection |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 9 metrology sites exhibit contact angle within target tolerance, Young-Laplace fit correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.995, zero drying watermarks detected post-aspiration, and inspection completed within the 30-minute cleanroom air Q-time limit.

critics.systems_engineer: Automated sessile drop goniometry requires tight closed-loop synchronization between the micro-dispensing piezo/solenoid syringe, the 3-axis motorized wafer stage, and the high-speed telecentric CMOS imaging system. Vibration coupling from cleanroom air-handling or stage movement during droplet detachment causes droplet oscillation and contact line pinning distortions, corrupting the Young-Laplace numerical fitting if droplet settling time (typically 500 ms to 1 s) is not strictly regulated prior to optical acquisition.
critics.domain_expert: For 180nm DRAM processing following dilute HF (DHF) etch and RCA-2 cleaning, silicon surface passivation shifts dramatically from hydrophilic Si-OH (silanol groups) to hydrophobic Si-H (hydride-terminated) bonds. Contact angle metrology must differentiate native chemical oxide re-growth and airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) adsorption from true hydride coverage, necessitating ultra-pure DI water (18.2 MOhm-cm, TOC < 2 ppb) to prevent spurious surfactant-induced contact angle depression below the required 75-85 deg threshold for fully stripped Si surfaces.
critics.supply_chain: High-purity dispensing consumables—specifically hydrophobic fluoropolymer-coated needle tips (30-34 gauge) and automated deionized water micro-syringes—face tight vendor lead times and contamination risks if standard laboratory-grade parts are substituted. Dual-sourcing of calibrated optical contact angle calibration standards (quartz optical reticles with lithographically defined droplet arcs) is required to ensure tool-to-tool matching across pilot and production lines.
critics.laya_pm: Cycle time overhead must remain under 3.5 minutes for a full 9-point radial wafer map. Automated droplet suction/wicking must be integrated to prevent water pooling on prime production wafers, or non-destructive sacrificial test sites on wafer edge exclusion zones must be formally designated so that water droplet residue and micro-droplet drying watermarks (silica dissolution stains) do not degrade active 180nm memory array yield.
critical_failure_modes: Evaporative volume reduction and contact line recession during prolonged optical exposure altering baseline contact angle (> 3 deg deviation within 5 seconds)
Airborne hydrocarbon/VOC contamination on hydrophobic Si-H surface during atmospheric queue time causing premature contact angle degradation prior to furnace loading
Dispensing needle clogging or wetting hysteresis causing non-axisymmetric droplet detachment and failure of the Young-Laplace circle/ellipse fitting algorithm

nodes.label: Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup

metrics_target.Acid Resistance: 100% PTFE / PFA and Polypropylene wet sinks
metrics_target.Safety Equipment: Calcium Gluconate gel and eyewash station present

nodes.sop_content:
1. Lắp đặt tủ hút hóa chất chịu axit với quạt hút chống ăn mòn PVC/PP.
2. Bố trí các bể ngâm PFA/PTFE riêng biệt cho axit HF, Piranha và dung môi hữu cơ.
3. Kiểm định vận tốc hút không khí tại mặt cắt đạt >= 0.5 m/s bằng máy đo gió anemometer.
4. Trang bị bộ sơ cứu đặc thù HF gồm kem canxi gluconat 2.5% và vòi tắm khẩn cấp.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Exhaust static pressure must maintain a reliable negative differential (minimum -0.75 in. w.g. / -187 Pa relative to cleanroom ambient) across all sash positions from 150 mm to full working opening of 450 mm. The acid scrubber intake ducting must incorporate a fail-safe pneumatic bypass damper with uninterruptible sensor telemetry to prevent toxic fume backdraft into the ISO 6/7 wet chemistry suite upon blower trip or scrubber water circulation failure.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: PTFE and virgin PVDF wet deck surfaces must withstand sustained immersion and thermal shock from exothermic Piranha (H2SO4:H2O2 3:1) mixtures exceeding 130°C without plasticizer leaching or micro-porosity formation. Drain plumbing must strictly segregate hot piranha Caro's acid streams from solvent or standard aqueous waste lines to eliminate catastrophic explosive gas generation (O2/SO2 evolution and solvent peroxidation) and thermal stress fracture of polypropylene drains.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Virgin semiconductor-grade PTFE (Teflon-PFA/PTFE, low-extractable trace metals < 0.1 ppb) and solid welded PVDF sheets face prolonged import lead times (12-16 weeks) in Vietnam. Sourcing certified flame-retardant polypropylene (FR-PP) or PVDF exhaust ductwork, explosion-proof Magnehelic differential pressure gauges, and PTFE aspirator/dump-rinser valves requires establishing dual-vendor qualified channels in Southeast Asia.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Installation and toxic chemical wet commissioning must not overlap with cleanroom ceiling HEPA/ULPA filter qualification or electrical drop certifications. Milestone M1 wet commissioning gate requires 72-hour continuous DI water flush, exhaust velocity grid validation, and emergency eyewash/drench shower certification prior to permitting the first liter of 96% H2SO4 or 30% H2O2 on site.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Loss of negative exhaust face velocity (< 0.4 m/s) leading to acid vapor escape into the cleanroom operator breathing zone during active 130°C Piranha etch.
1. Inadvertent drain cross-contamination of piranha oxidant with organic photoresist solvents causing explosive exothermic overpressure and drain manifold rupture.
1. Exothermic thermal degradation of non-virgin plastic or sealants causing acid breakthrough into structural under-bench containment pans.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-01` | **Fume Hood Face Velocity Uniformity and Dynamic Sash Containment Profile** | TSI 9565-P VelociCalc hot-wire anemometer, calibrated titanium tetrachloride / DI water fog generator, Magnehelic differential pressure gauge. | 1. Divide the sash open area into an equal 4x4 grid (16 measurement points). 2. Position the calibrated hot-wire anemometer at each grid node and log steady-state face velocity for 30 seconds per point. 3. Introduce visual tracer fog at 100 mm inside the lip across the entire deck and dynamically cycle sash between 150 mm and 500 mm. 4. Record plenum static pressure differential via Magnehelic gauge. | `Average face velocity must be 0.50 m/s with each point within 0.45 m/s to 0.55 m/s (tolerance +/- 10%); zero tracer fog escape outside sash boundary during dynamic sash actuation; duct static pressure between -180 Pa and -220 Pa.` |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-02` | **PTFE Chemical Bath Thermal Integrity and Over-Temperature Interlock Verification** | Dual Type-K PFA-encapsulated thermocouples, Keysight 34972A LXI data acquisition unit, automated DI water quench solenoid valve. | 1. Program PTFE immersion bath heater controller to ramp to 135°C at 2.0°C/min. 2. Verify surface temperature stability for 60 minutes across 5 spatial points along the carrier basket footprint. 3. Simulate thermocouple disconnection (open circuit) and heater runaway to verify dual redundant high-limit cut-off trips at 145°C. 4. Verify manual emergency stop cuts all heater contactor power and triggers cold DI quench interlock within 2.0 seconds. | `Bath temperature stability within +/- 1.0°C at 135°C; independent redundant limit cut-off actuates power disconnection at 145.0°C (+/- 2.0°C) with mechanical contactor drop-out; no warping, discoloration, or seal leakage observed on virgin PTFE liner.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy chemical-resistant butyl/neoprene gauntlet gloves over nitrile inner gloves, Full-face polycarbonate chemical splash shield with ANSI Z87.1 splash goggles, Heavyweight chemical-resistant virgin PTFE/PVC apron, Closed-toe acid-resistant safety boots with chemical-resistant overshoes, Continuous personal electrochemical SO2/acid gas gas-clip monitor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Immediately flush affected ocular or cutaneous areas with continuous tempered water (16°C-38°C) from emergency drench shower or eyewash for a minimum of 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing. Do not apply neutralizing chemical agents or oils to acid burns. In case of inhalation of acid mist or SO2/O2 thermal reaction vapors, immediately transport victim to fresh air, administer medical-grade humidified oxygen by trained personnel, and summon emergency paramedic medical response.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated corrosion-resistant PVDF/PP wet scrubbed acid exhaust ducting maintaining continuous face velocity of 0.50 m/s at maximum working sash aperture (400 mm). Minimum duct negative pressure of -200 Pa relative to cleanroom ambient, connected to packed-bed caustic (NaOH) wet fume scrubber with real-time differential pressure differential transducer and low-flow audible/visual beacon alarm.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Piranha bath solutions must be allowed to cool passively in the bath to ambient room temperature (< 35°C) for a minimum of 4 hours to ensure complete decomposition of peroxymonosulfuric acid (H2SO5) into H2SO4 and O2. Transfer slowly via PTFE aspirated drain lines to a dedicated acid waste neutralization (AWN) tank equipped with chilled DI water pre-dilution and automated 10-25% sodium hydroxide (NaOH) titration under continuous pH feedback control maintaining terminal effluent discharge pH 6.5 to 8.5.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sulfuric Acid** | `7664-93-9` | SEMI C1 / C7 Electronic Grade | `96.0% - 98.0%` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI C1 / C7 Electronic Grade | `30.0% - 32.0%` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid (Anhydrous / Aqueous)** | `7647-01-0` | Semiconductor Grade | `37.0% aqueous / 99.999% gas` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Wafers post-dry-etch / post-ion-implant with crosslinked organic photoresist crust and fluoropolymer sidewall polymer residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Atomically clean, organic-free, hydrophilic chemical oxide surface (OH-terminated SiO2, water contact angle < 5 degrees) ready for RCA clean or gate thermal oxidation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Airborne volatile organic compound (VOC) condensation and uncontrolled native oxide regrowth (> 0.6 nm) with airborne mobile ion (Na+/K+) contamination, resulting in gate oxide breakdown degradation and catastrophic threshold voltage shift in 180nm DRAM access transistors.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completed physical assembly, leak-tight plumbing integration, exhaust aerodynamics certification, and temperature-controlled piranha wet-clean qualification of the PTFE acid fume hood bench ready for Gen 1 180nm DRAM wafer fabrication.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ACID_HOOD_FACE_VELOCITY_MAP.csv`
- [ ] `PTFE_BENCH_COMMISSIONING_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `PIRANHA_BATH_THERMAL_PROFILING.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Average exhaust face velocity across 16-point sash grid at 400 mm working height** | `0.50 m/s` | +/- 0.05 m/s | Calibrated hot-wire anemometer TSI 9565 logged per TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-01 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **PTFE process tank liquid temperature steady-state control uniformity at nominal piranha cleaning setpoint** | `130.0°C` | +/- 1.5°C | Multi-channel calibrated PFA-shielded Type-K thermocouple datalogger per TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-02 |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Organic photoresist stripping cleanliness on 150mm test wafer monitor post-rinse and dry** | `0.0% residual carbon / contact angle < 5 deg` | < 10 particles at > 0.2 um; contact angle <= 5 deg | Laser surface particle scanner inspection and automated goniometer DI water contact angle measurement |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full mechanical, electrical, and fluidic installation signoff; 100% compliance on exhaust airflow containment with zero tracer escape; dual redundant over-temperature safety cutoffs functionally verified; all 3 quantitative assertions achieved with signed calibration artifacts archived in fab document control.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: PTFE Wet Bench Procurement & Acid Exhaust Ducting Integration
**Module:** Wet Chemistry / Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup  
**Technology Node Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type:** Make

---

### Process Execution Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  PTFE Bench Receiving  │
│        and Spec        │
│      Verification      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Acid Exhaust Ducting  │
│       and Flange       │
│      Interfacing       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Magnehelic       │
│      Differential      │
│   Pressure and Face    │
│   Velocity Balancing   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  DI Water Quick Dump   │
│   Rinse and Drainage   │
│      Flow Checks       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼

│        and Etch        │

└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Procurement & Material Verification:**
   - Procure and receive a semiconductor-grade, seamless-welded virgin Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) wet chemical bench equipped with segregated baths (HF/BOE native oxide stripping bath, SC-1/SC-2 RCA stations, and integrated Quick Dump Rinse [QDR] cascade tanks).
   - Inspect internal chemical supply lines (PFA/PTFE tubing), pneumatic acid-rated dump valves, and high-impact transparent chemical sash guards.

2. **Ducting & Flange Interfacing:**
   - Couple the wet bench acid exhaust collar to the sub-fab centralized acid scrubber lateral line using corrosion-proof, flame-retardant polypropylene (FRPP) or fluoropolymer-lined stainless steel ducting.
   - Install airtight EPDM/PTFE-encapsulated flange gaskets and torqued stainless steel band clamps along all duct joints.
   - Integrate an adjustable blast gate manual damper and a dedicated differential pressure tap (1/4-inch NPT) ahead of the main exhaust drop.

3. **Exhaust Aerodynamic Balancing & Pressure Verification:**
   - Commission and calibrate a dual-scale Magnehelic differential pressure gauge across the plenum duct connection.
   - Adjust the blast gate to balance negative duct draft until steady-state negative static pressure is achieved.
   - Measure multi-point face capture velocity across the open sash opening using a calibrated hot-wire anemometer to confirm zero chemical fume backflow into the cleanroom aisle.

4. **Safety Interlocks & Quick Dump Rinse (QDR) Drainage Commissioning:**
   - Wire low-exhaust static pressure cutoff interlocks to the master wet bench chemical dispensing solenoids to automatically isolate chemical dispense if exhaust failure occurs.
   - Plumb acid-waste drainage to the dedicated Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) collection pipe with double-containment piping.
   - Run ultra-pure DI water through the QDR cycle to verify rapid pneumatic dump timing, leak integrity, and drain clearance without bubbling or back-pressure.

5. **Final Substrate Clean Process Readiness:**
   - Ready the bench for critical 180nm DRAM front-end and back-end wet surface conditioning (such as pre-gate/pre-dielectric native oxide clean before furnace ONO oxidation and pre-metallization deglaze before PVD sputtering).

---

---

### Citations & Literature Context Integration

1. **Context: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
   - The wet bench provides critical surface preparation and wafer cleaning for stacked capacitor structures, ensuring zero interfacial contamination for tungsten plug contacts and high-$\kappa$ ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5\text{ / }\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dielectric stacks required to meet the minimum **$28\text{ fF/cell}$** capacitance budget and sub-**$1\text{ fA/cell}$** leakage limit at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. **Context: Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) Sputtering of Aluminum Metallization Interconnects**
   - The wet chemical station performs post-etch chemical residue removal and pre-metallization surface preparation prior to planar DC magnetron sputtering of **$\text{Al-0.5\% Cu}$** (350 nm $\pm 5\%$) to maintain low interconnect sheet resistance ($R_s < 0.08\,\Omega/\text{sq}$).
3. **Context: Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**
   - Upstream native oxide stripping and RCA clean in the PTFE wet bench prepare wafers prior to load insertion into the multi-zone quartz furnace (operated at $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ uniformity between $800^\circ\text{C}$ and $1150^\circ\text{C}$ with carrier gas flow regulated at $1\text{ to }5\text{ SLPM}$) to prevent defect nucleation and crystallographic slip.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The procurement specification lacks explicit interlock definitions between wet bench exhaust differential pressure switches and chemical dispense pump permissives. If the acid scrubber or dedicated FRP/PVDF exhaust duct suffers negative pressure collapse or blower trip, HF/SC-1 acid fumes will back-draft into the cleanroom bay unless fail-closed pneumatic isolation dampers and hardwired exhaust differential pressure interlocks (< -0.5 in. w.g.) immediately drop chemical heating baths to fail-safe idle and inhibit DI water dump rinser actuation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Specifying homogeneous white virgin PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) or PFA for immersion tanks is appropriate for hydrofluoric acid resistance, but using monolithic PTFE for structural bench casing without stress-relieved polypropylene (PP) outer jackets leads to creep and thermal sagging under sustained 75°C SC-1 / 180°C piranha cleaning bath loads. Furthermore, integration with the acid exhaust ducting must specify welded PVDF or ETFE-coated stainless steel rather than standard PVC, preventing embrittlement and catastrophic stress-corrosion cracking from hot acidic nitric/peroxide vapors.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring customized fully-welded virgin PTFE wet decks with integrated megasonic transducers (1 MHz) and automated cascade dump rinsers faces lead times exceeding 26-34 weeks from tier-1 equipment vendors. For Gen-1 180nm DRAM prototyping, procurement must establish dual-sourcing for chemical-resistant metering valves (PFA pneumatic valves), FM4910-compliant flame-retardant plastics, and standardized duct transition spigots to avoid fab fit-up delays.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Budget and schedule gating depends critically on cleanroom facility hookup synchronization. The mechanical acid exhaust duct tie-in to the wet scrubber header and sub-fab neutralization drain plumbing must be finalized at least 6 weeks before skid delivery; delivery without verified factory acceptance testing (FAT) of the emergency power-off (EPO) and fire suppression CO2/water deluge integration will freeze fab wet-processing commissioning milestones.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Loss of acid exhaust negative draft leading to toxic HF vapor roll-out past the bench sash face velocity threshold into operator breathing zones.
1. Creep and seam weld fracture of PTFE immersion tanks under continuous thermal cycling at 70-75°C, causing chemical drain leakage into structural secondary containment.
1. Static charge accumulation during high-resistivity (>18 MOhm-cm) DI water cascade dump rinse dumping, generating ESD discharge and ignition risks in adjacent chemical baths.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-1-01` | **Wet Bench Sash Face Velocity and Static Negative Exhaust Pressure Verification** | TSI 9565 VelociCalc Thermal Anemometer (calibrated hot-wire probe) and Dwyer Series 477AV Digital Manometer | 1. Measure exhaust duct static negative pressure at the wet bench exhaust collar test port via digital manometer. 2. Partition the sash opening plane into a 100 mm x 100 mm grid across width and height (minimum 12 sampling points). 3. Record instantaneous face velocity at each grid node for 30 seconds and calculate mean face velocity. 4. Simulate a 30% exhaust blower damper restriction and record bench audio/visual alarm trigger point. | `Pass if mean sash face velocity is 0.50 m/s with no single point < 0.40 m/s or > 0.65 m/s, static exhaust duct pressure is between -1.5 in. w.g. and -2.2 in. w.g., and low-exhaust visual/acoustic interlock trips at >= -0.75 in. w.g.` |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-1-02` | **PTFE Immersion Bath Thermal Stability, Level Sensor Interlock, and Chemical Leak Containment Test** | Fluke 52 II Dual-Input Digital Thermometer with PTFE-sheathed Type-K thermocouple, Keyence optical liquid level sensor test jig, and clean DI water tracer | 1. Program immersion bath PID controller to 75.0°C; ramp DI water bath from ambient (22.0°C) while logging thermal uniformity across four bath corners and center. 2. Drain bath water slowly to simulate boil-off/evaporation until low-level sensor triggers, verifying heater power cutoff response time. 3. Introduce 500 mL DI water into the secondary containment liner and measure optoelectronic leak detection relay trip time. | `Pass if bath reaches and maintains 75.0°C within +/- 1.0°C across all probe locations without PTFE wall deflection (> 1.5 mm), heater circuit isolates within <= 1.5 seconds upon low liquid level detection, and secondary containment sensor signals alarm in <= 2.0 seconds.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty Neoprene/Viton laminate chemical gauntlets over inner nitrile gloves (tested per EN 374-3), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash face shield combined with panoramic safety goggles, Full-coverage virgin PTFE or heavy vinyl/acid-resistant aprons with integral sleeves, Steel-toe neoprene rubber safety chemical boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For Hydrofluoric Acid exposure: Immediate continuous rinsing with copious cold UPW for exactly 1 minute, followed by aggressive manual massage of 2.5% Calcium Gluconate topical gel into exposed skin tissue until medical arrival; replace gel every 10 minutes. For inhalation, supply 100% medical oxygen and immediately nebulize 2.5% calcium gluconate solution. For TMAH skin exposure: Flush skin with water for >= 15 minutes; treat systemic neurotoxic and respiratory depression symptoms with immediate EMS dispatch and ALS support.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous lateral lip-slot and rear-plenum acid fume extraction connected via FM4910-rated PVDF/ETFE ductwork to central cleanroom packed-bed caustic scrubber; minimum design face velocity 0.5 m/s at nominal sash working height; hardwired static pressure differential transmitter triggering pneumatic emergency shutoff dampers on loss of negative pressure (< -0.5 in. w.g.).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated drainage lines: Fluoride-bearing waste (HF / BOE) routed to automated Ca(OH)2 / CaCl2 precipitation tanks for insoluble CaF2 settling; general acid/base waste (SC-1, SC-2 rinses) routed to automated two-stage continuous pH neutralization system (sulfuric acid and sodium hydroxide dosing to pH 6.5-8.5) before municipal sewer discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Tier-3 / VLSI Grade | `0.5% to 49.0% wt/wt aqueous` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (NH4OH)** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Tier-3 / VLSI Grade | `28.0% to 30.0% wt/wt aqueous` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Tier-3 / VLSI Grade | `30.0% to 32.0% wt/wt aqueous` |
| **Tetramethylammonium Hydroxide (TMAH)** | `75-59-2` | Electronic Grade (Metal-Ion-Free) | `2.38% wt/wt aqueous (0.26N)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned patterned or bare Si wafer with post-RIE polymer residues or native chemical oxide (~1.5-2.0 nm SiO2) exhibiting hydrophilic contact angle (< 10 degrees).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Atomically clean, particle-neutralized, hydrogen-terminated hydrophobic silicon surface exhibiting contact angle > 75 degrees and native oxide thickness < 0.2 nm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Uncontrolled regrowth of defective native oxide (SiO2 > 0.5 nm), airborne trace organic adsorption (hydrocarbon contamination), and airborne amine/boron particulate chemisorption causing gate dielectric breakdown voltage degradation and catastrophic DRAM storage node contact interface resistance spikes.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical delivery, utility hookup, safety interlock qualification, and wet acceptance testing of the virgin PTFE chemical bench and FM4910 acid exhaust duct tie-in, validating complete chemical isolation, face velocity compliance, and thermal/particle process baselines for 180nm DRAM RCA clean and HF etching steps.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `WET_BENCH_COMMISSIONING_AND_FACILITY_SIGN_OFF.pdf`
- [ ] `EXHAUST_AERODYNAMICS_AND_FACE_VELOCITY_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `DI_WATER_STATIC_DUMP_AND_BATH_PARTICLE_BASELINE.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wet bench operating sash average face velocity** | `0.50 m/s` | +/- 0.05 m/s | Multi-point calibrated hot-wire thermal anemometer traversing 12-point sash opening grid per SEMI S2/S8 standards. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Immersion tank SC-1 steady-state bath thermal uniformity** | `72.5 C` | +/- 1.0 C | Calibrated 5-point immersed PTFE-shielded Type-K thermocouple probe array logged over 60-minute duration. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Post-overflow cascade dump rinse water purity recovery resistivity** | `18.0 MOhm-cm` | >= 16.5 MOhm-cm | Inline Thornton 200CR high-purity resistivity sensor reading after 5 dump-and-fill rinse cycles. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Completion of 72-hour continuous uninterrupted burn-in under active exhaust with zero leak sensor trips, verified EHS safety interlock fail-safe cutoff on simulated exhaust and heater fault conditions, signed chemical compatibility inspection report, and written approval by the DRAM Integration Lead and Fab Facilities Safety Officer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Acid Bath PFA Plumbing, DI Quick-Dump Rinser & $\text{N}_2$ Purge Installation

**Module:** Architecture & Integration > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Wet Chemistry  
**Target:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (Gen 1 mm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Architecture & Flow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│     PFA Chemical      │
│   Distribution Bath   │
│       Plumbing        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Sub-Micron UPW Fill  │
│    & Cascade Dump     │
│        Rinser         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Resistivity Sensor   │
│   Monitoring: 18.2    │
│        MOhm-cm        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Point-of-Use 0.05um  │
│   Filtered N2 Purge   │
│        Drying         │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Installation & Commissioning Procedure

#### Step 1: PFA Wet Bench Acid Bath Plumbing Installation
1. Route high-purity Perfluoroalkoxy (PFA) dual-containment tubing with flared PTFE fittings to service the RCA-1 ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 : \text{UPW}$ at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }75^\circ\text{C}$), Native Oxide Strip ($1:50\text{ to }1:100\text{ HF} : \text{UPW}$ at $22^\circ\text{C}$), and RCA-2 ($\text{HCl} : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 : \text{UPW}$ at $75^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$) immersion stations.
2. Integrate ultrasonic/megasonic agitation modules ($1\text{ MHz}$) onto the immersion baths.
3. Torque all flare connections using calibrated torque wrenches according to PFA fitting diameter specifications; perform an initial pneumatic pressure decay integrity check on chemical delivery and gravity drains with dry nitrogen.

#### Step 2: DI Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) & Resistivity Probe Integration
1. Position and level the high-purity virgin PTFE/PVDF Quick-Dump Rinser (QDR) vessel within the chemical bench exhaust envelope.
2. Connect Ultra-Pure Water (UPW) supply headers delivering $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ water to the top spray manifolds and bottom fill diffusers.
3. Install the pneumatic bottom dump door mechanism, configuring rapid drain actuation via clean dry air/$\text{N}_2$ solenoid pilots.
4. Mount an in-line high-purity resistivity sensor probe inside the overflow weir/recirculation drain channel to monitor cascade dump-rinse cycles. Set controller logic for automated cascade cycles (5 dump-and-fill cycles minimum).

#### Step 3: High-Purity Filtered $\text{N}_2$ Purge Line Installation
1. Install electro-polished 316L stainless steel or ultra-clean fluoropolymer lines from the bulk nitrogen facility header to point-of-use wet bench drop points.
2. Mount point-of-use $0.05\,\mu\text{m}$ PTFE membrane gas filters immediately upstream of the bench-integrated Marangoni dry heads, manual filtered $\text{N}_2$ blow-off guns, and bath blanket spargers.
3. Connect and calibrate gas flow meters and pressure regulators to supply particle-free $\text{N}_2$ for wafer surface dry and head-space acid vapor displacement.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Inspection / Parameter | Target Metric | Engineering Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **QDR Rinse Endpoint Resistivity** | $> 16$ (Baseline: $18.2$) | $\text{M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | In-line calibrated resistivity conductivity sensor |
| **QDR Cascade Dump Cycle Count** | $5$ | Cycles | Automated PLC recipe counter |
| **RCA-2 Acid Bath Temperature Uniformity** | $75 \pm 2$ | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Immersion fluoropolymer-encapsulated RTD/thermocouple |
| **Continuous UPW Overflow Duration (Dev/Rinse)** | $60$ | $\text{seconds}$ | Integrated PLC digital sequence timer |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Context Alignment

* **RCA-1 (SC-1) & Cascade Dump Rinse Parameters:**  
  * *Citation:* `RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering`  
  * *Context:* 5 cycles cascade dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ UPW until bath resistivity reaches $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$; $70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }75^\circ\text{C}$ immersion bath with $1\text{ MHz}$ megasonic agitation.
* **Native Oxide Strip & RCA-2 (SC-2) Temperature & Drying:**  
  * *Citation:* `RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering`  
  * *Context:* $1:50\text{ to }1:100\text{ HF}$ at $22^\circ\text{C}$; RCA-2 at $75^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$; final overflow rinse to $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ followed by filtered $\text{N}_2$ Marangoni/IPA vapor drying.
* **Overflow Dump Rinse Timing & $\text{N}_2$ Dry Integration:**  
  * *Citation:* `Positive Photoresist Spin Dynamics, Soft Bake & Development Protocol`  
  * *Context:* Continuous overflow dump rinse with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water for $60\text{ seconds}$, followed by filtered $\text{N}_2$ drying.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Plumbing PFA (perfluoroalkoxy) manifolds and Quick-Dump Rinsers (QDR) requires dual-containment design and automated pneumatics. The pneumatic dump flapper valve in the QDR cycle must open within 1.5 seconds and trigger bottom purge spray nozzles concurrently to prevent backflow and liquid stagnancy. Interlocking the N2 blow-off purge with the acid exhaust draft differential pressure sensor is critical; if exhaust velocity drops below 0.5 m/s, automated N2 pressurization lines and chemical feed valves must failsafe close (NC) to prevent positive fume pressurization into the cleanroom bay.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm DRAM node front-end cleans (pre-gate oxidation, trench capacitor, and contact cleans), post-dilute HF and RCA bath rinsing must achieve an endpoint UPW resistivity of > 16 MOhm-cm within 4 to 5 dump cycles. Dead legs in PFA weldments or Flaretek fittings can trap concentrated HF or SC-1 chemistry, which bleeds back into the QDR chamber during dump steps, destroying native oxide control and shifting gate dielectric equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) by > 0.3 nm. All PFA components must be high-purity semiconductor grade (SEMI F57 compliant) and leached with 5% HNO3/UPW prior to wafer release.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Virgin PFA HP tubing (e.g., Entegris FluoroLine / Chemfluor), Flaretek PFA compression fittings, and pneumatically actuated PTFE diaphragm valves have lead times of 12 to 18 weeks. Sourcing secondary containment transparent PVC-C jackets and certified QDR vessels with built-in PVDF/PFA dump bottom gates requires local stock verification or pre-ordering spare diaphragm rebuild kits, as standard chemical vendors in Vietnam rarely maintain SEMI-grade PFA inventories.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Phase-gate milestone Gen-1 Wet Chemistry commissioning hinges on physical leak-integrity and DIW resistivity loop signoff before any dummy wafer dipping. Tool install budget cannot absorb acid fume contamination of adjacent stepper lenses. Commissioning must strictly allocate 4 days for hydrostatic pressure hold tests, DI water flow rate validation, and exhaust hood face velocity certification prior to chemical qualification.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. QDR bottom dump seal erosion or micro-leakage leading to bath chemical retention, insufficient dilution, and wafer surface cross-contamination with metallic and organic ions.
1. PFA flare fitting cold-flow relaxation or improper thermal flaring resulting in pressurized acid weeping into containment tray and HF/HCl vapor breakthrough.
1. N2 blow-off purge overpressurization or particulate shedding from unbaked PFA sub-micron filters contaminating wafers with > 0.2 µm particles during drying.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-2-01` | **PFA Manifold Hydrostatic Pressure Decay & Helium/N2 Leak Rate Qualification** | Digital calibrated pressure transmitter (0-10 bar, 0.05% FS accuracy, Yokogawa or Rosemount), calibrated N2 regulator, ultrasonic leak detector, SEMI S2 certified sniffer. | 1. Isolate downstream bath dispense heads and close all terminal PFA diaphragm valves. 2. Pressurize PFA manifold with filtered clean dry N2 (CDA/N2, 0.003 µm filtered) to 4.0 bar gauge (1.5x maximum operating pressure). 3. Isolate the inlet supply valve and record initial pressure P0. 4. Monitor line pressure continuously for 60 minutes at constant ambient temperature (22°C +/- 1.0°C). 5. Scan all flared joints and valve stems with ultrasonic leak detector. | `Total pressure drop over 60 minutes must be <= 0.02 bar (delta P <= 0.5% of test pressure). Zero detectable ultrasonic bubbling or acoustic leak signature (> 20 kHz acoustic leak signal < 10 dB above baseline).` |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-2-02` | **QDR Dynamic Dump Cycle, Cascade Efficiency & DIW Resistivity Recovery Verification** | In-line high-purity resistivity sensor (Thornton 770MAX or Mettler Toledo with 0.01 cm^-1 cell constant, NIST traceable), calibrated digital flow meter, high-speed pneumatic cycle timer. | 1. Trigger automated Quick-Dump Rinser sequence via PLC. 2. Measure actuation time of bottom flapper dump valve from trigger signal to complete gravity evacuation (< 5 seconds). 3. Initiate bottom spray fill and cascade overflow at 15 L/min. 4. Record resistivity recovery curve of effluent water continuously over 5 successive fill-and-dump cycles. 5. Repeat test 5 consecutive runs to confirm repeatability. | `QDR vessel must fully drain in < 3.5 seconds per dump. Effluent resistivity must recover from < 0.1 MOhm-cm to >= 16.5 MOhm-cm at 25°C within <= 4 dump-and-fill cycles (total time <= 150 seconds). Zero pneumatic valve sticking or error flags over 5 consecutive test iterations.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Butyl rubber acid aprons with sleeves (heavy duty), Viton or heavy-duty neoprene over-gloves over nitrile chemical-resistant inner gloves, Full-face acid gas respirator with multi-gas/P100 cartridge (ANSI Z87.1 certified face shield combined), Steel-toe chemical-resistant neoprene boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Calcium Gluconate 2.5% topical gel must be immediately accessible within 3 meters of the wet bench. For dermal HF exposure: Immediately flush affected area with emergency deluge shower for 2 minutes, then massage Calcium Gluconate gel continuously into skin until medical arrival. For eye exposure: Flush at dedicated eye wash station for 15 minutes with sterile saline or water; seek immediate emergency ophthalmological care. Provide oxygen in case of vapor inhalation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated acid wet bench polypropylene exhaust plenum with continuous negative static pressure (-150 to -250 Pa) and face velocity >= 0.55 m/s across the entire sash aperture (height 300 mm). Differential pressure gauge (Magnehelic) interlocked with tool PLC to trigger emergency shutoff of N2 purge and PFA chemical supply valves upon exhaust failure (< 0.40 m/s).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated drainage lines: Fluoride-containing waste (HF/dHF) routed strictly to dedicated Calcium Fluoride (CaF2) precipitation sump with Ca(OH)2 dosing; general acid-base effluent (SC-1, SC-2 rinses) routed to automated 3-stage equalization and neutralization system (NaOH/H2SO4 dosing) balancing effluent to pH 6.5 - 8.5 prior to municipal discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (HF)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 1 / UP-S | `0.5% to 49% aqueous` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)** | `7647-01-0` | SEMI Grade 1 / UP-S | `37% aqueous` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2)** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Grade 1 / UP-S | `30% aqueous` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (NH4OH)** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Grade 1 / UP-S | `29% aqueous` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-RIE or stripped silicon wafer with organic residues, metallic trace impurities (< 1e11 atoms/cm^2), and uncontrolled native oxide (1.2 - 1.8 nm).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Atomically clean, chemical-free silicon surface: Si-H passivated hydrophobic state following dilute HF dip (water contact angle > 75 degrees), or clean stoichiometric chemical oxide (0.6 - 0.8 nm) post SC-1/SC-2 with metallic contamination < 1e10 atoms/cm^2 and zero particle count increase (> 0.18 µm delta particles <= 5).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes native oxide re-growth (> 0.4 nm), airborne boron/phosphorus and volatile organic compound (VOC) re-adsorption, leading to gate oxide breakdown voltage (BVox) degradation and threshold voltage (Vth) shifts in 180nm DRAM access transistors.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete installation, pressure qualification, and dynamic process signoff of SEMI-compliant PFA plumbing, pneumatic automated QDR station, and filtered N2 purge subsystem for DRAM Foundation VN 180nm wafer cleaning benches.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `pfa_plumbing_leak_test_report_tc_wet_bench_safety_2_01.pdf`
- [ ] `qdr_dynamic_cycle_resistivity_recovery_log.csv`
- [ ] `fume_hood_exhaust_and_face_velocity_certification.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **PFA Manifold Static Pressure Decay over 60 minutes at 4.0 bar gauge N2** | `0.00 bar` | +0.02 bar maximum allowable drop | Calibrated digital pressure logger recording at 1 Hz over 3600 seconds |
| `ASSERT-02` | **QDR DIW Effluent Resistivity Recovery at cycle 4 endpoint** | `16.8 MOhm-cm` | >= 16.0 MOhm-cm at 25°C | In-line Thornton NIST-traceable calibrated conductivity/resistivity sensor |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Fume Hood Face Velocity across sash working opening (300 mm)** | `0.55 m/s` | +/- 0.05 m/s (minimum 0.50 m/s at all grid points) | Multi-point calibrated hot-wire anemometer grid scan per ANSI/ASHRAE 110 |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful zero-leak hydrostatic/N2 hold test, confirmed QDR resistivity return to >= 16.0 MOhm-cm within <= 4 dumps across 5 consecutive runs, verified emergency chemical shutoff on exhaust drop, and EHS sign-off on Calcium Gluconate and PPE staging at the wet bench.
