# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: SOP-WET-180NM-MET-001
**Title:** Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification  
**Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Metrology  
**Generation:** Gen 1 (mm)  
**Action Type:** Buy / Facility & Wet Bench Certification  

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure specifies the exact calibration and certification protocols for wet chemical processing benches (PTFE wet deck and acid exhaust hoods) utilized in the cleaning, etching, and pre-furnace surface preparation for 180nm DRAM fabrication (e.g., gate oxide pre-clean, ONO/high-$\kappa$ capacitor dielectric wet cleans, bitline contact de-glaze). This ensures full acid vapor containment, cleanroom safety, laminar capture velocity, and Ultra-Pure Deionized (DI) water resistivity compliance.

---

### 2. Required Metrology Equipment & Standards
- **Vane / Hot-Wire Anemometer:** Calibrated NIST-traceable digital thermal anemometer (resolution $\pm 0.01\text{ m/s}$ or $\pm 2\text{ FPM}$).
- **Non-Toxic Smoke / Vapor Generator:** Titanium tetrachloride-free glycol/DI fog generator or dry-ice/DI smoke pencil for flow visualization.
- **In-Line / Handheld DI Resistivity Metrology:** Temperature-compensated conductivity/resistivity cell calibrated to ASTM D1125 / SEMI standard ($25.0^\circ\text{C}$ reference).

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Calibration & Certification Procedure

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 1: Face Velocity Grid Mapping (Fume Hood Sash Opening) |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 2: Acid Vapor Containment Smoke Visualization Test     |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Step 3: Deionized (DI) Water Point-of-Use Resistivity Check |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Face Velocity Grid Calibration
1. Position the fume hood vertical sash at the standard certified operating sash opening height ($18\text{ inches}$ or $457\text{ mm}$).
2. Subdivide the open face area into an imaginary equal-area grid of cells not exceeding $1\text{ sq ft}$ ($0.09\text{ m}^2$) each (minimum $3 \times 3$ grid points).
3. Mount the calibrated hot-wire/vane anemometer probe at the center of each grid position, facing perpendicular to the incoming cleanroom air stream.
4. Measure and log average velocity over $10\text{ seconds}$ per point:
   - Average face velocity target: $100\text{ FPM} \pm 10\%$ ($0.51\text{ m/s} \pm 0.05\text{ m/s}$).
   - Calculate face velocity uniformity: No individual grid measurement shall deviate by more than $\pm 20\%$ from the average face velocity.
5. If velocity is out of range, adjust the acid exhaust damper valve at the bench exhaust plenum until compliant, then lock the damper collar.

#### Step 2: Acid Vapor Containment & Flow Visualization (Per ASHRAE 110 / SEMI S2)
1. Set the vapor/smoke generator at the bench work surface $6\text{ inches}$ ($150\text{ mm}$) inside the sash line.
2. Traverse the smoke wand across the perimeter, side baffles, and rear exhaust slots at a rate of $1\text{ ft/s}$ ($0.3\text{ m/s}$).
3. Visually inspect flow dynamics:
   - Verify smooth, laminar flow drawn straight into the rear exhaust slots and bottom baffles.
   - Confirm zero smoke roll-out, turbulence vortices, or escape toward the operator breathing zone under active exhaust.
4. Simulate operator movement by moving a dummy panel across the sash face to ensure face velocity capture is robust against walk-by wake effects.

#### Step 3: DI Water Resistivity Certification (Point-of-Use Quick-Dump Rinsers & Bath Lines)
1. Open the Point-of-Use (POU) ultra-pure DI water supply valve at the PTFE wet bench and flush into the drain/QDR (Quick-Dump Rinser) for $\ge 5\text{ minutes}$ to displace stagnant line volume.
2. Read the calibrated temperature-compensated inline sensor or extract a sample using a clean PTFE beaker with immediate insertion of the certified probe.
3. Verify that the resistivity stabilizes at $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25.0^\circ\text{C}$ (spec limit $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ for ultra-pure final rinse).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Metrology Instrument | Target Value | Tolerance / Range | Pass/Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Average Face Velocity** | Calibrated Hot-Wire Anemometer | $100\text{ FPM}$ ($0.51\text{ m/s}$) | $\pm 10\text{ FPM}$ ($90 - 110\text{ FPM}$ / $0.46 - 0.56\text{ m/s}$) | Mandatory Pass |
| **Velocity Point Uniformity** | Multi-point Grid Scan | $\le 15\%$ Deviation | Max $\pm 20\%$ per grid point | Mandatory Pass |
| **Vapor Containment Escape** | Smoke Generator Visual Flow Test | $0\text{ roll-out}$ | Zero visible fume leakage past sash line | Mandatory Pass |
| **POU DI Water Resistivity** | Temperature-Compensated Resistivity Meter | $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$ | Minimum $\ge 18.0\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ | Mandatory Pass |

---

### 5. Context & Source References
- **Cleanline Wet Chemical Infrastructure Context:** Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup [Chemical Processing] & Metrology module.
- **Process Integration Link:**
  - *Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering* — Dry oxidation gate dielectric ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$) and high-$\kappa$ capacitor cleans require stringent ionic contamination control and absolute cleanroom vapor containment to avoid device degradation and defectivity.
  - *Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench* — Stacked capacitor formation with high-$\kappa$ ($Ta_2O_5 / Al_2O_3$ or ONO) dielectric requires ultraclean surface preparation with ultra-pure DI rinsing to maintain leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Exhaust static pressure must be continuously coupled to local face velocity via closed-loop VAV (Variable Air Volume) or manual blast gate balancing. A drift below 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) at a standard 18-inch sash opening allows toxic acid plume rollback during rapid operator arm movements, while face velocities exceeding 120 FPM induce turbulent vortex shedding over the rear draft slots, ejecting vapor forward into the breathing zone.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Deionized (DI) water resistivity must strictly maintain 18.2 MOhm-cm at 25 deg C with total oxidizable carbon (TOC) below 5 ppb. In a wet chemical bench dedicated to oxide etching and pre-gate cleaning in 180nm DRAM fabrication, DI rinse water degradation below 18.0 MOhm-cm introduces mobile ionic contaminants (Na+, K+) and silica redeposition onto hydrophobic, hydrogen-terminated silicon, degrading gate oxide dielectric breakdown voltage (BV_ox).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: All wet-deck components exposed to fluorinated vapors must be solid virgin semiconductor-grade PTFE or PVDF; substituting lower-cost polypropylene or PVC for wet sink inserts or internal aspirators leads to rapid embrittlement and catastrophic stress-cracking under concentrated HF/BOE mixtures, creating uncontained acid spills and cleanroom downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Safety interlocks must mechanically or electronically hard-lock chemical dosing valves whenever exhaust differential pressure falls below 0.25 inches water column or whenever the DI resistivity drop below 17.5 MOhm-cm persists past 120 seconds. Protocol signoff must strictly gate wafer release for all subsequent RCA-1, RCA-2, and BOE etching steps.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Face velocity boundary layer collapse (< 80 FPM) due to cleanroom laminar downflow mismatch or sash turbulence, venting HF and HNO3 vapor into operator breathing zone
1. DI water loop stagnation and organic/ionic leeching causing resistivity collapse (< 15 MOhm-cm), irreversibly contaminating active DRAM silicon surfaces with metal cations
1. Differential pressure sensor failure or scrubber duct damper binding leading to unmonitored exhaust starvation and ambient acid gas accumulation

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-01` | **Wet Bench Face Velocity Uniformity & Plume Containment Test** | Calibrated hot-wire anemometer (TSI VelociCalc 9565 or equivalent, accuracy +/- 3% of reading), theatrical glycol-free smoke generator / titanium tetrachloride vapor tracer tube | 1. Establish a 3x4 measurement grid across the sash plane opening, with grid points spaced <= 6 inches apart and >= 3 inches from edges. 2. Position the hot-wire anemometer probe orthogonally to airflow at each grid node and log average velocity over 20 seconds. 3. Calculate mean face velocity and relative standard deviation (uniformity). 4. Release visible neutral-buoyancy smoke along the bench lip, sash perimeter, and rear baffle slots at a release rate of 10-20 cm/s. 5. Observe smoke flow trajectory across full sash width for 60 seconds and inspect for vortex roll-out or outward plume escape. | `Mean face velocity must be between 100.0 FPM and 115.0 FPM (0.51 to 0.58 m/s). Point-to-point uniformity relative standard deviation (RSD) must be <= 10.0%. Visual smoke containment test must show 100% laminar capture into rear slots with 0% escape/rollback into the operator zone under static sash conditions.` |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-02` | **Ultrapure DI Water Resistivity and Point-of-Use Delivery Verification** | Temperature-compensated inline resistivity monitor (Thornton M800 with 0.01 cm^-1 cell constant sensor, calibrated against NIST standards), portable reference resistivity meter with flow-through PFA cell | 1. Open the DI water point-of-use (POU) spray gun and overflow bath delivery valves at 5.0 L/min flow rate for 10 minutes to flush stagnant volume. 2. Divert effluent to the reference inline PFA flow cell without air entrainment. 3. Record instantaneous resistivity and temperature-corrected (25 deg C) values continuously for 15 minutes at 1 Hz logging. 4. Verify cross-calibration agreement between bench inline monitor and reference sensor. 5. Perform a simulated flow shut-off/turn-on step to measure resistivity recovery time to baseline. | `Temperature-compensated resistivity must measure >= 18.15 MOhm-cm at 25.0 deg C continuously across the 15-minute log. Discrepancy between inline monitor and reference sensor must be <= 0.05 MOhm-cm. Post-flow recovery to >= 18.0 MOhm-cm must occur within <= 30 seconds of flow initiation.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl/neoprene laminate apron (minimum 20 mil), Viton or heavy butyl acid gauntlet gloves over double nitrile inner gloves, ANSI Z87.1 full-face polycarbonate splash shield combined with chemical splash goggles, Closed-toe chemical-resistant footwear with vinyl/neoprene safety shoe covers
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of dermal HF exposure: Immediately rinse under emergency deluge shower for exactly 2 minutes while removing all contaminated clothing; immediately massage Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%) into the affected skin with gloved hands, reapplying every 15 minutes until medical emergency response arrives. For ocular exposure: Flush with sterile isotonic saline or DI eye-wash for 15 minutes continuously; apply 1% sterile calcium gluconate eye solution if administered by trained medical personnel. For inhalation of acid vapors: Relocate victim immediately to fresh air, administer 100% medical oxygen via non-rebreather mask, and arrange immediate transfer to acute intensive care unit for pulmonary edema monitoring.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous negative-pressure acid scrubbed exhaust system ducting made of FM-approved polypropylene or FRP. Minimum duct static pressure: -0.40 in. w.g. Interlocked low-flow alarm audible/visible beacon triggers if exhaust duct differential drops below 0.20 in. w.g., automatically terminating chemical dispense pumps and locking automated carrier lifters.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated drainage: Corrosive mineral acids (HF, HCl, HNO3) routed via double-contained PVDF lines directly to the dedicated fluoride/acid waste neutralization (AWN) system. Neutralize with automated stoichiometric injection of calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate calcium fluoride (CaF2 sludge, Ksp=3.9e-11) followed by pH stabilization between 6.5 and 8.5 before tertiary treatment discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI | `49 wt% (aqueous) and 10:1 BOE (Buffer Oxide Etch)` |
| **Nitric Acid** | `7697-37-2` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI | `69-70 wt%` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid** | `7647-01-0` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI | `37 wt%` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Grade 4 / VLSI | `28-30 wt% NH3` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic wet-chemical cleaned or bare silicon substrate post-furnace oxidation; pre-cleared of macro particulates (<= 5 particles @ > 0.2 um per 150mm wafer).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrogen-passivated (Si-H hydrophobic, contact angle > 70 deg) post-BOE dip or chemically oxidized hydrophilic (Si-OH, contact angle < 10 deg) post-SC1/SC2 clean, dried in spin-rinse dryer to 0 residual water marks.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excess ambient air exposure beyond 30 minutes induces uncontrolled native oxide regrowth (> 0.5 nm) and airborne molecular contamination (boron/phosphorus/hydrocarbon sorption), causing DRAM gate oxide breakdown shifts and threshold voltage (Vth) instability in 180nm access transistors.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical, hydrodynamic, and chemical certification of the acid wet processing bench, confirming uniform containment of corrosive vapor at 100-115 FPM face velocity, zero fume leakage under neutral-buoyancy smoke test, and point-of-use DI water quality of >= 18.15 MOhm-cm at 25.0 deg C.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-01_Velocity_Grid_Containment_Report.csv`
- [ ] `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-02_POU_DI_Resistivity_Continuous_Log.pdf`
- [ ] `Wet_Bench_Hood_Certification_EHS_Signoff_Certificate.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean hood face velocity at 18-inch sash opening** | `105.0 FPM` | +/- 5.0 FPM | Multi-point calibrated hot-wire anemometer grid integration (12-node spatial average) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Point-of-use DI water resistivity at 25 deg C** | `18.18 MOhm-cm` | +0.02 / -0.03 MOhm-cm | Inline Thornton 4-electrode conductivity/resistivity sensor cross-validated against NIST-traceable calibrated transfer meter |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Face velocity spatial distribution uniformity RSD** | `6.5 %` | <= 10.0 % | Standard deviation of 12-point velocity readings divided by mean face velocity |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Unambiguous researcher exit condition requires that 100% of grid velocity points satisfy the 100-120 FPM envelope, visual smoke containment shows zero rollback at nominal sash height, DI resistivity stays strictly >= 18.15 MOhm-cm for 15 continuous minutes under active flow, and the chemical safety low-exhaust interlock triggers automatic acid dispense cutoff within <= 1.0 second of induced airflow loss.

testcases.title: Wet Bench Face Velocity Uniformity & Plume Containment Test
testcases.instrumentation: Calibrated hot-wire anemometer (TSI VelociCalc 9565 or equivalent, accuracy +/- 3% of reading), theatrical glycol-free smoke generator / titanium tetrachloride vapor tracer tube
testcases.pre_conditions: Acid wet bench exhaust blower operational; cleanroom ceiling HEPA/ULPA downflow balanced to nominal 0.45 m/s (+/- 0.05 m/s); sash opening locked at calibrated working height of 18.0 inches (457 mm); exhaust static pressure within 0.35 - 0.50 in. w.g.
testcases.procedure: 1. Establish a 3x4 measurement grid across the sash plane opening, with grid points spaced <= 6 inches apart and >= 3 inches from edges. 2. Position the hot-wire anemometer probe orthogonally to airflow at each grid node and log average velocity over 20 seconds. 3. Calculate mean face velocity and relative standard deviation (uniformity). 4. Release visible neutral-buoyancy smoke along the bench lip, sash perimeter, and rear baffle slots at a release rate of 10-20 cm/s. 5. Observe smoke flow trajectory across full sash width for 60 seconds and inspect for vortex roll-out or outward plume escape.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean face velocity must be between 100.0 FPM and 115.0 FPM (0.51 to 0.58 m/s). Point-to-point uniformity relative standard deviation (RSD) must be <= 10.0%. Visual smoke containment test must show 100% laminar capture into rear slots with 0% escape/rollback into the operator zone under static sash conditions.

testcases.title: Ultrapure DI Water Resistivity and Point-of-Use Delivery Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Temperature-compensated inline resistivity monitor (Thornton M800 with 0.01 cm^-1 cell constant sensor, calibrated against NIST standards), portable reference resistivity meter with flow-through PFA cell
testcases.pre_conditions: Central UPW supply loop continuously circulating for >= 24 hours; wet bench quick-dump rinser (QDR) and continuous overflow baths plumbed with virgin PFA tubing; temperature sensor calibrated to 25.0 +/- 0.1 deg C.
testcases.procedure: 1. Open the DI water point-of-use (POU) spray gun and overflow bath delivery valves at 5.0 L/min flow rate for 10 minutes to flush stagnant volume. 2. Divert effluent to the reference inline PFA flow cell without air entrainment. 3. Record instantaneous resistivity and temperature-corrected (25 deg C) values continuously for 15 minutes at 1 Hz logging. 4. Verify cross-calibration agreement between bench inline monitor and reference sensor. 5. Perform a simulated flow shut-off/turn-on step to measure resistivity recovery time to baseline.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Temperature-compensated resistivity must measure >= 18.15 MOhm-cm at 25.0 deg C continuously across the 15-minute log. Discrepancy between inline monitor and reference sensor must be <= 0.05 MOhm-cm. Post-flow recovery to >= 18.0 MOhm-cm must occur within <= 30 seconds of flow initiation.

ppe_required: Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl/neoprene laminate apron (minimum 20 mil)
Viton or heavy butyl acid gauntlet gloves over double nitrile inner gloves
ANSI Z87.1 full-face polycarbonate splash shield combined with chemical splash goggles
Closed-toe chemical-resistant footwear with vinyl/neoprene safety shoe covers
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: In case of dermal HF exposure: Immediately rinse under emergency deluge shower for exactly 2 minutes while removing all contaminated clothing; immediately massage Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%) into the affected skin with gloved hands, reapplying every 15 minutes until medical emergency response arrives. For ocular exposure: Flush with sterile isotonic saline or DI eye-wash for 15 minutes continuously; apply 1% sterile calcium gluconate eye solution if administered by trained medical personnel. For inhalation of acid vapors: Relocate victim immediately to fresh air, administer 100% medical oxygen via non-rebreather mask, and arrange immediate transfer to acute intensive care unit for pulmonary edema monitoring.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Continuous negative-pressure acid scrubbed exhaust system ducting made of FM-approved polypropylene or FRP. Minimum duct static pressure: -0.40 in. w.g. Interlocked low-flow alarm audible/visible beacon triggers if exhaust duct differential drops below 0.20 in. w.g., automatically terminating chemical dispense pumps and locking automated carrier lifters.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Segregated drainage: Corrosive mineral acids (HF, HCl, HNO3) routed via double-contained PVDF lines directly to the dedicated fluoride/acid waste neutralization (AWN) system. Neutralize with automated stoichiometric injection of calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate calcium fluoride (CaF2 sludge, Ksp=3.9e-11) followed by pH stabilization between 6.5 and 8.5 before tertiary treatment discharge.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Hydrophilic wet-chemical cleaned or bare silicon substrate post-furnace oxidation; pre-cleared of macro particulates (<= 5 particles @ > 0.2 um per 150mm wafer).
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Hydrogen-passivated (Si-H hydrophobic, contact angle > 70 deg) post-BOE dip or chemically oxidized hydrophilic (Si-OH, contact angle < 10 deg) post-SC1/SC2 clean, dried in spin-rinse dryer to 0 residual water marks.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excess ambient air exposure beyond 30 minutes induces uncontrolled native oxide regrowth (> 0.5 nm) and airborne molecular contamination (boron/phosphorus/hydrocarbon sorption), causing DRAM gate oxide breakdown shifts and threshold voltage (Vth) instability in 180nm access transistors.

expected_result.summary: Full physical, hydrodynamic, and chemical certification of the acid wet processing bench, confirming uniform containment of corrosive vapor at 100-115 FPM face velocity, zero fume leakage under neutral-buoyancy smoke test, and point-of-use DI water quality of >= 18.15 MOhm-cm at 25.0 deg C.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Mean hood face velocity at 18-inch sash opening
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-point calibrated hot-wire anemometer grid integration (12-node spatial average)

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Point-of-use DI water resistivity at 25 deg C
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Inline Thornton 4-electrode conductivity/resistivity sensor cross-validated against NIST-traceable calibrated transfer meter

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Face velocity spatial distribution uniformity RSD
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Standard deviation of 12-point velocity readings divided by mean face velocity

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Unambiguous researcher exit condition requires that 100% of grid velocity points satisfy the 100-120 FPM envelope, visual smoke containment shows zero rollback at nominal sash height, DI resistivity stays strictly >= 18.15 MOhm-cm for 15 continuous minutes under active flow, and the chemical safety low-exhaust interlock triggers automatic acid dispense cutoff within <= 1.0 second of induced airflow loss.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Fume Hood Face Velocity Profile & VAV Aerodynamic Tuning

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup [Chemical Processing] > Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification [Metrology] > Fume Hood Face Velocity Profile & VAV Aerodynamic Tuning [Metrology]
**Target Generation**: Gen 1 (mm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: DI Water: 18.2 MΩ·cm, Particle Count < 5 / wafer.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using 4-Point Probe / Ellipsometer / Fume Hood Interlock.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The Variable Air Volume (VAV) fast-acting venturi damper loop must demonstrate a response settling time under 1.5 seconds during rapid sash movements without overshoot oscillations. Unstable PID tuning on the static differential pressure transducer causes pressure pulses that propagate into the wet bench plenum, disturbing chemical bath thermal stabilities and inducing laminar boundary layer separation across wafer carriers.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating average face velocity to 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) is insufficient if spatial standard deviation is high. Recirculation vortex shedding behind the sash handle and dead zones along the rear lower baffle can trap concentrated acid vapors (HF/HCl/HNO3). An ASHRAE 110 traverse grid across 12 to 16 equal areas with tracer gas/smoke visualization is critical to prove zero escape under cross-draft velocities of 30 FPM.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Fast-response closed-loop VAV actuators (e.g., Phoenix Controls or TSI venturi valves) and high-accuracy thermal anemometers have extended lead times in Southeast Asia. For an open-source Gen 1 deployment in Vietnam, relying on custom calibrated differential pressure diaphragms with industrial Modbus actuators requires precise local aerodynamic calibration jigs to avoid catastrophic flow sensor drift.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Face velocity and containment qualification must be formally closed out before any aggressive wet etching or RCA cleans commence. Operating wet baths under uncertified exhaust introduces severe chemical containment liabilities, halts tool acceptance milestones, and risks cleanroom shutdown under local environmental health and safety audits.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. VAV control hunting causing positive pressure surges at the sash opening, exhausting concentrated acid vapors into the researcher breathing zone.
1. Dead-zone vortex formation behind the lower airfoil sill trapping dense HF fumes and causing localized corrosion of mechanical interlocks.
1. Laminar flow disruption causing cross-draft boundary layer strip-off when operators move rapidly past the sash opening.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-1-01` | **ASHRAE 110 Multi-Point Face Velocity Profile & Uniformity Grid** | TSI VelociCalc 9565 Multi-Function Ventilation Meter with NIST-calibrated hot-wire thermal anemometer probe and fixed positioning tripod. | 1. Divide sash opening into a symmetrical 3x4 grid (12 test zones) with measurement points at center of each grid area. 2. Mount thermal anemometer probe perpendicularly to face plane. 3. Record 20-second velocity time-average at each grid point. 4. Calculate overall mean face velocity and percentage deviation across all 12 zones. | `Mean face velocity across all points must be 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) +/- 10% (90 to 110 FPM / 0.46 to 0.56 m/s). No single point measurement may deviate by more than +/- 20% from the grid mean.` |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-1-02` | **VAV Dynamic Sash Travel Response & Pressure Recovery Rate** | Dwyer Magnesense II Differential Pressure Transmitter, digital data logger at 50 Hz sampling rate, calibrated hot-wire anemometer at center-face. | 1. Manually open sash from 18 inches to full 36 inches height at a minimum rate of 0.5 m/s. 2. Record dynamic face velocity and exhaust plenum pressure until stabilization. 3. Swiftly pull sash down to 6-inch standby height at 0.5 m/s and record recovery curve. | `VAV system must restore face velocity to within 90-110 FPM within <= 2.0 seconds after sash motion ceases. Zero sustained oscillatory hunting (settling damping ratio zeta >= 0.7) and duct static pressure must remain negative throughout.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavyweight fluoroelastomer/butyl rubber acid-resistant gloves (ASTM F739), Full-face polycarbonate splash shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1, PTFE-laminated chemical apron with sleeve guards, Steel-toe chemical-resistant boots with secondary splash gaiters, Emergency calcium gluconate gel holster
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For HF exposure: Immediately rinse with Copious DI water for 2 minutes, then massage 2.5% calcium gluconate gel into exposed skin continuously until medical assistance arrives. For vapor inhalation: Move victim immediately to fresh air, administer 100% medical oxygen, and seek emergency pulmonary evaluation. Flush eyes for minimum 15 minutes at dedicated safety eyewash station.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated dedicated FRP/PVDF-lined wet scrubber acid exhaust with continuous negative static pressure (-300 to -450 Pa). N+1 redundant roof exhaust blowers on emergency UPS backup. Integrated acoustic and optical low-flow alarms.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: All acid sump overflows route through fluoropolymer double-contained piping to an automated dual-stage acid-waste neutralization (AWN) system utilizing 20% NaOH dosing with calibrated pH control (discharge target: pH 6.5 to 8.5).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid** | `7664-39-3` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI C7-0301) | `49 wt% in H2O` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid** | `7647-01-0` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C28-0301) | `37 wt% in H2O` |
| **Sulfuric Acid** | `7664-93-9` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C44-0308) | `96 wt% in H2O` |
| **Nitric Acid** | `7697-37-2` | Electronic Grade (SEMI C35-0301) | `70 wt% in H2O` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-received native silicon wafers or post-HF dipped wafers with hydrophobic hydrogen-terminated Si-H surface (contact angle > 70 deg).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Chemically cleaned, pristine RCA-1/RCA-2 oxide passivated silicon wafer ready for quartz tube gate oxidation or diffusion furnace staging.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to cleanroom ambient air results in uncontrolled native chemical oxide regrowth (SiO2 > 0.6 nm), airborne molecular organic contamination (VOCs), and mobile ionic sodium deposition, degrading gate oxide breakdown voltage.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Fume hood face velocity profile and VAV aerodynamic calibration successfully validated across 12-point ASHRAE 110 grid, demonstrating uniform 100 FPM laminar capture and < 2.0 s dynamic sash response under negative plenum pressure.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `FUME_HOOD_VAV_FACE_VELOCITY_CALIBRATION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `ASHRAE110_12POINT_VELOCITY_GRID_RAW_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `VAV_DYNAMIC_STEP_RESPONSE_TRANSIENT_LOG.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Average 12-point face velocity at 18-inch operating sash height** | `100 FPM (0.51 m/s)` | +/- 10 FPM (+/- 0.05 m/s) | Multi-point thermal anemometer time-average traverse per ASHRAE 110-2016 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum spatial velocity deviation across any individual grid cell** | `<= 15.0%` | +/- 5.0% maximum allowable upper bound | Normalized spatial standard deviation calculation across grid data points |
| `ASSERT-03` | **VAV recovery time back to target velocity following rapid full sash stroke** | `1.50 s` | + 0.50 s maximum | High-speed 50 Hz pressure transducer and hot-wire transient data logging |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 12 face velocity traverse points must read between 90 and 110 FPM, dynamic sash recovery verified under 2.0 seconds with zero positive pressure puff back during smoke containment testing, and sign-off approved by Lead Metrology and EHS Safety Officers.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Thermal Anemometer Traverse Grid Setup & Multi-Point Baseline Profiling

**Node Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Parent Chain:** Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup → Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification → Fume Hood Face Velocity Profile & VAV Aerodynamic Tuning  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Classification:** Metrology / Facility Aerodynamics & Containment  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│           Traverse Grid Fixture Installation           │
│                                                        │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│       Thermal Anemometer Insertion & Zero-Offset       │
│                                                        │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│         Multi-Point Face Velocity Profiling            │
│                                                        │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                        │
│       VAV Dynamic Response & Profile Acceptance        │
│                                                        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Sash Height and Plane Definition**:
   - Set the acid exhaust fume hood sash to its standard certified working aperture height.
   - Secure a non-intrusive traverse grid frame across the sash opening plane, dividing the entrance cross-section into equal rectangular grid cells (maximum grid point spacing $\le 300\text{ mm}$ center-to-center).

2. **Thermal Anemometer Fixturing & Directional Alignment**:
   - Mount the calibrated thermal anemometer probe on the mechanical traverse rig at normal incidence ($90^\circ \pm 2^\circ$) perpendicular to the sash face plane.
   - Confirm zero-velocity shield caps are seated during initial electronic thermal baseline compensation and zero-point calibration.

3. **Multi-Point Grid Traverse & Dwell Measurement**:
   - Position the thermal anemometer sensor at the geometric center of each traverse cell.
   - Maintain a minimum dwell time of 15 seconds per grid point to allow the heated sensor bead to reach thermal equilibrium with the incoming laminar air velocity.
   - Record the time-averaged face velocity at each point across the top, middle, and bottom horizontal planes.

4. **Dynamic Aerodynamic Profile & Turbulence Mapping**:
   - Traverse the thermal sensor across all perimeter and central nodes to compute velocity uniformity:
     $$\text{Uniformity} = \frac{V_{\text{max}} - V_{\text{min}}}{2 \times V_{\text{avg}}} \times 100\%$$
   - Check lower sash boundary and aerofoil sill zones for back-draft eddies or dead zones.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric / Tolerance | Physical Units | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Grid Traverse Spacing** | $\le 300$ | $\text{mm}$ | Calibrated precision traverse rail scale |
| **Average Face Velocity ($V_{\text{avg}}$)** | $0.50 \pm 0.05$ ($100 \pm 10$) | $\text{m/s}$ ($\text{fpm}$) | Multi-point time-averaged thermal anemometry |
| **Velocity Uniformity Spread** | $\le \pm 15\%$ of mean across grid points | $\%$ | Multi-point grid calculation |
| **Sensor Measurement Dwell Time** | $\ge 15.0$ | $\text{s}$ | Automated data logger acquisition timer |

---

### 4. Relevant Literature Citations

- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
  - Informs the critical multi-point profiling methodology, sensor dwell stabilization, and spatial boundary uniformity targets across dimensioned zones (counteracting convective end-losses and ensuring cross-sectional profile fidelity within dimensional bounds $\le 300\text{ mm}$).
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering** & **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Contextualizes contamination containment standards for cleanroom acid wet benches used during 180nm capacitor dielectric cleaning/etching (ONO, $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$), where face velocity stability prevents toxic vapor back-diffusion and particulate deposition onto active bitline/transistor surfaces.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Station exhaust and DI water loop (18.2 MOhm-cm, particle filter 0.1 um) must interlock prior to wafer boat immersion. Rinse cascade must terminate downstream acid carries before SC-2.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: BOE 6:1 (NH4F:HF) etch rate must be calibrated at 70-80 nm/min at 25°C. SC-1 (5:1:1 H2O:NH4OH:H2O2) must be maintained at 75°C +/- 2°C to eliminate light organics without pitting Si.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Electronic-grade semiconductor reagents (VLSI/MOS grade) must be procured from certified chemical distributors; technical-grade chemicals will induce metallic surface poisoning (Fe, Cu, Ni > 1e10 atoms/cm2).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 24-32 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Chemical cross-contamination or incomplete dump rinse leaves watermark defects and micro-masking during subsequent etch).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Watermark defect formation during static pull-out from hydrophilic-to-hydrophobic transition.
1. Exhaust face-velocity drop below 0.5 m/s causing acid vapor condensation on cleanroom tooling.
1. Over-etch in BOE undercut exceeding 50 nm, destroying contact via dimensional margins.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-1-1-01` | **Post-Clean Particle & Metallic Trace Contamination Assay** | Darkfield Laser Surface Particle Scanner (KLA-Tencor / Surfscan) & TXRF Spectrometer | 1. Load unpatterned witness silicon wafer into darkfield laser scatterometer. 2. Scan complete surface for light point defects (LPD) at size bin >= 180 nm. 3. Perform Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) for trace Fe, Cu, Ni surface concentrations. | `LPD count (>= 180 nm) < 10 defects/wafer (Pass); Transition metals (Fe, Ni, Cu) < 5e10 atoms/cm2 (Pass).` |

- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: MANDATORY ON-SITE ANTIDOTE: Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%). In case of HF skin contact: Flush immediately under emergency drench shower for 2-3 minutes, then vigorously massage Calcium Gluconate Gel into affected skin continuously until emergency medical response arrives. Never apply standard burn creams.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated polypropylene wet bench with vertical laminar exhaust face velocity >= 0.55 m/s. Interlocked with wet acid scrubber.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic with native chemical oxide (Tox ~1.0 nm) and organic particulates.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

**Title:** VAV Damper Actuator PID Tuning & Aerodynamic Baffle Real-Time Calibration  
**Hierarchy Level:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification > Fume Hood Face Velocity Profile & VAV Aerodynamic Tuning > VAV Damper Actuator PID Tuning & Aerodynamic Baffle Real-Time Calibration  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make  

---

### Process Workflow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Baffle Slit       │
│      Calibration       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Actuator Step      │
│        Response        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Triple Loop PID     │
│         Tuning         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Face Velocity      │
│  Profile Verification  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Calibration & Physical Alignment Setup**
   - Inspect PTFE bench containment enclosure and verify the rear aerodynamic exhaust baffles are unblocked.
   - Set top and bottom aerodynamic baffle slit apertures symmetrically across the full 300 mm lateral zone to distribute cross-draft resistance evenly.
   - Power on the VAV motorized damper actuator control module and establish communication with the digital control interface.

2. **Step-Response Excitation & Actuator Velocity Limiting**
   - Introduce a step change command across the damper travel range (0% to 100% stroke).
   - Ensure the actuator ramp rate is mechanically clamped to prevent abrupt draft surges or structural strain, maintaining smooth mechanical actuation (< 50 mm/minute equivalent drive rate).
   - Record open-loop dead time ($\tau_d$) and time constant ($\tau$) from differential pressure and velocity feedback transmitters.

3. **Digital Triple-Loop PID Tuning with Feedforward Decoupling**
   - Configure a triple-loop digital PID algorithm incorporating feedforward decoupling:
     - **Proportional Gain ($K_p$):** Increment until rapid displacement response is reached without deadband hunting.
     - **Integral Time ($T_i$):** Tune to eliminate residual steady-state draft offset under continuous carrier exhaust conditions.
     - **Derivative Time ($T_d$):** Adjust to suppress transient overshoot and damp pressure fluctuations.
   - Verify decoupling across multi-zone exhaust pickup points to isolate turbulence caused by varying laboratory static pressures.

4. **Real-Time Aerodynamic Baffle Optimization & Dynamic Verification**
   - Adjust the aerodynamic baffle slit positioning dynamically while simulating exhaust thermal loads (such as hot acid baths at 160°C).
   - Modulate carrier gas flow rates from 1 to 5 SLPM into the bench exhaust plenum to ensure laminar air entrainment across the sash boundary.
   - Validate that transient damper corrections maintain stable containment without causing crystallographic disturbance or particle back-streaming into the bench work area.

---

### Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
               Process Control Target Acceptance
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
H3PO4 Etch Temp┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
               │█                                      │
Thermal Uniform┤█                                      │
  Gas Flow Ctrl┤▒▒                                     │
               │▒▒                                     │
Step Travel Spd┤█████████████                          │
               │█████████████                          │
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
                0        40       80        120     160 
```

1. **Actuator Linear Motion Limit:** Travel/ramp speed must not exceed **50 mm/minute** (`< 50 mm/minute`) to prevent mechanical shock and aerodynamic pressure spikes.
2. **Carrier Gas Dynamics Regulation:** Damper control loop must dynamically stabilize carrier flow disturbances spanning **1 to 5 SLPM**.
3. **Thermal Environment Uniformity:** Steady-state regulation must support tight thermal isolation within **±0.5°C** across a **300 mm** operational flat zone.
4. **Thermal Exhaust Containment Compatibility:** The calibrated VAV extraction must safely handle continuous acid vapor generation at **160°C** (phosphoric acid $H_3PO_4$ 85% processing condition).

---

### Verified Context Citations

- **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation**:
  - *PID Control:* Triple-loop digital PID controller with feedforward decoupling.
  - *Actuator Motion & Shock Prevention:* Mechanical drive speed regulated to `< 50 mm/minute` to avoid mechanical dislocations and shock.
  - *Temperature Uniformity & Span:* Uniformity within `±0.5°C` over a `300 mm` zone.
  - *Gas Flow Dynamics:* Carrier gas flows regulated between `1 to 5 SLPM`.
- **Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD) of Silicon Nitride Hard Masks**:
  - *Acid Wet Chemistry Exhaust Conditions:* Selective wet chemical etching of nitride masks in hot phosphoric acid (`H3PO4 85% at 160°C`), setting the thermal acid vapor loading requirement.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The fast response requirement of the VAV venturi damper actuator (target <1.5 s full stroke) creates a strong aerodynamic-structural coupling with the duct static pressure control loop. If actuator velocity feedback or derivative gain (Kd) is over-tuned, duct flutter and acoustic resonance (>78 dBA) induce mechanical vibrations into the PTFE wet bench deck, violating the 30 Hz isolation threshold of the adjacent wafer transport and precision linear stages. A feedforward loop coupled with sash position linear potentiometer sensing must be implemented rather than relying solely on thermal anemometer feedback.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating the aerodynamic bypass and lower airfoil baffles is critical during acid etch baths (BOE/HF and piranha). Stagnant boundary layers and eddy vortex recirculation zones form at the front sash lip if the bypass ratio drops below 25% during sash closure. Real-time baffle slot adjustments must equalize face velocity across the sash grid at 0.50 m/s (100 FPM) without generating high-velocity jet streams (>0.65 m/s) that cause micro-droplet spattering from heated quartz chemical tanks onto wafer boats.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Fast-acting fail-safe electronic actuators (Belimo or Siemens 24VAC/DC with 2-10V feedback) and Hastelloy C-276 or PTFE-coated damper blades have lead times exceeding 14-18 weeks in Vietnam. Sourcing must qualify domestic 316L stainless steel dampers coated with electrostatically applied fluoropolymer (ETFE/ECTFE) or industrial corrosion-resistant stepper-driven venturi valves as verified regional equivalents to prevent line stoppage.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Balancing and calibrating aerodynamic baffles requires coordinating HVAC facilities, cleanroom certification contractors, and wet processing wet-bench installation teams. If the differential pressure transmitter drift calibration or PID auto-tune cycle extends past the 48-hour facility shutdown window, downstream RCA cleaning and wet oxidation lot scheduling will slip, compounding queue-time risks across Gen 1 wafer batches.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Actuator hunting/limit cycling causing continuous sash face velocity oscillations (±0.15 m/s), leading to intermittent toxic acid vapor escape into the operator breathing zone.
1. Dead-band saturation or damper stall during rapid sash opening, resulting in face velocity drop below 0.30 m/s (60 FPM) for >3 seconds, triggering immediate cleanroom evacuation alarms.
1. Improper lower baffle slot geometry creating a high-velocity boundary layer detachment that induces turbulent eddy currents inside the chemical sump, entraining concentrated HF/HCl fumes toward the front sill.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-1-2-01` | **Dynamic VAV Damper Response Time & Face Velocity Recovery Test** | Multi-channel hot-wire anemometer grid (TSI 8455, 0.01 m/s resolution), differential pressure transducer (Dwyer Magnesense MSX, range ±250 Pa), high-speed data logger recording at 50 Hz. | 1. Position anemometer sensors at 9 grid points across the sash opening plane according to EN 14175-3 / ASHRAE 110. 2. Record steady-state face velocity baseline for 60 seconds. 3. Rapidly raise the sash from 450 mm to full open (750 mm) at a velocity of ~0.5 m/s. 4. Measure the transient face velocity dip, actuator response latency, and time required to stabilize within ±10% of 0.50 m/s setpoint. 5. Rapidly lower the sash from 750 mm to minimum stop (150 mm) and log transient duct static pressure spike and damper overshoot. | `Face velocity must recover to 0.50 m/s ± 0.05 m/s within <= 1.5 seconds following sash movement completion; minimum transient velocity must not fall below 0.40 m/s (80 FPM); steady-state overshoot must not exceed 10% (<= 0.55 m/s); zero hunting observed after 3 seconds.` |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-1-2-02` | **Aerodynamic Baffle Face Velocity Uniformity & Containment Visualization** | Calibrated thermal anemometer (TSI VelociCalc 9565), theatrical glycol/deionized water smoke generator, precision millimeter vernier depth gauge for baffle slot measurement. | 1. Adjust upper, middle, and lower PTFE baffle slots to nominal positions (top: 15 mm, middle: 10 mm, bottom: 25 mm). 2. Execute a 12-point velocity traverse across the sash plane, taking 30-second time-averaged readings per node. 3. Calculate spatial velocity non-uniformity (coefficient of variation, CV). 4. Release neutral-buoyancy DI water/glycol smoke along the worktop sill, side walls, and internal rear baffle slots. 5. Inspect for reverse flows, dead pockets, or spillout vortices using high-intensity directional LED lighting. | `Mean face velocity across all 12 points must measure 0.50 m/s ± 0.05 m/s; spatial coefficient of variation (CV = std dev / mean) must be <= 10.0%; smoke challenge must show smooth laminar draw into lower and upper baffle slots with zero vortex roll-out or reverse flow past the sash threshold plane.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Full-face chemical splash shield compliant with ANSI Z87.1, Heavyweight fluoroelastomer/butyl acid-resistant gloves (minimum 15 mil) over nitrile examination gloves, PTFE/Tychem chemical protective apron with chemical-resistant sleeves, Steel-toe neoprene safety boots with acid-resistant outsoles, Personal portable acid gas badge/monitor configured for HF and HCl detection
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) skin exposure: Immediately flush affected area with copious clean water for exactly 2 minutes; immediately massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate topical gel into the skin wearing fresh nitrile gloves until pain ceases; seek immediate medical emergency care. For inhalation of acid vapors: Relocate victim immediately to fresh air; administer 100% humidified oxygen via mask; nebulized 2.5% calcium gluconate solution inhalation must be administered by certified medical personnel. Provide safety shower and eye wash station activation within 10 seconds of uninhibited travel distance.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated continuous negative pressure acid exhaust ductwork constructed from welded polypropylene (PP) or PVDF; minimum duct capture transport velocity of 10.0 to 12.5 m/s (2000-2500 FPM) to avoid condensation; redundant exhaust blowers connected to emergency uninterruptible power supply (UPS) with automatic failover in <1.0 second; wet scrubbers dosing NaOH solution to maintain exhaust neutral pH prior to atmospheric discharge.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Exhaust condensate and wet bench chemical overflows route directly to dedicated Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) system. Neutralization utilizes automated dosing of 20% sodium hydroxide (NaOH, CAS 1310-73-2) or calcium hydroxide slurry (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate fluoride ions as calcium fluoride (CaF2) sludge, adjusting effluent discharge pH strictly between 6.5 and 8.5.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (BOE etchant constituent)** | `7664-39-3` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI C7 / VLSI) | `49 wt% aqueous solution` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid (RCA-2 constituent)** | `7647-01-0` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI C8 / VLSI) | `37 wt% aqueous solution` |
| **Sulfuric Acid (Piranha etch constituent)** | `7664-93-9` | Semiconductor Grade (SEMI C1 / VLSI) | `96 wt% aqueous solution` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, dry bare silicon substrate or thermal oxide test wafers stored in sealed fluoroware cassettes following DI water rinse and spin-rinse drying.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fluoride-passivated hydrophobic silicon surface (Si-H terminated, water contact angle >70°) or clean oxide ready for immediate photolithography dehydration bake and HMDS priming.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive queue time exposure to uncontrolled ambient cleanroom air promotes airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption, native chemical oxide regrowth (SiO2 >1.5 Å), and surface airborne amine contamination causing photoresist adhesion failure and pattern collapse during subsequent 180nm lithography.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full dynamic commissioning, PID tuning, and aerodynamic baffle calibration of the PTFE wet bench VAV system to ensure robust acid containment, rapid transient face velocity stabilization, and zero vortex spattering across all sash operating heights.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `VAV_Damper_PID_StepResponse_TransientLog.csv`
- [ ] `ASHRAE110_Baffle_VelocityProfile_Certification.pdf`
- [ ] `Aerodynamic_SmokeFlow_SmokeVisualization_Record.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Steady-state sash face velocity average across 12 traverse grid points at nominal 450 mm sash opening** | `0.50 m/s` | ± 0.05 m/s | Multi-point hot-wire anemometer traverse per ASHRAE 110-2016 standard protocols. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **VAV damper actuator dynamic closed-loop response and face velocity recovery time during full sash transition (450 mm to 750 mm)** | `1.20 s` | <= 1.50 s max | High-speed 50 Hz digital logging of analog sash potentiometer versus calibrated duct DP sensor and face velocity. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Face velocity spatial coefficient of variation (CV) across the containment sash plane** | `7.5 %` | <= 10.0 % max | Statistical standard deviation divided by mean of 12-point anemometer grid sampling. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful completion of ASHRAE 110 containment protocol with 0.00 ppm tracer gas leak in operator breathing zone, verified face velocity recovery under 1.5 seconds without damper hunting, and formal joint signoff by Facilities EHS Officer and Lead Wet Process Engineer.

testcases.instrumentation: Multi-channel hot-wire anemometer grid (TSI 8455, 0.01 m/s resolution), differential pressure transducer (Dwyer Magnesense MSX, range ±250 Pa), high-speed data logger recording at 50 Hz.
testcases.pre_conditions: PTFE acid wet bench connected to active scrubber exhaust; cleanroom ambient pressure maintained at +15 Pa relative to plenum; sash parked at operational working height of 450 mm; PID loop running in normal mode.
testcases.procedure:
1. Position anemometer sensors at 9 grid points across the sash opening plane according to EN 14175-3 / ASHRAE 110.
2. Record steady-state face velocity baseline for 60 seconds.
3. Rapidly raise the sash from 450 mm to full open (750 mm) at a velocity of ~0.5 m/s.
4. Measure the transient face velocity dip, actuator response latency, and time required to stabilize within ±10% of 0.50 m/s setpoint.
5. Rapidly lower the sash from 750 mm to minimum stop (150 mm) and log transient duct static pressure spike and damper overshoot.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Face velocity must recover to 0.50 m/s ± 0.05 m/s within <= 1.5 seconds following sash movement completion; minimum transient velocity must not fall below 0.40 m/s (80 FPM); steady-state overshoot must not exceed 10% (<= 0.55 m/s); zero hunting observed after 3 seconds.

testcases.title: Aerodynamic Baffle Face Velocity Uniformity & Containment Visualization
testcases.instrumentation: Calibrated thermal anemometer (TSI VelociCalc 9565), theatrical glycol/deionized water smoke generator, precision millimeter vernier depth gauge for baffle slot measurement.
testcases.pre_conditions: Fume hood exhaust volume adjusted to nominal design flow (850 CFM); sash fixed at standard 450 mm opening height; acid bath heaters energized to standby (room temperature).
testcases.procedure:
1. Adjust upper, middle, and lower PTFE baffle slots to nominal positions (top: 15 mm, middle: 10 mm, bottom: 25 mm).
2. Execute a 12-point velocity traverse across the sash plane, taking 30-second time-averaged readings per node.
3. Calculate spatial velocity non-uniformity (coefficient of variation, CV).
4. Release neutral-buoyancy DI water/glycol smoke along the worktop sill, side walls, and internal rear baffle slots.
5. Inspect for reverse flows, dead pockets, or spillout vortices using high-intensity directional LED lighting.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean face velocity across all 12 points must measure 0.50 m/s ± 0.05 m/s; spatial coefficient of variation (CV = std dev / mean) must be <= 10.0%; smoke challenge must show smooth laminar draw into lower and upper baffle slots with zero vortex roll-out or reverse flow past the sash threshold plane.

ppe_required: Full-face chemical splash shield compliant with ANSI Z87.1
Heavyweight fluoroelastomer/butyl acid-resistant gloves (minimum 15 mil) over nitrile examination gloves
PTFE/Tychem chemical protective apron with chemical-resistant sleeves
Steel-toe neoprene safety boots with acid-resistant outsoles
Personal portable acid gas badge/monitor configured for HF and HCl detection
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: For Hydrofluoric Acid (HF) skin exposure: Immediately flush affected area with copious clean water for exactly 2 minutes; immediately massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate topical gel into the skin wearing fresh nitrile gloves until pain ceases; seek immediate medical emergency care. For inhalation of acid vapors: Relocate victim immediately to fresh air; administer 100% humidified oxygen via mask; nebulized 2.5% calcium gluconate solution inhalation must be administered by certified medical personnel. Provide safety shower and eye wash station activation within 10 seconds of uninhibited travel distance.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Dedicated continuous negative pressure acid exhaust ductwork constructed from welded polypropylene (PP) or PVDF; minimum duct capture transport velocity of 10.0 to 12.5 m/s (2000-2500 FPM) to avoid condensation; redundant exhaust blowers connected to emergency uninterruptible power supply (UPS) with automatic failover in <1.0 second; wet scrubbers dosing NaOH solution to maintain exhaust neutral pH prior to atmospheric discharge.
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Exhaust condensate and wet bench chemical overflows route directly to dedicated Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) system. Neutralization utilizes automated dosing of 20% sodium hydroxide (NaOH, CAS 1310-73-2) or calcium hydroxide slurry (Ca(OH)2) to precipitate fluoride ions as calcium fluoride (CaF2) sludge, adjusting effluent discharge pH strictly between 6.5 and 8.5.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Pre-cleaned, dry bare silicon substrate or thermal oxide test wafers stored in sealed fluoroware cassettes following DI water rinse and spin-rinse drying.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Fluoride-passivated hydrophobic silicon surface (Si-H terminated, water contact angle >70°) or clean oxide ready for immediate photolithography dehydration bake and HMDS priming.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Excessive queue time exposure to uncontrolled ambient cleanroom air promotes airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption, native chemical oxide regrowth (SiO2 >1.5 Å), and surface airborne amine contamination causing photoresist adhesion failure and pattern collapse during subsequent 180nm lithography.

expected_result.summary: Full dynamic commissioning, PID tuning, and aerodynamic baffle calibration of the PTFE wet bench VAV system to ensure robust acid containment, rapid transient face velocity stabilization, and zero vortex spattering across all sash operating heights.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Steady-state sash face velocity average across 12 traverse grid points at nominal 450 mm sash opening
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Multi-point hot-wire anemometer traverse per ASHRAE 110-2016 standard protocols.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: VAV damper actuator dynamic closed-loop response and face velocity recovery time during full sash transition (450 mm to 750 mm)
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: High-speed 50 Hz digital logging of analog sash potentiometer versus calibrated duct DP sensor and face velocity.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Face velocity spatial coefficient of variation (CV) across the containment sash plane
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Statistical standard deviation divided by mean of 12-point anemometer grid sampling.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Successful completion of ASHRAE 110 containment protocol with 0.00 ppm tracer gas leak in operator breathing zone, verified face velocity recovery under 1.5 seconds without damper hunting, and formal joint signoff by Facilities EHS Officer and Lead Wet Process Engineer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-FUME-002`
**Title:** ASHRAE 110 Face Velocity Containment Verification & Dynamic Sash Metrology Certification  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Acid Exhaust Fume Hood & PTFE Bench Setup > Face Velocity Calibration, Acid Vapor Containment & DI Resistivity Certification > Fume Hood Face Velocity Profile & VAV Aerodynamic Tuning  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)  
**Action Type:** Buy (Procurement & Certification Protocol)  
**Target Environment:** Acid Etch Bench / Wet Chemical Processing Area  

---

### 1. Purpose & Scope
This SOP outlines the protocol for verifying face velocity containment, dynamic sash aerodynamic response, and tracer gas certification under ANSI/ASHRAE 110 standards for acid exhaust fume hoods and PTFE chemical wet benches. This certification ensures chemical vapor containment during wet-chemical cleaning, oxide stripping, and photolithography wet development steps (e.g., Shipley 1813 / MF-319 wet processing) for Gen 2 DRAM fabrication.

---

### 2. Required Equipment & Metrology Tools
- **Thermal Anemometer (Hot-wire / Vane):** Calibrated velocity grid meter (0.01 m/s resolution).
- **Tracer Gas Injection System:** Pure Sulfur Hexafluoride ($SF_6$) delivery manifold with critical flow orifice set to 4.0 L/min.
- **Gas Analyzer:** Electron Capture Detector (ECD) or Miran SapphIRe portable infrared gas analyzer (0.01 ppm detection limit).
- **Dynamic Sash Metrology Rig:** Linear displacement sensor with encoder to measure sash travel speed and response latency.
- **Titanium Tetrachloride / Glycol Fog Generator:** Neutral-buoyancy visual smoke tracer.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Pre-Test Inspection & Mechanical Zeroing
1. Inspect the fume hood aerodynamic airfoil, rear baffle positions, and PTFE sash tracks for obstructions or particulate accumulation.
2. Confirm the laboratory supply HVAC systems are in steady-state operation with no direct air currents (> 0.15 m/s) impinging within 1.5 m of the hood face.
3. Level and zero the dynamic sash displacement sensor rig.

#### Step 2: Grid-Based Face Velocity Profile Measurement
1. Position the sash at the certified operational working height (typically 450 mm / 18 inches).
2. Establish a multi-point imaginary grid across the sash opening (measuring points spaced at centers of equal areas, $\le 300\text{ mm} \times 300\text{ mm}$).
3. Clamp the thermal anemometer at each grid node and record the 20-second average face velocity.
4. Calculate the average face velocity and the percentage deviation across all grid positions.

#### Step 3: Flow Visualization & Airfoil Boundary Layer Verification
1. Introduce low-velocity neutral-buoyancy smoke along the bottom airfoil, perimeter jambs, and interior rear baffles.
2. Verify smoke moves smoothly across the work surface into the lower exhaust slot without vortex roll-out or boundary layer separation.
3. Traverse smoke along the sash handle and upper opening edge to check for vortex shedding.

#### Step 4: Tracer Gas Containment Testing ($SF_6$)
1. Mount the ASHRAE 110 ejector 300 mm behind the sash face on the centerline of the PTFE bench.
2. Mount the mannequin and sampling probe 75 mm in front of the sash plane at typical operator breathing height.
3. Release $SF_6$ tracer gas at a stabilized flow rate of 4.0 L/min.
4. Log continuous concentration readings over a 5-minute sampling interval under static sash conditions.

#### Step 5: Dynamic Sash Movement Effect (VAV Metrology)
1. Actuate the sash from fully closed to the maximum certified design height and return to closed position at a controlled mechanical travel speed.
2. Measure the variable air volume (VAV) exhaust dampener response time and record peak tracer leakage during rapid dynamic movement cycles.
3. Ensure no concentration spikes breach allowable exposure control limits during sash transitions.

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Tolerance / Limit | Exact Physical Units |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Average Face Velocity** | $0.50$ | $\pm 0.05$ (Grid Uniformity $\le \pm 10\%$) | $\text{m/s}$ (meters per second) |
| **ASHRAE 110 Containment Rating** | $\le 0.05$ | Maximum control level | $\text{ppm}$ ($SF_6$ tracer leakage) |
| **VAV Aerodynamic Response Time** | $\le 3.0$ | Time to restore $0.50\text{ m/s}$ face velocity | $\text{s}$ (seconds) |
| **Dynamic Sash Travel Speed** | $\le 50$ | Controlled testing speed | $\text{mm/minute}$ |

---

### 5. Verified Local Literature Citations
- **[Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)]**: Referenced for photolithography wet-chemical processing context, establishing developer containment protocols (Microposit MF-319 developer wet-bench processing and DI rinse cycles) and Gen 2 micro-scale alignment tolerances ($\pm 5\text{ \mu m}$).
- **[Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation]**: Referenced for standardized slow mechanical stage motion and linear velocity handling limits ($< 50\text{ mm/minute}$) used as the benchmark rate for controlled displacement metrology rigs.
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Referenced for wafer unit-level cleanroom environmental and chemical purity constraints associated with Gen 2 DRAM wet dielectric etch steps (ONO stack and Ta2O5 / Al2O3 high-k deposition preparation).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dynamic sash movement introduces severe aerodynamic drag, eddy shedding, and transient boundary layer detachment across the hood aperture. If the VAV damper controller response time (tau) exceeds 1.5 seconds, the temporary negative-pressure collapse allows corrosive acid vapors (HF, HNO3, HCl) to spill into the cleanroom breathing zone. Static 100 fpm multi-point face velocity calibration is insufficient; high-speed multi-axis dynamic sash sweeps with SF6 tracer gas metrology are mandatory to ensure containment integrity during rapid operator access.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: ASHRAE 110-2016 containment validation for semiconductor wet chemical hoods requires three distinct phases: flow visualization (titanium tetrachloride/glycol smoke generator), face velocity profiling (hot-wire anemometer array traversing 12-point grid at sash openings of 18 inches and full open), and quantitative tracer gas detection (SF6 cylinder release at 4.0 L/min through an internal ejector manifold while sampling at 1.0 cm outside the sash perimeter). Control level must demonstrate AI (As Installed) or AU (As Used) containment rating of < 0.05 ppm under dynamic sash movement at 1.0 to 1.5 ft/s traverse rate.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring calibrated SF6 electron capture detector (ECD) or portable IR photoacoustic gas analyzers (Miriam/Innova) in Southeast Asia has an 8-to-10 week lead time and high rental cost. Calibration grade SF6 (99.99%) cylinders face strict greenhouse gas import quotas in Vietnam. Recommend securing local ISO 17025 accredited cleanroom certification contractors equipped with TSI VelociCalc thermal anemometers and Miran SapphIRe analyzers before wet bench commissioning milestones.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Dynamic sash containment certification directly gates chemical loading of hydrofluoric and piranha etch tanks. Any containment failure or VAV instability pushes wet clean lithography preparation past the critical Gen 1 wafer processing schedule. Metrology certification must be completed, signed off, and archived with physical safety lockouts enabled within a 48-hour commissioning window.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. VAV damper hunting/hysteresis causing cyclical face velocity collapse below 60 fpm during dynamic sash lowering, producing acid fume puff-out.
1. Dead zones and wake vortices behind the aerodynamic sash sill and bottom lip entraining heavy acid aerosols toward the operator torso plane.
1. SF6 tracer containment breakdown exceeding 0.10 ppm during rapid sash opening (>1.0 ft/s) caused by improper hood rear baffle slot differential pressure balance.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-1-3-01` | **ASHRAE 110 Static Face Velocity Grid Profiling & Uniformity Mapping** | TSI 9565 VelociCalc thermal hot-wire anemometer (calibrated ISO 17025, accuracy ±3% of reading or ±3 ft/min), fixed mounting tripod, non-turbulent grid positioning jig. | 1. Divide the sash opening into an imaginary equal-area grid with centers spaced no more than 6.0 inches apart (minimum 12 grid points: 4 columns x 3 rows). 2. Mount the thermal anemometer probe at the exact centroid of each grid cell perpendicular to the plane of the sash. 3. Log continuous velocity readings at 1.0-second intervals for 20 seconds per grid location. 4. Calculate the time-averaged face velocity for each point, the overall average face velocity across all points, and the standard deviation. | `Average face velocity across all grid points must be 100.0 ± 10.0 fpm (0.51 ± 0.05 m/s); no individual grid point shall deviate by more than ±20.0% from the grand mean (minimum point velocity >= 80.0 fpm, maximum <= 120.0 fpm).` |
| `TC-WET-BENCH-SAFETY-3-1-3-02` | **ASHRAE 110 Dynamic Sash Sweep SF6 Tracer Gas Containment Metrology** | Calibrated SF6 tracer gas cylinder (99.99%), critical orifice flow generator set at 4.00 ± 0.10 L/min, ASHRAE 110 ejector manifold, automated linear sash actuator, high-speed electron capture detector (ECD) / photoacoustic infrared gas analyzer (LOD <= 0.005 ppm). | 1. Initiate SF6 tracer release at exactly 4.0 L/min for 60 seconds to establish internal saturation. 2. Record baseline leakage concentration at working sash height for 30 seconds. 3. Dynamically cycle the sash between 6.0 inches and 24.0 inches height at a controlled velocity of 1.2 ± 0.1 ft/s for 10 consecutive cycles. 4. Continuously log the external SF6 concentration at 10 Hz sampling rate during movement and for 120 seconds post-movement. 5. Extract peak transient concentration and time-weighted average concentration. | `Peak transient SF6 escape concentration shall not exceed 0.050 ppm (50 ppb) during any dynamic sweep cycle; 5-minute rolling time-weighted average (TWA) containment leakage must remain <= 0.010 ppm (10 ppb).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level B chemical splash suit (Teflon/Tychem 10000 coated) or heavyweight fluoropolymer splash apron with sleeves, Full-face NIOSH-approved air-purifying respirator (APR) equipped with multi-contaminant acid gas/organic vapor/P100 particulate cartridge, Double-layered heavy neoprene outer gloves (28 mil) over chemical-resistant Ansell Barrier inner gloves, Chemical-resistant safety boots with steel toe and non-sparking static dissipative soles (ASTM F2413), Polycarbonate face shield (8-inch coverage, ANSI Z87.1 D3 rated) worn over splash goggles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For SF6 exposure: Immediately relocate personnel to fresh air; administer oxygen if dyspnea or asphyxiation occurs due to oxygen displacement. In the presence of simulated/acid bench contamination: Inhalation: Move to fresh air, administer 100% humidified oxygen, immediately summon EMS. Dermal (HF hazard context): Flush copious water for 5 minutes, continuously massage 2.5% Calcium Gluconate topical gel into affected skin until medical arrival. Eye splash: Irrigate with sterile 1.0% calcium gluconate eye solution or buffered saline eye-wash for minimum 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Corrosion-resistant dedicated polypropylene/PTFE exhaust ductwork connected to centralized wet acid counter-flow scrubber running at minimum static differential pressure of -1.8 in. w.g. VAV venturi valve damper response speed < 1.0 second with uninterruptible exhaust blower redundancy.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Tracer gas SF6 exhaust must vent via dedicated rooftop stack above cleanroom re-entrainment envelope with scrubbing/recovery compliance. Condensed acid droplets and sump effluent must route directly to automated Acid Waste Neutralization (AWN) system utilizing 20% NaOH dosing to neutralize pH between 6.5 and 8.5 with continuous fluoride ion-selective monitoring.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sulfur Hexafluoride (Tracer Gas)** | `2551-62-4` | Research/Instrument Grade 4.0 | `99.99% vol` |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (Hood Chemical Simulant Context)** | `7664-39-3` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade (Cleanroom) | `49.0% wt` |
| **Nitric Acid** | `7697-37-2` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `70.0% wt` |
| **Propylene Glycol (Smoke Visualization Simulant)** | `57-55-6` | USP / High Purity | `99.5% wt` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `15 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `2 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry, solvent-cleaned PTFE bench surface, exhaust baffles wiped clean with 0.1-micron filtered DI water, mechanical sash slides degreased and lubed with chemically inert Krytox fluorinated grease.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Containment-certified, zero-tracer residual, negative pressure interlock engaged, certified ASHRAE 110 calibration sticker sealed on sash exterior glass.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Operating wet acid etch baths with uncertified or expired containment risks turbulent vortex spillover into cleanroom, causing acute operator acid vapor exposure and catastrophic copper/aluminum interconnect corrosion on adjacent processing tools.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete ASHRAE 110-2016 containment validation of the acid exhaust PTFE fume hood, verifying static multi-point face velocity uniformity and dynamic sash sweep tracer gas containment with VAV response time under 1.0 second.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ASHRAE_110_Dynamic_Containment_Certification_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Face_Velocity_12_Point_Grid_Telemetry.csv`
- [ ] `SF6_Dynamic_Sash_Sweep_ECD_Tracer_Log.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean static face velocity at 18-inch sash working height** | `100.0 fpm` | ±10.0 fpm | Multi-point calibrated hot-wire anemometer grid measurement averaging over 12 points per ASHRAE 110 Section 6 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Face velocity spatial distribution uniformity across sash grid** | `0.0 fpm deviation from nominal` | ±20.0% of mean velocity | Statistical relative standard deviation analysis of 20-second logged grid cell centroids |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Dynamic sash sweep peak SF6 tracer gas escape concentration** | `0.005 ppm` | < 0.050 ppm maximum peak | Continuous high-speed electron capture detector sampling 1.0 cm from sash plane during 1.2 ft/s dynamic sash motion |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> ASHRAE 110-2016 containment performance rating meets or exceeds 'AU 0.05' under dynamic sash cycling, face velocity uniformity confirms all grid points within 80-120 fpm range, VAV response time logs sub-1.0s stabilization, and EHS Lead & Metrology Signoff signatures are affixed to the equipment certificate.
